docs.title: Ability Atomic Treat
docs.text:
"Always gives a bee an Ability Rate Mutation."

The Ability Atomic Treat is a treat that always gives a bee an Ability Rate mutation. It works like an Atomic Treat, but the mutation is always Ability Rate instead of a random one.

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
• +1,000 bond.
  • Always mutates the bee. The new mutation replaces any mutation it already had.
Mutation Chance Value % Ability Rate Always +1% to +5%

The value is random and leans towards the low end, but 7% of the time it rolls the maximum. The bee's level doesn't change the range.

docs.title: Ways to obtain
docs.text: • Rebirth rewards (rebirth number, with the amount in brackets): 17 (5), 19 (10), 20 (25), 30 (100), 33 (400).

docs.title: Ability Tokens
docs.text:
Ability tokens are tokens generated by bees, which can be collected to activate special abilities and buffs. Almost all bees spawn ability tokens, with the exceptions being ungifted Basic Bee and Brave Bee without Beequips. If the player doesn't collect a token within a certain amount of time, it fades away. Ability tokens are only sent to the bee's owner, so players can't see or collect tokens made by other players' bees. Collection is checked by the server: you collect a token when you are within 4 studs of it horizontally and 6 studs vertically. Prior to the May 7th, 2018 update, other players' tokens were visible, but still couldn't be collected by others.

Some tokens aren't generated by the player's bees (such as honey tokens from flowers). The player can tell apart the two types of tokens by the fact that tokens dropped by bees give off gold sparkles, while tokens generated through other means do not sparkle. Also, tokens dropped by someone else's bees are not visible to the player, which means every visible token is collectible (though there is a bug where some loot tokens cannot be collected, usually at the end of a Honeystorm or Snowstorm).

docs.title: Spawning categories
docs.text:
Ability tokens fall into 3 categories, based on when a bee can spawn that token:

  • Gather: Ability tokens that can be generated when the bees are collecting pollen. Most ability tokens that can be generated under this situation can collect pollen and/or boost pollen collection.
  • Battle: Ability tokens that can be generated when the bees are targeting/attacking mobs. Most ability tokens that can be generated under this situation can inflict damage or debuffs to enemies and boost bees' combat process.
  • Idle: Ability tokens that can be generated when the bees are not doing any other activities (gathering, attacking, converting,...)

Some ability tokens fall into multiple or all of the categories above.

docs.title: Spawning attempts
docs.text:
When a bee pauses after making movement (either to gather a flower, to attack, or to simply turn), it will attempt to spawn its ability tokens.

Each ability token has 3 variables that dictate how often the ability token can spawn:

  • Use cooldown: The amount of time it takes after the ability token has been spawned for the bee to attempt to summon that ability token again.
  • Attempt cooldown: The amount of time a bee has to wait in-between attempts before it can attempt to spawn the ability token again.
  • Attempt success rate: The probability that the attempt succeeds. If the attempt succeeds, the ability token is added to a pool that the bee uses to spawn its ability tokens.

When a bee attempts to spawn its ability tokens, it goes through every token ability it can spawn and check if its use cooldown and attempt cooldown has expired. If it has, the bee attempts to spawn the token. If this attempt succeeds, the token is added to a pool. Once every ability has been checked, the bee looks in its pool and picks a random token to spawn, removing that token while keeping every other token in the pool for the next spawn attempt. The spawned token then starts its use cooldown again.

A bee can spawn at most one ability token per action (gathering, attacking or idling), and none while it is converting at the hive or fetching. Gifted bees also roll Inspire when they gather.

The average time between two tokens of the same ability can be found using the formula: \(time=useCooldown+attemptCooldown\times ({\frac {1}{attemptSuccessRate}}-1)\). The first attempt happens as soon as the use cooldown ends, and each failed attempt adds one attempt cooldown. If the attempt cooldown is longer than the use cooldown, use the attempt cooldown in place of the use cooldown.

docs.title: Stats
docs.text: These are stats which affect the characteristics of ability tokens.

docs.title: Bee Ability Rate
docs.text:
Bee Ability Rate increases or decreases how often bees spawn their ability tokens, by dividing the use cooldown and attempt cooldown, as well as multiplying the attempt success rate. Note that because of this, Bee Ability Rate increases or decreases ability tokens' spawn rate by much more than its stated amount. Ability rate can't go below 0.1, and the success rate is capped at 100%.

For example: a 200% bee ability rate will reduce an ability's use and attempt cooldown to 50% of its original value (100% ÷ 200%), and increase its success rate by 100% (or double it).

docs.title: Ability Token Lifespan
docs.text:
Ability Token Lifespan extends the duration of uncollected ability tokens generated by bees before they despawn. It can be boosted by a Gifted Stubborn Bee and Cog Amulet and by the Paper Angel and Paperclip beequips, and also temporarily by adding the Drooping Stubborn Bee Sticker to the Sticker Stack. The maximum amount currently possible is 145%.

A token's lifetime is its base lifetime × the Ability Token Lifespan multiplier. Most buff tokens last 4 seconds, and tokens with no set lifetime last 20 seconds. Lifespan sources in the game's code include the Melittology "Lingering Tokens" perk (ability tokens last 3 times longer), the Gifted bonus "+15% Ability Token Lifespan" and the Steering Wheel Ornament (+5%).

docs.title: Ability Duplication Chance
docs.text:
When there is a chance, ability tokens will spawn its duplicated/duped variants randomly on a field. Duped tokens hover over the field and last for double the tokens' lifespan, and that lifespan is further increased by 5% per Digital Bee's level. Duped tokens can be collected/activated by standing beneath it for 1 second.

Ability duplication chance can be increased by field corruption from Digital Bee's Glitch and Map Corruption ability tokens. It also can be increased from Gifted Digital Bee. Other than from Digital Bees, ability duplication chance can also be increased by the 'Corrupt' upgrade purchasable from the Robo Bear Challenge and only applies during that challenge. It can also be provided by Science Bear during his "Corrupting The Glitched Drive" quest, where he corrupts the Clover, Spider, Pineapple, Rose, Pine Tree and Mountain Top fields at random.

docs.title: Bee Movespeed
docs.text:
Bee Movespeed affects how fast bees move and perform actions.

While not directly related to ability tokens, having more Bee Movespeed allows bees to make more attempts at creating Ability Tokens, and vice versa. This overall increases or decreases the average spawn rate of an ability token.

docs.title: Bomb
docs.text:
Red BombBlue BombBuzz Bomb Red Bomb+Blue Bomb+Buzz Bomb+

Bomb collects pollen from flowers in an area. All Bomb tokens have a black disc. Red, Blue and Buzz Bombs share one icon, tinted red, blue or white, and the Bomb+ tokens use the same icon with a plus sign.

Split by the types of flowers the ability collects, there are 3 categories:

  • Buzz Bombs collect 7 pollen from all types of flowers.
  • Red Bombs collect 10 pollen from only Red flowers.
  • Blue Bombs collect 10 pollen from only Blue flowers.

The amount of pollen collected increases by 10% per level (e.g., 200% on a level 20 bee).

Split by the range of the ability, there are 2 categories:

  • Bomb tokens collect from 13 surrounding flowers.
  • Bomb+ tokens collect from 29 surrounding flowers.

Collecting Bomb tokens also grants the Bomb Combo buff, which grants a buff to Bomb Power.

Many bees have at least one of the bomb variants:

  • Red Bomb is granted by Rascal, Demon, and Shy Bees.
  • Red Bomb+ is granted by Fire, Demon, and Festive Bees.
  • Blue Bomb is granted by Bumble, Bubble, and Buoyant Bees.
  • Blue Bomb+ is granted by Frosty, Ninja, and Vicious Bees.
  • Buzz Bomb is granted by Bomber, Commander, and Exhausted Bees.
  • Buzz Bomb+ is granted by Demo, Lion, and Fuzzy Bees.

There are also other sources of Bomb tokens:

  • Balloons during a Surprise Party have a chance to generate Blue and a Buzz Bomb tokens.
  • Many Beequips can give the bee that equipped it Bomb abilities, if the beequip has them.
  • Bang Snaps can give Bomb and Bomb+ of any color.
  • Smiley Stickers can give Blue Bomb.
  • Bottle Caps can give Buzz Bomb.

If Red Bomb Sync is on, all Red Bombs collect white pollen. If Blue Bomb Sync is on, all Blue Bombs collect white pollen. If both Syncs are active, all Bombs collect any color of pollen.

When Pollen Haze is active, all Bomb ability tokens are automatically collected, and they may also pollinate flower patches that they collect from.

Bomb falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Bomb has a use cooldown of 8 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 4 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 25%. This gives an average spawn rate of 1 token every 20 seconds.

The token lasts for 4 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Boost
docs.text:
Red BoostBlue BoostWhite Boost

Boost grants the player the Boost buff of the respective color, which gives buffs to the matching-color pollen. When collected, red/blue (depending on the type) and white sparkles appear on the player's bees and their character.

Many bees have at least one of the Boost variants:

  • Red Boost is generated by Rad, Riley, and Shy Bees.
  • Blue Boost is generated by Frosty, Cool, Bucko, Diamond, and Tadpole Bees.
  • White Boost is generated by Windy Bee.
  • A Gifted Crimbolt Bee's Trio passive has an independent 33% chance every 4.5 seconds to spawn a Red, Blue and White Boost together.

There are also other sources of Boost tokens:

  • Balloons during a Surprise Party have a chance to generate White and Blue Boost tokens.
  • Unactivated targets from Target Practice spawn Red Boost tokens.
  • Festive Gifts and Festive Mark commonly spawn Red Boost tokens as one of its rewards.
  • Many Beequips can give the bee that equipped it Boost abilities, if the beequip has them.
  • Berets can give Blue Boost.
  • Leis can give Red or Blue Boost.

Sometimes flowers generate Boost tokens instead of Honey tokens. These tokens look almost identical to Boost tokens generated by bees, except the latter have gold sparkles while the former does not. Boost tokens from flowers take more time to fade away. These Boost tokens generated by flowers do not count for Ability Token quests and badges. Token Links collect Boost tokens generated by the player's bees, but not tokens spawned by the field.

The buff granted by the Boost token can be found in other sources. For more information, see the relevant article.

Boost falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Boost has a use cooldown of 4.5 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 4.5 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 33.33%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 13.5 seconds.

The token lasts for 4 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Haste
docs.text:
Haste

Haste gives the player the Haste buff, which grants extra movement speed. Haste does not affect the speed of bees or of players while using the Parachute or Glider.

Hasty, Shocked, Ninja, Photon and Crimbolt bees have the ability. Other sources of Haste tokens include:

  • Balloons during a Surprise Party have a chance to generate Haste tokens.
  • Toy Drums and Whistles can give the bee that equipped it the ability, if the beequip has it.

The Haste buff can be consumed by the player's Tornado to improve the summoned tornado.

The buff granted by the Haste token can be found in other sources. For more information, see the relevant article.

Haste falls into the Gather, Battle, and Idle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers, while attacking mobs, and while idling.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Haste has a use cooldown of 4.5 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 4.5 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 33.33%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 13.5 seconds.

The token lasts for 4 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Honey Gift
docs.text:
Honey Gift

There are 2 types of Honey Gift tokens in the game, visually identical to each other. They serve the same purpose of giving the player honey.

  • Honey Gift tokens are worth 100 honey multiplied by bee level squared.
  • Honey Gift+ tokens are worth 250 honey multiplied by bee level squared.

These amounts can be increased by having a higher Honey from Tokens percentage.

Honey Bee is the only bee to have the Honey Gift ability, and Diamond Bee is the only bee to have the Honey Gift+ ability. There are no other sources of Honey Gift nor Honey Gift+ in the game.

Honey Gift falls into the Gather, Battle, and Idle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers, while attacking mobs, and while idling.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Honey Gift has a use cooldown of 120 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 60 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 25%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 300 seconds.

The token lasts for 10 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Focus
docs.text:
Focus

Focus gives the player the Focus buff, which grants extra Critical Chance. When collected, green and white sparkles appear on the player's bees and their character.

Looker, Commander, and Music bees have the ability. Other sources of Focus tokens include:

  • Activated targets from Target Practice spawn Focus tokens, and collecting Target Practice outside of a field has an 80% chance of granting the buff.
  • Reindeer Antlers and Pink Shades can give the bee that equipped it the ability, if the beequip has it.

Focus falls into the Gather and Battle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers and while attacking mobs.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Focus has a use cooldown of 4.5 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 4.5 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 33.33%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 13.5 seconds.

The token lasts for 4 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Token Link
docs.text:
Token Link

A Token Link collects all other ability tokens (except for other Token Links) and grants 25 honey and an additional 10 honey per level for each other token collected this way (e.g. 175 honey per token collected on level 15 bee).

For stacking purposes, note that the ability tokens are collected based on how early they were spawned. If two or more link tokens are collected at the same time, they may link the same tokens. The other tokens activate once, but the player gets two sets of honey from link tokens.

A Token Link can also collect Honey Gift tokens generated by Honey Bee, Diamond Bee, honey tokens from Vicious Bee's Impale, treat tokens from Puppy Bee's Fetch ability, tokens from Festive Bee's Festive Gift ability, tokens from Cub Buddy gifts, and tokens from mobs. However, it does not collect honey tokens generated by Coin Scatter, Gummy Star or Target Practice.

Exhausted, Rage, Shocked, Music and Crimbolt bees have the ability. Other sources of Token Link tokens include:

  • Balloons during a Surprise Party have a chance to generate Token Link tokens.
  • Paper Angels, Paperclips and Bead Lizards can give the bee that equipped it the ability, if the beequip has it.

Token Link falls into the Gather and Battle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers and while attacking mobs.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Token Link has a use cooldown of 5 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 5 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 33.33%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 15 seconds.

The token lasts for 4 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Mark
docs.text:
Pollen MarkHoney Mark

A Mark token deploys a Mark in a random area on a field that grants a specific buff when the player stands in its range. When a mark is activated, its radius and the green light on top of the mark lights up, and the player is given a buff based on what mark they activated.

Each Mark can be stacked to increase its effect, done by linking with each other (i.e. overlapping each other). If the player stands in a Mark that is linked to another one, all linked Marks are activated.

There are currently 4 types of marks in the game:

  • Pollen Mark gives the Pollen Mark buff, which increases all pollen.
  • Honey Mark gives the Honey Mark buff, which grants conversion links and increases Convert Rate.
  • When the player walks off the Honey Mark's range, conversion links remain, and bees still convert honey normally until they finish converting. The player will lose the Convert Rate buff, however.
  • Precise Mark gives the Precise Mark buff, which increases Critical Chance and Super-Crit Chance. See the dedicated section for more details.
  • Festive Mark gives the Festive Mark, which grants several buffs. See the dedicated section for more details.

The rest of this section will only concern Pollen Marks and Honey Marks.

The two Mark abilities are split into the Mark and Mark+ variant.

  • The Mark variant spawns Marks that lasts for 7 seconds (+0.2s per bee level) with a range of 14 studs.
  • The Mark+ variant spawns Marks that lasts for 8 seconds (+0.25s per bee level) with a range of 18 studs.

Many bees have at least one of the Mark variants:

  • Pollen Mark is granted by Stubborn and Carpenter Bees.
  • Pollen Mark+ is granted by Vector Bee.
  • Honey Mark is granted by Honey and Festive Bees.
  • Honey Mark+ is granted by Carpenter Bee.

There are also other sources of Mark tokens:

  • Balloons during a Surprise Party have a chance to generate Pollen Mark and Honey Mark tokens.
  • Smiley Stickers can give the bee that equipped it the Honey Mark ability, if the beequip has it.

Mark falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Mark has a use cooldown of 20 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 5 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 25%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 35 seconds.

The token lasts for 8 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

The player can see other people's Marks, but they can't see those Marks' range, the Marks don't grant buffs to them, they can't be linked with their Marks, and vice versa (with the exception of Festive Marks).

docs.title: Rage
docs.text:
Rage

Rage gives the player the Rage buff, which grant bees extra attack. When collected, an angry war scream can be heard, which happens in increasing pitch with higher stacks of Rage.

Only Rage Bee and Spicy Bee have the Rage ability. There are no other sources of Rage in the game.

Rage falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Rage has a use cooldown of 50 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 3 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 50%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 53 seconds.

The token lasts for 24 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Baby Love
docs.text:
Baby Love

Baby Love gives the player the Baby Love buff, which grants extra pollen and loot luck. When collected, a baby's laugh can be heard, and pink and white sparkles appear on the player's character.

Only Baby Bee and Gifted Tadpole Bee have the Baby Love ability. Reindeer Antlers can also give the bee that equipped it the Baby Love ability, if the beequip has it.

Baby Love falls into the Gather, Idle, and Battle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers, while idling, and while attacking mobs.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Baby Love has a use cooldown of 60 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 5 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 11.11%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 100 seconds.

The token lasts for 8 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Melody
docs.text:
Melody

Melody gives the player the Melody buff, which grants extra Critical Power. When collected, black and white sparkles appear on the player's bees and their character.

Only Music Bees have the ability. Other sources of Melody tokens include:

  • Balloons during a Surprise Party have a chance to generate Melody tokens.
  • Toy Horns, Kazoos, Whistles and Charm Bracelets can give the bee that equipped it the ability, if the beequip has it.

Melody falls into the Gather and Battle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers and while attacking mobs.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Melody has a use cooldown of 45 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 15 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 33.33%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 75 seconds.

The token lasts for 8 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Inspire
docs.text:
Inspire

Inspire is an ability exclusive to Gifted Bees.

When collected, it gives the player the Inspire buff, which grants extra pollen. A small glowing star appears, floating up from the token while fading away.

The buff granted by the Inspire token can be found in other sources. For more information, see the relevant article.

Inspire falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Inspire has a use cooldown of 60 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 5 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 1%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 555 seconds.

The token lasts for 8 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Inflate Balloons
docs.text:
Inflate Balloons

Inflate Balloons is an ability token exclusive to Buoyant Bee.

When collected, Buoyant Bee increases the pollen stored inside the player's balloons on the field the player is in by +5%, which increases by +0.01% per level. It then summons a Blue Balloon that floats around the field for 20 seconds (+2s per level), with capacity that scales with the player's capacity, the bee that summoned the token's level, and currently active field boost stacks.

If Buoyant Bee is gifted, there is a 5% (+0.5% per lvl, doubled if the field is boosted) chance to summon a Gold Balloon instead.

Standing under a balloon gives the Balloon Aura buff, which increases Pollen and Honey From Tokens.

Inflate Balloons falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Inflate Balloons has a use cooldown of 28 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 8 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 25%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 52 seconds.

The token lasts for 4 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Surprise Party
docs.text:
Surprise Party

Surprise Party is an ability exclusive to Gifted Buoyant Bee.

When collected, 1 Gold Balloon (+1 every 5 levels) is summoned for each player on the server. All of the player's Balloons then start spawning random ability tokens for a few seconds.

Visually, a big party popper appears with a server-wide announcement: 🎉Surprise balloons from {Username}!!".

Ability tokens spawned by balloons through Surprise Party include:

  • Blue Boost
  • White Boost
  • Blue Bomb
  • Buzz Bomb
  • Pollen Mark
  • Honey Mark
  • Haste
  • Token Link
  • Melody

If the player has triggered Surprise Party within the last 8 minutes, Inflate Balloons is activated instead, though it guarantees spawning a Gold Balloon. The cooldown is only applied to the player.

Surprise Party falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Surprise Party has a use cooldown of 360 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 15 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 12.5%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 465 seconds.

The token lasts for 24 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Fuzz Bombs
docs.text:
Fuzz Bombs

Fuzz Bombs is an ability exclusive to Fuzzy Bee.

When activated, 2 fuzz bombs (+1 every 5 levels) are summoned. Fuzz bombs wander around the field in a zigzag path on which they are spawned for 8 seconds. When touched by players, tornadoes, or Petal Shurikens, it collects pollen from 29 surrounding flowers and may pollinate nearby flowers. It also grants the Bomb Combo buff, which increases Bomb Power. The amount of pollen collected scales with Buzz Bomb multiplier and bee level.

Fuzz Bombs falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Fuzz Bombs has a use cooldown of 20 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 10 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 33.33%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 40 seconds.

The token lasts for 4 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Pollen Haze
docs.text:
Pollen Haze

Pollen Haze is an ability exclusive to Gifted Fuzzy Bee.

When activated, a haze is summoned over the field for 30 seconds. During that time, up to 30 random flowers pollinate every second, flowers grow faster, and Bomb Tokens are automatically collected and have a chance to pollinate flowers.

If there has been a Pollen Haze over the field within the last 3 minutes, Fuzz Bombs is activated instead.

Pollen Haze falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Pollen Haze has a use cooldown of 75 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 15 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 16.67%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 150 seconds.

The token lasts for 8 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Target Practice
docs.text:
Target Practice

Target Practice is an ability exclusive to Precise Bee.

When collected on a field, it causes the bee to fly above the field the player is in and face the part of the field it is opposite from. Then it projects 3 targets, from the closest to farthest from the bee. Walking on and passing the target(s) activates it.

After a few seconds:

  • All of the activated targets will be shot by the bee, collecting pollen from 29 surrounding flowers and spawning a Focus token.
  • The amount of pollen collected is equal to x2 Precise Bee's attack and increased by +10% per level.
  • With Flame Heat, the shot gains up to x4 pollen and up to +50% instant conversion.
  • All of the inactive targets spawn Red Boost tokens instead.

If the player is shot while standing on a target, all ability tokens are collected, and all of the player's current Flame Heat buff is used to instantly convert pollen from the player's container, with half of that turning into 5 honey tokens around the shot target. The amount of pollen converted is equal to 50% total conversion + x10 Precise Bee's convert amount, and increased by up to x10 with consumed Flame Heat and up to x3 with field boost stacks.

When all 3 targets are activated, all ability tokens are collected and the player is granted a stack of Precision, which grants extra super-crit chance.

If the player collects a Target Practice token that is outside of a field, or when the bee that summoned the token is outside the field, they will immediately be granted either the Precision or Focus buff. The chances of getting the Precision buff are 20%, and 80% for Focus buff.

Target Practice falls into the Battle and Gather categories, meaning it spawns while attacking mobs and while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Target Practice has a use cooldown of 24 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 6 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 25%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 42 seconds.

The token lasts for 8 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Precise Mark
docs.text:
If Precise Bee is gifted, the farthest target appears in purple. When only the farthest target is activated, it will summon a Precise Mark for 12 seconds (+0.5s per level) with an 18-stud radius.

When a Precise Mark is activated, the player is granted the Precise Mark buffs, which grants extra Critical Chance and Super-Crit Chance.

docs.title: Inferno
docs.text:
Inferno

Inferno is an ability primarily exclusive to Spicy Bee.

When collected, 6 flames are summoned in a circle around the collected token, and 2 Fire Bees spawns inside the circle. The bees last for 15 seconds (+1 second per level) with levels equal to 2 less than the bee that summoned them. If the bee that summoned the token is gifted, each summoned Fire Bee has a 10% (+1% per lvl) chance of being gifted.

Only Spicy Bee has the ability by default, but equipping a Demon Talismans to a Demon Bee can allow the bee to spawn the token if the beequip has the ability.

Inferno falls into the Gather and Battle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers and while attacking mobs.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Inferno has a use cooldown of 30 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 5 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 16.67%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 55 seconds.

The token lasts for 4 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Flame Fuel
docs.text:
Flame Fuel

Flame Fuel is an ability exclusive to Gifted Spicy Bee.

When collected, the player is given the Buffs & Debuffs#Flame Fuel buff, which increases flame duration. During the buff's uptime, oil will be tossed to every newly created flame, causing them to convert 50,000 pollen + 10% of the player's total hive convert. Oil will also be tossed to every newly created dark flames even if they were from the same flames.

Triggering Flame Fuel while an ability is spawning flames will only prolong part of the ability's flames, due to Token Links not activating tokens instantaneously.

Flame Fuel falls into the Gather and Battle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers and while attacking mobs.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Flame Fuel has a use cooldown of 45 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 15 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 33.33%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 75 seconds.

The token lasts for 8 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Summon Frog
docs.text:
Summon Frog

Summon Frog is an ability exclusive to Tadpole Bee.

When collected, a Frog is summoned at the position of the collected token. It lasts for 20 seconds (+2 seconds per level).

If the Tadpole Bee is gifted, Summon Frog has a 10% (+2% per level) chance to summon a Gifted Frog instead.

Summon Frog falls into the Gather and Battle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers and while attacking mobs.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Summon Frog has a use cooldown of 50 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 10 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 25%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 80 seconds.

The token lasts for 8 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Triangulate
docs.text:
Triangulate

Triangulate is an ability exclusive to Vector Bee.

When activated, a triangle is drawn between the positions of the collected token, the bee, and the player. Vector Bee starts moving in a random direction without stopping until the ability ends.

After 3 seconds, the triangle collects ability tokens and 10 pollen (+2 per level) from all flowers inside the triangle. Additionally, any marks inside the triangle boosts the pollen collected by Triangulate by 50%. There are also additional buffs based on what mark types are inside the triangle:

  • If the triangle contains at least 1 pollen mark, it gains x2 white pollen.
  • If the triangle contains at least 1 honey mark or festive mark, it gains 50% instant conversion.
  • If the triangle contains at least 1 precise mark, it always lands a critical hit.

If the token is collected while the container is full, the triangle does not appear.

Triangulate falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Triangulate has a use cooldown of 20 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 10 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 33.33%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 40 seconds.

The token lasts for 4 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Mark Surge
docs.text:
Mark Surge

Mark Surge is an ability exclusive to Gifted Vector Bee.

When collected, all active marks collect 7 pollen (+10% per level) from all flowers inside their radius, and extends their duration by 1 second (+0.1 seconds per level). There are extra effects for specific types of marks:

  • If the mark is a honey mark or festive mark, the pollen from the mark is instantly converted.
  • if the mark is a precise mark, it always lands a critical hit.

Each mark can only perform up to 5 surges.

Mark Surge falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Mark Surge has a use cooldown of 24 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 6 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 25%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 42 seconds.

The token lasts for 4 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Bear Morph
docs.text:
Black BearBrown BearPanda BearPolar BearMother BearScience Bear

Bear Morph is an ability exclusive to Bear Bee.

When collected, the player is granted the Bear Morph buff, which transforms the player into the bear on the token (either Black Bear, Brown Bear, Panda Bear or Polar Bear). This gives the player a buff in pollen gain, and sets the player's base movement speed and base jump power to a higher value than normal.

If Bear Bee is Gifted, it has a 20% chance to produce a morph for Mother Bear or Science Bear, which enhances on the base buff:

  • Mother Bear Morph grants more pollen than the base buff, as well as extra bee gather pollen.
  • Science Bear Morph grants an extra conversion link.

Note that while every morph comes from the same token, they are seen by the game as different buffs, meaning the player can have multiple Bear Morphs at the same time. This has a multiplicative effect, but does not increase the player's base movement speed and base jump power further, as each morph sets the two values to a given amount instead of increasing them. It is not possible to stack the same type of morph multiple times - it will only reset the buff's uptime.

Bear Morph falls into the Gather, Battle, and Idle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers, while attacking mobs, and while idling.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Bear Morph has a use cooldown of 45 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 15 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 50%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 60 seconds.

The token lasts for 20 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

Collecting the Bear Morph plays the same sound as collecting a Boost token.

If the player dies while Bear Morph is active, the effect is lost.

docs.title: Pulse
docs.text:
Blue PulseRed Pulse

Pulse refers to 2 abilities, Blue Pulse and Red Pulse, exclusive to Cobalt Bee and Crimson Bee respectively.

When activated, a pulse is fired, hopping between its matching-color bees that are active (Blue bees for Blue Pulse, Red bees for Red Pulse). When the pulse lands on a bee, it collects pollen from 9 surrounding flowers around them. It collects more pollen increases with each hop, and the amount of pollen collected is increased by 10% per level (e.g. 200% on a level 20 bee).

If the player activates either Pulse and they own both Cobalt and Crimson Bees, both Red and Blue Pulses are released. If this token is Duped, it will only fire a matching-color pulse, regardless of if the player owns both bees or not.

Pulse falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Pulse has a use cooldown of 12 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 6 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 25%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 30 seconds.

The token lasts for 12 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

Two Passive Abilities, Haste Pulser and Focus Pulser, can fire a pulse. However, neither fires two Pulses if the player has both of the guards or bees.

docs.title: Bomb Sync
docs.text:
Blue Bomb SyncRed Bomb Sync

Bomb Sync refers to 2 abilities, Blue Bomb Sync and Red Bomb Sync, exclusive to Cobalt Bee and Crimson Bee respectively.

When collected, the player is granted the Bomb Sync buff of the matching color, which allows matching-color Bombs to collect pollen from white flowers for 30 seconds (Blue Bombs for Blue Bomb Sync, Red Bombs for Red Bomb Sync), and also grants extra pollen and matching-color instant conversion.

If both are active, both Blue and Red Bombs can collect pollen from all flowers.

Bomb Sync falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Bomb Sync has a use cooldown of 30 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 15 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 33.33%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 60 seconds.

The token lasts for 24 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Festive Gift
docs.text:
Festive Gift

Festive Gift is an ability exclusive to Festive Bee.

When collected, every player in the server is granted random gifts (tokens) in a circle around them. The quality of the gifts is improved with Festive Bee's level, and whether Festive Bee is gifted. The player can't see or collect any other player's gifts. Visually, a big present appears above all players and a server-wide message announces: 🎁 Festive Gifts from {Username}! 🎁

Notably, this and Festive Sprouts are the only renewable methods to spawn the Festive Blessing and Beesmas Cheer tokens. They are not guaranteed from the gift, however.

The gifts include If Festive Bee is Gifted Red Boost Token

Festive Blessing Token Treats Sunflower Seeds Strawberries Pineapples Blueberries Honey Gumdrops Royal Jellies Ticket (Rare) Blue Extract (Rare) Red Extract (Rare) Magic Bean (Rare) Micro-Converter (Rare) Festive Bean (Exceptionally rare) Flying Festive Bee Sticker (Beesmas only, Unbelievably rare, odds increase with bee's level)

Beesmas Cheer Token

Glue (Rare) Oil (Rare) Enzymes (Rare) Glitter (Rare) Star Jelly (Rare) Field Dice (Rare)

Festive Gift falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Festive Gift has no use cooldown, an attempt cooldown of 30 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 25%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 120 seconds.

The token lasts for 24 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

The gifts (tokens) fade away in 8 seconds, ignoring any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Festive Blessing
docs.text:
Festive Blessing

Festive Blessing grants the player the Festive Blessing buff, which gives Instant Conversion and Conversion Rate.

Festive Blessing tokens are granted by Festive Gifts and Festive Sprouts. When collecting this token, a message appears: Activated "Festive Blessing" (Duration: [Time])

docs.title: Beesmas Cheer
docs.text:
Beesmas Cheer

Beesmas Cheer grants the player the Festive Blessing buff, which gives extra bee movespeed and pollen.

Beesmas Cheer tokens are granted by Festive Gifts (if Festive Bee is gifted) and Festive Sprouts. When collecting this token, a message appears: Activated "Beesmas Cheer" (Duration: [Time])

docs.title: Glob
docs.text:
Glob

Glob is an ability exclusive to Gummy Bee.

When collected, 49 (81 when gifted) flowers surrounding the position of the collected token is covered in Goo.

Glob falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Glob has a use cooldown of 6 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 3 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 33.33%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 12 seconds.

The token lasts for 4 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

This and Gumdrop Barrage can be used to activate Gummy Morph.

Glob makes a splatter noise when collected.

docs.title: Gumdrop Barrage
docs.text:
Gumdrop Barrage

Gumdrop Barrage is an ability exclusive to Gummy Bee.

When activated, multiple Gumdrops are launched in a large area, covering the field in Goo. The effect is similar to using Gumdrops (the item).

Gumdrop Barrage falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Gumdrop Barrage has a use cooldown of 9 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 4 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 25%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 21 seconds.

The token lasts for 4 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Beamstorm
docs.text:
Beamstorm

Beamstorm is an ability exclusive to Photon Bee.

When activated, 25 yellow beams (+2 per level) are fired from the sky into flowers in a 15x15 flowers area around the position of the collected token. When a flower is hit, all the pollen in it is collected, with a x2 Pollen multiplier.

If Photon Bee is gifted, the Beamstorm token's beams appear as white and the pollen collected by the beams is instantly converted into honey, in addition to white pollen collected being tripled.

Beamstorm falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Beamstorm has a use cooldown of 20 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 10 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 33.33%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 40 seconds.

The token lasts for 12 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Puppy Love
docs.text:
Puppy Love

Puppy Love is an ability exclusive to Puppy Bee.

When collected, the bond of the nearest 10 bees is increased by 30 (+10 bond per average level of all bees in the player's hive), It also grants the player the Puppy Love buff, which grants extra bee movespeed and bee gather amount.

Visually, a dog bark can be heard, a light is emitted, and a tiny heart appears.

Puppy Love falls into the Gather and Idle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers and while idling.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Puppy Love has a use cooldown of 80 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 10 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 20%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 120 seconds.

The token lasts for 8 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Fetch
docs.text:
Fetch

Fetch is an ability exclusive to Puppy Bee.

When collected, a ball spawns in front of the player. The player must kick the ball by touching it or it despawns in 5 seconds. Then the Puppy Bee chases the ball to try and pass it back to the player, despawning in the same amount of time. The player and the Puppy Bee can keep passing the ball back to each other until it despawns.

As the ball is passed over, it can collect pollen, tokens (other than treat tokens from Fetch itself), pop fuzz bombs, and bubbles. The amount of pollen collected is increased by 100% (+15% per level, e.g. 400% pollen increased on level 20 bee).

Every 3rd kick made by Puppy Bee creates a combo that spawns a treat token at Puppy Bee's current location, which increases in value. Unlike other treat tokens, these can be collected by Token Link. As the combo continues, the ball moves faster when kicked and it collects more pollen until it reaches the max combo that gives 256 treats (9 combos). Any further combo won't spawn treat tokens. The player can get a maximum of 511 treats per fetch ability, under normal conditions.

Fetch falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Fetch has a use cooldown of 140 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 5 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 50%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 145 seconds.

The token lasts for 8 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

The ball can sometimes fall outside of the field, out of range for the player or Puppy Bee to continue passing the ball to each other. It also sometimes gets stuck and allows the player to 'pass' it easily.

While the Puppy Bee plays Fetch, it does not do anything else but play Fetch. Playing Fetch can be dangerous if the player's bees are attacking enemies, as they can run into an enemy as they chase the ball.

If Puppy Bee is wearing the Reindeer Antlers beequip, the ability is enhanced to Reindeer Fetch.

docs.title: Scratch
docs.text:
Scratch

Scratch is an ability exclusive to Tabby Bee.

When collected, 7 (+1 per level) pollen is collected from 3 lines of 4 flowers. The pollen collected can be increased through #Tabby Love. If Tabby Bee is Gifted, Scratch always lands critical hits.

Visually, a cat's growl is heard and three cat claws rip through the field around the token.

Scratch falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Scratch has a use cooldown of 12 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 6 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 25%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 30 seconds.

The token lasts for 20 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Tabby Love
docs.text:
Tabby Love

Tabby Love is an ability exclusive to Tabby Bee.

When collected, the player is granted a permanent stack of Tabby Love, which permanently improves the stats of a player's Tabby Bee, making it collect more pollen, convert more pollen, and improving #Scratch's pollen gain.

If Tabby Love reaches max stacks, it instead grants the Tabby Blessing buffs, giving the player extra Critical Chance and Critical Power. If Gifted, the buff is changed to Tabby Blessing+, granting Super-Crit Chance on top of prior buffs.

Tabby Love falls into the Gather and Battle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers and while attacking mobs.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Tabby Love has a use cooldown of 120 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 60 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 20%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 360 seconds.

The token lasts for 16 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Impale
docs.text:
Impale

Impale is an ability exclusive to Vicious Bee.

Vicious Bee generates an Impale token that summons a number of spikes equal to the bee's level, that damages enemies for 5% of their current health and increases with Vicious Bee's attack, but the damage is reduced past 1,000. Mobs that have been hit by a spike take less damage from other consecutive spikes.

Each enemy hit by a spike generates a honey token worth 50 (+50 per level) honey. These honey tokens can be collected by Token Link and take 10 seconds to fade.

If Vicious Bee is Gifted, gold spikes spawn instead of normal ones. Impale will have +1 levels of accuracy added (meaning Vicious Bee's spikes can hit mobs that are one level higher than it without missing).

A more detailed explanation of the ability is provided below:

  • Impale first targets every living enemy in a 75-stud radius of the player.
  • If it finds a group of targets, it summons a spike at the nearest target's position, then waits up to 0.2 seconds before summoning another at the next target. This is repeated until every target in the group has been damaged once.
  • It then prepares a number of spikes equal to the level of the Vicious Bee that activated the ability.
  • If Impale has not run out of spikes yet, it will target every living enemy in a 75-stud radius of the player again. This is repeated until it runs out of spikes, or there are no more living targets in the radius.
  • The number of times an enemy has been targeted is stored, henceforth referred to in formulas as cnt.
  • The summoned spikes' accuracy work the same way as bee attacks, just with 1 extra level if Vicious Bee is gifted.
  • The damage dealt is calculated in this order:
  • Let atk be Vicious Bee's attack at the time of activation. Then \(baseDamage=2\times atk\).
  • If the target has the Humanoid tag (as of the current update, every enemy has this tag), adds 5% of target's HP to baseDamage.
  • \(baseDamage>1000\), excess damage is square rooted: \(baseDamage=1000+{\sqrt {baseDamage-1000}}\)
  • The damage then is nerfed by the number of times the enemy has been targeted: \(baseDamage=baseDamage\times 0.05+{\frac {baseDamage}{cnt}}\times 0.95\).
  • Critical hits and Super-Crits are then applied, along with any Impale damage multiplier, resulting in the variable finalDamage.
  • If a critical hit or Super-Crit occurred, the damage is nerfed to 75%: \(finalDamage=\left\lfloor {finalDamage\times 0.75+0.5}\right\rfloor\)
  • The enemy is dealt finalDamage damage.

Impale falls into the Battle category, meaning it spawns while attacking mobs.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Impale has a use cooldown of 30 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 1 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 100%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 30 seconds.

The token lasts for 24 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Tornado
docs.text:
Tornado

Tornado is an ability exclusive to Windy Bee.

When collected, all of the player's Haste stacks are taken to summon a tornado at the position of the token, assuming the token is on a field. The tornado moves around the field while dealing damage to mobs, collecting pollen and tokens, and popping bubbles and fuzz bombs, around a 5-tile-radius range (approximately 49 surrounding flower tiles) every second. It will also collect pollen out of balloons it passes through.

The speed, damage, and lifespan of a summoned tornado depends on the number of Haste stacks spent and the level of the bee that summoned it. Let x be the number of Haste stacks spent and y be the level of the bee that summoned it, the following formulas can be used:

  • \(multiplier=1+0.1\times {({\frac {y-1}{19}})}^{2}\)
  • \(duration=10+x\times 0.4+{\frac {x^{1.4}}{3.2}}\), add 2 if at least 1 stack of Haste was spent
  • \(damage=10+y^{1.5}\)
  • \(\left\lfloor 3.5+{\frac {y}{3}}\right\rfloor\) pollen from each flower around its radius per second. Pollen collected is multiplied by multiplier.
  • \(\left\lfloor 0.5+damage+(20+y^{1.5}\times 1.75-damage)\times {({\frac {x}{3}})}^{2}\right\rfloor\) damage to each enemy in its radius per second.
  • \(7+18\times {\frac {x}{10}}\) studs a second.
  • Lasts for \(\left\lfloor duration\times multiplier+0.5\right\rfloor\) seconds.

Note that if the Tornado token is collected outside or above the field, it does not summon a tornado but still spends Haste stacks.

Tornado falls into the Gather and Battle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers and while attacking mobs.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Tornado has a use cooldown of 80 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 10 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 33.33%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 100 seconds.

The token lasts for 24 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Glitch
docs.text:
Glitch

Glitch is an ability exclusive to Digital Bee.

When collected, the field the player is currently in is corrupted for 20 seconds (+1s per level). A glitch effect will occasionally appear on the field (which can be disabled in the System Page), every ability token collected in that field has a chance to be duplicated or "Duped", and Digital Bee will be able to spawn ☺︎ tokens.

The corruption on the field can be increased to raise the ability duplication chance and the pollen collection and instant conversion of duped abilities. The corruption can be increased by enhancing Digital Bee with Drives. Colored Drives increase the corruption of field with matching flowers while Glitched Drives increase corruption of all fields.

Glitch falls into the Gather and Battle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers and while attacking mobs.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Glitch has a use cooldown of 60 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 10 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 33.33%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 80 seconds.

The token lasts for 12 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Map Corruption
docs.text:
Map Corruption

Map Corruption is an ability exclusive to Gifted Digital Bee.

When collected, a random field is corrupted by a small amount for 3 minutes (+15s per level) for all players in the server.

Once the token is collected, a server-wide message announces: ☺︎ {Username}'s Digital Bee corrupted the [Field Name] ☺︎

The amount of corruption from this can be increased by enhancing Digital Bee with Drives. There are also special effects based on the most recent drive used to enhance Digital Bee:

  • If the most recent drive is a colored drive, Map Corruption is more likely to corrupt the field with more flowers matching the color of that drive
  • If the most recent drive is Glitched Drive, the field it chooses will be completely random but gains 25% more corruption.

Map Corruption falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Map Corruption has a use cooldown of 360 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 15 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 12.5%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 465 seconds.

The token lasts for 24 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Mind Hack
docs.text:
Mind Hack

Mind Hack is an ability exclusive to Digital Bee.

When collected, the minds of up to 3 nearby enemies (+1 per 3 lvls) are "hacked", stunning them for 3 seconds (+0.1s per lvl). While hacked, the enemies take 25% more damage (+0.1% per Glitched Drive Digital Bee has been enhanced with). Hacking is only half as effective against bosses.

This token also spawns a ☺︎ token if collected inside the field.

Mind Hack falls into the Battle category, meaning it spawns while attacking mobs.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Mind Hack has a use cooldown of 90 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 2 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 33.33%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 94 seconds.

The token lasts for 16 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: ☺
docs.text:
☺ (otherwise known as Smile Tokens) is an ability exclusive to Digital Bee.

The token can only be generated as a duped token, while inside a corrupted field. When collected, they temporarily:

  • increase field corruption and activate all duped tokens,
  • hack a nearby non-boss enemy (with a similar effect as Mind Hack),
  • and collect and double pollen equal to 50% of Digital Bee's gather amount (+50% pollen multiplier per duped token activated) in a "☺", "&", "*", "~" or "?" arrangement of flowers, with 50% of the pollen being instantly converted.
  • The flowers collected by this are also stamped for 10 seconds, causing them to yield x2 pollen.

The frequency for this token to be generated increases with the number of Glitched Drives Digital Bee has been enhanced with. Bee Swarm Simulator's patch notes give these timings (not checked in Re://:Swarm's code):

  • The average base delay between Smile Tokens is 22 seconds.
  • At maxed Glitched Drives, this average is 14 seconds.
  • The first Smile Token will always be created after half the average of the base delay.

☺ tokens last 4 seconds before despawning. They never spawn from the normal ability roll; they only come from corrupted fields and Mind Hack.

docs.title: Crimbolt Rockets
docs.text:
Crimbolt Rockets

Crimbolt Rockets is an ability exclusive to Crimbolt Bee, a Re://:Swarm event bee. Crimbolt Bee also has Token Link and Haste, and the Combined Forces passive.

When collected, Crimbolt Bee flies into the air and fires 3 rockets at random flowers in the field. Each impact collects pollen from the same 13 flowers as a regular Bomb token, and every flower struck spawns a Crimbolt Flame.

Each rocket impact has a 1 in 1,750 chance to give the Menacing Crimbolt Bee sticker and a 1 in 10,000 chance to give the Explosion sticker.

Crimbolt Rockets falls into the Gather and Battle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers and while attacking mobs.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Crimbolt Rockets has a use cooldown of 24 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 6 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 25%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 42 seconds.

The token lasts for 8 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Color Splat
docs.text:
Color Splat

Color Splat is an ability exclusive to Painter Bee.

When collected, it turns 18 surrounding flowers your Paint colour (Red, Blue or White, picked in the Painter panel) for 10 seconds (+2 seconds every 2 levels) and pollinates them.

Collecting a Color Splat token can give a Paint Splatter sticker in your Paint colour (1 in 1,000).

Color Splat falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Color Splat has a use cooldown of 20 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 5 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 25%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 35 seconds.

The token lasts for 8 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Painter's Haze
docs.text:
Painter's Haze

Painter's Haze is an ability exclusive to Painter Bee.

When collected, a haze in your Paint colour covers the field for 30 seconds. Every second it repaints and pollinates a random 3x3 patch of flowers, turning them your Paint colour for 10 seconds (+2 seconds every 2 levels).

Only one haze can exist at a time. While a haze is active, and for 1 minute after it ends, this ability uses Color Splat instead.

Summoning a Painter's Haze can give the Gifted Painter Bee sticker (1 in 5,000).

Painter's Haze falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Painter's Haze has a use cooldown of 75 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 15 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 16.67%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 150 seconds.

The token lasts for 8 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Snowglobe Shake
docs.text:
Snowglobe Shake is an ability exclusive to bees that have the Snowglobe beequip equipped.

When collected, they give all players in the server the Cool Breeze for 20 seconds, granting a plethora of stats.

The same buff can also be obtained from using Snowflakes during the Beesmas event, which add 10 seconds of Cool Breeze per use.

Snowglobe Shake falls into the Gather, Battle, and Idle categories, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers, while attacking mobs, and while idling.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Snowglobe Shake has a use cooldown of 300 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 30 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 16.67%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 450 seconds.

The token lasts for 8 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Festive Mark
docs.text:
Festive Mark

Festive Mark is an ability exclusive to Festive Bees that have the Festive Wreath beequip equipped.

When collected, a Festive Mark is deployed in a random area in the field that the player is standing in for 12 seconds (+0.5s per level), with a ~22-tile radius. Standing within its range grants the Festive Mark buff, which gives extra Honey Per Pollen, Bomb Pollen, Red Bomb Pollen, Instant Bomb Conversion, and Conversion Links.

Unlike other marks, Festive Mark also grants boosts to other players and its range can be seen by other players. It also can link with other players' marks. However, the Festive Mark buff cannot be stacked even if two festive marks overlap each other.

When Festive Mark is active, it summons random gifts within its range that can be collected by any player and flashes colors cycling through red, blue, green and yellow at the top of the pole. Rarer gifts appear more likely with bee level and certain gifts are only obtainable when Festive Bee is gifted. Every 4th token generated by the festive mark is always a Red Boost token.

The gifts include:

  • Red Boost Tokens.
  • Treats.
  • Strawberries.
  • Pineapples.
  • Blueberries.
  • Sunflower Seeds.
  • Royal Jelly.
  • Ticket.
  • Gumdrops.
  • Star Jelly (Rare).
  • Magic Bean (Rare).
  • Blue Extract (Rare).
  • Red Extract (Rare).
  • Glue (Rare).
  • Oil (Rare).
  • Glitter (Rare).
  • Enzymes (Rare).
  • Neonberry (Rare).
  • Field Dice (Rare).
  • Micro-Converter (Rare).
  • Gingerbread Bear (Very rare).
  • Festive Bean (Exceptionally rare).
  • Flying Festive Bee Sticker (Beesmas only, Unbelievably rare in red fields, odds increase with bee's level)

Festive Mark falls into the Gather category, meaning it spawns while gathering from flowers.

Without any Bee Ability Rate modifiers, Festive Mark has a use cooldown of 300 seconds, an attempt cooldown of 30 seconds, and an attempt success rate of 16.67%. This give an average spawn rate of 1 token every 450 seconds.

The token lasts for 16 seconds before despawning, without any Ability Token Lifespan modifiers.

docs.title: Reindeer Fetch
docs.text:
The Reindeer Antlers beequip, when equipped to Puppy Bee, enhances its Fetch ability into Reindeer Fetch.

Puppy's ball glows bright red and emits white sparkles, and every combo grants the player the Reindeer Guidance buff, which grants extra capacity.

Additionally, the ball has a small chance to spawn 1 Gingerbread Bear at high combos (max 1 per day). While 256 treats is normally the highest amount from a combo, it's possible to get to 512 treats if the gingerbread bear spawns in the middle of the combo progression.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Stacking 10 marks will give the Saturn Sticker.

  • Fuzz Bombs used to be called "Dust Bunnies".[1]

  • The description for the Red Bomb Sync boost used to be "If Red Bomb Sync is active, 🍎 s (apples) to blue flowers too." This was an Easter Egg after Onett accidentally typed "apples" instead of "applies" in Red Bomb Sync's description.

  • This was later changed to the apple emoji, and then was changed to the proper word "applies" in the Beesmas 2021 update.
  • The audio for the Festive Gift, Festive Blessing, and Beesmas Cheer make up parts of the Christmas song Deck the Halls, respectively using the melody of the lines "Deck the halls with boughs of holly", "fa-la-la-la-la", and "la-la-la-la".

docs.title: Aged Gingerbread Bear
docs.text:
This piece of content is unobtainable or inaccessible.

This content can no longer be obtained or accessed but still exists in the game. This content may still be subject to updates, so feel free to edit below.

Aged Gingerbread Bear

"This cookie has aged an entire year or more! Gives 500 bond to the fed bee and has a 1.1% chance to turn that bee Gifted."

Not to be confused with Gingerbread Bears.

An Aged Gingerbread Bear is a type of treat that was added in the 2021-12-26 update. When fed to a bee, it raises its bond by 500 and has a 1.1% chance of turning the bee gifted. Unused Gingerbread Bears would transform into aged gingerbread bears after the next Beesmas has started. These cannot be used to purchase items from Bee Bear's Catalog.

The formula for the chance of turning a bee gifted is as follows: \(([1 - 0.989^x]\times 100)\%\), where x is the number of Aged Gingerbread Bears fed to a bee.

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text: • The only way to obtain Aged Gingerbread Bears is by saving Gingerbread Bears until the start of the next Beesmas.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This, along with Gingerbread Bears and Star Treats, are the only items that can turn Event bees gifted (as they lack favorite treats.)
  • Aged Gingerbread Bears do not apply for quests that ask for the player to feed Gingerbread Bears to their bees, such as Bee Bear's "Snow Cub Reformation (2/5)" quest.
  • Feeding 100 Aged Gingerbread Bears to a bee does not guarantee to turn it gifted. The chance of it becoming gifted is about 66.9%.

docs.title: All-Time Fastest Crab Slayers
docs.text:
The Fastest Crab Slayers is one of the 64 leaderboards in the game. This leaderboard shows the least time in which the player has defeated the Coconut Crab. It shows 10 leaderboard positions at one time. The player can scroll down the leaderboard to see more players, all the way to the 100th place.

If the player has never defeated the Coconut Crab the pad will prompt, "You haven't defeated the Coconut Crab".

docs.title: Location
docs.text: It is located past the Windy Bee Gate inside the Coconut Cave. The player will need to defeat the Coconut Crab to enter the Cave and see their score.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This is the first and only leaderboard to rank by time (time before defeated).
  • This leaderboard, the Highest Snowbear Level leaderboard, and the Top Stick Bug Fighters leaderboard are the only three leaderboards to rank "bosses".
  • This is the only leaderboard for the shortest amount of time to accomplish a goal.
  • This leaderboard is currently updated and has been repolished.
  • Onett accidentally put Coconut Crab's Health to only 20 and fixed it later, in the duration of the oversight, many players were able to reach faster times than usual. The leaderboard was later reset in June 2024.

docs.text:
The Global Top Ant Exterminators Leaderboard is one of the 64 leaderboards in the game. This leaderboard shows the top Ant Challenge scores of players. It shows 10 leaderboard positions at one time. However, the player can scroll down the leaderboard to see more scores of other players, all the way down to the 100th place.

If the player steps on the white pad in front of it, the message "Your Highscore: X" will appear. (X = Your Highscore)

The structure conceals a secret passage containing an ant pass, and the Gummy Bee Claimer.

docs.title: Location

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• When the 2018-11-25 update came out, all of the scores on this leaderboard had been reset.
  • The lowest score on the leaderboard is 530 points, which was achieved by the players from 67th to 100th place.
  • On 2024-01-12, many players on the leaderboard, including Natmab, lost their Top Ant Exterminator points highscore. The reason behind the data wipe is currently unknown.

docs.title: All-Time Top Battlers (Most Battle Points)
docs.text:
The Global Top Battlers (also called the Battle Points Leaderboard) is one of the 64 leaderboards in the game. This leaderboard shows how many battle points players have collected over time. It shows 10 leaderboard positions at one time. The player can scroll down the leaderboard to see more players, all the way to the 100th place. Only legitimate players appear on the leaderboards for lengths of time (hackers/exploiters will be removed). Battle points are collected from certain mobs in the game.

If the player steps on the white pad in front of it, the message, "You have x Battle Points", x being the number of battle points, will appear.

docs.title: Location
docs.text: It is located on the yellow platform, besides Panda Bear, in front of the Bamboo Field, and behind the Blue Flower Field.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• It is one of the two leaderboards to be in the game in its release, the other being the Global Top Honeymakers Leaderboard.
  • Sugarsmacks12 was the number 1 person in the global top battlers for 3 years before being dethroned. It is the longest-sustaining of the number one spot in all of the leaderboards in the game.
  • Bubble Bee Man used to be located behind this leaderboard before being moved to the 30 Bee Zone in the Beesmas 2019 update.

docs.title: All-Time Top Honeymakers
docs.text:
The All-Time Top Honeymakers is one of the 64 leaderboards in the game. This leaderboard shows how much honey players have collected over time. It shows 10 leaderboard positions at one time. The player can scroll down the leaderboard to see more players, all the way to the 100th place. Only legitimate players appear on the leaderboards for lengths of time (exploiters will be removed).

If the player steps on the white pad in front of it, the message "You've made [x] Honey" will appear; x being the amount of honey the player has made in total.

docs.title: Location
docs.text: It is located near the hives and on the opposite side of the fence to the Dandelion Field. It is on the opposite side of the path in front of the hives from the Daily Top Honeymakers leaderboard.

docs.text:

docs.text:
The Highest Robo Bear Challenge Scores is one of the 64 leaderboards in the game. This leaderboard shows the top 100 people who've earned the highest scores in the Robo Bear Challenge, showing ten ranks at a time. The player can scroll down the leaderboard to see more players, all the way to the 100th place.

If the player steps on the white pad in front of it, the message "Your highest score in Robo Bear's Challenge: {Player's High Score}" will appear.

docs.text:

docs.title: All-Time Top Stick Bug Fighters
docs.text:
The Global Top Stick Bug Fighters is one of the 64 leaderboards in the game. It can display 10 leaderboard positions at a time If the player stands on the white pad in front of the leaderboard, "Your highscore: "..ScoreVariable.."" "ScoreVariable" being the score obtained from the Stick Bug Challenge This allows for players to view their current Highscore for the Stick Bug Challenge. This leaderboard tracks the top 100 scores from fighting Stick Bug in the Stick Bug Challenge. The player can scroll down the leaderboard to see more players, all the way to the 100th place.

The Top Stick Bug Fighters leaderboard was reset at one point due to glitches with the fight. The glitches were fixed on 2019-09-27.

It was later reset again on 2022-12-26.

The leaderboard was recently reset once more in 2024-01-12 due to the technique of using attack buffs in Robo Bear's Challenge to increase damage drastically.

The Top Stick Bug Fighters leaderboard.

docs.title: Location
docs.text: It is located right behind Stick Bug, on top of the biggest mushroom in the Mushroom Field. One method to get there is to use the Red, Blue, or Yellow Cannons paired with either the Parachute or Glider. Another way to get there is to parachute or glide from a tall place, like near the Lion Bee Gate. Doing the Mushroom Field Obby and jumping and gliding to the tallest mushroom is also a viable solution.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This leaderboard, the Highest Snowbear Level leaderboard, and the Fastest Crab Slayers leaderboard are the only three leaderboards to rank "bosses".
  • After the leaderboard got reset again in 2024-01-12, the score displayed when stepping on the podium is your score before the reset. But it does not display in the leaderboard.

docs.title: Amulet
docs.text:
This piece of content contains information obtained through datamining.

Due to the nature of the information, details may be inaccurate or outdated.

Datamined information: How Amulets are generated. — December 19th, 2024

An amulet is an item introduced in the 2018-07-11 update. They grant several buffs to the player and/or their bees, and can be obtained by completing certain special challenges.

docs.title: Obtaining
docs.text:
Collecting an amulet will bring up a table with the old and new amulets' stats, and the option to keep the old amulet or replace it. The scheme on the left shows an example table, with the player's amulet type as well as other rewards. If the player has obtained the amulet from the Ant Challenge or Stick Bug Challenge, their score will be shown above the rewards.

Clicking "Keep Old" will cause the player to keep their current amulet and clicking "Replace" will cause the player to receive a confirmation message asking if they want to replace it. If the player has agreed to replace their amulet after the confirmation message, the player's old amulet will be replaced with the new one. This cannot be reversed. Note that the drops will still be received even if the player didn't replace their amulet. If two or more tables are shown, the previous table(s) are closed, and the newest table is displayed. As of the 2020-06-06 update, a confirmation message will now pop up if the player tries to replace an amulet if they already had that type of amulet, and, as of the 2021-12-26 update, disconnecting while a recently generated amulet is undecided gives the player another chance to choose upon going back in a server.

docs.title: Generation
docs.text:
Amulets are generated with a given quality, which changes based on doing certain actions (for example, different scores yield proportionally different qualities, with a limit). Increasing the quality of an amulet will improve the probability of getting a better amulet. Note that this does not eliminate the possibility of getting a worse amulet.

Details of how this works are provided below. For the raw data of every amulet, see Module:Amulet Stats/data.

docs.title: Choosing Stats
docs.text:
An amulet's stats can be split into multiple stat groups. When an amulet is generated, it picks out a number of stats from each group to put on the amulet. Some stat groups will only appear with a certain probability.

After a stat is picked, it checks if it has a probability of appearing (different from the probability of the stat group it's in); if it does, it may randomly remove itself from the amulet based on the probability. This is why some amulets may have a lower number of stats than expected.

As of currently, this process is not influenced by the amulet's quality.

docs.title: Getting Stat Strength
docs.text:
Picked stats on an amulet go through a process to determine its strength, before the amulet is given to the player. The strength of the stats are influenced by the amulet's quality, by placing a heavy bias at a certain value that increases with the amulet's quality, making it so the stat's strength are more likely to be near that bias.

More specifically:

  • Every stat have a bias table, which consists of 2 values, dubbed biasQuality and biasDirect respectively.
  • A higher biasQuality makes it so the amulet's quality have a bigger effect on the stat's bias, and vice versa.
  • A higher biasDirect directly affects the stat's bias, regardless of the amuelet's quality.
  • The default value for both variables (assuming one isn't assigned by the game) is 1.
  • The bias is calculated by the formula: \(bias=minValue+(maxValue-minValue)\times biasDirect\times {\frac {quality}{\max(1,biasQuality\times (1-quality))}}\), where minValue and maxValue are the minimum and maximum possible values of the stat's strength.

After that, the RandomBias function is called with the following paramenters, and the result is rounded to the stat's resolution interval to give the stat's strength: randomBias(minValue, maxValue, bias, 1) For more information on how this function works, see the designated module page.

docs.title: Ant Amulet
docs.text:
The Ant Amulet is an amulet that is obtained from participating in the Ant Challenge.

The amulet gives the player buffs and will always boost Convert Rate. There are five tiers of Ant Amulets, each awarded for reaching a certain point milestone in the Ant Challenge.

The amulet's quality is your Ant Challenge score divided by 400, capped at 1. It is the same linear formula for every tier, so quality is maxed at a score of 400.

docs.text: The Ant Challenge Info is located behind the Ant Gate and to the right of the Ant Challenge. It provides basic information on the Ant Challenge. When the players steps on the white pad, they will be prompted with a message that reads, "Read Ant Challenge Info".
