docs.title: Ant Challenge
docs.text:
The Ant Challenge is a challenge found past the Ant Gate, with the objective being to defeat as many ants as possible.

The Ant Challenge arena.

docs.title: Accessing and Participating
docs.text: The player needs 20 bees in order to pass the Ant Gate and play the Ant Challenge. An ant pass is also required each time to participate in the challenge. The player can obtain a free Ant Pass every two hours by using the Free Ant Pass Dispenser behind the Ant Gate. If players wish to get more ant passes, they can purchase another one for 10 Tickets each at the Ant Pass Dispenser. Panda Bear also gives ant passes in his quests sometimes.

docs.title: Gameplay
docs.text:
Upon entering, the remaining pollen in a player's bag is instantly converted. The player has 5 minutes to defeat as many ants as they can. The timer on the right side of the anthill shows the time remaining for the challenge. The ants come in waves, starting with level 1 and 2 ants, and they increase in level with each wave. Each wave launches an assortment of ants that contain Regular Ants, Fire Ants, Army Ants, and/or Flying Ants. Every 5th wave always contains a Giant Ant, with the exception of every 40th wave, which contains 2 giant ants. Each ant defeated grants 1 point.

To progress, fill the meter on the anthill by gathering pollen. The amount of pollen needed to progress to the next wave starts at 4,000 and increases by at least 2,000 more than the previous requirement for each wave.

Upon reaching wave 8, the white doors on the sides will start flashing red. This indicates that a lawnmower is about to come out and pass through the lane the door directs to. Move away from the targeted lane to avoid getting damaged. Getting hit by a lawnmower deals 50 base damage.

Lawnmowers will move faster and appear more frequently as the challenge progresses, with multiple lawnmowers running simultaneously possible near the end of the challenge.

The challenge ends upon the player's death, leaving the challenge, or when the 5 minutes are up, whichever happens first. While having the Haste+ buff, if the player walks up the ant hill, the player may leave the challenge. This is a common glitch.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
See also: Ant Amulet

After the challenge ends, a message box pops out on the player's screen presenting the rewards.

Guaranteed Rewards List Ant Amulet

Royal Jellies Honey

One of the rewards from this list Treats

Sunflower Seeds Strawberries Blueberries Pineapples Neonberries Jelly Beans Robo Pass Bandage Bottle Cap Candy Ring Camphor Lip Balm Poinsettia(Only During Beesmas) Left Facing Ant Sticker(Very Rare) Ant Field Stamp Sticker(Unfathomably Rare) x2 Convert Speed Voucher(Nearly Impossible)

The rewards increase in quality and quantity relative to the player's score. A higher score will also give players higher-tier Ant Amulets:

Requirements Amulet 0-24 Points Bronze Ant Amulet 25-49 Points Silver Ant Amulet 50-99 Points Gold Ant Amulet 100-149 Points Diamond Ant Amulet 150+ Points Supreme Ant Amulet

If the player already has an existing Ant Amulet, they may choose to keep their old one or replace it with the new one, depending on which one has better/more favorable buffs.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Try to collect as many tokens (Haste, Baby Love, Bear Morph, etc.) as possible before participating in the challenge.
  • Rage tokens can be used to take out ants faster, as they increase Bee Attack.
  • Certain mutations on bees that increase attack will also help in defeating ants faster.
  • Higher level bees will be able to make the later waves easier to get through. Bees with higher attack and/or speed will also prove to be more effective than those with lower attack and/or speed.
  • A high-level Vicious Bee is vital, as the spikes from its ability, Impale, can deal significant damage to multiple ants. In addition, wait to activate the ability when many ants are in the arena to maximize it effectively.
  • A Gifted Stubborn Bee can help in this case as it increases the lifespan of ability tokens, giving the player more time to spawn ants before activating abilities.
  • Windy Bee's Tornado can be even more effective than Impale in the Ant Challenge. Not only does it collect pollen, but it also deals massive area damage (which cannot miss) and collects tokens. However, haste stacks and powerful sprinklers are required to maximize their potential.
  • Honey tokens can be used to fill the progress meter on the anthill, so the player may consider using Honey Bees or Diamond Bees to spawn Honey Gift tokens, or using a Festive Bee to collect honey tokens from Festive Gifts.
  • Having amulets that boost bee attack damage, a Gifted Brave Bee, and a Gifted Rage Bee makes it easier to defeat ants.
  • The Fire Mask and Demon Mask will boost attack and add Flame-generating passives. Well placed Flames will grant Flame Heat, collect pollen, and do damage to nearby ants.
  • Using Stingers will boost attack for a short time, which helps clear ants faster and deal with higher-level ants. The player can also use Red ExtractsRed and Blue Extracts, Oils, Glues, Tropical Drinks, and Gumdrops. This will help with honey production and boost bee capabilities but isn't necessary to get a good score.
  • Coconuts can prove to be an unpredictable but powerful tool to take out clusters of ants. Coconuts can deal incredible amounts of damage, are capable of damaging high-level ants, and collect decent amounts of pollen.
  • If the player has Coconut Clogs, catching coconuts will also grant Coconut Haste, which temporarily makes the player and their bees faster. This can be useful to escape dangerous areas.
  • To maximize the score, defeat as many ants as possible in the first three minutes, as later waves get more difficult and the lawnmowers appear more frequently and move faster.
  • Tools are the best way to fill up the honey meter, this because your bees will be attacking and won't be able to collect pollen.
  • If there is too many ants and the bees can't deal with them, the player shouldn't use their Tool because it will fill up the honey meter (if in the field) and summon more ants.
  • Since the player has 100% Instant Conversion in the Ant Challenge, don't try to go after tokens from Coin Scatter or coconuts, since they won't have much value, as they have nothing to convert from, making them virtually useless.
  • Sprinklers can be useful for regenerating flowers and making pollen collection easier, especially when ants and lawnmowers cut the player off from certain areas of the field.
  • During any beesmas, try to play the ant challenge with the Honeyday Buff, this will increase how fast the meter fills
  • Using the Glider can help as the player can glide over ants and fire trails, escaping from certain situations.
  • Zoom out all the way to see where all the ants are and where lawnmowers may be coming from.
  • When new ants spawn, it is a good idea to go as far away from the ant hill as possible, to avoid being hit by an incoming ant.
  • Star Saw, a Supreme Star Amulet passive, is very effective at defeating ants and collecting pollen.
  • Standing near the side of the field where the lawnmowers come out can make the lawnmowers easier to avoid.
  • The player use the small gap between the field and the wall to avoid running over fire trails, though lawnmowers and ants can still damage the player.
  • If a Honeystorm is summoned during the challenge, it is a good idea to go after the honey tokens in earlier waves or when there aren't too many ants since the honey tokens collected can contribute significantly to the honey meter when a large number of tokens are collected.
  • While the Coconut Canister’s ability, Emergency Coconut Shield, is active, getting hit by the lawnmowers will heal the player instead of damaging them.
  • Wear the Gummy Mask and intentionally activate Gummy Morph during harder stages of the challenge, as this grants +300 attack to Gummy Bee.
  • Intentionally activate the Emergency Coconut Shield 2–4 minutes before starting the challenge to avoid wasting it in early levels.
  • Though the ants spawned during the challenge are random, it is possible to predict what ants might spawn. During the first 15 rounds, flying ants are generally more common than army ants. After 15 rounds, army ants become much more common. Giants ants spawn every 5 waves, and always come with either fire ants or regular ants. This information can be helpful when dealing with quests that require defeating specific types of ants.
  • Having Invigorating Nectar can help buff bee attack.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• If a player uses a Whirligig during an Ant Challenge, it used to teleport the player to the starting platform after teleporting to the hive, thus ending the challenge and granting an amulet with the score the player left with.
  • During an unknown update, this was fixed to teleport the player to the center of the field.
  • However, during a later unknown update, the player is instead teleported back to their hive, which teleports them back to the challenge platform and ends the challenge.
  • Despite being lawnmowers, they actually do not affect any of the flowers when they pass through.
  • Prior to the 2018-11-25 update, the Ant Challenge can only hold up to 20 ants at once.[1]
  • Since the Egg Hunt 2019 update, the player can get Jelly Beans as a reward from the Ant Challenge.

  • If the player uses jelly beans while inside or right outside the Ant Challenge, no jelly bean tokens will appear.

  • Upon entering the arena, the player's bag will instantly be converted, and the player will gain a boost of +100% Instant Conversion. The boost is represented by the Ant Pass icon.

  • There used to be a visual glitch that when leaving the ant challenge, the player would still have this buff. It was only a visual glitch, so the player did not actually have a +100% Instant Conversion boost active.
  • Before the 2018-11-25 update, a Haste token with an expired timer would represent the boost is now represented as the Ant Pass icon.
  • There is an ant pass token hidden behind the Ant Challenge area. To get it, go behind the leaderboard and follow the hallway around the corner. This also leads to the Gummy Bee Claimer.
  • If the player has equipped their tool and dies right when the Ant Challenge is about to end, they will respawn without their pollen collector equipped. However, the character's arm will be positioned to look like it's actually holding it.
  • There used to be a bug where the pollen meter displayed the cumulative total instead of the total required to reach the next wave. This was fixed in the 2018-09-10 update.
  • Players are able to glitch into the Ant Field without triggering the actual challenge. This can only be achieved by having a slow internet connection or bear morph and/or Haste+.
  • If the player leaves their sprinkler(s) in the field and the challenge ends without the player dying, the sprinklers remain in the field.
  • If a player glitches inside and then someone starts it, then the player who glitched in will be kicked out.
  • There is a rare glitch where an Ant or a Fire Ant can get stuck on the wall where the lawnmowers come from.
  • There was a glitch prior to February 2022, where sometimes, when the player starts the challenge, they won't actually be teleported inside, forfeiting the challenge instantly.
  • Giant Ants will give the player's bees 3 bond, being the least efficient way to level up bees.
  • It is only possible to go through 100 waves of the challenge. This is because it takes about three seconds to progress to the next wave and there is a total time limit of 5 minutes (300 seconds). 300 seconds divided by 3 seconds per wave would be 100 waves.
  • If the player manages to somehow glitch out of the Ant Challenge, the player will be teleported back to the center of the field. However, if you do this repeatedly, eventually the challenge will end and a message will pop up saying "Ant Challenge ended because you left."

The Ant Field is a field located past the Ant Gate and near the Top Ant Exterminators leaderboard. It can only be accessed by starting the Ant Challenge which will summon waves of ants.

This field can produce honey and ticket tokens while collecting pollen.

The only bee that likes the Ant Field is Lion Bee. There are no bees that dislike the Ant Field.

Planters cannot be planted in this field, although Onett has stated that the Ant Field contains Invigorating Nectar.

This is a 12×32 field, containing 384 flowers. The flowers are white, red, and blue, and the only natural size in single.

Note: flower counts within the table may vary due to rounding. Additionally, in game, all flowers are randomly generated and may not precisely align with the percentages.

docs.title: Obtaining Boosts
docs.text:
• Using an Ant Pass to start the Ant Challenge will give 100% Instant Ant Field Conversion.
  • There is no possible to way to boost the pollen for the Ant Field.
  • The flowers can still be pollinated.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• You can collect pollen from the Ant Field outside the challenge by using the Sticker-Seeker or spawning flames with the Scythe.
  • Lion Bee is the only bee to like the Ant Field; all other bees are neutral to this field.
  • The Ant Field is the only field to have exclusively single flowers.
  • The flowers on this field contain 50 pollen per flower, and instead of going up by 15 pollen per tier, go up 10 per pollination tier up to 90, although pollen multiplier remains the same as regular flowers.
  • The Ant Field is the only field that can't be boosted with glitter, the only field where a magic bean cannot be planted, the only field where clouds cannot be summoned, the only field that had no Market Boost from the Boost Market, the only field that can't get winds from the Wind Shrine, and the only field where planters cannot be planted.
  • The Ant Field is the smallest field in the game with 384 flowers, smaller than the Pumpkin Patch with 561 flowers and the Stump Field with 563 flowers.
  • Players are able to glitch into the Ant Field without triggering the actual challenge. This can only be achieved by having a slow internet connection or bear morph and/or haste+.
  • Despite being impossible to boost, the Ant Field has an unused Field Boost icon.

The Ant Gate, also called the 20 Bee Gate, is a gate that requires 20 bees to pass through. It is found near the Noob Shop, behind the traveling/event bear (e.g. Sun Bear) area. The gate gets its name from the large Army Ant on it.

docs.title: Music
docs.text:
During daytime, the audio "Wax" plays here.

During Beesmas, the audio "Drone" plays during daytime instead.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This gate and the Bear Gate are the only gates that don't have a bee to represent them.
  • This gate and the Windy Bee Gate are the only gates in the game that don't have a Royal Jelly token in the area behind it.
  • However, the Windy Bee Gate has a Star Jelly token, making this the only gate without any royal jelly tokens at all.
  • This gate and the Windy Bee Gate are also the only gates that is designed based on a component of the zone (e. g. The Ant Gate has the Ant Challenge in it).
  • The Gummy Bee Claimer is near this gate, to the side of the Ant Gate closest to the hives.
  • There is a Ticket token on top of the gate.
  • The Army Ant on top of the gate has glowing eyes, but in the Ant Challenge, Army Ants (and all the other ants) do not have glowing eyes.
  • As of the 2019-09-28 update, you will get teleported back to spawn if you manage to bypass the gate.
  • There is a secret path behind the Global Top Ant Exterminators Leaderboard, which leads to an Ant Pass and the Gummy Bee Claimer.
  • This gate indirectly has a temporary quest giver, being Gummy Bear and his quest "Gummy Bear's Goo Years Beacon".
  • This and the Basic Bee Gate are the only gates that lead to an area where there is nothing able to be purchased with Honey.
  • This is the only gate to have a mob representing it.

docs.text:
Ant Pass Dispenser Information Cost(s) 10 Tickets Usage Obtaining Ant Passes with Tickets Requirement(s) 20 Bees, less than 10 Ant Passes Cooldown None Location Behind the Ant Gate, next to the Free Ant Pass Dispenser

Not to be confused with the Free Ant Pass Dispenser, which gives ant passes for free with a cooldown.

The Ant Pass Dispenser is a dispenser that is located behind the Ant Gate and to the right of the Free Ant Pass Dispenser. It gives an Ant Pass for 10 Tickets, which can be used to access the Ant Challenge. The price does not increase and there is no cooldown on using the dispenser, unlike the Free Ant Pass Dispenser. Players cannot use the dispenser if they already have 10 or more ant passes in their inventory.

  • This, the Royal Jelly Dispenser, and the Robo Pass Dispenser are the only dispensers that require tickets to use.

docs.title: Ant Pass
docs.text:
Ant Pass

"Grants you 1 admission to the Ant Challenge."

COOLDOWN

No cooldown

CAP

10

An Ant Pass is an inventory item that was added in the 2018-07-11 update. You must use one in order to participate in the Ant Challenge. Players can only have a maximum of 10 ant passes in their inventory at a time (unless they had more than 10 passes before the 2019-04-05 update, purchased them from Robux packs, or received them from quests).

An ant pass can be used by stepping on the pad in front of the Ant Challenge and pressing "E" on the player's keyboard or by clicking on the prompt.

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• There is a Free Ant Pass Dispenser past the Ant Gate which can be used every two hours.
  • There is also an Ant Pass Dispenser to the right of the Free Ant Pass Dispenser which gives an ant pass for 10 tickets with no cooldown.
  • If the player already has at least 10 ant passes, they cannot claim a free ant pass from the Free Ant Pass Dispenser or use the Ant Pass Dispenser.
  • Completing Panda Bear's Ant Questline rewards an ant pass after every quest. (Excluding Ultimate Ant Annihilation 5)
  • A possible reward from a Ladybug, Rage Aphid, King Beetle, and Tunnel Bear when defeated.
  • Defeating the Commando Chick will reward ant passes if the player reaches certain milestones.
  • Ant passes are sometimes available in the Robux Shop, generally combined with other things in sale packs.
  • There are two ant pass tokens hidden in the game.
  • Behind the Ant Challenge (go behind the Top Ant Exterminators Leaderboard, then go through the tunnel and exit out through the other side).
  • At the very back of the Star Hall behind the Supreme Star Amulet Generator.
  • Summoning and defeating a level 4 Snowbear rewards 3 Ant Passes.
  • Purchasing the Poinsettia Bundle from Bee Bear's Catalog for 250 Snowflakes and 25 Gingerbread Bears gives 5 Ant Passes and other items.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• If the player finds an ant pass token, it will say "You found a Ant Pass" instead of "You found an Ant Pass."
  • The plural of the ant pass is incorrectly spelled as "Ant Passs".

docs.title: Ant
docs.text:
Ant Location Ant Field while the Ant Challenge is active.

Not to be confused with Ants, the family of mobs that includes Ants along with the other ant types.

An Ant is one of five mobs that is part of a family called Ants that are exclusively found in the Ant Challenge, past the Ant Gate.

This is the first Ant Challenge mob that the player will encounter, appearing on the very first wave.

Ants move in a fixed straight line and are the most generic ant. They are the most common ant and will always appear in the first few waves. They are the easiest ant to deal with due to how basic they are compared to the other ants.

An ant's level can increase depending on what wave of the Ant Challenge the player is on. They can range from level 1 up to level 16.

They are by far the least threatening of the five ant types, as they are often easily and completely avoidable.

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
• Ants move in predetermined straight lines and are quite slow. This enables to player to easily dodge any coming their way.
  • Standing near the ant will allow your bees to quickly target the ant to quickly deal damage and defeat it.
  • Ants will come out in groups and they could overwhelm the player if they are collecting pollen quickly to advance to the next waves. Vicious Bee and Windy Bee provide excellent crowd control with their Impale and Tornado abilities which could greatly help counter the large amounts of Regular Ants landing on the field. Digital Bee can also stun many ants at once and allow them to take extra damage via Mind Hack.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Diamond Ant Amulets represent an ant.
  • This is the only mob to have the same name as a group of mobs.
  • They have the same health per level as Fire Ants.
  • The ant was the first mob Onett made for the game.[1]
  • It was supposed to be a regular spawning mob, but Onett replaced them with Ladybugs because he wanted the ants to be more "ant-like" (works as a team).[2]

docs.title: Ants
docs.text:
A statue of an Army Ant on the Ant Gate.

Ants are mobs exclusively found in the Ant Field during the Ant Challenge, past the Ant Gate. In the Ant Challenge, the player fights waves of ants before the timer runs out. The level and health of the ants gradually increase as the player completes more rounds in the Ant Challenge.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
There are 5 types of ants. Giant Ants, Army Ants, and Flying Ants are the only types that give bond upon defeat. Giant Ants give 3 bond each, while army ants and flying ants give 1 bond to each of the player's bees (not accounting for Bond From Battle, though it is usually too small of a boost to change the amount). The bond from ants don't appear as a notification.

All ants deal 40 damage on contact except the giant ant, which deals 60 damage.

docs.title: Ants
docs.text:
Main article: Ant

Ants move in a predetermined straight line and are the most generic ant. They only have around 25 health at level one and are by far the least threatening of the five ant types, as they are often easily and completely avoidable. They are the most common ant and will always appear in the first few waves.

docs.title: Army Ants
docs.text:
Main article: Army Ant

Army Ants have army helmets on their heads and will pursue the player. They have the ability to pounce, have a higher damage output, and have a little more health than normal and fire ants (about 35 at level one). Less damage is dealt to these ants because of their defense. Army Ants can spawn as early as the first wave, but they usually start appearing at around the second or third waves. If they appear, they occasionally spawn in waves, but not always.

docs.title: Flying Ants
docs.text:
Main article: Flying Ant

Flying Ants are ants with wings that track the player. They are the fastest out of the five ant types and have the ability to pounce on players from a considerably farther distance than the army ant. However, the twist is that they also have low health, similar to the amount of an Army Ant or even sometimes a normal one. Flying Ants can spawn as early as the first wave, but they usually start appearing at around the second or third wave. They deal higher damage than a normal ant.

docs.title: Giant Ants
docs.text:
Main article: Giant Ant

Giant Ants are enormous versions of the normal ant that relentlessly pursue the player. They are relatively slow, ensuring that if the player constantly moves away, it cannot reach them. However, they have large amounts of health (about 10 times the health of an ordinary ant) and high attack power to compensate. Because of their high health, they can 'tank' hits from bees and allow their smaller, faster comrades to attack the player without any chance of being defeated. Their size makes them harder to avoid. A Giant Ant will spawn every five waves (5th, 10th, 15th, etc.)

docs.title: Fire Ants
docs.text:
Main article: Fire Ant

Fire Ants are colored red and act the same as regular ants, but they leave a damaging fire trail behind them as they move. Their flames deal 30 damage if touched. The flames will linger even after the Fire Ant that left it is defeated. The fire disappears after a short amount of time. Fire Ants typically spawn in the later waves, such as after the first Giant Ant. Noted by Panda Bear, the fire from a Fire Ant is not affected by Defense, but this seems to be untrue. However, having 100% defense (though Emergency Coconut Shield) will nullify the damage.

docs.title: Use in Quests
docs.text:
• After completing Panda Bear's Gold Egg questline, Panda Bear has 15 Ant Quests. Each of these quests requires the player to defeat several ants, with an occasional other requirement added in. Each ant quest grants at least one ticket and one Ant Pass. Most of the quests also grant royal jellies. The main prizes from the questline are a Diamond Egg (after five ant quests), Star Egg (after ten), and Star Treat (after all 15).
  • Each of Onett's five Star Journey quests requires the player to defeat ants along with several other requirements.
  • In Sun Bear's second visit, he has some quests that require the player to defeat normal Ants and Giant Ants.
  • Science Bear's "Limits of Language" quest requires defeating ants along with several other requirements.
  • Gifted Bucko Bee's "Bombard" and "Picnic" quests require the player to defeat Ants and Army Ants.
  • Gifted Riley Bee's "Rampage" and "Picnic" quests require the player to defeat Fire Ants.
  • Gummy Bear's Beesmas 2020 quest, "Gummy Bear's Goo Years Beacon", requires the player to defeat 75 ants. This quest is no longer obtainable.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Jumping usually helps get away from Army Ants, Flying Ants, and Giant Ants (a Parachute or Glider helps in this strategy).
  • Bees will focus on one ant at a time. If the player wants a specific ant defeated, they just have to get closer to it than any other ant, which will cause the bees to attack it.
  • In this regard, prioritizing defeating Fire Ants is a good choice, since their flames can easily become extremely disruptive.
  • Getting higher level bees will make sure that the bees will land their hits.
  • Bees with high attack like Lion Bee, Cobalt Bee, Crimson Bee, Brave Bee, etc., are very helpful in dealing good damage.
  • Gifted Bees do extra damage and can provide bonuses (e.g., Brave Bee give +1 Attack, Looker Bee gives +25% Critical Power, and Commander Bee give +25% Critical Chance).
  • Vicious Bee and Windy Bee provide excellent crowd control, especially since ants often come in pairs or packs. Digital Bee can also stun many ants at once, and allow them to take extra damage via Mind Hack.
  • When a wave starts, the player should stay by the glass wall opposite the anthill to avoid ants pouncing/landing on them when they spawn.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Normal and Fire Ants, along with Wild Windy Bee, Rogue Vicious Bee, Mondo Chick, Stick Bug, and stick nymphs are the only mobs that do not grant battle points when defeated.
  • All ants, along with the Coconut Crab, Cave Monsters, Robo Bear Challenge mobs and Snowbear are the only mobs to not drop Honey upon defeat.
  • Ants and Stick Bug don't have a respawn timer or time range, unlike other mobs. The only way to spawn them is by starting a Challenge.
  • The amount and types of ants vary for each round, and it's possible to get a different score each time.
  • Ants, aphids, chicks, Stick Nymphs (Festive Nymphs), Mechsquitos, Cogmowers, Cogturrets, and Mega Mechsquitos are the only mobs that come in different varieties.
  • All types of ants, Mechsquitos, Cogmowers, Cogturrets, and Mega Mechsquitos are the only mobs to not drop any loot upon defeat.
  • The Supreme Ant Amulet is the only Ant Amulet that resembles a Flying Ant while the others are normal Ants.

docs.title: Aphid
docs.text:
Aphid Location Leaves; every field in game (except the Ant Field, Hub Field and Stump Field). Respawns Every N/A; small chance from leaves.

Aphids are hostile mobs that have a 0.932% chance (1 in 107) of spawning from collecting leaves, with the chances increasing when a Field is experiencing a period of low activity (i.e. players are not visiting said field very often). Their level and health correlate to which field the aphid spawns in, like Rogue Vicious Bee. Sharing a similar trait with Tunnel Bear, Coconut Crab, Chicks, Hostage Chicks, Wild Windy Bee, Mondo Chick, and Puffshrooms, players have a limited time (30 seconds) to defeat an aphid. After the time is up, the aphid despawns. The timer is shown above its health. Aphids attack in a similar matter to Stick Nymphs and Giant Ants, following the nearest player around slowly. Aphids are public mobs, meaning that anyone can collect the drops regardless of whether or not they attacked it.

Defeating an aphid awards 10 Battle Points (20 if defeating one of the 3 rare types), Bond, and various other rewards. Some rewards have a cooldown, meaning that they will not be obtainable for a while after receiving them once, regardless of the level or type. However, you can still get them through other players spawning an aphid with said rewards at the expense of applying the same cooldown to them also.

docs.title: Types
docs.text: Aphids always appear as 1 of 4 different variants: Normal, Rage, Armored, and Diamond. Different types of aphids may spawn at different encounter rates. Rewards vary between these types. Honey amounts depend on the aphid's level and player's honey per token boost.

docs.title: Normal Aphid
docs.text:
This is the most common aphid that can be encountered. They possess the least amount of health and deal the least amount of damage out of all aphids. It has a green body with red eyes and neon yellow-green legs and antennae.

docs.text:
The Rage Aphid is one of the 3 rare types of aphids, the others being Armored Aphid and Diamond Aphid. The Rage Aphid has a higher chance to spawn in fields with red flowers. The Rage Aphid has higher health and deals the most damage out of all the aphids. They are colored similar to a Gifted Rage Bee or Gifted Spicy Bee, with red bodies and green eyes, legs, and antennae.

docs.title: Armored Aphid
docs.text:
The Armored Aphid is one of the 3 rare types of aphids, the others being Rage Aphid and Diamond Aphid. The Armored Aphid has a higher chance of spawning in mixed fields and fields with white flowers. The Armored aphid has higher defense compared to other types of aphids, allowing it to survive for a longer amount of time. It has a metallic gray body with red eyes and black legs and antennae.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Jumping and/or running around aphids will prevent them from attacking effectively since they slowly follow players.
  • If players cannot defeat an aphid due to higher level and health, leveling up bees and having bees specializing in attack, such as Vicious Bee, will help kill the aphid faster.

docs.text:
An Army Ant is one of five mobs that is part of a family called Ants that are exclusively found in the Ant Challenge, past the Ant Gate.

Army Ant Location Ant Field while the Ant Challenge is active.

This is one of the first Ant Challenge mobs that the player will encounter, capable of appearing on the very first wave. Despite being able to appear on the first wave, Army Ants usually start appearing at around the second or third waves.

Army Ants have army helmets on their heads and will pursue the player. They have the ability to pounce on the player and have a little more health than most other ants. Less damage is dealt to these ants because of their defense.

An Army Ant's level can increase depending on what wave of the Ant Challenge the player is on. They can range from level 1 up to level 16.

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
• Army Ants are quite slow which gives the player time to react and dodge before they pounce on the player.
  • Jumping past the Army Ant will enable your bees to lock onto the Army Ant while letting the player get around the Army Ant without getting pounced on.
  • If they appear, they occasionally spawn in waves, but not always. Vicious Bee and Windy Bee provide excellent crowd control with their abilities which could greatly help counter the large amounts of Army Ants landing on the field. Digital Bee can also stun many Army Ants at once and allow them to take extra damage via Mind Hack.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• These are the only mobs to wear equipment that gives defense against attacks.
  • There is a gate dedicated to it, which is the Ant Gate.
  • This mob is depicted on the Ant Pass.

docs.title: Atomic Treat
docs.text:
Atomic Treat

"Always causes a random Mutation in a bee! Mutations grant bonus stats."

An atomic treat token.

An Atomic Treat, when fed to a bee, raises its bond by 1000 and gives the bee a random mutation. The mutations are Attack, Convert Amount, Gather Amount, Energy, and Bee Ability Rate. These are not the favorite treat of any bee.

docs.title: Typed Atomic Treats

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Realistic max is the best you can expect to actually see: the most picks of that upgrade that about 1 in 1,000 fully waxed 5 ★ beequips get, each at its top value. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Baby Bee and Tadpole Bee tie for the smallest bees in the game. They are also the only two bee types to have a different size compared to other bees.
  • Baby Bee is the only bee that cannot attack any mobs, even if it has an attack mutation.
  • Baby Bee used to be able to attack and could do damage if the player had any damage boosts. After the 2018-11-25 Update, this is no longer the case.
  • According to Black Bear, the reason why they don't attack is because "They're too dumb to notice" the mobs.
  • Attack added to Baby Bee still counts towards total attack even if it is not displayed in-game. This can help with passives that rely on total attack like Star Saw.
  • Baby Bee's stats have many specialities:
  • It has the second-lowest base energy (lowest being Tadpole Bee), second-lowest base Convert Rate (lowest being Fuzzy Bee), and the lowest base gather amount in the game.
  • It also has the second-slowest base gather speed (lowest being Tadpole Bee and Fuzzy Bee).
  • It, along with Bumble Bee, Demon Bee, and Exhausted Bee, are tied as the slowest bees in the game.
  • Baby Bee has the most field preferences in the game. It also dislikes the most fields.
  • Baby Bee prefers the lower-tier fields (Dandelion, Blue Flower, Sunflower, Mushroom) and dislikes the higher-tier fields (Rose, Cactus, Pine Tree Forest, Spider, Pepper, and Stump).
  • It is the only bee that isn't red to like the Mushroom Field.
  • It is also the only bee to have a higher number of disliked fields than liked fields.
  • Baby Bee and Stubborn Bee are the only Colorless bees that like strawberries.
  • Baby Bee and Rage Bee are the only bees with three unique colors on their skins. Baby Bee is also the only gifted bee with three unique colors on its skin.
  • Before 2018-11-25 update, the Gifted Hive Bonus of Baby Bee was +5% Loot Luck, which was then changed to +10% in said update. This was then changed to +20% Loot Luck in the 2019-04-05 Update and once again to +25% Loot Luck in the Beesmas 2019 update.
  • Onett paid $2 for the laughing baby sound that Baby Love uses. It can be bought here.
  • There is a small chance that a Baby Bee egg will drop from Tunnel Bear.
  • This is one of the only 4 bees that has a specific egg obtainable from mob drops, with the others being a Rascal Bee egg from ladybugs, a Bumble Bee egg from rhino beetles, or a Honey Bee egg from cave monsters.
  • Baby Bee, along with Basic Bee and Bumble Bee, are shown on Onett's Lid Art.
  • When gifted and in the Dandelion Field, Sunflower Field, Mushroom Field, or Blue Flower Field it has a very rare chance to find a Pale Heart Sticker.

docs.title: Badge Bearer's Guild
docs.text:
The Badge Bearer's Guild is a shop located near the Pine Tree Forest. The player will need at least 15 badges of any rank past Junior to be permitted to enter the shop.

The shop sells a set of tools called sprinklers. There are currently 5 sprinklers that can be bought in the shop. The player can also find the Blender here, where they can craft certain items from other materials. There is a Star Jelly token on top of the Blender that requires an accessory that boosts Jump Boost or Bear morph activated to reach it. The Mega Memory Match can also be found inside of this building.

On the opposite side of where the sprinklers are is a gate that requires 1 Ace Badge to pass through. Behind it, the player will discover another shop. This shop sells the Honeycomb Belt, Crimson Guard, Cobalt Guard, and Honey Mask, which appear to be hanging inside of a large honeycomb. In front of the honeycomb, there is another Star Jelly token. Behind the honeycomb, there is a secret glass-like passage that cannot be entered. It leads to a void-like area below the map.

Outside, it is decorated with the Badge icon in the menu on top of the entrance, along with a large Basic Sprinkler on the roof. The large sprinkler is not solid and can be walked through. The Mythic Meteor Shower Summoner also resides on the roof.

docs.title: Badges
docs.text:
Badges are part of the achievement system of Re://:Swarm. There are currently 155 badges in Re://:Swarm (including inactive badges). 30 of the badges are currently unobtainable.

Most of these badges are based on collecting a certain amount of pollen from a certain field. Obtaining a non-event badge awards Tickets and a permanent boost. Boosts in the same category do not stack - earning a higher-ranked badge overwrites the old boost with the new one. The number of Tickets earned depends on the rank of the badge earned.

The player needs the Goo Hotshot badge to enter Gummy Bear's Lair, 15 badges of any tier to enter the Badge Bearer's Guild, and one ace badge to access the special room in the Badge Bearer's Guild.

Certain badges also unlock the chance to obtain special one-time badge rewards from the Wind Shrine called Badge Shivers, which can be obtained by donating specific items. The more items you donate, the higher chance you have of a Badge Shiver.

To get more Coconuts from the Coconut Dispenser, the player must get better Coconut Badges, and to get more Glue from the Glue Dispenser, better Goo Badges are needed.

Event badges are the only badges that don't give any tickets, permanent buffs, or even show up in the badge menu, and the Egg Hunt 2019, Egg Hunt 2020, and the Ready Player Two badges each gave an item for the player's Roblox avatar. The only exception to this were the fifteen badges from The Classic, the eight badges from The Games, and the 2 badges from the Winter Spotlight. which didn't give any avatar items, but counted as currency in the event hubs.

Upon claiming any non-event badge, it will be announced in the server publicly, and a cheerful audio will play in the background, saying:

🥇 {Username} earned the {Badge Name} - {Badge Rank} 🥇

docs.title: Bags
docs.text:
Bags are accessories that can be bought in the various shops around the map. The main purpose of bags is to store pollen gathered by the player until it is full, to which the player will need to go to their hive and convert it into honey, use a Coconut, use an Instant Converter, use a Micro-Converter, use a Honeysuckle (only converts some) or admire Black Bear's Honey Wreath (only during Beesmas). When the player's bag is full, the following message is displayed: Pollen container full. Go to your hive to make honey. They may use an Instant Converter to instantly get all their honey (costs 1 ticket) or use a micro-converter. Certain bags are intended to give the player additional boosts other than capacity, such as Instant Conversion, Convert Rate, Bee Attack and even Passives (currently only from the Coconut Canister). There are other accessories (such as belt bags) that increase capacity. The Pouch bag is given automatically to new players. There are currently 12 bags in the game.

docs.title: Balloon
docs.text: Balloons are items that hold pollen for players and bring it back to the hive to convert into honey later. There are 6 types of balloons: pink, red, white, black, blue and gold. Pink, red, white, and black balloons are summoned with items. Blue and gold balloons are summoned by Buoyant Bee's abilities. The balloons return to the hive after reaching full capacity or after reaching their time limit. Capacity and time limit depends on the balloon type.

docs.title: In Fields
docs.text:
Balloons float around the field, similar to Clouds, and cast a 5-tile radius shadow on flowers underneath them. Pollen collected from these flowers is absorbed by the balloons above them. If multiple balloons have control over the same flower, the pollen is absorbed by the balloon with the lowest pollen amount in it. Balloons cannot absorb pollen from other players.

The pollen in balloons can also be increased by Buoyant Bee's Inflate Balloons ability, though this can only happen 10 times maximum per balloon.

Standing underneath any player's balloon grants a stack of the Balloon Aura buff. Each balloon the player is in radius of gives 1 stack of the buff, capping at x10 Balloon Aura. Each stack gives x1.02 pollen and +2% honey from tokens, capping at x1.2 pollen and +20% honey from tokens.

Gifted Frogs from Gifted Tadpole Bee, the Tide Popper's waves and Windy Bee's Tornado can also convert some pollen in the player's balloon into honey tokens. If the balloon is returning to the hive, it can still be converted from, and will drop its tokens around its last location on the field.

When a surprise party activates, all balloons (regardless of color) will generate random ability tokens for a few seconds. These can be white and blue boost tokens, buzz and blue bombs, marks, Haste, Token Link, and Melody tokens. The boost tokens spawned seem to be based off the primary color of the field.

docs.title: Hive Balloon
docs.text:
When a balloon reaches the player's hive, it becomes part of the "Hive Balloon". The Hive Balloon will float in place, waiting to be converted. Once the player begins converting, their bees will first convert anything in their bag before beginning to convert the hive balloon.

The hive balloon grants Balloon Blessing when fully converted, which grants Capacity and Honey at Hive. The buffs given increase as the pollen needed for another stack increases. It takes 10 trillion pollen stored in the Hive Balloon to reach the maximum stack (x100) of Balloon Blessing, which grants x4 Capacity and x2.5 Honey at Hive. When granting the buff, it displays " 🎈The hive balloon granted you x{stacks} of Balloon Blessing! "

If the blessing of hive balloon is lower than what the player currently has, fully converting it will instead refresh their balloon blessing timer, with the message " 🎈The hive balloon refreshed your Balloon Blessing! ".

Pollen in the hive balloon will begin to deplete depending on how big it is relative to the player's capacity. The slowest it will shrink is 20% per hour, and the fastest it will shrink is 99.99% in 10 minutes (if it contains over 100x the player's capacity). Keep in mind that this does not happen all at once, but rather gradually overtime until it reaches a sustainable level of pollen.

docs.title: Gold Balloon

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• If a balloon of any color is used and the player leaves the game, the balloon will disappear.
  • Balloons are the only non-limited/event items that aren't in crafting recipes. They also cannot be donated.
  • No matter what color balloon is used, when it arrives at the hive it will always turn blue.
  • Balloons are currently only obtainable through quests and mobs.
  • When converting at the hive, it is possible to glitch the Balloon Blessing. When converting the balloon, wait for the balloon to disappear, but leave the hive before it is finished converting. This will make the game put back the balloon in the hive with the same Balloon Blessing, yet give the Balloon Blessing buff, effectively duplicating the balloon.
  • It is possible to get multiple "🎈The hive balloon refreshed your Balloon Blessing!" messages in 1 hive conversion as long as there are new balloons coming to the hive at the correct time.

docs.text:
Bamboo Field

The Bamboo Field is a field located past the Basic Bee Gate, to the right of the Spider Field, and 2 fields away from the Strawberry Field. It is protected by two Rhino Beetles, one being level 2 and the other level 3.

This is an 18×39 field, containing 702 flowers. The flowers are blue and white, in sizes of single, double, and triple.

This field grants Comforting Nectar when a planter is planted here.

This field can spawn honey, blueberry, ticket, blue boost, magic bean, and blue extract tokens when collecting pollen.

Bees that like the Bamboo Field are Cool Bee, Bucko Bee, Buoyant Bee, Carpenter Bee, and Ninja Bee. Bees that dislike the Bamboo Field are Riley Bee, Precise Bee, & Windy Bee.

docs.title: Obtaining Boosts
docs.text:
• Using the Blue Field Booster may give a Bamboo Field Boost. When it does, it will give +100% Bamboo Field pollen for 15 minutes.
  • Using Glitter will add 100% Bamboo Field pollen onto the current boost for 15 minutes if the boost isn't already maxed out.
  • Using Field dice, Smooth Dice, or Loaded Dice may add +100% to 300% of Bamboo Field pollen for 15 minutes based on what type of dice is used, and also based on the current stack before the boost is added.
  • Bamboo Field Winds can be obtained through the Wind Shrine or codes. They have a base of +20% instant Bamboo Field conversion and give +5% instant Bamboo Field conversion and +15% Bamboo Field pollen for each stack. Bamboo Field Winds can stack up to a total of 13 times.
  • It can be boosted by the King Beetle Amulet. If it has a Bamboo Field Boost, it can boost the field by +1% to +100%.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This is one of six fields that fireflies can travel to, with the others being Cactus Field, Pineapple Patch, Rose Field, Spider Field, and Strawberry Field.
  • The player can find 2 royal jellies near the Bamboo Field, one in a nook under the ramp to the Brave Bee Gate, and the other at the end of an obstacle course, starting in between this field and the Spider Field.
  • The bamboo stems have claw marks on them, presumably from Panda Bear.
  • If a player stands on the corner of the Bamboo Field closest to the Spider Field while a Snowbear is summoned, the Snowbear can throw snowballs and damage the player.
  • The three bees that dislike the Bamboo Field also have another disliked field (Riley Bee and Precise Bee; Pine Tree Forest, Windy Bee; Strawberry Field)

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Realistic max is the best you can expect to actually see: the most picks of that upgrade that about 1 in 1,000 fully waxed 5 ★ beequips get, each at its top value. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

The Basic Bee Gate, also called the 5 Bee Gate, is the first gate a player is tasked with unlocking. The gate requires you to own 5 bees or more to pass through.

It gets its name from the large Basic Bee that's on top of it.

The audio known as "bpatrol" plays in the daytime while you are past this gate.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This is the only gate to have more than one gate directly leading from it, with those being the Brave Bee Gate and the Honey Bee Gate.
  • This gate requires the least amount of bees to pass through.
  • This and the Ant Gate are the only gates that lead to a zone where there is nothing that can be purchased with Honey.
  • Bubble Bee Man used to be behind the Global Top Battlers leaderboard. However, he was removed after Beesmas 2018.
  • Before the 2020-06-06 update, Honey Bee was located next to the ramp.
  • Underneath the ramp, on the side facing the Blue HQ, there is a ticket token, previously a Plastic Egg.
  • Due to a glitch, the Onett statue, located near the hives could have been seen near this gate. This glitch is now patched.
  • This gate is the only gate that cannot have a Wild Windy Bee spawn in any of its fields (without the assistance of Onett, during Beesmas or flying there from another field) (not counting the Ant Gate as it has only a challenge field or Bear Gate as the Bear Gate does not have any fields).
  • This gate is the only gate that doesn't teleport you back to the spawn point if you don't have the required bees.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Basic Bee is the only type of Common bee.
  • Due to the large number of appearances Basic Bee makes within the game and thumbnails, it is considered the main mascot of Re://:Swarm.
  • Basic Bee is one of three bees to have an official plushie on the Official Bee Swarm Simulator Website, the others being Tabby Bee and Vicious Bee.
  • The statistics for all other bees are described in terms of their difference from Basic Bee’s statistics. For example, +20 collection means that the bee it's describing has collected 20 more pollen than Basic Bee.
  • Basic Bee and Brave Bee are the only bees without abilities.
  • However, if they are in their gifted forms, they still can produce Inspire tokens.
  • And specific Beequips grants abilities like Focus or Melody tokens.
  • Because of this, during Bee Bear's "Ability Token Tidings" quest Bee Bear refers to Basic Bee and Brave Bee as "Poor little merely mortal bees".
    • Bee Bear also says they aren't magic due to this fact.
  • Basic Bee and Event Bees are the only types of bee that cannot be obtained from a normal royal jelly since Basic Bee is a Common Bee.
  • The code, "DontUseThisJelly" (expired) gave a Basic Bee jelly that could be used on a bee to transform any bee into a Basic Bee.
  • Basic Bee and Demo Bee share the same skin color pattern when they are not in their gifted forms.
  • Basic Bee and Honey Bee possess the same colors but in a different pattern.
  • Basic Bee's gifted bonus used to give +20% Pollen, but it later got buffed after the 2019-04-05 update into x1.2 Pollen, so it can now increase with any additional pollen multipliers that the player has.
  • An image of a winking Basic Bee face appears at the end of the White Tunnel.
  • This may refer to the currently valid code called "Wink".
  • This also appeared in the thumbnail of the 2018-06-02 update.
  • Basic Bee is the only kind of bee to appear in every different version of the thumbnail for the game.
  • Basic Bee, along with Tabby Bee and Rascal Bee, are all of Onett's favorite bees.
  • This was revealed through Onett's dialogue.
  • Basic Bee's face appears on the bee menu icon, found near the top left corner of the screen.
  • Its face is also visible on Treats, Tickets, and the Beequip Case.
  • The chances of getting a Gifted Basic Bee from sunflower seeds is 1 in 12,000.
  • The same chances apply to Legendary Bees if you feed them their favorite treats.
  • The chances of hatching a Gifted Basic Bee from a Basic Egg is 0.348% (1 out of 287.35632184).
  • On very rare occasions, Basic Bee's face would disappear on most surfaces that use its texture.
  • Basic Bee, Tadpole Bee, Tabby Bee, Lion Bee, Puppy Bee, and Bear Bee are the only bees to represent realistic animals.
  • But only the Tadpole Bee, Tabby Bee, Lion Bee, Puppy Bee, and Bear Bee represent realistic animals if Basic Bee is not counted since all the bees in this game are bees.
  • Basic Bee, Brave Bee, Honey Bee, Lion Bee, and Windy Bee are the only bees in the game featured on a gate.

docs.title: Basic Egg Shop
docs.text:
Basic Egg Shop Information Usage Obtaining Hive Slots through Basic Eggs Requirement(s) Honey (varies) Cooldown None Location Between the Sunflower Field and the Dandelion Field

The Basic Egg Shop is a shop located next to the Sunflower Field and behind an Instant Converter. It sells Basic Eggs for increasing amounts of honey.

The cost begins at 1,000 honey and increases exponentially (see Formula section below), eventually capping off at 10,000,000 honey for the 22nd egg and beyond.

Basic Eggs Honey 1 1,000 2 2,500 3 4,250 4 6,708 5 10,313 6 15,669 7 23,670 8 35,648 9 53,596 10 80,506 11 120,858 12 181,378 13 272,151 14 408,304 15 612,527 16 918,857 17 1,378,348 18 2,067,580 19 3,101,426 20 4,652,191 21 6,978,337 22+ 10,000,000

docs.title: Formula
docs.text:
The cost of egg number N is calculated as follows:

base = 1000
cost = base
i = 0
while i < N-1 do
    cost = 1.5*cost + base/(i+1)
    i = i + 1
end

This comes out roughly exponential, but there isn't a "nice neat numbers" exponential formula.

Base = 1000
t = Base
i = 0
NN = 21
For [i=0; t= Base, i < NN, i++, t=1.5*t+Base/(i+1);{Print[Floor[t+0.5]]}]

This does not work for Term 22, as the price caps out at 10,000,000 honey.

Basic Sprinkler Requirement 10 Cadet Badges Cost 1,111,111 Honey Description When planted in the ground, causes [sic] nearby flowers to regrow faster!

The Basic Sprinkler is the lowest tier sprinkler available for purchase in the Badge Bearer's Guild. To unlock it, the player must obtain 10 different Cadet badges. Once the player unlocks it, they can purchase it for ~1.1 million Honey. Its description reads, "When planted in the ground, causes [sic] nearby flowers to regrow faster!"

The Basic Sprinkler is comprised of an individual sprinkler, meaning the player is able to place down only one sprinkler at any moment. Previous sprinklers are removed if a new one is placed.

Its radius extends to 7 flower tiles, its rate is 5 seconds, and its power is 7.

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Realistic max is the best you can expect to actually see: the most picks of that upgrade that about 1 in 1,000 fully waxed 5 ★ beequips get, each at its top value. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

docs.title: Bean Bug
docs.text:
Bean Bug Location All fields except the Ant Field. Respawns Every Every ~30 minutes, or can be spawned through the Wind shrine.

Higher chance to spawn using 50-100 basic eggs or a Honey Bee egg.

The Bean Bug is a passive mob that can randomly appear in any field (except the Ant Field), be spawned through the Wind Shrine by donating 50-100 eggs or be manually spawned by Onett. They often spawn in one field in groups of 3 or more, and later split up.

When they spawn, they spit 1-3 Jelly Beans tokens in volleys over the field which any player can pick up, or can also spit out a Standing Bean Bug Sticker very rarely. Then they hop to another location on the field and spit more. The tokens only last for a few seconds, much less time than the tokens spawned from regular Jelly Beans. After 7-15 volleys of Jelly Beans, the Bean Bugs hop to other fields to spit Jelly Beans. This process repeats until they despawn after a while. Rarely, it may spawn a Standing Bean Bug Sticker.

Bean Bugs can aid the player in collecting Pollen/Honey, as Jelly Bean tokens can boost the player's pollen collection, Critical Chance, Instant Conversion, and other stats.

The beans were used for the limited time Sun Bear questline to receive 250 Tickets and for the limited 2019 Bee Bear questlines. They are also used for Spirit Bear's questline, and also used for Bee Bear's questline. Sun Bear and Bee Bear's Bean Bug questlines could only be received as a part of an event.

Players are unable to damage it, nor can it damage players, hence why it is a passive mob.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Bean Bugs, frogs, fireflies, chicks, Spotted Chicks, and Hostage Chicks are the only passive mobs in the game, as they cannot deal damage to players.
  • They were first introduced in the 2019-09-28 Update when Sun Bear accidentally released the Bean Bugs.
  • Sometimes, they can get stuck in various areas, including the Mushroom Field, Cactus Field, Bamboo Field, Basic Bee Gate, the Vicious Bee Claimer and fields that have solid object(s) while jumping. If they get stuck, they can't change course and will remain useless until de-spawning. Onett joked about this being "natural selection".
  • These and fireflies are the only passive mobs that are able to produce tokens.
  • This, Stick Bug, Snowbears and Mechsquitos are the only mobs being able to spawn a debuff. Stick Bug can spawn the Splinter Trap, Snowbear can Freeze with its Snowballs, Mechsquitos can apply Mechsquito Toxin by firing at the player, and Bean Bugs can spawn spoiled Jelly Beans.
  • As confirmed by Bee Bear, Bean Bugs have small brains and cannot understand the concept of naughty or nice.
  • At the end of Beesmas 2020, Onett spawned them as "The Bean Bug Brigade".
  • They then returned at the end of Beesmas 2021 as they "Awoke from Hibernation".
  • Bean Bugs are the first mob that use jumping to move around, with frogs being the second.
  • While, technically, chicks jump when they go inside their egg, this is the only time they do so.

Bear Bee is a Colorless Event bee. You can get this bee by redeeming a Bear Bee Voucher, which can be obtained by purchasing in the Robux Shop for 800 Robux, from trading, as an incredibly rare drop from Tunnel Bear.

Bear Bee likes the Pumpkin Patch and the Pine Tree Forest. It dislikes the Blue Flower Field.

The Bear Gate, also known as the 30 Bee Gate, is a gate added in the 2018-7-11 update that requires 30 bees to pass through. It is located past the Mountain Top Field, between the Ticket Shop and the Mountain Top Instant Converter. Two quest-giving NPCs reside here, that being Onett and Bubble Bee Man.

Underneath the platform in the gate, there is a Diamond Egg token and Shadow Bear behind it. To reach the egg token, equip either the Parachute or the Glider. Touching the floor kills the player, so it is advised to have an empty container before attempting to reach the Diamond Egg.

  • There used to be a glitch where if the player respawned and ran to the red cannon, they could use the Cannon to enter the gate without dying if they were quick enough using the forcefield applied on respawn. This glitch has since been patched.

docs.title: Bee Attack
docs.text:
Bee Attack is a mechanic that causes bees to attack mobs in a radius. When attacking, bees will deploy a small red laser (presumably a stinger) to deal damage based on the amount of bee attack power they possess. Bee attack boosts are split into five categories, regular bee attack, colorless bee attack, red bee attack, blue bee attack, and bee attack multiplier.

Regular bee attack, or known as just 'bee attack,' improves bee attack to all bees. Colorless, red, and blue bee attack improves bee attack to matching bees. Bee attack multiplier improves bee attack to all bees by multiplication after the sum-up of other bee attack statistics. Base bee attack refers to the total attack of one bee before any multipliers but after add additive bonuses. For example, a Lion Bee with 10 bee attack with items that give +3 bee attack and +1 colorless bee attack has a base bee attack of 14.

The starting bee attack of all bees ranges from 0 to 10, although attack can be increased beyond that. The bee with the highest starting bee attack is Lion Bee with 10 attack, and the bee with the lowest starting bee attack is Baby Bee with 0 attack, however even if Baby Bee's attack is raised, it will still be unable to attack mobs.

For an increased bee attack stat, first the additives (+ bee attack and + colourless, blue or red bee attack) is added and then, the Bee attack multiplier is added. For example, for a gifted Brave Bee of a player wearing the Porcelain Port-O-Hive with no amulets, guards and belt, since the base attack of a Brave Bee is 5, the +2 bee attack from the said bee's Gifted Hive Bonus and Porcelain Port-O-Hive are first added, making the bee attack till now 7. With the x1.5 bee attack of the Gifted buff, its bee attack is 10.5. Thus, the Brave Bee's attack stat will be displayed as 10.5 in the stats menu of the said bee.

docs.title: Improving Bee Attack
docs.text: Bee attack can be improved in many ways, every type of bee attack can be improved depending on the player's regular bee attack, colorless bee attack, red bee attack, blue bee attack, and bee attack multiplier.

docs.title: Regular Bee Attack
docs.text:
• Collecting a rage ability token grants a bonus +1 bee attack, stacking up to 4 times, for a maximum of +4 bee attack.
  • Gifted Brave Bee grants a bonus +1 bee attack.
  • King Beetle Amulet, Ant Amulet, and Stick Bug Amulets have a chance to grant +1 bee attack.
  • The Hiking Boots and Beekeeper's Boots both grant a bonus +1 bee attack.
  • The Coconut Clogs grant a bonus +2 bee attack.
  • The Gummy Boots grant a bonus +3 bee attack.

docs.title: Colorless Bee Attack
docs.text:

  • The Brave Guard grants a bonus +1 colorless bee attack.
  • The Cog Amulet (Gold+) has a chance to grant +1 or +2 colorless bee attack.

docs.text:

  • Using a stinger grants x1.5 bee attack multiplier for 30 seconds.

  • The Fire Mask grants a bonus +15% bee attack multiplier.

  • Activating the Emergency Coconut Shield grants x1.25 bee attack multiplier for 10 seconds.
  • The Coconut Combo buff gives up to +50% bee attack at 100 stacks.
  • The Rose Field Market Boost grants +10% bee attack multiplier along with other buffs for 30 minutes. (unobtainable)
  • Invigorating Nectar grants a bonus of +1% to +10% bee attack multiplier.
  • Certain Beequips. (Example: Icicles)

  • Adding the Walking Stick Nymph to the Sticker Stack grants +1% Bee Attack.
  • Adding the Theatrical Intruder to the Sticker Stack grants +1% Bee Attack.
  • Adding the Tough Potato to the Sticker Stack grants +1% Bee Attack
  • Adding the Festive Pea to the Sticker Stack grants +1% Gifted Bee Attack.

  • Adding the Stick Cub Skin to the Sticker Stack grants +1% Bee Attack.
  • Festive Nymph Blessing gives % bee attack, up to +5%.

docs.title: Robo Bear Challenge Upgrades
docs.text:
The Robo Bear Challenge provides increases or decreases Bee Attack in the form of adding or multiplying depending on which upgrade you purchase with Cogs. These buffs last until your Robo Bear Challenge ends, however they are only active when you are doing a round.

  • Common Upgrades:
  • Sharpen: This upgrade starts at x1.2 Bee Attack and maxes at 10 upgrades with x3 Bee Attack.
  • Rare Upgrades:
  • Blue Screen: This upgrade grants x1.03 Bee Attack and Blue Bee Attack for every blue boost stack you have, maxing out at x1.3 Bee Attack and Blue Bee Attack.
  • Equalize: This upgrade grants +1 Bee Attack and x1.25 Ungifted Bee Attack.
  • Saturate: This upgrade starts at x1.25 Blue and Colorless Bee Attack, but x0.8 Red Bee Attack, it maxes at 3 upgrades with x1.75 Blue and Colorless Bee Attack and x0.4 Red Bee Attack.
  • SSD: White: This upgrade lowers Bee Attack, starting at x0.8 Bee Attack and maxes at 3 upgrades with x0.6 Bee Attack.
  • Epic Upgrades:
  • Fission: This upgrade grants +1 Bee Attack.
  • Furnace: This upgrade does not improve Bee Attack, but it grants x1.5 Flame Damage.
  • Inject: This upgrade grants +2 Blue Bee Attack, +1 Colorless Bee Attack, and x1.25 Impale Damage.
  • Malware: This upgrade starts at +3 Bee Attack and maxes at 3 upgrades with +9 Bee Attack.
  • NFT: This upgrade lowers Bee Attack, it grants -3 Bee Attack.
  • Pop-Up: This upgrade grants +2 Blue Bee Attack.
  • Legendary Upgrades:
  • Bluetooth: This upgrade gives x2 Blue Bee Attack.
  • Codec: This upgrade lowers Bee Attack, it grants x0.8 Bee Attack.

docs.title: Others
docs.text:
These ways are to improve certain bees' attacks which don't count up to regular bee attack, colorless bee attack, red bee attack, blue bee attack, nor bee attack multiplier.

  • Critical hits increase the damage outcome of bees by the amount of Critical Power. (minimum of 100% more damage)
  • Super-crits increase the damage outcome of critical hits by the amount of Super-Crit Power, but it is only 33% as powerful as a pollen super-crit.
  • Every gifted bee gains x1.5 bee attack for themselves.
  • Certain mutations increase the individual bee's attack by 1 or a multiplier (%).
  • Activating Gummy Morph grants +300 bonus bee attack only to Gummy Bee, along with other buffs.
  • Adding the Flying Brave Bee to the Sticker Stack grants +2 Rare Bee Attack.
  • Adding the Coiled Snake to the Sticker Stack grants +1 Epic Bee Attack.
  • Adding the Evil Pig to the Sticker Stack grants +1 Epic Bee Attack.
  • Adding the Left Facing Ant to the Sticker Stack grants +1 Legendary Bee Attack.

docs.title: Bee Bear's Catalog
docs.text:
Bee Bear's Catalog is a limited-time shop that players can use to purchase various products during Beesmas 2020, 2021, 2022, Summer 2024, Winter 2024, and 2025. It can be accessed through a side tab on the right side of the screen. Its description is: "Beesmas event shop! Purchase items for Gingerbread Bears and Snowflakes."

In Re://:Swarm, the 2025 catalog is still open: each of its bundles expires at the 2025 Beesmas deadline, which is set to the year 2057.

There is a countdown below the icon of the shop, which counts down the time until Beesmas ends.

The shop sells items and bundles of many varieties. The player cannot purchase an item or bundle more than once.

Buying items from the Catalog is sometimes required in NPC quests like Bee Bear's.

You can only buy items in this shop with Snowflakes and Gingerbread Bears.

Successfully purchasing items from the catalog gives a message: Purchased {Item/Bundle}!

Attempting to purchase items from the catalog without sufficient items gives a message:

Can't afford {Item/Bundle}

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Items from the Bee Bear's Catalog are all one-time purchases, meaning that the player can only buy them once and can't buy them again.
  • In order to buy all the items from the catalog, the player would have needed:
  • 29,460 Snowflakes and 1,118 Gingerbread Bears during Beesmas 2020.
  • 55,571 Snowflakes and 1,195 Gingerbread Bears during Beesmas 2021.
  • 107,635 Snowflakes and 1,379 Gingerbread Bears during Beesmas 2022.
  • 111,729 Snowflakes and 1,546 Gingerbread Bears during Beesmas Summer 2024.
  • 153,857 Snowflakes and 1,619 Gingerbread Bears during Beesmas Winter 2024.
  • 188,224 Snowflakes and 1,738 Gingerbread Bears during Beesmas 2025.
  • Shortly after Beesmas Summer 2024 released, Onett reduced sticker requirements for some quests and made a few stickers purchasable in the catalog as well as making a few of them more common.
  • Since Onett didn't update every single server, some servers didn't have the new sticker offers in the catalog.
  • The next day, Onett updated the Hive Hubs to fix Bee Bear's 15th quest. Because all of these servers were updated to the latest version, you could easily go to the Hive Hubs if you didn't want to keep looking for a server with the updated catalog.
  • If the player bought something from the catalog, the system would say +[Item Name] (From [Item Name]). This was changed in Beesmas 2022 to simply say +[Item Name].
  • This was the very first limited time shop or catalog in the game to exist.
  • The 2020 Beesmas Pinecone Bundle used to have a scripting error, where it gave 30 Glues instead of 30 Enzymes.
  • This was the only non-robux shop to have bundles sold in it.
  • During Beesmas 2021, The Catalog's timer was extended with the release of Beesmas Part 2 to give the players more time to complete the new quests, since the Beesmas Part 2 update came late.
  • Items bought in the Bee Bear's Catalog can exceed the items cap.
  • Gingerbread Bears from last year's Beesmas turn into Aged Gingerbread Bears when the next Beesmas event starts.
  • These Aged Gingerbread Bears can not be used to buy items from Bee Bear's Catalog — only Gingerbread Bears obtained in the same Beesmas event can.
  • Aged Gingerbread Bears do not age further than they have, so there will be no difference between Aged Gingerbread Bears that came from 2020 versus those that came from 2022.
  • This, the Mondo Gift Box, Sticker-Seeker Quest Machine and the leaderboards are the only non-robux ways to obtain a Gifted Mythic Egg.
  • Its description changed from "Winter" to "Beesmas" during Beesmas 2024, most likely due to it releasing in the summer.
  • During the summer of Beesmas 2024, the price on the Percussive Bundle of 808 Snowflakes (and 8 Gingerbread Bears) is a reference to the Roland TR-808 drum machine, commonly referred to simply as an "808".
  • The 808 is the most popular drum machine in the history of music, being initially used in '80s new wave music, and since then, in nearly every rap or hip hop song ever made. Similarly, the 8 Gingerbread Bears are likely a reference to the Roland TR-08 Rhythm Composer, which is a digital re-release of the original drum machine, and/or it may refer to the Roland TR-8S, which also uses the same percussive sound.
  • The format for the timer is DD:HH:SS (D for Days, H for Hours, and S for Seconds).
  • The button is placed on the same place the Bear Bee Offer was placed during its release, and has a similar appearance.

Not to be confused with Bear Bee, an Event bee with a similar name.

Bee Bear is a traveling bear who appears during Beesmas. He is one of the four temporary quest givers, the others being Sun Bear, Gummy Bear and Bubble Bee Man.

In 2018, his quests were focused on creating Presents, which could be later given to NPCs. At the end of his quests, he gave players a special bee, Festive Bee. Alternatively, if the player already had one by buying the Festive Bee Pack or from the Ticket Tent, he gave 500 Tickets instead. He was located in front of the Ant Gate between December 19, 2018, to January 31, 2019.

His second visit was from December 22, 2019, to February 10, 2020. Bee Bear rewarded the player a Cub Buddy after the 10 quests that a player completed, and the Bee Cub after another 5 quests. His quests consisted of a variety of different requirements. Some included collecting Pollen, Tokens, Goo, defeating mobs, putting Ornaments on the Beesmas Tree, and more. He stood in front of the Dandelion Field, next to the Festive Present, the first time that a traveling Bear was not located in front of the Ant Gate.

His third visit was from December 25, 2020, to March 1, 2021. His quests were used to help introduce Beequips. His quests also required completing and using Beesmas Decorations from multiple NPCs, collecting Snowflakes, purchasing items from his Catalog, and delivering Presents. He rewarded players with a Festive Bee ( or 500 Tickets if Festive Bee was already owned by the player) when his first 15 quests were completed, and rewarded a Festive Wreath Beequip for the Festive Bee when all his quests were completed.

His fourth visit was from December 26, 2021, to April 1, 2022. His quests were used to help introduce the new planters, rewarded a special type of his own (Festive Planters), alongside giving players the opportunity to obtain a Cub Buddy (or a Star Treat if already owned) by completing his first 15 quests once again. In the second part of Beesmas, he rewards players a Snow Cub after all of his quests (new ones included) were completed.

His fifth visit was from December 26, 2022, to May 7, 2023. His quests were used to help introduce the Robo Bear Challenge and drives, another new addition in the update. He rewarded players with a Cub Buddy (or a Star Treat if Cub Buddy was already owned by the player) when his first 15 quests were completed. In the second part of Beesmas, he rewarded players a Peppermint Robo Cub after all of his quests (new ones included) were completed.

His sixth visit was from July 17, 2024, to October 29, 2024 (confirmed with an in-game timer). His quests were used to help introduce stickers. After 5 of his quests were completed, he rewarded players a Sticker Planter and a Star Jelly. After 10 of his quests were completed, he rewarded players a Wavy Festive Hive Skin. Upon completing a further 5 quests, he rewarded players a Cub Buddy (Cub Buddy Voucher if the player already owns a Cub Buddy). When completing the final 5 quests, he rewarded players with a Doodle Cub.

His seventh visit was originally for a Roblox event, the Winter Spotlight; however, he remained in the game for a few more months even though the event had ended. His visit lasted from December 17, 2024, at 9-10 pm 2024 to May 1, 2025. The focus was on almost everything in the game, not just one specific concept. The rewards included a Festive Planter, a Cub Buddy, and a Gloomy Cub.

His eighth visit started on December 25, 2025; however, none of his quests were introduced until December 27, 2025, where he gave out ten quests for rewards including a Festive Planter. On January 16, 2026, 5 more quests were introduced for a Cub Buddy (Cub Buddy Voucher if the player already owns a Cub Buddy). On April 23, 2026, the last 5 quests were released, rewarding the player with the Petal Cub skin on completion. The main focus on his quests were Blooms. His visit ended on June 8, 2026, at midnight EST (GMT-5).
