docs.title: Obtaining Boosts
docs.text:
• Using glitter will add 100% Coconut Field pollen onto the current boost for 15 minutes if it isn't already maxed out.

  • Using field dice, smooth dice, or loaded dice may add +100% - 300% Coconut Field pollen for 15 minutes based on the type used if it isn't already maxed out.

  • Coconut Field Winds can be obtained through the Wind Shrine or codes. They have a base of +20% Instant Coconut Field Conversion and give +5% Instant Coconut Field Conversion and +10% Coconut Field pollen for each stack. Coconut Field Winds can stack up to a total of 15 times.

  • Using the Coconut Dispenser will always give Coconut Field Boost x1 (if the player has Coconut Badge cadet or higher), along with coconuts depending on the player's badge.
  • Equipping the Coconut Clogs grants x1.15 Coconut Field pollen.
  • Equipping the Coconut Belt grants x1.1 Coconut Field pollen.

docs.title: The methods below are no longer possible.
docs.text:
• Giving Gummy Bear a present gave Coconut Field Boost x3 + other stuff.
  • Redeeming certain expired codes:
  • Gumaden10T (Gave Coconut Field Boost x1 and Coconut Field Winds x3 + other stuff)
  • DarzethDoodads (Coconut Field Code Buff + other stuff).
  • FrozenBugReboot (Coconut Field Code Buff and Coconut Field Boost x4 + other stuff
  • Purchasing a Coconut Field Market Boost from the Boost Market will give x1.5 Coconut Field Capacity, x1.25 Coconut Field Pollen, x2.5 Pollen from Coconuts, and x1.1 White Pollen.
  • Mocito100T (Gave Coconut Field Boost x2 and Coconut Field Capacity x2 + other stuff).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This is the only field where sprouts and leaves can yield coconuts and tropical drinks.
  • It is also the only field to have a regular boss defending it.
  • This is one of four fields to solely have contain triple flowers without pollination, the others being the Mountain Top Field, Stump Field, and the Pepper Patch.
  • Furthermore, this field is the only triple-flower field dominated by white flowers.
  • Under the coconut tree opposite of the cave and closest to Spirit Bear, there is a coconut token that can be collected to give 10 coconuts.
  • This and the Pepper Patch are the only fields where sprouts cannot naturally appear or be planted with the Special Sprout Summoner.
  • Like the Pepper Badge, the Coconut Badge requires more pollen collected than the other field badges. For example, the cadet badge for the Coconut Field requires 50,000,000 (50 million) pollen, compared to the normal requirement of 250,000 (250 thousand) pollen.
  • It is possible to gather pollen from this field without 35 bees from the ledge facing the Ticket Tent.
  • Players can also collect from the field by going outside the map and finding the back of the Ticket Tent. Jumping on the Ticket Tent with enough jump height will reach the field, allowing bees to farm.
  • The Coconut Dispenser used to boost this field differently based on the player's Coconut Badge, with the Junior badge giving no boost, Cadet giving a +100% pollen boost, Hotshot giving a +200% pollen boost, and anything Ace and above giving a +300% pollen boost. After the Beesmas 2019 update, the Coconut Dispenser will always provide a +100% pollen boost, regardless of the player's Coconut Badge.
  • This field, the Ant Field and the Hub Field are the only fields without any bees to dislike them.

docs.title: Coconut
docs.text:
Coconut

"Drops a huge Coconut into the field. Catch it to convert Pollen to Honey Tokens."

COOLDOWN

3 seconds

CAP

500

A Coconut is an inventory item that was added in the 2019-09-28 update. It will spawn a large, green circle on the field you used it on. If caught, it will convert pollen into a ring of 10 honey tokens. It can also collect pollen for the player that summoned it, damage mobs, and can be used in certain crafting recipes.

Pollen from coconuts can be increased with the Coconut Clogs, pollination, and the Coconut Field Market Boost (now impossible to obtain as the Boost Market has been removed).

A maximum of 500 coconuts can be held at a time, as the item's highest capacity limit, excluding items that don't have a capacity limit.

There's also an On/Off switch on the player's hotbar (if the coconut Item is in the player's hotbar). The coconut will be used automatically when this switch is turned on.

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• Defeating the Coconut Crab grants coconuts (depending on the time taken to defeat it).
  • Growing sprouts in the Coconut Field.
  • Farming in the Coconut Field.
  • Harvesting Leaves here may also yield Coconuts.
  • There is a token worth 10 coconuts under the leaves of the palm tree closest to Spirit Bear.
  • Using the Coconut Dispenser grants 3 Coconuts (amount increases with each Coconut Badge tier obtained, up to 15 Coconuts).
  • Redeeming certain valid codes:
  • 1MLikes (Gives 1 Coconut + other items).
  • Winning them from Mega Memory Match and Extreme Memory Match (available in increments of 3 and 5 Coconuts respectively).
  • As a rare gift from Cub Buddy in increments of 1.
  • As a drop from an Armored Aphid.
  • Harvesting planters in the Coconut Field, Pine Tree Forest or Pepper Patch.
  • As a drop from puffshrooms within the 35 bee zone.
  • Purchasing the Reindeer Bundle from Bee Bear's Catalog for 250 Gingerbread Bears grants 100 Coconuts and other items.
  • The Palm Tree sticker rewards 10 Coconuts when added to the Sticker Stack.

docs.title: Conversion
docs.text:
When the coconut lands on a player, Pollen is converted in your Backpack and has a maximum amount of 100% of the player's total hive convert amount. For example, if a player has 500,000 total hive convert amount and a coconut lands on them, up to 500,000 pollen would be converted into honey tokens.

The amount of honey received from the coconut is multiplied by Honey From Tokens.

docs.title: Cog Amulet
docs.text:
The Cog Amulet is an amulet that can be obtained from the Robo Bear Challenge. In order to obtain one, the player must beat certain rounds during the Robo Bear Challenge. The more rounds the player beats, the higher the tier of the Cog Amulet.

The amulets grant buffs to the owner and always increase capacity and attack as they go up a tier. Higher tier amulets grant more and better buffs.

The amulet's quality (0 to 1) comes from three parts of your run: 0.45 × (rounds beaten / 25) + 0.35 × (final score / 125,000) + 0.2 × (average bee level / 20). The rounds and score parts are each capped at 1, the bee level part is kept between 0.05 and 1.25, and the total is capped at 1. Fewer than 5 rounds gives no amulet.

This article is about the items used in the Robo Bear Challenge. Not to be confused with 7-Pronged Cog.

Cog

"Used for purchases during Robo Bear's Challenge. Removed when the challenge ends."

COOLDOWN

N/A

Cogs are inventory items added in the 2022-12-26 update. They are used to purchase upgrades, purchase drives, and reroll bees and upgrades in the Robo Bear Challenge. They are removed from the inventory when the Robo Bear Challenge ends. Additionally, you can reach 250,000 Cogs collected in total to unlock the Robo Cub.

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• Completing quests in the Robo Bear Challenge.
  • Starting a challenge gives 10 Cogs.
  • The harder the quest, the more Cogs it gives.
  • You may get bonus cogs for completing a quest within the first two minutes.
  • You may also get bonus cogs from certain upgrades you can purchase in the challenge.
  • Defeating a Golden Cogmower guarantees at least 14 Cogs and scales up to 18.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This is the first item to be added that is not only exclusively rewarded in a challenge, but also used as a temporary form of currency.
  • This is no longer the case, as you can now get a cog outside of the Robo Bear Challenge from Bubble Bee Man.
  • The item slightly resembles the cog on top of the Noob Shop.

docs.title: Cogmower
docs.text:
Not to be confused with Golden Cogmowers, the rarer, golden counterparts of Cogmowers or Party Cogmowers, the Beesmas Edition of these.

Cogmower Location Any field while the Robo Bear Challenge is active.

A Cogmower is a mob that exclusively appears during Robo Bear's Challenge.

This is the second mob in the Robo Bear Challenge that the player encounters, appearing as early as round 5.

Cogmowers rise from the field before slowly moving around the field aimlessly in a straight line, destroying layers and removing goo from flowers upon going near them. when the player switches fields, the Cogmower sinks in the former field and ascends to the field the player is currently/recently standing in to follow the player. Cogmowers bounce in different directions when hitting the field's borders or another cogmower. The higher the level of the Cogmower, the more pollen is drained. They only take half the damage from Critical Hits.

In rounds 10 and 20. Cogmowers are the main target mobs, requiring to defeat 10 in Round 10 and 20 in Round 20. In these rounds, cogmowers do not randomly spawn but will always stay in the same field and not follow the player whenever they stand in another field.

In round 10, cogmowers spawn in 3 sets of fields. The first set always contains 4 cogmowers, spawning in either Pineapple Patch, Bamboo Field, or Clover Field. The second set contains 3 cogmowers and will spawn in either Dandelion Field, Sunflower Field, or Strawberry Field. The third set contains 3 cogmowers and will spawn in either Cactus Field, Pumpkin Patch, or Pine Tree Forest.

In round 20, 4 sets of cogmowers spawn and there are 5 cogmowers each set. They spawn in nearly the same fields as round 10, with the addition of the Rose Field.

A Cogmower's level can range from 5-22, depending on what round of Robo Bear's Challenge the player is on.

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
• Cogmowers do not aim for the player, allowing players to sidestep them easily.
  • A Cogmower's hitbox is directly in front of it instead of over it, so you can stand inside of one to ensure your bees target them.
  • Stand near the Cogmower, this allows your bees to lock on to the Cogmower and quickly deal damage.
  • Vicious Bee and Windy Bee provide excellent crowd control, especially since Cogmowers often come in pairs or packs. Digital Bee can also stun many Cogmowers at once, and allow them to take extra damage via Mind Hack.
  • The Star Saw' Passive from the Supreme Star Amulet can be useful as it circles you for 30 seconds when activated and can damage multiple Cogmowers simultaneously.
  • Frogs, Pollen Haze, and multiple amounts of Supreme Saturators can provide great amounts of field regeneration, which can combat the flowers drained by the cogmowers.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Cogmower is a portmanteau of "Cog" and "Lawnmower'.
  • Cogmowers have a unique golden counterpart known as a Golden Cogmower.
  • They also have a Beesmas variant called the Party Cogmower.
  • Cogmowers, Golden Cogmowers, Party Cogmowers, Cogturrets, Party Cogturrets, and Wild Windy Bee are the only mobs that are able to collect layers of flowers.
  • If a Cogmower is stunned due to Digital Bee's Mind Hack, and is hit by an unaffected one, it would still bounce.

docs.title: Cogturret
docs.text:
Cogturret Location Any field while the Robo Bear Challenge is active.

Not to be confused with Party Cogturrets, the Beesmas Edition of these.

A Cogturret is a mob that appears during Robo Bear Challenge.

This is the third type of mob the Player will encounter while doing the challenge, first appearing at round 11.

Cogturrets always position themselves on the field's edge and follow the player similar to cogmowers where they descend to the former field and ascend to the current/recent field the player has visited. Cogturrets behavior is a fixed cycle. First, Cogturrets hide under the field and move along the field's edges, either randomly or at the player, during this state, cogturrets cannot be targeted. Then, they ascend and become targetable again. After a few seconds, they blast a giant red cog projectile in a straight line that destroys flowers, removing all layers of the flower and any goo covering it. After this, the Cogturret hides again and repeats the cycle.

Cogturrets' level can range from 11 to 22 depending on the current round of the Robo Bear Challenge.

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
• Cogturrets aim either at the player or randomly and have a delay on attacking whenever they ascend. Because of this, moving to the side after they fire a cog will often result in Cogturrets missing their attack.
  • Cogturrets will always shoot straight at where they are facing so you can avoid their attacks simply by not being in front of them.
  • Stand near the Cogturrets, this allows your bees to lock on to the Cogturrets and quickly deal damage.
  • Vicious Bee and Windy Bee provide excellent crowd control, especially since Cogturrets often come in pairs or packs. Digital Bee can also stun many Cogturrets at once and allow them to take extra damage via Mind Hack.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Cogturrets have a Robo Party variant named Party Cogturrets.
  • Cogturrets, Cogmowers, Golden Cogmowers, Party Cogmower, Party Cogturrets, and Wild Windy Bee are the only entities who can collect from flowers.

  • Buying the Frozen Forest Pack from Bee Bear's Catalog for 1,200 Snowflakes and 60 Gingerbread Bears grants 1 Comforting Vial and other items.
  • Giving a Present to Gifted Bucko Bee rewards 1 Comforting Vial and other items.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Commander Bee's skin is the same as Looker Bee's.
  • This bee, Buoyant Bee and Frosty Bee are the only 3 bees in the game that wear hats by default.
  • Of the three, this one is the only colorless bee to have one.
  • Festive Bee and Puppy Bee, however, can have an accessory by using the Festive Wreath and Reindeer Antlers respectively.
  • This bee is one of the 3 bees that have the Focus ability by default, the other 2 are Looker Bee, and Music Bee.
  • Commander Bee is the only epic bee added in an update.
  • A Commander Bee Egg can be obtained by capturing Commando Chick 200 times.
  • As the name and model suggest, this bee is likely inspired by the eponymous video game protagonist known as Commander Keen.
  • This point is further supported by the expired code "Keen4", which yielded a Commander Bee Jelly.

docs.title: Commando Chick's Hideout
docs.text: The Commando Chick's Hideout is a location in the Starter Zone that can be entered by completing the obby between the Blue HQ and the Wealth Clock. To enter the parkour, the player first needs to cut the vines blocking the entrance with either the Clippers, Scissors, Scythe or the Dark Scythe. It is home to the Commando Chick.

docs.title: Strategy
docs.text: Standing on the last stair, nearest to Commando Chick's hideout normally makes the chick flee. However, if the player stands on the edge of that stair (as close as possible to the hideout where one of your body parts is inside of the hideout), the Commando Chick does not flee; therefore, the player's bees can defeat the Commando Chick whilst they take no damage. This strategy does not 100% work as there could be a slight chance of the Commando Chick fleeing. The player could just move into the hideout and then back onto the stair again to fix this.

docs.title: Music
docs.text: The music "Crawlers" plays in the hideout.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This location used to house the Most Commando Captures leaderboard before it was removed from the game.
  • In Beesmas 2019, this location contained the Golden Present.
  • The obstacle course remained after the presents were removed. When the 2020-04-06 update came out, it was repurposed into the hideout.

docs.title: Commando Chick
docs.text:
This piece of content contains information obtained through datamining.

Due to the nature of the information, details may be inaccurate or outdated.

Datamined information: The formula for calculating Commando Chick's level at a given capture count. — December 19th, 2024

Commando Chick Location Commando Chick's Hideout Respawns Every 30:00 (25:30 with Gifted Vicious Bee hive boost)

The Commando Chick is a mini-boss chick that spawns in its hideout. Its hideout is located to the left of Brown Bear and the Wealth Clock. To cut the vines, the Clippers, Scissors, Scythe or Dark Scythe needs to be equipped. Once the vines are cut, they will never regrow back.

The Commando Chick has a respawn time of 30:00 (25:30 with Gifted Vicious Bee). When Commando Chick hides in its egg, it throws grenades (1 if it has more than 2/3 of its health, 2 if it has less than 2/3 of its health, 3 if it has less than 1/3 of its health, 4 if less than 1/100).

The Commando Chick deals 20 damage when colliding with the player and 50 damage if the player is near a grenade when it explodes. Starting at 150 health and level 3, the chick increases in health and level with each successive capture, reaching level 6 by the fifth capture. The chick will grow another level after a progressively higher amount of captures per level up.

Commando Chick has a similar appearance to other Chicks but is twice as large as a normal one. It also has a green shell and red eyes.

The Commando Chick stays still and blocks attacks when it is in its shell. After some time, it jumps out of its shell and resumes running around within the hideout.

docs.title: Levels
docs.text:
The Commando Chick's level is based on the number of kills the player has recorded against it. The following formula can be used to find the Commando Chick's level at a given number of kills:

  • Let the number of kills be \(x\).
  • \(x<2\), its level is 3.
  • Otherwise, its level is \(3+\left\lfloor {{\frac {-1.375+{\sqrt {0.390625+1.5x}}}{0.75}}+1}\right\rfloor\), clamped between 1 and 25.

The higher Commando Chick's level is, the more HP it has and the faster it moves, specifically by 0.5 more studs per level. The below table gives the number of kills required for a certain level, and the amount of HP it has at that level.

  • Commando Chick tokens will be automatically collected when they fade away.
  • Milestone rewards:

    • Drops Gold Egg upon the 10th capture.
    • Drops Star Jelly upon the 15th capture.
    • Drops 3 Blue Extracts upon the 20th capture.
    • Drops 100 Tickets upon the 25th capture.
    • Drops 10 Stingers upon the 30th capture.
    • Drops 10 Ant Passes and 10 Stingers upon the 40th capture.
    • Drops Mythic Egg upon the 50th capture.
    • Drops Star Treat upon the 100th capture.
    • Drops Commander Bee Egg upon the 200th capture.

docs.title: Strategy
docs.text:
• Standing on the last stair, nearest to Commando Chick's hideout normally makes the chick flee. However, if the player stands on the edge of that stair (as close as possible to the hideout), Commando Chick does not flee and the player's bees can defeat Commando Chick whilst they take no damage.
  • This strategy does not guarantee success, as there could be a slight chance of the chick fleeing or accidentally jumping onto the stair as it hops when entering the egg.
    • The player could just move into the hideout and then back onto the stair again to fix this.
  • Re-entering the hideout when the Commando Chick is still in its egg will cause it to change back to its roaming state; although still spawning another set of grenades.
  • This mob can be damaged by any player, as such, having another player help can make progress faster.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This is one of the few mobs to have its own hideout with the others being King Beetle and Tunnel Bear.
  • Commando Chick's hideout is the only one of the three where you have to complete an obby to enter it.
  • Commando Chick is the only chick to have a green color egg.
  • Commando Chick can spawn many grenades by leaving and reentering Commando Chick's spawn area multiple times.
  • Commando Chick is the only chick with red eyes; all other chicks have black eyes.
  • Commando Chick is one of the two chicks to drop a Mythic Egg, the other being the Mondo Chick.
  • Commando Chick is one of two mobs whose health is saved if the player leaves mid-session, the other being the Stump Snail.
  • Other player's bees can attack your Commando Chick.
  • Only your Commando Chick can damage you by contact, but all grenades can damage all players.
  • There used to be a leaderboard behind where it spawns called the Most Commando Captures Leaderboard. Since 2020-04-07, the leaderboard has been removed.
  • There is a glitch where Commando Chick will disappear while being actively fought. When this occurs, a different fleeing message will appear: [🐣 Commando Chick got away! 🐣]
  • The normal message is [🐣 Commando Chick fled! (HP Saved) 🐣]
  • There is a glitch where Commando Chick's feet clip into the ground. This will cause it to slide and move extremely fast, even if it is in its egg. If it hits a corner, it will not change direction and stay there until it goes into its roaming stage again.
  • There was a glitch where Commando Chick would stay in its egg and would not go out of its egg, even when it was moving. This can also make some player's bees keep on missing their shots. The easiest way to fix this glitch was to exit Commando Chick's Hideout and re-enter it

docs.title: Crimbolt Bee
docs.text:
Crimbolt Bee Original Gifted "A harmonious bee embodying the united force of red, white, and blue." RarityEvent ColorColorless Energy1500 Speed21 Attack12

Crimbolt Bee is a Colorless Event bee that is only in Re://:Swarm. Its body is red on the left, blue on the right and white on the front, with a "C" crest, and it carries a rocket tube on its back.

Its egg description reads: "The symbol of all colors in unison. Uses Token Link, Haste, and Crimbolt Rockets, and empowers its hive through Combined Forces."

It fires rockets at the field with its own ability, Crimbolt Rockets, and also has Token Link and Haste. Its passive, Combined Forces, boosts Instant Conversion of all three colours and your critical hits.

Crimbolt Bee has no favourite treat. It likes the Rose Field and Clover Field, and dislikes the Pineapple Patch. Only one can be in a hive.

docs.title: Stats
docs.text:
Stat Value Rarity Event Colour Colorless Energy 1,500 Speed 21 Attack 12 Gather 75 pollen every 4 seconds Convert 280 honey every 3 seconds Gifted bonus x1.2 Pollen, +8% Instant Conversion, +2 Attack

The bee info panel lists its bonuses as: +7,400% Energy, +50% Movespeed, +25% Convert Speed, +50% Gather Amount, +180 Convert Amount, +11 Attack. Two of those don't match its real stats: it gathers 75 pollen against a Basic Bee's 10 (x7.5), and makes 280 honey against 80 (+200).

Crimbolt Bee has the highest Energy of any bee in the game.

docs.title: Crimbolt Rockets
docs.text:
Crimbolt Rockets

"Causes Crimbolt Bee to fly into the air and fire 3 rockets at random flowers in the field. Each impact collects pollen in the same 13-flower pattern as a regular Bomb token, and every flower struck spawns a Crimbolt Flame."

The rockets fire 0.45 seconds apart and land on 3 different flowers. Each impact counts as a Bomb and a Buzz Bomb, so it works with Bomb Combo and Bomb Power.

  • Attempt cooldown: 6 seconds
  • Use cooldown: 24 seconds
  • Chance per attempt: 25%
  • Token lasts 8 seconds
  • Spawns while gathering and in battle

Each rocket that lands in a field has a 1 in 1,750 chance to give the Menacing Crimbolt Bee sticker and a 1 in 10,000 chance to give the Explosion sticker.

See Ability Tokens for more.

docs.title: Token Link
docs.text:
Token Link

"Collects all other ability tokens, granting 25 Honey (+10 per lvl) per token collected."

  • Cooldown: 5 seconds
  • Chance: 1 in 3

docs.title: Haste
docs.text:
Haste

"Grants +10% player movespeed for 20 seconds. Stacks up to 10 times."

  • Cooldown: 4.5 seconds
  • Chance: 1 in 3

docs.title: Passive: Combined Forces
docs.text:
While Crimbolt Bee is in your hive, you get:

  • +20% Instant Red, Blue and White Conversion
  • +5% Critical Chance
  • +100% Critical Power
  • +5% Honey Per Pollen
  • +35% Defense Piercing

docs.title: Passive: Trio (Gifted only)
docs.text: While gathering, a Gifted Crimbolt Bee has an independent 33% chance every 4.5 seconds to spawn a Red, Blue and White Boost token together. This doesn't lower its other ability chances.

docs.title: Crimbolt Flame and Crimbolt's Heat
docs.text:
Every flower a Crimbolt Rocket hits spawns a Crimbolt Flame. It works like a normal Flame, collecting pollen every second, but:

  • It lasts 6 seconds (longer with flame duration bonuses).
  • It is red, white and blue.
  • It can never turn into a Dark Flame.
  • Standing near it gives Crimbolt's Heat instead of Flame Heat.

Crimbolt's Heat fills up while you stand near your own Crimbolt Flames, up to 20 seconds. It fills twice as fast as Flame Heat, and more flames fill it faster. Its bonuses grow as it fills. At a full 20 seconds it gives:

  • x2 Red, Blue and White Pollen
  • x2 Super-Crit Power
  • +5% Super-Crit Chance

Crimbolt's Heat and Flame Heat are separate buffs, so you can have both. It is lost when you leave the game. See Critical Hits for how Super-Crits work.

docs.title: How to obtain
docs.text:
• Sun Bear's 15th Crimbolt quest, "Crimbolt's Final Test", gives a Crimbolt Bee Egg. See Crimbolt Quests.
  • Rebirth 34 rewards a Crimbolt Bee Egg. See Rebirths.

Hatching the egg also gives a Crimbolt Bee Jelly, which turns any bee into a Crimbolt Bee. Like other Event bees, it can be made Gifted with a Star Treat.

The game also has a Gifted Crimbolt Bee Egg, but nothing gives it yet. No shop, code or Robux pack sells any Crimbolt item.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The only difference between Crimson Bee and Cobalt Bee's field preferences is that the Crimson Bee likes the Rose Field, whereas Cobalt Bee prefers the Pine Tree Forest.

docs.title: Critical Hits
docs.text:
This piece of content recently got an update.

We are in the process of catching up to the game. Please feel free to help us by updating the following information: The #Trivia stats need updating.

Critical Hits are moments of increased pollen collection and attack damage, doubled at its base power. Their frequency is increased with higher Critical Chance, and their strength is increased by greater Critical Power. A critical hit's pollen or damage number shows 1.25 times larger, similar to the animation below. Some critical hits become even stronger Super-Crits.

+5,627!

The animation of a critical hit for pollen.

-1,139

The animation of a critical hit when attacking.

You can see the stats for all critical hit statistics in the System Page.

docs.title: How critical hits work
docs.text:
• Base values: Critical Chance starts at 0% and Critical Power at x2. Bonuses to both are added together, then any multipliers are applied. There is no cap, so 100% Critical Chance makes every hit a crit.
  • When the game rolls:
    • A scoop, a bee gathering, or a bee ability makes one roll for the whole collection, and every flower in it shares the result.
    • Pollen collected one flower at a time, such as walking over flowers, rolls once per flower.
    • Attacks roll once per hit.
  • Pollen: a crit multiplies the pollen collected by Critical Power.
  • Attacks: a crit multiplies the damage by Critical Power.
  • Melittology adds these pollen-only bonuses after the normal stats:
    • Upgrade Focus: +2% Critical Chance per Focus stack, up to +40%.
    • Critical Edge (tool pollen only): +25% Critical Chance and x2 Critical Power.
    • Critical Abilities (bee abilities, not bombs): +5% Critical Chance and x1.5 Critical Power.
    • Ability Ascension (bee abilities, not bombs): +10% Critical Chance.
    • Precision Conversion: 20% extra instant conversion on crits (not bomb crits).

docs.title: Critical Chance
docs.text: Critical Chance is the chance of a hit being critical hit. The player can see how much their Critical Chance is by looking for the Critical Chance stat in the System Page. Critical Chance can be improved by a variety of ways such as ability tokens, guards, and inventory items.

docs.title: Tokens
docs.text:
• Focus gives +3% Critical Chance per token and caps at +30% Critical Chance from 10 tokens.
  • Precise Mark from the Target Practice ability gives +7% Critical Chance per token and caps at +21% Critical Chance from three Marks.
  • The Tabby Blessing buff, granted from collecting Tabby Love while having maximum Tabby Love stacks, grants +1% Critical Chance.

docs.title: Gifted Hive Bonuses
docs.text: • Gifted Commander Bee gives +3% Critical Chance.

docs.title: Beequips
docs.text:

  • A Charm Bracelet gives from +1% Critical Chance to +14% Critical Chance.
  • A Bang Snap gives from +1% Critical Chance to +3% Critical Chance. Using waxes can increase the amount up to +23% Critical Chance.
  • Pink Shades can give from +22% Critical Chance to +26% Critical Chance. Using waxes can increase the amount up to +50% Critical Chance.
  • A Beesmas Top gives from +5% Critical Chance to +10% Critical Chance. Using waxes can increase the amount up to +20% Critical Chance.
  • A Beesmas Tree Hat gives from +2% Critical Chance to +5% Critical Chance. Using waxes can increase the amount up to +10% Critical Chance.
  • A Snow Tiara gives +1% Critical Chance.
  • A Toy Drum gives +1% Critical Chance.

docs.title: Super-Crit
docs.text:
A Super-Crit is a stronger critical hit. Whenever a hit is already a crit, the game makes a second roll against Super-Crit Chance, so the real chance of a Super-Crit is Critical Chance × Super-Crit Chance. A Super-Crit number shows in purple with a violet outline, 1.5 times larger, and shimmers before it fades.

+28,140!!

The animation of a Super-Crit.

docs.title: How Super-Crits work
docs.text:
• Base values: Super-Crit Chance starts at 0% and Super-Crit Power at x2, with no cap.
  • Pollen: Super-Crit Power multiplies on top of Critical Power, so with base stats a Super-Crit collects x4 pollen (x2 × x2). All of a Super-Crit's pollen is converted to honey instantly.
  • Attacks: only a third of the extra Super-Crit Power applies, using Critical Power × (1 + (Super-Crit Power − 1) / 3). With base stats a Super-Crit hit does about x2.67 damage.
  • Super-Crits roll at the same times as crits: once per scoop, gathering or ability, once per flower when walking, and once per hit when attacking.
Pollen Attack damage Normal x1 x1 Crit (base) x2 x2 Super-Crit (base) x4, converted instantly x2.67

docs.title: Super-Crit Chance
docs.text:
Super-Crit Chance is how often a critical hit becomes a Super-Crit. It can be raised by:

  • Bees
    • Precise Bee: +3% Super-Crit Chance, and another +3% when Gifted.
  • Buffs
    • Precise Mark (from Precise Bee's ability): +7% Super-Crit Chance and +7% Critical Chance per stack, up to 3 stacks (+21%).
    • Precision: +2% Super-Crit Chance per stack, up to 10 stacks (+20%) for 60 seconds.
    • Crimbolt's Heat (Crimbolt Bee): +0% to +5% Super-Crit Chance, higher the more time the buff has left.
    • Super Smoothie: +1%.
    • Tabby Blessing+: +1% (also +1% Critical Chance and +25% Critical Power).
    • Galentine's Blessing: +1%.
    • Console Launch Boost (event buff): +1%.
    • Bloxiade (Retro Challenge only): +1% (also +5% Critical Chance).
  • Beequips
    • Six-Point Shuriken: +15% to +20%, plus +1% to +2% per wax upgrade (up to 12).
    • Demon Talisman: +5% to +10%, plus +2% per wax upgrade (up to 10).
    • Pink Shades: +10% to +15%, more from wax upgrades, and +1% from Caustic Wax.
  • Robo Bear Challenge
    • Bruteforce (Legendary): +6% Super-Crit Chance and x1.25 Red pollen.
  • Other
    • Violet petals from blooms: +5%, growing slightly with each stack.
    • Gummy Globe ornament on the Beesmas Tree: +1%.

docs.title: Super-Crit Power
docs.text:
Super-Crit Power is how strong a Super-Crit is. It can be raised by:

  • Buffs
    • Dark Heat (from the Dark Scythe and Honey Hammer): x1.05 Super-Crit Power per stack, up to 100 stacks.
    • Crimbolt's Heat (Crimbolt Bee): x1 to x2 Super-Crit Power, higher the more time the buff has left.
  • Beequips
    • Six-Point Shuriken: +75% to +110%, plus +7% to +10% per wax upgrade (up to 12).
    • Pink Shades: Super-Crit Power from wax upgrades.
    • Demon Talisman: +2% hive bonus per Caustic Wax (up to 5).
    • Whistle, Kazoo (+1%) and Camo Bandana (+1%): Super-Crit Power hive bonuses from Caustic Wax.
  • Amulets
    • Diamond Cog Amulet: +10% to +15% (one of its random stats).
    • Supreme Cog Amulet: +15% to +25% (one of its random stats).
  • Robo Bear Challenge
    • Pseudo-RNG (Legendary): x1.25 Super-Crit Power, +3% Critical Chance and x2 Clover Field pollen.
  • Stickers in the Sticker Stack, +1% each: Purple 4-Point Flower, Stretched Head Bear, Squashed Head Bear, Royal Bear, Purple Fleuron, Precise Eye and Royal Symbol.
  • Other
    • Bread Climp ornament on the Beesmas Tree: +5%.

No tool raises Super-Crit stats by itself, and no Melittology node changes them.

docs.title: Cub Buddy
docs.text:
A Cub Buddy is a small, baby version of a bear that follows the player around, collects tokens, and creates gifts. Whenever the player's cub buddy gets too far away, it will teleport back to them.

Cub buddies have settings that can be accessed and viewed through the Cub Console, which is located on the System Page.

When the player's cub buddy produces items, it dances, emits heart particles, and an in-game message will pop up, saying:

🐻(Cub Buddy Name) made some gifts!

docs.title: Cub Console
docs.text:
The Cub Console can be accessed by clicking on the green Cub Console button under the options menu, and allows the player to customize and check their Cub Buddy. The player can equip or unequip their Cub Buddy, modify its name, and view its statistics.

If the player has a Cub Buddy, they may rename it by clicking on the "Name" window, typing in the desired name, and pressing enter. This name is subject to filtering, and may be rejected by the system.

Cub Buddies age depending on how long it has been equipped while the player is in-game. If it is at the age of newborn, that means that it has been equipped for less than an hour. Once it has been equipped for more than one hour, the Cub Console will measure its age in hours. Once it has been equipped for more than 24 hours, the Cub Console will measure its age in days and hours. Once it has been equipped for more than 3 days, the Cub Console will no longer measure its age in hours. Instead, the Cub Console will solely measure its age in weeks and days. Once it has been equipped for more than 4 weeks, the Cub Console will measure its age in months and weeks.

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• Redeeming a Cub Buddy Voucher by:
  • Purchasing in the Robux Shop for 600 Robux.
  • An unfathomably rare reward from Robo Bear's Challenge.
  • Trading with other players.

docs.title: Cub Skins
docs.text:
• Obtainable by completing 300 Brown Bear quests (gives the Brown Bear Cub skin).
  • Obtainable by collecting 250,000 Cogs, beating Round 25 in Robo Bear Challenge, or placing Top 10 on the Daily Top Robo Bear Challenge Scores (gives the Robo Cub skin).
  • Obtainable by placing Top 50 on the Daily Stick Bug score leaderboard or as a drop from Stick Bug (Unbelievably Rare) (gives the Stick Cub skin).
  • For the end of challenge reward, the odds vary from around 1 in 25,000 (10 million score) to around 1 in 670 (over 1,000,000,000 score) [1]
  • Obtainable by sticking all 12 Star Signs to the Sticker Stack, rolling it from the Sticker Printer, or from purchasing a Diamond Star Amulet (1 in 1,000,000 chance) (gives the Star Cub skin).

docs.title: Possible Gift Rewards
docs.text:
Cub buddies will produce gifts in a ring of 5 tokens, which usually contain common items like Treats, but can also produce rarer items like tickets or Royal Jellies. When a cub buddy starts to dance and heart particles appear above its head, that means it's about to produce some gifts. Cub buddies produce gifts every 1–5 minutes. Similar to sprouts and leaves, the rewards granted by cub buddies typically depend on the field the player stands in (e.g. getting 3 sunflower seeds while standing in the Sunflower Field).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• While Bee Bear said that the cub buddies are dolls animated by "Beesmas magic," Polar Bear said, "He says the [Cub Buddies] are animated by the magic of Beesmas... But in reality, Bee Bear had to build and program them himself.” Also, Science Bear said, "They're just robots, you know. But they're so lifelike, it's uncanny!"
  • If the player bought the Cub Buddy Launch Pack, and then completed Bee Bear's 10th quest, the player was rewarded with 250 tickets since the player can only have one of each cub buddy skin.
  • If the process is reversed, the player will instead be rewarded with 250 tickets in addition to the 250 tickets that they would normally get for a total of 500 tickets and the Noob Cub skin for purchasing the pack.
  • When the player gets their first cub buddy, it will automatically be named "Buddy".
  • A cub buddy uses the wave emote when idle, the point emote when collecting a token, the dance emote before it produces gifts, and the cheer emote when it makes the gifts.
  • Most cub buddies use the Cartoony Animation Package. The Brown Cub, Snow Cub, Robo Cub, Peppermint Robo Cub, Petal Cub, and Gloomy Cub are the only cubs to use a different one, being the Knight Animation Package, the Ninja Animation Package and Robot Animation Package, Stylish Animation Package, and Elder Animation Package respectively.
  • Coincidentally, the Cartoony Animation Package is the one used by Black Bear, Noob Bear, and Bee Bear.
  • There used to be a glitch that would make cub buddies "wear" an item if they teleported on top of it, such as the Demon Mask, Elite Blue Guard, and Riley Guard. This could also happen if the owner died/reset on top of the cub buddy. This was because the cub buddy is a Humanoid Model. This Glitch was patched in an unknown update.
  • There is a glitch that causes cub buddies to stay in the game after their owners leave. The cub buddy can still collect any public tokens when it is left in the game, but it doesn't give the rewards to their owner.
  • Cub buddies used to be the most expensive item in the Ticket Tent, costing 2,000 tickets.
  • The maximum number of characters in a cub buddy name is 16. The name can also be filtered by Roblox.
  • Although a cub buddy can collect any token, either the player's or public, it cannot collect its own gifts it made unless it picks up a Token Link.
  • All of the cub skins except for the Gingerbread Bear, Doodle, Peppermint Robo, and the Gloomy Cub skin are based on their original NPC/mob counterpart.
  • However, the Gingerbread cub skin looks like a bigger and more elaborate version of a Gingerbread Bear, and the Peppermint Robo cub is a reskin of the normal Robo cub.
  • The Doodle cub fits the sticker update, and goes with the Doodle Hive skin too.
  • Bee Bear has stated that a Snow Cub’s favorite treat is Basic Eggs.
  • Cub buddies are affected by the player's Haste stacks.
  • The Robo Cub skin is the first of 3 skins to have 2 ways to be obtained, the other two being the Stick Cub and Star Cub, added in the same update.
  • It is also the first skin to have 3 ways of obtainment.
  • The Peppermint Robo Cub next to Bee Bear is the only NPC that does an emote originating from the Roblox catalog. The emote it does is the Robot.

  • Rarely, a special gift will be made, always consisting of 1 Tropical Drink, 1 Enzymes, 1 Red Extract, 1 Blue Extract, and 1 Oil.

docs.title: Dandelion Field
docs.text:
Dandelion Field

FIELD COLOR

White

BEE PREREQUISITES

None

NECTAR TYPE

Comforting Nectar

FIELD DIMENSIONS

36 × 18 flowers

FLOWER COUNT

648

BEE PREFERENCES

LIKE

DISLIKE

The Dandelion Field is one of the five starting fields any player is able to visit upon starting the game. There are no mobs that protect this field.

This field can produce honey, red boost, blue boost, ticket, glue, glitter, magic bean, and treat tokens when collecting pollen.

Item Drops list Treat (20% Chance)

Glue (0.01% Chance) Magic Bean (0.0059% Chance) Glitter (0.005% Chance)

Bees that like the Dandelion Field are Baby Bee, Bomber Bee, Demo Bee, Exhausted Bee, Music Bee, Stubborn Bee, Windy Bee, Fuzzy Bee, and Digital Bee. Bees that dislike the Dandelion Field are Commander Bee, Brave Bee, and Vicious Bee.

This field gives Comforting Nectar when a planter is placed here.

A level 1-5 Wild Windy Bee can spawn here.

This is an 18x36 field, containing 648 flowers. The flowers are white, red, and blue, in sizes of single and double.

Flowers White Red Blue Total Single 468 72.25% 28 4.25% 55 8.5% 551 85% Double 83 12.75% 5 0.75% 10 1.5% 97 15% Triple 0 0% 0 0% 0 0% 0 0% Total 551 85% 32 5% 65 10% 648 100%

Note: flower counts within the table may vary due to rounding. Additionally, in game, all flowers are randomly generated and may not precisely align with the percentages.

docs.title: Obtaining Boosts
docs.text:
• Using the Field Booster may give a Dandelion Field Boost. When it does, it will give +300% Dandelion Field pollen for 15 minutes.
  • Using glitter in the field will add 100% Dandelion Field pollen onto the current boost if it isn't already maxed out.
  • Using field dice, smooth dice, or loaded dice may add +100%-300% Dandelion Field pollen for 15 minutes based on the dice used if the current boost isn't already maxed out.
  • Dandelion Field Winds can be obtained through the Wind Shrine or codes. They have a base of 20% instant Dandelion Field conversion and give +5% instant Dandelion Field conversion and +25% Dandelion Field pollen for each stack. Dandelion Field Winds can stack up to a total of 13 times.
  • Redeeming certain valid codes:
  • PlushFriday (Gives Dandelion Field Code Buff + other stuff).
  • It can be boosted by the Shell Amulet. If it has a Dandelion Field Boost, it can boost the field by +5% to +30% depending on the amulet rarity.

docs.title: The methods below are no longer possible.
docs.text:
• Giving presents to certain NPCs:
  • Mother Bear gave Dandelion Field Boost x5 and other items.
  • Onett gave Dandelion Field Boost x1 and other boosts and items.
  • Mother Bear gave x3 Dandelion Field Boost and other items.
  • Redeeming certain expired codes:
  • AccentMaster (Gave Dandelion Field Boost x1 + other stuff).
  • Sure (Gives Dandelion Field Boost x3 + other stuff).
  • Wink (Gives Dandelion Field Boost x7 + other stuff).
  • Afternoon (Gave Dandelion Field Boost x5 + other stuff).
  • NikTacAttack (Gave Dandelion Field Boost x5 + other stuff).
  • Noobasha+ (Gave Dandelion Field Boost x6 + other stuff).
  • SunBearSendoff (Gave Dandelion Field Boost x6 + other stuff).
  • Waiting (Gave Dandelion Field Boost x6 + other stuff).
  • SDMittens1T (Gave Dandelion Field Boost x3 + other stuff).
  • Crafty (Gave Dandelion Field Boost x4 + other stuff).
  • RebootCode (Gave Dandelion Field Boost x5 + other stuff).
  • Breeze (Gave Dandelion Field Boost x3 + other stuff).
  • TornadoGlitch (Gave Dandelion Field Boost x3 and Dandelion Field Winds x3 + other stuff).
  • WindyWeekend (Gave Dandelion Field Boost x1 and Dandelion Field Winds x3 + other stuff).
  • BeesmasBegins (Gave Dandelion Field Boost x3 and Dandelion Field Winds x6 + other stuff).
  • FestiveFinale (Gave Dandelion Field Boost x3 and Dandelion Field Winds x4 + other stuff).
  • SpaceReboot (Gave Dandelion Field Boost x3 and Dandelion Field Capacity x3 + other stuff).
  • RebootFriday (Gave Dandelion Field Code Buff + other stuff).
  • Purchasing a Dandelion Field Market Boost from the Boost Market gave 1.25x Dandelion Field Pollen along with x1.5 Dandelion Field Capacity, +10% Bee Ability Rate, and x1.25 Convert Rate At Hive.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Before the 2019-09-28 update, the Dandelion Field was the only field that was mob-proof, meaning no mobs could spawn/attack there.
  • There is a royal jelly token on top of the tallest dandelion which can be obtained by using the Parachute/Glider with cannons or from a high place.
  • This is also the only dandelion in the field that has collision at its top.
  • The Bubble Wand model on the Blue HQ can grow a face and blow sparkles onto this field, along with the Mushroom Field, Clover Field, and Blue Flower Field.
  • The All-Time Top Honeymakers Leaderboard is adjacent to the Dandelion Field.
  • There used to be a glitch where Stick Bug could fall from the tallest mushroom and land in the Dandelion Field. This has now been patched.
  • During the Ready Player Two event, the field can be seen glitching after using the Computer.
  • Onett threatens to remove every field but the Dandelion Field if the bees and bears don't stop complaining in his Star Journey 2 quest dialogue. He then follows this up stating he wouldn't really do this though.

docs.title: Dapper Bear's Shop
docs.text:
Dapper Bear's Shop Location Past the Brave Bee Gate, near the Stump Field.

Dapper Bear's Shop is a shop located behind the Brave Bee Gate. Located on a hilltop, the player is able to access the shop by jumping between ledges to climb the hill. The shop sells reusable Planters and 6 beequips, with the 3rd, 4th, 5th, and 6th beequips requiring you to complete a certain number of Dapper Bear's quests in order to unlock them. You also have to pay honey and tickets for each beequip with the amounts scaling from the quality of the beequip. This is also where Dapper Bear is located.

To enter Dapper Bear's Shop, the player must be equipped with the Propeller Hat and the Hiking Boots, or any hat and boots of higher quality. If the player approaches wearing gear of a lower tier (such as the Helmet, Strange Goggles, or Basic Boots), a red barrier will block entry and display the message: You Must Wear a Nice Hat and Cool Boots to enter Dapper Bear's Shop.

The shop has a tan interior with a blue floor and ceiling, as well as two windows in the front. Above the entrance is an image of a Beequip Case. On the left side of the interior, there is the Beequip shop and the Highest Damage to a Single Puffshroom leaderboard. On the right side of the shop is the Planter shop. The roof of the shop has a Royal Jelly token, 25 Honeysuckles, 3 Smooth Dice and a Bloom Shaker.

The shop has an obstacle course on the right side of the shop that leads up to the roof. It splits up into two paths: a rocky wall and a moon obby. The rocky wall allows access the roof, where a royal jelly and a honeysuckle token are hidden. The moon obby leads to a Star Jelly on a platform behind the shop. It is also possible to bypass the obby by using a Glider.

As of the time of writing, during every Beesmas since 2021, Dapper Bear's Samovar is located next to the shop entrance. In many Beesmas events since, Gift Boxes were also placed on the roof, or near the shop in some capacity.

docs.title: Beequip Shop
docs.text:
The Beequip Shop sells Beequips in 6 slots. Each slot shows one beequip and can be bought once per refresh. Every player sees the same offers, because each slot rolls from a seed based on the slot and the current refresh window.

Slot Refreshes every Unlocks after 1 2 hours Always open 2 4 hours Always open 3 4 hours 5 Dapper Bear quests 4 8 hours 10 Dapper Bear quests 5 8 hours 15 Dapper Bear quests 6 24 hours 20 Dapper Bear quests

When a slot refreshes, it picks one beequip at random, with equal odds, from the beequips allowed in that slot. Its potential is then a random half-star step within that beequip's range for the slot, with equal odds for each step.

docs.title: Prices
docs.text:
The price depends on the beequip and its potential. With q = potential ÷ 5:

  • Honey = min × (max ÷ min)q, rounded to 2 significant digits. Honey cost rises exponentially with potential.
  • Tickets = min + (max − min) × q, rounded. Ticket cost rises in a straight line.

For example, a 2.5★ Bottle Cap (q = 0.5) costs about 2.5M × 10000.5 ≈ 79M Honey and 18 Tickets.

Dapper Bear is a quest giver, and one of the eight permanent quest Bears that can be accessed in the game, the others being Black Bear, Brown Bear, Mother Bear, Panda Bear, Science Bear, Polar Bear and Spirit Bear. Dapper Bear is located inside his shop next to Stump Field.

Inside Dapper Bear's shop, he sells many different planters ranging from750K-100T Honey (alongside crafting materials). He also sells many different types of Beequips for Honey and Tickets, with some being locked behind a certain amount of Dapper Bear Quests completed.

After speaking with him, Dapper Bear rewards the player 3 Ticket Planters and a Beequip Case (if the player does not already have one).

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: You need the following Accessories to enter Dapper Bear's shop, those being the Hiking Boots and the Propeller Hat. Players can also use gear that is better than the ones previously listed.

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
Dapper Bear currently has 16 Quests. His 16 main quests focus on collecting nectar, collecting tokens from planters, and popping Puffshrooms; with the exception of the 16th quest (added after the 2026-01-19 Update) which focuses mainly on stickers instead of the aforementioned. The quest for obtaining the Blue Drive in order to repair Robo Bear does still focus on Puffshrooms, planters, and nectar, however.

His 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 14th and 16th Quest rewards an additional Beequip Case slot. If you received Beequip Case slots from Bee Bear previously, you will instead be rewarded one Ticket Planters until you catch up to the amount of additional slots a new player would have.
