docs.title: Dialogue
docs.text: Currently, Dapper Bear has 15 quests that were added in Beesmas 2022, and 1 more added in the 2026-01-16 Update. However, more quests for him will be added upon further updates. Upon interacting with him, he will first give dialogue explaining Planters and a reward of Ticket Planters. Since the Beesmas 2022 update, a questline has been given to him. Dapper Bear gives plenty of information in his dialogues. Some of the information he gives is not found anywhere else in the game.

docs.title: Main Quests
docs.text:
Source Dialogue First interaction Hi, I like your hat, and your boots too. I guess you could call me snooty, but that's the only reason you got in. Appearances are everything, and our attire is more than skin deep. I take pride in how I present myself and my shop, in my own way. So much pride that you could call me Dapper Bear. I've set up shop here in hopes of meeting creative bears, beekeepers, and bees. Who aren't afraid to be a little bold, in a subtle sort of way... Tending towards an aesthetic sense to unlock our, hm, unique potentials. The mission is a little vague, but it should come together in time. For now, take this: A [Beequip Case]. With this, you can equip Beequips to your bees. Beequips are accessories your bees can wear to improve their stats, and even teach them new abilities. Every bee no matter how small or unassuming has the potential to stand out with the right Beequip. But I'll teach you all about that later. For now, I need to finish setting things up. But if you return throughout the Winter event, I'll have some quests for you. Feel free to take a look at my Planters, I'll teach you more about those later as well. Just know that the gist is, they're as helpful as they are neat looking. Sort of like me, and I'm guessing sort of like you. Place Planters on flower fields and they'll automatically grow over playtime. If you leave the game, the Planter will pause growing, but it will stay on the field and still be there when you return. As Planters grow, they store Pollen, prizes like Treats and crafting materials like Waxes, And of course, Nectar. Nectar is a special substance that grants temporary boosts to the honeymaking of your hive. By standing on a field with a Planter, your bees can visit it to sip Nectar. When they do, they gather a little bit of Nectar and help speed up the growth of the Planter. Placing Planters on different fields is essential to gathering materials and Nectar. But I'll have many quests to help explain it more in depth. For now, I'll also give you some [Ticket Planters] for you to test this out. Some Planters, like those [Ticket Planters] can only be harvested once. But all the Planters for sale in my shop can be reused endlessly. Now if you'll excuse me, I've got to keep prepping. Check in with you soon. Speaking to Dapper Bear before the main questline was added I’m still setting up shop, but I’ll have a lot more I want to talk with you about soon. For now, getting yourself aquainted with Beequips and Planters ought to be helpful. Here are a few pointers that ought to get you started:
  • Each Planter type is likely to give you a special reward the first time you harvest it, every once in a while
  • If you use [Glitter] on a field with a Planter, the Planter will grow 25% faster until you harvest it. This lasts even after the boost wears off.
  • Different types of Planters may give different rewards based on the Field you place them on.

Feel free to browse my selection of Planters. I’ll check in with you soon.

Planter Practice Place a Planter in a field and it'll grow as you play. Once its [sic] done growing, you can harvest it to collect a variety of rewards. The rewards you get change depending on the Planter you used and the field you planted it in. But one of the rewards will always be a type of Nectar - special buffs that'll be a real help. When it comes to Planters, experimentation and patience are key. Try them out yourself and you'll see what I mean. Collect 1 hour of Nectar... Collect 25 tokens from Planters... And collect 2,000,000 pollen from the Pineapple Patch.

-During-

Planters take a while, but that patience pays off.

-Completion-

Planter growth is slow, but steady and constant. Kinda like me, and my shop, and you... and your Beequip Case. Every time you complete 2 of my quests, I'll expand you case with a [Beequip Case Slot]. Each one allows you [to] equip an additional bee with a Beequip. Every time you complete 5 of my quests, my shop will expand to offer more Beequips at once. The Beequips I have in stock constantly cycle, so you ought to check in periodically. The ones I have in stock now aren't the best quality... and they aren't super rare. But as you complete more of my quests, my inventory will improve. For now, take this [Ticket Planter]. I do appreciate the help.

Liquid Motivation My shop is a reflection of myself, full of stuff that's swayed me. Caught my eye. Whenever I feel stagnant, like I'm just roaming around without direction, I try to seek motivation in unexpected places. Over the years, I've found it in all kinds of things: like little knick knacks from around the world, outdated Planter pots... Stuff other people might overlook or even toss into the trash. With an open mind and observant eye, the most peculiar things can inspire you. But when I'm really stuck in a rut, there's always Motivating Nectar. Motivating Nectar grants bonus Blue Pollen, Convert Rate, and Bee Ability Rate. Bee Ability Rate makes you bees spawn their ability tokens more often. You can collect Motivating Nectar from Planters in the Mushroom, Spider, Stump, and Rose Fields. For this next quest, give Motivating Nectar and try for yourself. It'll perk you and your bees right up.

-During-

Ever wake up feeling like you don't even want to get out of bed? Well, before you brew a cup of coffee, why not give Motivating Nectar a try? I love coffee but Nectar is way healthier for your bees. Collect Motivating Nectar from Planters in the Mushroom, Spider, Stump, and Rose Fields.

-Completion-

With all that Motivating Nectar, you must be feeling pretty inspired. What'll you do next? Join a book club? Paint a painting? Hit the gym? Heh. I don't think Motivating Nectar works that way. But it might give you the push you need to complete more of my quests. Each one will require you to collect even more Nectar. To do that, you need to know the nuances of Planters. For example, when you stand in the same field as a Planter, your bees will sometimes sip Nectar from it. When they do, they speed up the growth of the Planter by a small amount. Basically, if you want a Planter to grow faster, standing near it will help. But for now, take this [Beequip Case Slot] as a token of my appreciation. It'll allow you to equip an additional bee with a Beequip. When you're ready, feel free to stop by again. I have more work for you, if you're willing.

A Good Infection Hi. Have you happened to plant one of those [Ticket Planters] yet? If so, did you notice how the bulb started to smoke when it finished growing? Well that "smoke" isn't actually smoke. It's the spores of a Puffshroom. Puffshrooms are a type of mushroom that sometimes infect fully grown Planters. But they're not a bad thing. They're, hm... a good type of infection. When you collect pollen near a Puffshroom, the Puffshroom fills up. When it's completely full, it'll pop and spawns [sic] some rewards, like [Bitterberries] and Wax. It may also spawn more spores, which can spread to different fields. If you find a Puffshroom, you should try popping it. It'll take you on a short adventure. For this next quest, you'll need to pop 25 Puffshrooms. If you don't have any [Ticket Planters] left, don't worry[,] a Puffshroom spawns automatically on a random field twice every hour.

-During-

You can collect Invigorating Nectar from the following fields: Clover Field, Cactus Field, Mountain Top Field, and the Pepper Patch. And if you're having trouble finding Puffshrooms, they spawn twice an hour. 15 minutes past the hour, and 45 minutes past the hour, on a random field. And if you're looking for bubbles, well, try to find someone who has Bubble Bee or Tadpole Bees. You don't have to make the bubbles yourself - you just have to pop them.

-Completion-

Puffshrooms spread like crazy. It can get a bit chaotic. But they won't last for long. Around 5 minutes at most. They're the best source for Waxes, which are useful for upgrading Beequips. To use a Wax: Just drag it from your Eggs Menu to the hive slot of the bee holding the Beequip you want to upgrade. But keep in mind, it may not always work out in your favor. [Soft Wax will always provide a minor buff to a Beequip but [Hard Wax] will only work 60% of the time. When it does though, it provides twice as much of a buff as [Soft Wax]. [Caustic Wax] is the flakiest wax of all... It works 25% of the time, and if it fails, it destroys your Beequip. Why would you ever use [Caustic Wax] huh? Well, because it grants the best bonuses. Some stats, hive bonuses, and even abilities can only be unlocked by using a [Caustic Wax]. Just something to keep in mind. For now, you'll probably want to use your Waxes to purchase other things, like the Planters I'm selling. Upgrading Beequips can come later.

All About Appearances I might come off as a bit pretentious compared to other bears. Maybe that's just my self-consciousness coming around. Could be a defense mechanism, who knows. Cultivating myself, my tastes, and my appearance is how I tackle my insecurities. So much of who you are is what you're perceived to be. That's why how we look and what we wear is so important. Have you wondered how Beequips improve the stats of your bees? My theory's that it's pretty much all in their heads. A well-dressed bee can tell they're looking sharp. Maybe even a little intimidating. That bit of pizzazz helps them overcome their own self-doubt. Gives them an edge over the others. Buuut on the other hand, bees so seem pretty simple. For this next quest, let's experiment with Beequips. It'll help inform the direction I'll steer my shop. Find some Beequips you like, equip them to your bees, and try upgrading them with [Soft Waxes]. Here are some tips before you go: For a bee to equip a Beequip, the bee's level must be greater than or equal to the Beequip's level. Some Beequips also have other equip requirements, like a certain bee color or type. A Beequips [sic] "limit" lets you know how many Beequips of that type you can equip to your hive at once. Hope that helps. Good luck out there.

-During-

Hey there. Just a reminder: Satisfying Nectar can be obtained in the Sunflower Field, Pineapple Patch, and Pumpkin Patch. And if you're having trouble finding Waxes, try popping some Puffshrooms.

-Completion-

Your bees are looking pretty fresh! See what a little accessorizing can do? I don't think anyones [sic] actually looks bad by nature. They're just got to find a look that works for them. For some bees, all it takes is a [Paperclip] taped to their head. Fashion is strange. Always 10 steps ahead of what you'd think people'd [sic] like. Anyways, here's a [Beequip Case Slot] so you can spruce up yet another bee. Oh, and how about some Planter wisdom for you before you go: If you notice the plant growing in one of your planters is turning brown... That means the field has been depleted. A field becomes depleted if you grow too many Planters on it in a short time. Brown Planters grow way slower than green ones, and you don't want that. But don't worry, the field will naturally regenerate over a couple days. Until then, try placing your Planters in different fields. Just something to keep in mind going forward.

Means of Mutation You're quite observant. At least you come off that way. So I take it you're beginning to understand how this all works, I'll always give you a quest that involves collecting Nectar, with a few other tasks thrown in. Often times I'll need you to pop Puffshrooms. Sometimes you gotta collect or use various items. I'm sort of living vicariously through you. Seeking inspiration through your perspective. I'm not a beekeeper, but I like what you all do. And at the same time, well, the resources you collect are helping me expand my shop. After every quest, I'll reward you with either a [Beequip Case Slot] or a [Ticket Planter][,] In addition to some other little things I have on hand. And here's where it gets interesting: Every 5th quest, I'll have an advanced challenge for you. Completing these challenges will increase the number of Beequips I sell at once in my shop. And they'll also reward some, hmmm, special bonuses. For example, if you complete this next quest, I'll give you a [Star Jelly]. It's definitely difficult, but I can tell you're cut out for it. I mean, just look at you. Those are [sic] eyes are full of determination. Or something else, who knows. Now before you go: this quest requires you to give a bee a Mutation. You can do that by feeding [Bitterberries] to your bees. But it's not very likely unless you make them radioactive first. Feeding a [Neonberry] to a bee turns it radioactive for a short while, which greatly increases the chance of mutations.

-During-

[Neonberries] are pretty hard to come by, but Puffshrooms are a pretty reliable source. This entire quest is a doozy, though. You'll work it out.

-Completion-

This boutique is starting to come together. It's blossoming into a place with a particular yet distinguished character. And that's primarily thanks to you and your bees. When I first opened, I had some doubts. I mean, I second guess myself a lot. But this was a big move for me. I've lived around the world, from Toronto to Tokyo. But I wasn't sure if the residents of a smaller place like this would slick with my sensibilities. Having someone like you around does help. So thanks. I'd like you [to] take this [Star Jelly], in addition to some other things. From now on, I'll also offer 3 Beequips at a time in my shop. We seem to share a vision. Minds in sync like that - they're hard to come by. I'm hoping we can keep a good things going. If you complete 5 more quests, I'll even give you a [Diamond Egg]. Not that I'm trying to buy your friendship with eggs. Well, you can see it that way if you want to. Check in with you soon.

Creative Comforts Running a shop is a lot of work. By the end of the day I get pretty pooped. And when you're worn out, it's tempting to crawl to the comforts of bad habits. Just laying around, snacking, scrolling through videos for hours on end... Boy it's hard to resist, ain't it? But you probably won't cultivate a unique perspective from such passive behavior. At least, not if that's all you do. Or if you do it, uh, uncritically. Basically, you don't forge new things when you're too comfortable. So when I'm stressed out, I try not to give in. Instead, I allow myself a little Comforting Nectar. Comforting Nectar increases your Convert Rate when you're back at the hive. It'll help you empty your backpack or hive balloon faster, but not while in a field. It doesn't affect abilities that scale with regular Convert Rate like Honey Marks or Coin Scatter. Next time you're feeling stressed, try working on this quest. While you're farming, maybe listen to some new music. You could play with friends. Consider the most optimal ways to complete the tasks. Hopefully that'll do more good than sinking into social media. Questionable, but maybe. I'm not a psychologist or anything. Just thinking out loud.

-During-

The [Candy Planter] is the most reliable source of [Gumdrops], as far as Planters go. It's a bit expensive, but it's worth the investment. Planting [Candy Planters] on the Blue Flower Field, Strawberry Field, and Pineapple Patch... Has a chance to grant extra [Gumdrops]. And any type of Planter on the Stump Field also got some increased [Gumdrops] odds.

-Completion-

At first, the rewards you get from Planters seem random. Once you're gotten more familiar with them, however, there's some rhyme to their reason. Different Planters are more likely to grant different items[,] and the types of items they grant are influenced by the fields you place them on. Some Planters, when grown on specific fields, grant better rewards. By playing around with different combinations you can grow some good stuff. For now, here's another [Beequip Case Slot]! Use it to equip another bee with a Beequip, then check back in with me.

Keeping It Chromatic At the start of spring in India they celebrate a festival called Holi. People throw around vibrantly colored powders while they celebrate and dance. When I visited, it really struck me how colorful the place was in general. Loved it. I'm a huge proponent of keeping things colorful. I figure that by making my surroundings vibrant and chromatic some of that vibrancy will seep into me. Maybe subconsciously. Then the things I do and create might also become more vivid and varied. Different colors, different flavors, different sensations, etc. They provide the contrasts and the, hmm, juxtapositions that keep life interesting. That's part of why I enjoy collecting a wide array of colorful Planters. Not only do they look different, they each help collect different types of Nectar. If I get tired of one, I just cycle out to another to keeps [sic] things fresh. But I rarely ever throw a Planter out. They call have their purposes. For example... The [Tacky Planter], when grown on the Pumpkin Patch, will likely give you a [Swirled Wax]. When grown on the [Bamboo Field], it's got a good chance to give you a [Caustic Wax]. These drops are almost guaranteed to happen once a month. Additionally... There are certain Beequips that the [Tacky Planter] can reward that other Planters will not. So even if you've upgraded to, say, the [Petal Planter] it's still worthwhile to use a [Tacky Planter] every now and then. Just like with the colors I decorate with, and the things I wear, I always try to keep mixing it up. Let's work on that with this quest.

-During-

Making much progress? In case you've forgotten, Refreshing Nectar can be obtained from the following fields: the Blue Flower Field, the Strawberry Field, and the Coconut Field.

-Completion-

You have fun out there? Hmm... Getting Rare Puffshrooms to grow on specific fields can be a challenge, huh. Higher level puffshrooms are more likely to be rare, so keep that in mind. Puffshrooms are more likely to level up when the spore travels to a different field. And when a puffshroom spore is the first of it's lineage to land on a field It should level up even more. On the other hand, if it lands in the same field as the one you just popped The Puffshroom might reduce in level. Chase Puffshrooms to different fields to level them up After that, juggle them around the specific field you're targeting. But you're already starting to get the hang of it. You're smart, right? Well, here's some stuff to make up for all the thing I just had you use. Hope you enjoy! Check in with you again soon.

Wandering Ambition How do we broaden our minds? Is it all about learning new stuff? Hmm... I'm not sure you can expand your mind through obtaining knowledge alone. I think you've got to experience new stuff - feel new feelings. To step out of your own shoes and into some shoes you never imagined you'd wear. But how do you do that, huh? Where do you even start? Throw a dart at a map and just go where it lands? Drop out of school? Quit your job? How far do you have to go? Questions like this have kept me wandering and searching. Searching for what exactly? I dunno. I want to break free and to carve my own path. To do something truly new. Something great and grand. Maybe that's too much to ask. But hopefully setting up this shop is a step in that journey.

-During-

Here's a tip for farming [Neonberries]: Plant the [Pesticide Planter] on the Stump Field, Mountain Top Field, and Coconut Field in that order. The specific chain produces a larger yield of [Neonberries]. But you have to grow it fully each step. In general, the [Pesticide Planter] on those fields produce more [Neonberries]. But once a week, if you collect it at full growth and in that specific order... it should yield at least 25 [Neonberries].

-Completion-

How was it out there? Did the quest spark any new ideas? Well, if you ever come up with something cool, feel free to share. Here's another [Beequip Case Slot] for all your efforts. And some tips regarding Planters: The amount of Nectar a bee sips from a Planter is based on the Gather Amount of the bee. Increasing the Gather Amount of your swarm through leveling, mutations, and Beequips... Also increases the rate at which you can collect Nectar. Ok. If you complete 2 more quests, I've got a [Diamond Egg] ready for you. Check in with me again whenever you're ready for more.

Unintended Intimidation Over the years I've gone through many different styles. For a while, I wanted nothing more than to look as tough as possible. I've always been smaller than my peers, and I didn't want to be seen as weak. I figured wearing spikes might make me more intimidating. Sort of like a cactus. Did it work? Eh, in a way I suppose. People didn't find me tough. But they were put off enough to leave me alone. After a while my fear of being messed with faded away, and I grew bored of that look. But I still try to incorporate a sort of sharp, piercing edginess into everything I do. Maybe edgy is a strong word... Well, the lingering effect is subtle. For this next quest, let's reflect a little of that, hm, sharp aesthetic.

-During-

[Whirligigs] can be obtained from Planters in the Pine Tree Forest. In a pinch, you can use a lot of [Paper Planters] to collect more tokens faster. But keep in mind, [Paper Planters] don't have any special loot assigned to them. Every other Planter type has bonus rewards that only it can give. For example, the [Blue Clay Planter] can give [Whirligigs] on any field.

-Completion-

I really admire Vicious Bee, even if it's a nuisance. It's dedicated to keeping others on their toes. Maybe it's easier to admire when I'm not the one out there getting spiked. Thanks for taking those pokes for my sake. Help me with just one more quest and that [Diamond Egg] is all yours. But before you go, here's something to keep in mind: The potential of a Beequip plays a huge role in how beneficial it's stats will be. The higher the potential, the more likely it is to give increased stats. and rarer ones too. This applies to the base stats of the Beequip, but also to any bonuses applied by waxes. Invest in Beequips with high potential, and save your rarer Waxes for those.

The Long Haul Hi again. We've come a long way already, huh? But we've still got a long way to go. I'm thinking you and I will be in this for a while. Case in point: this quest ought to take you some time. But if you complete it, I've got a [Diamond Egg] with your name on it. And if that's not enough to compel you, well, don't worry. It'll come with some other good stuff. Including a [Beequip Case Slot], and an expansion to my beequip shop selection. Don't fret if it seems to [sic] hard. I'm not in a rush. Things are going pretty well for my shop so far. But at the same time, you know… If it got done sooner, I wouldn't think less of you.

-During-

In most cases, Puffshrooms only have a chance to be Epic at levels 8 or higher. The higher the level, the higher the chance. Getting Puffshrooms to high levels can be difficult if the first Puffshroom starts low. For that reason, Puffshrooms spawned by better Planters will be more useful. Better Planters spawn higher level Puffshrooms from the start. Wild Puffshrooms that spawn naturally always start at level 1.

-Completion-

Finished already? Huh. You're something else. In a really good way. I'd say your bees are lucky to have you as their keeper. So I know this [Diamond Egg] will be well off… That is, uh, you know. If you actually hatch it. For the record, I wouldn't really recommend that. You're far enough into your beekeeping career now that obtaining Legendary Bees shouldn't be a problem. Instead, why not use it to craft a [Diamond Mask]? Now that's an accessory that makes a statement. And if you've already got one - lucky you - you could consider offering to the Wind Shrine. I'm not superstitious, but hey, it could be good luck somehow. Now that's all done, I can expand my shop to offer 4 Beequips at once. I've also got another [Beequip Case Slot] for you, if that wasn't enough. Thanks for all your help. I appreciate it, truly. I'll more quests for you later, but I've got to make a few preparations first. Check in with you soon.

The Trick To Tickets On this mountain, honey is money. That's cute, no doubt. And convenient for a beekeeper like you. But honey isn't quite enough for me... To craft more intricate things, like my Planters, I require stuff that can't be bought with honey. That makes earning those things more special somehow. They make you go out of your way a bit. And going out of your way, well, that's where the unexpected can happen. Although I admit there is a currency that makes pretty much everything easier around here. And that's [Tickets]. Surely you've noticed by now how useful those are. And while you can purchase [Tickets] for honey, the cost gets out of hand pretty fast. Thankfully there are lots of other ways to obtain them. For this next quest, I'll need you to test some of those out. Oh, I should mention. If you complete 5 more quests, I've got a [Mythic Egg] for you. Other stuff too, but that's the stand-out.

-During-

[Glue] is most reliably obtained from the [Candy Planter]. If you fully grow it 3 times in a row within the Stump Field, it should give you 10 [Glues]. That can happen about once a week. But you probably won't need to do that, as it can give [Glue] any times it's fully grown. Oh, and collected [Tickets] from Windy Bees will take at least 2 days. This is because you can only obtain up to 20 [Tickets] from Windy Bees per day.

-Completion-

Hi. You know, over the years as shopkeeper, I've developed an interest in economics. That stuff was never my forte in school. But it's still intriguing. How do we decide what something is worth? Seems, hm... arbitrary, so much of the time. How value channels between objects, markets, changes hands between demographics But it's all kind of elegant, and automatic. Huh. Anyways, those [Tickets] will be useful for purchasing Beequips from my shop. They can also be used to expand your Beequip Storage. And there's always a chance, I suppose, that additional uses for [Tickets] will come in the future. So they're good to stockpile. Complete 1 more quest and I'll give you an additional [Beequip Case Slot]. Complete 4 more, and the [Mythic Egg] will be yours as well. Thanks for your help! Check back in when you're ready for more.

Invigorating View I travel a lot. Seeking inspiration. Per usual. Typically I seek it out in urban places. I enjoy people watching. And hey, I kinda like being seen too. But sometimes it's best just to get away. If you want to clear your mind and put things in perspective... I find it's best to seek out scenic places, with vast expansive views. Mountains and stuff. Valleys. Places that make you feel small, but in a good way. There's a mountain named Denali in Alaska that's absolutely breathtaking. Specifically because of its prominence. From visible base to tip, it's the tallest thing you'll see on Earth. It's not the highest peak if we're talking distance above sea level. That'd be Mount Everest. But like I say, it's all about appearances, right? The mountain we're on now might not be Denali, but it's not too shabby. For this next quest, try to take in it's views. Jot them down, help me come up with ideas.

-During-

Having trouble finding the items for this quest? Heres some tips. Planters placed in the Dandelion Field, Blue Flower Field, and Rose Field have a chance to give [Honeysuckles]. Planters in the Cactus Field have a chance to give [Stingers]. And if you fully grow the [Red Clay Planter] in the Clover Field, Spider Field and Cactus Field, in that order It should grant 10 [Stingers], about once every 2 weeks.

-Completion-

How's it looking out there? Feeling invigorated from those views? Eh, maybe we're just too used to it up here. Speaking of the mountain: Did you know a [Candy Planter] on the Mountain Top Field is almost guaranteed to give a [Caustic Wax] once per month? Similarly, a [Tacky Planter] up there should give a [Loaded Dice] once a month. Anyways, great work out there. I think it's time I gave you another [Beequip Case Slot]! And if you complete 3 more, I'll be able to expand my shop. On top of giving you a [Mythic Egg], of course.

Ongoing Maintanence[sic] Business has been pretty good for my boutique. But I can't let that lull me into complacency. My customers expect something new every time they step through that door. They come here because they trust that I'm constantly seeking new styles. It's a never ending process, maintaining an eye for design. I wouldn't say my tastes become more refined... It's more of a, hm.. maintanence[sic] of dispositions. In the constant reflecting and responding to trends themselves, I maintain a disposition that my customers find valuable. Presumably. Sounds like a bunch of frou frou non-sense when I put it that way. Not that that's a bad thing. The point is: I can never stop trying to improve my products. To do that, I've got to constantly endeavor to upgrade myself. So lets play around with upgrades. You know Robo Bear, right? That thing is incredibly cool. For this quest, let's seek out inspiration in it. That whole techno-mechanical aesthetic it's got going on, It's what I'm feeling right now.

-During-

I haven't attempted Robo Bear's Challenge myself. I don't have any bees, obviously. But I've been told there are certain upgrades that help collect [Cogs] faster. Upgrades like Credit, which increase Cogs Per Round, are your best bet. Other upgrades that do that include RAM and Subscribe. Oh, and if you've forgotten where to get Comforting Nectar... It can be obtained on the Dandelion Field, Bamboo Field, and Pine Tree Forest.

-Completion-

Hi there. How'd the Robo Bear Challenges go? Find any interesting upgrades? The cool thing about them is, they aren't always objectively beneficial. Forces you to be selective. When it comes to upgrading Beequips with Waxes, they're pretty much all useful. But you're forced to be selective with which Beequips you use, and invest Waxes into. If you find a rare Beequip with high potential, you might not want to just fill it up with 5 [Soft Waxes]. That's because they have a higher chance for rare upgrades, especially through [Caustic Waxes]. There's an opportunity in those that you could argue is wasted through [Soft Waxes]. But [Soft Wax] definitely has its place, especially earlier in your beekeeping career. Anyways, thanks again for the help. Gotta keep moving though. 2 more quests to go until that [Mythic Egg]'s all yours.

Solitarily Steadfast Hey, got a moment? Let me ask you something. Whats [sic] it mean to you to be cool? Like, what makes you see someone and think: "Whose [sic] that? They seem cool."? It can't be as simple as what they're wearing. Although thats [sic] gotta be a part of it. I feel like it all comes down to attitude, right? How we look and how we talk - that's all a reflection of our attitude. And what I'm finding in all "cool" attitudes is a sort of a.. uh... steadfastness. Staying committed to a certain goal, or ideal, or sensibility, or something else at all times. Those people are playing their own game, essentially. On their own journeys. Not easily swayed by whatever's going on around them. And I think everyone else can sense that. At least I think I can. Those are the type of people who can actually teach you something. Show you new things. And that's cool. Does that make sense? Ehhh. Maybe the mystery of coolness is what makes it cool. But I know one thing for sure. I know you're pretty cool. You've got a goal with these quests and you just keep on truckin. So let's just keep at it. I'll have another [Beequip Case Slot] for you after this one's done.

-During-

There isn't anything very tricky about this quest. It just takes time. A practice in that steadfastness we were talking about, huh. The Epic Puffshrooms are probably the hardest part. There are strategies, though, that make getting them easier. Consider farming Puffshrooms in the 15 bee zone, with a few friends. One of you standing on each field. Those fields are close to each other. That reduces the time it takes for the spores to hop fields, increasing the number of Puffshrooms. But ultimately, it all comes down to chance.

-Completion-

Nice job out there. Stick Bug is pretty cool too, huh? Say, have you noticed with Puffshrooms that the loot seems to decrease the more your [sic] do them? That's because there are daily cooldowns to their rewards. Basically, the more loot you get in a day, the less likely that same loot becomes. But it all resets around midnight CST. Just something to keep in mind. Thanks for the help. With all that complete, I've got another [Beequip Case Slot] for you. And after the next quest that [Mythic Egg] should be ready too.

More Than Myth Just about ready to expand my shop again. We're making incredible progress. So after this next quest, I'll reward you a [Mythic Egg]. I don't know too much about bees, but I do know Mythic Bees are in a league of their own. I mean, they're so special we call them the "myths". As if the legends of their powers are so unbelievable, we can't even be sure if they're real or not. When of course, they are. I see them all the time. So that's just some next level hyperbole. In any case, it wasn't easy getting my hands on this thing. So this next quest is going to require a bit of work. Like I said before, every 5th quest of mine is harder. That's because the bigger my shop gets, the harder it gets to stay inspired. Or maybe I just want to keep you around as long as possible. Wouldn't that be nice?

-During-

Here's some tips, in case the dice are giving you problems: The [Tacky Planter] is a reliable source for [Field Dice]. The first time you fully grow it, about once every day, it should give at least 3. And any Planter in the Dandelion Field has a higher chance for [Field Dice] as well. Oh, and if you're wondering what Meteors are... Those are spawned by Mythic Meteor Showers, which require 3 Mythic Bees discovered to activate. Catching a Meteor has a chance to grant a [Moon Charm]. You might need someone else's help for that. Good luck out there. The [Mythic Egg] is almost yours.

-Completion-

Oh, hey. Didn't expect you back so fast. Guess I should know by now nothing slows your bees down for long. With all that work done, I can expand my shop to offer 5 Beequips at once. And as a reward, I've got a plenty to give you. Including this [Mythic Egg]. You know, while you were out there, I was thinking I may want to pivot, take the boutique in a different direction. Source some new products. Watching you complete quests is inspiring for sure, but I need to get out there myself a bit. And more practically: I need to collect more things to reward you with. In any case, you deserve a rest. Can't thank you enough. Check in with you soon.

Sticker Style As you well know by now, I'm an advocate for self-expression. I celebrate it, really. Of decoration for the sake of it - the superfluous charms which set us apart. And while I'm all about Beequips and Planters, there's something else I'm enamored with. And that's Stickers. Those silly doodles people stick to their hives. They can tell you a lot about someone, you know? How they choose to express themselves within fairly limited constraints. Some people get really creative. While others treat them as an afterthought. Or ignore them alltogether. In any case, how a hive is decorated with Stickers reveals a lot about their character. If I had a hive, I'd try my best to get weird with it. I've actually got a pretty sizable collection of Stickers myself, and I'd like to keep expanding it. If you help me with that, I think I'll be able to expand your [Beequip Case] again.

-During-

Obtaining specific Stickers straight from their natural source can be quite tedious. But miscellaneous ones, like the kind I ask for, are often quite common within the overall economy. And because I tend to ask different people for different Stickers, your best bet, quite frankly, is to trade for them. You can hop around Hive Hub servers to get an idea of values, and perhaps find what you're looking for. But there are also other markets, if you go looking for them. You could even consider trading Beequips from my shop for Stickers. I certainly wouldn't complain.

-Completion-

Hi. How'd the Sticker hunt go? You ready to hand those over? Cause I'm ready to give you this: a [Beequip Case Slot]. So, I'm sure you've realized this by now, but just in case: The Sticker Sprout in the Hive Hub spawns once every 3 hours, across all Hive Hub servers at the same time. A message is sent out globally shortly before they spawn. Sticker Sprouts are guaranteed to drop 3 [Sticker Planters], which are one of the best sources for Stickers, including some really rare ones. On top of that, they've got a pretty decent Nectar multiplier as well. An entire planter dedicated to Stickers. Now that's right up my alley, heh. Now, for your extraordinary effort, and your generous donation... I've got something else quite special for you this time: A [Nectar Shower Vial]. This ain't no ordinary Nectar Vial. In fact, it's pretty much all 5 of them in 1. But wait, there's more. When you use this, it won't just give the Nectar to you - it'll give it to every player in the server. That's right. 20 hours of Nectar, to you and any one of your buddies you might like enough to share with. May be able to maneuver some favors out of that, right? Just a thought. Personally, as a generous bear myself, I try to use them in the Hive Hub so more players can benefit. Up to you, of course. Thanks for your help. I'll check in with you again soon.

Conclusion I'm still setting up shop, but I'll have a lot more I want to talk with you about soon. For now, getting yourself aquainted with Beequips and Planters ought to be helpful. Here are a few pointers that ought to get you started:
  • Each Planter type is likely to give you a special reward the first time you harvest it, every once in a while
  • If you use [Glitter] on a field with a Planter, the Planter will grow 25% faster until you harvest it[.] This lasts even after the field boost wears off.
  • Different types of Planters may give different rewards based on the Field you place them on.

Feel free to browse my selection of Planters. I'll check in with you soon.

Exclusive Beesmas Dialogue 2021 (TBA) Exclusive Beesmas Dialogue 2022 Somehow I knew you'd get something for me this year. We're on the same page. I've been thinking about you too. I'll go ahead and open my gift now. ...(krumple krumple)... Ah hah, a funky little Bumble Bee pin for my lapel! I don't usually like accessories as gifts - I prefer to pick my own But this one hit's [sic] the right spot. Thank you! Now why don't you open mine? There's a few things in there: A [Ticket Planter], a vial of [Motivating Nectar]...And the [Potpourri Ornament]. It's filled with flowers and leaves I grew in my Planters. The fragrance is pretty strong... but hey, smells like Beesmas. With this on the tree, you'll receive the following boosts: +25% Convert Rate +25% Capacity in the Dandelion Field And +5% Nectar. Hope you like it. I know I'll be flaunting this pin around for weeks. Thanks again, and Happy Honeydays.

docs.title: Blue Drive Quest
docs.text:
Source Dialogue Barter For The Blue Drive Hey there. What's that? Oh, a [White Drive]? What a coincidence. I've got a [Blue Drive] just like it. Picked it up at an electronics shop in Akihabara a few years back. I suppose I could give it to you... If you're willing to give a little back. I'm a business man after all, and that [Blue Drive] wasn't cheap. So why not partake in some of my Beequips? And while you're at it, help me harvest some Puffshrooms. That is, only if you reallly want this [Blue Drive]. Cause I'll be honest, from the rumors I've heard... I'm not so sure you're ready for it any how.

-During-

N/A

-Completion-

Well if it wasn't my most loyal customer. Heh. As a token of appreciation for your recent purchases... The [Blue Drive] is all yours! When i bought this thing, the shopkeep tried to tell me something. My Japanese isn't great, but I think it was, hm, a warning or something. Basically, the Robot Bear is only for the most advanced beekeepers. So even if you manage to repair it, you might not get much out of it. At least not for a while. But it can't hurt to try, right?

Dialogue The Honeydays are a time where even the most subdued pepole get decorative. I appreciate when people try to spruce things up. And given how drab and cold winters can be otherwise... We need that extra bit of spice to warm us up, right? Well. I've got some thing that'll melt away your winter woes. One sip from my Samovar, and you'll be feeling toasty. A Samovar is a traditional device originating from Russia, usually used for tea. I lugged this back on a trip from Tula. And I use it to warm Nectar, and reconsitute [Honeysuckles]. But it's become a bit tarnished and dull. Want to help me polish it up? If you do, I'll let you use it too, free of charge. Well, apart from a few stickers Stickers, that is. Looks like you've finished your scavenger hunt. That [sic] everything I'll need to polish this up. ...(scrub scrub)... Mmhmm. See, like a Diamond Bee in the rough. As the Samovar's brew gets stronger, you'll also get more Honeysuckles. Use it enough and you might be surprised how much joy it can bring you. Just don't drink it too fast - pace yourself. Samovar is something you're supposed to savor, I've heard. Happy Honeydays! Check in with you later.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Dapper Bear is shorter than every other bear in the game. This is referenced in his dialogue and is a key detail in the Tacky Planters chain that rewards the Dapper From Above Sticker.
  • Dapper Bear, Gummy Bear, Tunnel Bear, Noob Bear, Pro Bear, Top Bear, and Shadow Bear are the only bears to reside indoors.
  • Dapper Bear and Gummy Bear are the only quest bears to reside indoors.
    • Dapper Bear is the only permanent quest bear to reside indoors.
  • This bear, Mother Bear, Gummy Bear, Robo Bear, and Bee Bear are the only bears to own a shop.
  • This bear, Bee Bear, and Mother Bear are the only quest bears to own a shop.
  • This bear, Mother Bear, and Robo Bear are the only permanent bears to own a shop.
  • Like Mother Bear, Dapper Bear uses the Stylish Animation Pack.
  • Like Mother Bear and Gummy Bee, Dapper Bear's face emits light. This is most noticeable if the player looks at Dapper Bear at night.
  • He is the only permanent quest giver whose first quest was a seasonal one.
  • Dapper Bear may have a possible Russian background. When the player completes his Samovar quest (the Samovar is also of Russian origins), Dapper Bear mentions that he made room for some beequips and the Samovar on his travel back to Moscow.
  • In Beesmas Winter 2024, one of the requirements for his samovar quest was “Collect 25 tokens from planters in the Pineapple Patch” However, it was broken and no tokens collected in Pineapple Patch would count towards the quest. This was later fixed by setting the requirement to finished for all players.
  • Dapper Bear, Sun Bear, and Spirit Bear are the only bears to wear 3D accessories.
  • Of the three, Dapper Bear is the only one to wear accessories that the player can't use.
  • Upon the soft launch of Beesmas 2025, Dapper Bear's shop was broken to some players.
  • This resulted in a broken UI when the shop was opened, and for the beequips to appear to be 5 Red Extracts per beequip.
  • Dapper Bear, Gifted Bucko Bee, and Gifted Riley Bee are the only NPCs that own shops that require quests to be completed to unlock certain items in their shop.
  • This also makes Dapper Bear the only bear to own a shop with items requiring the player to complete quests.

docs.title: Dark Scythe
docs.text:
Dark Scythe Overview Price (Needs to have 250 Gifted Riley Bee quests complete) 1,500 Red Extracts, 150 Stingers, 100 Hard Waxes, 50 Caustic Waxes, 50 Super Smoothies, 3 Invigorating Vials, 2.5T Honey Shop Red HQ Pollen Collection Range 35 Flowers Collecting Pattern Crescent collectedyou (facing up) Collecting Time 0.5 Base Collection 13 Flowers Single Double Triple Large Star White 13 26 39 52 65 Red 13 26 39 52 65 Blue 13 26 39 52 65 Special Multiplier(s): ?

Not to be confused with the Scythe.

The Dark Scythe is a tool that can be crafted in the Red HQ. The player needs to have completed at least 250 Gifted Riley Bee quests to unlock it.

Crafting Ingredients 2.5T Honey

1,500 Red Extracts 150 Stingers 100 Hard Waxes 50 Caustic Waxes 50 Super Smoothies 3 Invigorating Vials

It collects 13 pollen from 35 patches in 0.5 seconds. It has an average base pollen collection rate of 910 pollen per second.

If a flame gets hit by the Dark Scythe's collection, it will turn it into a Dark Flame and flame fuel (if active) is reapplied, as well as its lifespan being reset.

A Dark Flame grants a stack of Dark Heat, which grants +10% Instant Red Ability Conversion and x1.05 Super-Crit Power, with each additional Dark Flame granting an extra x0.05 Super-Crit Power to the stack and +1% Instant Red Ability Conversion, capping at x6 Super-Crit Power and 109% Instant Red Ability Conversion. An active Dark Flame always gives the player a stack of dark heat whether they are touching the flame or not.

Touching a Dark Flame grants 33% more growth to Scorching Stars than normal flames. Dark Flames also deal 50% more damage than regular flames.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Dark Scythe's blue counterpart is the Tide Popper, and its white counterpart is the Gummyballer.
  • The Dark Scythe's scooping trail can pop bubbles.
  • If the player's backpack is full and scooped their Dark Scythe while in a field, it will prompt the full backpack message three times.
  • This is the only red collector that doesn't multiply the amount of red pollen collected. This is the same case as Tide Popper.
  • This is tied with the Tide Popper for being the fifth most expensive item in the game, both having a cost of 2.5T Honey. In front of the Dark Scythe and Tide Popper is the Petal Planter, costing 5T Honey, Coconut Belt costing 7.5T Honey, the Gummyballer, costing 10T Honey, and The Planter Of Plenty, costing 100T Honey.
  • The Dark Scythes's raw ingredients cost:

  • On December 28, 2021, there was an exploit that could have been used to obtain the Dark Scythe, as well as Tide Popper and Gummyballer for free. This was later patched by Onett, and everybody who used the exploit got a full reset on their account.

docs.title: Day/Night Cycle
docs.text: The Day/Night Cycle is a feature added in the 2018-09-10 update. Before the update, it was always daytime.

docs.title: Day
docs.text: Daytime previously lasted from around 10 to 30 minutes (for an average of 20 minutes). All music plays as normal. This is the default setting for the game.

docs.title: Night
docs.text:
When the day ends, the sun goes down quickly, and the sky shifts to black, indicating that it is nighttime. During this cycle, all outdoor music is replaced by mountaincall. Entering any area that plays the vendor, crawlers, gbtune1, hibernation1, starhall music or music playing during an Ant, Robo or Stick Bug Challenge will override the night music. Fireflies will also appear, stopping in different fields. The background of the server and walls will turn pitch black. A Rogue Vicious Bee has a higher chance of spawning every night. A moon sprout also has a 60% chance of spawning every night.

Walking near a firefly will make it fly into the air and leave a 1x1 patch of sparkles. Once a player has removed all the fireflies, one of the tokens below will appear in the middle of their formation:

  • Moon Charms (increments of 1, 5, or 10).
  • Glitter (Very rare).
  • Star Jelly (Extremely rare).
  • Night Bell (Extremely rare).
  • Star Treat (Exceptionally rare).
  • Waxing Crescent Moon Sticker (Rare)
  • Glowing Smile Sticker (Extremely Rare)
  • Star Signs (Extremely Rare)
  • Cyan Star Sticker (Exceptionally Rare)
  • Shining Star Sticker (Exceptionally Rare)

Fireflies can only stop in the same field three times. After removing all the fireflies in a field three times, they will fly to a different field. Fireflies will only stop in the Rose Field, Cactus Field, Pineapple Patch, Spider Field, Strawberry Field and Bamboo Field.

Night lasts 2 minutes 35 seconds, which is the duration of the night theme (mountaincall). Ever since the 2018-11-25 and 2018-12-19 updates, moon-shaped platforms leading to the Diamond Mask and the platforms leading to Bubble Bee Man and the Night Memory Match are solid yellow only during nighttime if the player has a Moon Amulet (if the player owns the Diamond Mask, the platforms to the Diamond Mask will be blue and stay permanently solid). When sprouts are planted at night, there is a 60% chance for it to be a moon sprout, with the odds of all other sprout types being altered (Supreme Sprouts become more common while the rest are rarer).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• If the Stick Bug Challenge ends at night, the normal music will play instead of the night music. If the time cycles from night to day or day to night while a Honeystorm or mythic meteor shower is active, the fog will disappear, but the honeystorm or mythic meteor shower will still be active.
  • In some occasions, the nighttime OST doesn't have to end for it to be daytime, it just simply fades.
  • A Night Bell and Spirit Bear can manually summon nighttime.
  • Onett can also summon nighttime, but does it globally and with a message (ex: "🌙 One of Mother Bear's cubs has summoned nighttime... 🌙").
    • A full gallery of these messages can be found in the Night Bell page.
  • Sometime before Beesmas 2025 started, there was a bug that caused the day/night cycle to rapidly speed up, having daytime last only approximately 2–10 minutes.

docs.title: Debug Wax
docs.text:
Debug Wax

"100% chance to greatly improve a Beequip."

Debug Wax is an inventory item and a type of wax added in the 2024-07-17 update that can be used on a Beequip to boost its stats. Upon usage, it has a 100% chance of greatly improving the Beequip's stats. Debug Wax has an Upgrade Value of 4.

When applying Debug Wax to a bee's Beequip, a message pops up saying: The Wax improved the Beequip!

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• Rebirth rewards: 1, 3 or 10 depending on the rebirth, plus Mother Bear's rebirth quest.
  • Blender (takes 5 minutes):
  • 1 Turpentine
  • 500 Swirled Wax
  • 500 Caustic Wax

docs.title: Crafting Uses
docs.text: • 10 Debug Wax are used to make Fluxite Wax.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This item functions almost the same as a Caustic Wax, the only difference being that it always succeeds.
  • This item originally shared its icon with Caustic Wax before the 2024-12-25 update.
  • This item originated from the Test Realm, being a risk-free way to upgrade Beequips, before officially being added to the game.
  • This wax, Soft Wax, and Swirled Wax are the only waxes guaranteed to change a beequip's stats.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Demon Bee is one of the slowest bees in the game, but is also one of the most powerful in terms of attack and gather amount.
  • Demon Bee is the only bee in the game to have 2 bomb abilities (Red Bomb and Red Bomb+).
  • Demon Bee, Riley Bee, and Rascal Bee have the same skin colors.
  • Both Demon Bee and Fire Bee have the same flame effect.
  • The Demon Mask, which can be purchasable in the Lava Obby, has a special design, name, and stats dedicated to Demon Bee.
  • Onett has said on Discord that during early stages, it was supposed to summon Fire Bees. This role has now been taken over by Spicy Bee.
  • Before the 2020-04-06 Update, Demon Bee had the highest base gather amount in the game with the exception of a Tabby Bee with a 500+ stack of Tabby Love. Since then, Fuzzy Bee has taken that position.
  • Demon Bee is the red counterpart of Diamond Bee.
  • One reason Demon Bee dislikes the Mountain Top Field might be because it is closer to heaven (the sky) than all other Fields.
  • This bee can be summoned by the Honeyday Candles.
  • This Bee, Fire Bee, Precise Bee, Festive Bee and Crimson Bee are the only red bees that do not like Strawberries.
  • In the in-game stat menu for Demon Bee, its attack is stated to be 6 more than the normal amount (1). However, it is actually 7 more.

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Realistic max is the best you can expect to actually see: the most picks of that upgrade that about 1 in 1,000 fully waxed 5 ★ beequips get, each at its top value. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The light colors around Diamond Bee make it nearly translucent.
  • Diamond Bee has the highest base convert rate out of all bees, only beaten by Tabby Bee when its Tabby Love stack is at 626 or higher.
  • Diamond Bee and Honey Bee are the only bees in the game which can generate Honey Gift or Honey Gift+ tokens.
  • This, Bubble Bee, Fire Bee, Honey Bee, Demon Bee, and Gummy Bee are the only bees to have masks based on them, specifically the Diamond Mask for Diamond Bee.
  • Diamond Bee is the blue counterpart of Demon Bee.
  • Diamond Bee and Gummy Bee are the only bees to have a sparkle effect.
  • Diamond Bee has a unique conversion link color (cyan/light blue). It is the only bee to have a conversion link that is not yellow.
  • Diamond Bee is one of only two bees to have the same name as an egg they can hatch from; the other being Basic Bee, and those eggs being the Diamond Egg and Basic Egg respectively.
  • Diamond bee may like the Pineapple Patch because pineapples have historically been symbols of wealth.

Diamond Drenchers Requirement 10 Master Badges Cost 4,444,444,444 Honey Description Four enhanced sprinklers made of durable artificial diamond!

The Diamond Drenchers are the 4th tier sprinkler available for purchase in the Badge Bearer's Guild. To unlock it, the player must obtain 10 different Master badges. Its radius extends to 8 flower tiles, its rate is 4 seconds, and its power is 9.

Diamond Mask Description "Proudly show your extreme wealth to the world. Shine so brightly that others will complain." Cost 5,000,000,000 Honey, 250 Blue Extracts, 150 Oil, 100 Glitter, 5 Diamond Eggs, 1 Comforting Vial. Bonus Stats x1.5 Blue Pollen

+15% Instant Blue Conversion+25% Pollenx3 Capacityx1.5 Bubble Pollen+35% Defense+20% Bee Ability Rate+Passive: Bubble Bombs (Needs Bubble Mask)+Passive: Diamond Drain

The Diamond Mask is a mask and the blue counterpart of the Demon Mask. It can be reached by finding the doorway near the end of the Cloud Obby, then completing an additional obstacle course made up of moon platforms. The player is able to skip the Cloud Obby by using a Parachute or Glider with enough height to steer themselves to the entrance to the Diamond Room. If the player owns the Diamond Mask, the moon platforms in the Diamond Room are permanently solid and are shaded a deep blue.

Crafting Ingredients 5B Honey

250 Blue Extracts 150 Oils 100 Glitter 5 Diamond Eggs 1 Comforting Vial

Once the 30th blue ability token is collected, the Diamond Mask's passive ability activates.

• x1.5 Blue Pollen
  • +15% Instant Blue Conversion
  • +25% Pollen
  • x3 Capacity
  • x1.5 Bubble Pollen
  • +35% Defense
  • +20% Bee Ability Rate
  • +Passive: Bubble Bombs (Requires Bubble Mask in order to use):
  • Every 25th Bomb Ability Token spawns 25 Bubbles that last for 8 seconds. if a player touches them, they pop, collecting 4R/6W/8B pollen, increased by 15% per Gifted blue Bee type, from 29 nearby Flowers and causes them to grow. (Cooldown: 2 minutes)
  • +Passive: Diamond Drain:
  • Every 30th blue Ability Token converts 5 million Pollen plus a percentage of the Convert Amount of all of your bees combined, increased by 10% per blue bee and +50% per gifted blue bee type in your Hive. It also Pollinates 10 (+3 per blue bee) blue flowers within the field. (Cooldown: 45 seconds)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Prior to the 2019-09-28 Update, the player was unable to jump on the moon platforms during the day, similar to the moon platforms in the Bear Gate and behind Dapper Bear's Shop, even if they already own the Diamond Mask.
  • If the ingredients to craft this item were to be crafted, a total of 5,000,000,000 honey, 4,000 Royal Jellies, 12,500 Blueberries, 7,500 Sunflower Seeds, 100 Magic Beans, 2,500 Moon Charms, and 5 Diamond Eggs are needed, or 2000 tickets if one decides to purchase all the diamond eggs from the ticket tent.

  • The Diamond Mask Shop, the Hub Field Shop, and the Demon Mask Shop are the only shops in the game that have a single item.
  • This, the Demon Mask, and the Gummy Mask are the only masks with decorative accessories (the Diamond Mask has a tiara).
  • Unlike the Demon Mask and Gummy Mask, the sound effect of its passive is not based on music in the game.
  • This mask and the Demon Mask are the only masks that require an obby to equip or reach the shop.

docs.title: Digital Bee
docs.text:
Digital Bee Original Gifted "A virtual bee with malfunctioning AI. It corrupts the game itself." RarityEvent ColorColorless Energy20 Speed11.9 Attack1 Color Scheme Skin#717779#bab088#e7daaa

Not to be confused with Digital Bee's NPC counterpart from the Ready Player Two event.

Digital Bee is a Colorless Event bee that hatches out of a Digital Bee egg, which is available in the Robo Bear's Shop for 7,777,777 Honey, 5 Red Drives, 5 Blue Drives, 5 White Drives, and 5 Glitched Drives. It also requires the player to unlock (not equip) the Diamond Cog Amulet to unlock crafting it. If Digital Bee is already owned, 1,000 Tickets will be granted instead.

Unlike most other Event bees, Digital Bee has favorite treats: Caustic Wax, Sunflower Seeds, Pineapples and Moon Charms. It can also be made gifted by feeding it a Star Treat, Gingerbread Bears or Aged Gingerbread Bears.

Digital Bee likes the Dandelion Field, Mountain Top Field, and Coconut Field. It dislikes the Pine Tree Forest.

docs.title: Stats
docs.text:
• Collects 10 Pollen in 4 seconds.
  • Makes 80 Honey in 4 seconds.
  • -15% Movespeed, +10% Critical Chance, up to +1000 Convert Amount, up to +125 Gather Amount, up to +15 Attack, up to +25% Ability Rate
  • 🌟 Gifted Hive Bonus: +1% Ability Duplication Chance

docs.title: AbilitiesLevels 1-8Levels 9-16Levels 17-24Levels 25-31
docs.text:
• Glitch Corrupts the Field you're in for 20s (+1s per Level), granting collected Ability Tokens a chance to be duplicated (or "Duped").
  • Duped Tokens hover over the field for a duration equal to the lifespan of the original Ability Token x2 (+5% per Digital Bee Level). Standing beneath a Duped Token for 1s causes it to activate.
  • Increasing a field's Corruption increases the chance for abilities to be duplicated (8%-20%) and boosts the pollen collection and Instant Conversion of Duped Abilities (x1.1 - x3 Pollen from Duped Abilities, 20%-90% IC from Duped Abilities). Enhancing Digital Bee with Drives causes this ability to grant more Corruption: Colored Drives increase the Corruption of fields with matching flowers while Glitched Drives increase the Corruption of all fields.
  • While this is active, Digital Bee will occasionally spawn ☺︎ Tokens. Activating a ☺︎ token temporarily increases the field's Corruption, causes all Duped Tokens to be activated, and collects pollen equal to +50% of Digital Bee's gather amount from a random arrangement of flowers, then multiplies the Pollen collected by +50% per Duped Token collected with 50% being instantly converted. The flowers are stamped for 10s, granting them a x2 pollen multiplier. The stamped flowers also come in a "☺", "&", "?", "*", or "~" shape. The frequency of ☺︎ tokens increases with the number of Glitched Drives Digital Bee has been enhanced with.
  • Mind Hack Hacks the minds of up to 3 nearby enemies (+1 per every 3 lvls), stunning them for 3s (+0.1s per lvl). While hacked, the enemies take 25% more damage (+0.1% per Glitched Drive Digital Bee has been enhanced with). Hacking is only half as effective against bosses.
  • If in a field, this also spawns a ☺︎ token.
  • 🌟Gifted Ability: Map Corruption Digital Bee corrupts a random field by a small amount for all players for 3 minutes (+15s per lvl). The amount of Corruption is increased by the number of Drives Digital Bee has been enhanced with up to 300 corruption (other players receive 1/3 of the corruption).
  • Fields with more flowers matching the color of the most recent colored Drive you've used are more likely to be selected. If your most recent Drive is a Glitched Drive, the field is completely random but gains 25% more Corruption.
  • Passive: Drive Expansion Using a Drive while this bee is active in Robo Bear's Challenge corrupts the field you're standing in by an amount proportional to the number of flowers that match the Drive's color (Glitched Drives corrupt all fields equally). Additionally, it permanently enhances this bee, increasing the Corruption of its abilities and granting it the following stats:

: - Red Drive: +0.03 Attack : - Blue Drive: +2 Convert Amount : - White Drive: +0.25 Gather Amount : - Glitched Drive: +0.05% Ability Rate

  • Every 10 Glitched Drives Enhancements also grants a Hive Bonus of +0.03% Ability Duplication Chance.
  • Digital Bee can be enhanced with up to 500 of each type of Drive. You can view the number of enhancements by clicking on Digital Bee's hive slot.
  • Upon maxing out with all 2000 Drives, Digital Bee gains +10 Movespeed and grants a Hive Bonus of +0.5% Ability Duplication Chance.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Digital Bee first made its appearance in the Ready Player Two event.
  • This also makes Digital Bee the first and only bee to make an appearance in the game before being implemented as an actual bee.
  • Digital Bee was available in an old package at the time of its release. It was the only way to obtain the bee other than purchasing it in Robo Bear's Shop.
  • Digital Bee is the only bee that requires an amulet to be unlocked as of right now. It is also the only event bee to require multiple materials to be purchased.
  • Digital Bee's favorite operating system is TempleOS, according to Onett.
  • Digital Bee is currently the most expensive bee that was sold in the Robux Shop, with a price of 2,500 Robux
  • Digital Bee is the only bee that can be upgraded with the use of items, which are drives.
  • The shapes that Digital Bee makes when collecting a ☺︎ token are the same shapes made by the bee's NPC counterpart during its field puzzles.
  • Digital Bee is the only event bee that has a passive and gifted ability.
  • It is also the only non-mythic bee to have a gifted ability.
  • Digital Bee is the only event bee to have a negative stat, whose movespeed has a value of 11.9 which is below the normal speed value (14).
  • Digital Bee's ☺ is a reference to an old computer malware called "You are an idiot" aka "youdontknowwhoiam" aka "offiz trojan" which overloads your computer's RAM and CPU usage every time you try to close the program; Digital Bee references this behavior with its ability.
  • Digital Bee's gifted form's face resembles the blue screen of death, which is a common problem for Windows computers.
  • Digital Bee, Windy Bee, Gummy Bee, Vicious Bee, and Bear Bee are the only event bees that have an obtainment method not involving tickets.

docs.title: Dispensers
docs.text:
A Dispenser is a machine whose main purpose is to dispense various items or boosts to the player typically under a cooldown.

To use a dispenser, simply stand on the pad in front of the dispenser to use it. Some of the dispensers have certain requirements in order to be used, such as having enough tickets. Others have indirect requirements, such as the Glue Dispenser, which sits in Gummy Bear's Lair and needs 2 Goo badges, or the Coconut Dispenser, which is inside the Coconut Cave. The Free Ant Pass Dispenser needs 20 bees and the Free Robo Pass Dispenser needs 30 bees.

Unlike in Bee Swarm Simulator, the Honey, Treat, Blueberry and Strawberry Dispensers do not need Bee Swarm Simulator Club membership in Re://:Swarm.

docs.title: Dispensers by Area
docs.text:
There are currently 14 dispensers, plus 2 bee claimers that turn an item into a bee egg once. Ticket dispensers cost tickets each use; the rest are free on a cooldown.

docs.text:
• The Blue Extract Dispenser and the Red Extract Dispenser are unique to Re://:Swarm.
  • The Honey Dispenser, the Strawberry Dispenser, the Blueberry Dispenser, the Royal Jelly Dispenser, and the Glue Dispenser are the only dispensers that are required to be used for a quest ("Honey Bee's Honey Wreath?" from Honey Bee requires the player to use the Honey Dispenser, "BBM's Naughty List" from Bubble Bee Man requires the player to use the Royal Jelly Ticket Dispenser, and "The Power of Information" from Science Bear requires the player to use the Strawberry Dispenser, the Blueberry Dispenser, and the Glue Dispenser).
  • There are three dispensers that give treats in the game being the Treat Dispenser, the Blueberry Dispenser, and the Strawberry Dispenser.
  • The Glue Dispenser, the Free Ant Pass Dispenser, Ant Pass Dispenser, Free Robo Pass Dispenser, Robo Pass Dispenser, and the Coconut Dispenser are the only dispensers to not grant haste.
  • The Glue Dispenser, the Free Robo Pass Dispenser, and the Free Royal Jelly Dispenser are the only dispensers with a 22-hour cooldown, the longest in the game.
  • The Free Ant Pass Dispenser, the Ant Pass Dispenser, the Robo Pass Dispenser, and the Free Robo Pass Dispenser are the only dispensers that don't have any visible faucets, and instead have a small compartment, like a vending machine that gives out tickets.
  • The Glue Dispenser and the Coconut Dispenser are the only dispensers that give more items when the player upgrades the badge that corresponds to it.
  • The Coconut Dispenser is the only dispenser to give a field boost.

docs.title: Drives
docs.text: Drives are inventory items that were introduced in the 2022-12-26 update. They can be used to repair Robo Bear, purchase Digital Bee, upgrade Digital Bee, and grant boosts during a round of the Robo Bear Challenge. All Drives (except Broken Drives) can be purchased from Robo Bear's Shop for 50 Cogs (100 Cogs for Glitched, and 5 of each other drive), and an increasing amount of Honey with each purchase.

docs.title: White Drive
docs.text:
The White Drive, when used, grants the following boosts during a single round of Robo Bear's Challenge:

  • x1.25 White Pollen
  • x1.25 White Field Capacity
  • +1 Colorless Bee Attack

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• Purchasing it for 50 Cogs and a base of 250,000 Honey in Robo Bear's Shop.
  • The nth drive costs \(\displaystyle P(n)=250{,}000\cdot n^{2}\).
  • Chance to receive from Robo Bear's Challenge.
  • Completing Science Bear's "Repairing The White Drive" quest gives 1 White Drive, replacing the Broken Drive.
  • As a reward for finishing your own Robo Party.

docs.title: Red Drive
docs.text:
The Red Drive, when used, grants the following boosts during a single round of Robo Bear's Challenge:

  • x1.25 Red Pollen
  • x1.25 Red Field Capacity
  • +1 Red Bee Attack

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• Purchasing it for 50 Cogs and a base of250,000 Honey in Robo Bear's Shop.
  • The nth drive costs \(\displaystyle P(n)=250{,}000\cdot n^{2}\).
  • Chance to receive from Robo Bear's Challenge.
  • Completing Panda Bear's "Ready For The Red Drive?" Quest gives 1 Red Drive (Requires you to finish Science Bear's White Drives quest first)
  • As a reward for finishing your own Robo Party.

  • Completing Dapper Bear's "Barter For The Blue Drive" Quest gives 1 Blue Drive (Requires you to finish Science Bear's White Drive quest first)

docs.title: Glitched Drive
docs.text:
The Glitched Drive, when used, grants the following boosts during a single round of Robo Bear's Challenge:

  • x1.25 Field Capacity
  • +1 Bee Attack

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• Purchasing it for 100 Cogs, 5 Red Drives, 5 Blue Drives, 5 White Drives and a base of1,000,000 Honey in Robo Bear's Shop.
  • The nth drive costs \(\displaystyle P(n)=1{,}000{,}000\cdot n^{2}\).
  • It requires a Gold Cog Amulet to unlock the ability of purchasing it.
  • Completing 10 or more rounds of Robo Bear's Challenge has a chance to reward a Glitched Drive, increased chance as the player finishes the challenge on a higher round.
  • 1 Glitched Drive is guaranteed as a reward once a day after completing round 20.
  • 1 Glitched Drive is guaranteed upon completing round 25, with a 1/7 chance for a second.
  • Completing Science Bear's "Corrupting The Glitched Drive" quest gives 1 Glitched Drive (Requires you to complete Science Bear's White Drive quest, Dapper Bear's Blue Drive quest, and Panda Bear's Red Drive quest).
  • As a reward for finishing your own Robo Party.

  • This may be a reference to the unused yellow flowers found in Onett's decal inventory.
