docs.title: Easter Eggs
docs.text: Throughout the map, plenty of Easter Eggs can be found. Some of them have been removed, while some still exist.

docs.title: Codes
docs.text: Codes or hints for codes have been scattered across the map. They are written in white and are usually in peculiar places. The codes and their hiding places are:

docs.title: Puppy Bee with Reindeer Antlers and Festive Bee with Festive Wreath (Level 2)
docs.text:
The Puppy Bee with the Reindeer Antlers statue doesn't actually have the Antlers, but it's still called 'Puppy Bee with Reindeer Antlers' because of its nose. The Festive Bee with the Festive Wreath was added when Part 2 of Beesmas 2020 came, and was right next to Puppy Bee with Reindeer Antlers.

The Puppy Bee with Reindeer Antlers and Festive Bee with Festive Wreath can be found behind the wall of the Blue HQ outside the map.

You can get to this by:

  1. Using a Red Cannon in combination with the parachute/glider to glide towards here.
  2. Jump from a far distance towards here.

docs.title: Onett Statue
docs.text:
The statue is one of the easiest easter eggs to find and can be found on the top of the rightmost hive (6th hive). Behind him, there is a Royal Jelly. On his backpack you can see the number 38217, which is actually a code that will give you 5 tickets. You can get to him using a few methods.

  1. Using the Yellow Cannon, Red Cannon, or Blue Cannon (only glider) in combination with the parachute/glider to glide to the top of the hive.
  2. On very rare occasions the statue will fall to the ground, and actually could be found inside the honeycombs within the rightmost hive. Rarely, he can be found behind the 5-Bee Gate.
  3. You can jump on the Puppy Bee's tail on the Ticket Tent or the Gifted Photon Bee on the ticket tent and jump on top of the hive if you have enough jump power or speed.
  4. You can jump in the Gummy Bee in Gummy Bee Claimer, and use the Glider to get on the hives.
  5. Jump and use glider from the coconut field to get on top of the hives.

Unlike the Onett NPC found in the Bear Gate, he cannot be interacted with.

docs.title: Dancing Bear / Shadow Bear
docs.text:
Main article: Shadow Bear

Shadow Bear can be found under the platform Onett (NPC) is located on. He looks the same as Tunnel Bear, but he will not kill upon contact and is much bigger. In front of him is a Diamond Egg token you can collect, however, if the player touches the ground for long enough, the player will die. If you have enough speed, you can run across the floor without dying. This makes getting the Diamond Egg a challenge.

If you have enough ping, you can hold jump as the floor only kills you after a set amount of time, which is increased by ping.

docs.title: Hallway Behind Badge Bearer's Guild
docs.text: There is a hallway behind the Ace Shop that is inaccessible without glitching/cheating, but can be seen inside using ROBLOX's Shift Lock feature. It leads to an entrance to the area (see Honey Void) under the game. It can also be seen by looking at the ceiling of the area. In the test realm, this path was open. This area was blocked off by a transparent wall in the main game, but the hole can still be seen using shift lock.

docs.title: Honey Void
docs.text: Out of bounds past the Red HQ, towards a large green wedge outside the map, there is a hole. Upon entering the hole, there is a large expanse of flat land. This area, unofficially called the Honey Void, has its own music, known as Hibernation1.

docs.title: Bee Hibernation
docs.text: Something interesting is that bees also appear to freeze or go under hibernation when they first enter the area, as the name of the music suggests. It should be noted that this did not exist for a majority of this area's appearance in the game. However, the bees can occasionally unfreeze if the player goes near a corner, and freeze again as the reach the player.

docs.title: Strange Drawing
docs.text: Inside the Honey Void, there is a drawing of the game. It sits roughly in the middle of this area. It is completely two dimensional; therefore, it can only be viewed from the front. It depicts a Bear, Windy Bee, Vicious Bee, Coconut Crab, Onett with a Petal Wand and Petal Belt and Beekeeper's Mask, Basic Bee, King Beetle and Stick Bug.

docs.title: Vector Bee and Tadpole Bee Statues (Level 2)
docs.text: In the same area as the strange drawing in the honey void, there are two bee models of a Tadpole Bee and a Vector Bee. They cannot be interacted with.

docs.title: Windy Bee and Vicious Bee Statues (Level 2)
docs.text: If you go out of bounds to the right of the map, you will see a Vicious Bee and Windy Bee statue that are level 2. They cannot be interacted with.

docs.title: +5 Pollen Text
docs.text: This Easter Egg is located outside the map next to the Stump Field. Behind it, there is a text decal written "+5". Since it does not float near the ground, as the area around it does not have collision enabled, it may be necessary to use the glider tool to get close.

docs.title: Red HQ Room
docs.text: This room is hidden behind a wall in the Red HQ. When it was first added, the room had an unusable Red Extract dispenser. The room had a slight change in the 2021-12-26 update, and another change in the 2022-12-26 update. It cannot be accessed without the use of glitches.

docs.title: Red HQ Attic
docs.text: By going out of bounds, a hole on the back of the wall where Red HQ would be can be found. If you fly into it, then you will be inside of the Red HQ's attic.

docs.title: Egg
docs.text:
Eggs are a type of inventory item where the player drags into their hive to hatch a bee, can be donated to the Wind Shrine or are used to roll the Sticker Printer. They are also the items that help players start playing in the game. Eggs come in many different types, some offering chances at different rarities of bees, and some hatching a specific bee. Currently, a total of 6 (or 11 if counting the gifted variants) different types of eggs exist in the game, not including Plastic Eggs, specific bee eggs, the Flight of the Bumble Egg, or the Swarming Egg of the Hive.

Ever since the 2019-09-28 update, players do not need a vacant hive slot to hatch an egg. Now, players can hatch an egg on top of an existing bee to replace it. The level of the bee remains the same, acting like a Royal Jelly.

Please also note that due to regulations in the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Australia, any eggs in the Robux Shop won't be available to purchase for British, Dutch, Belgian, and Australian consumers. This restriction applies to most of the eggs in the shop.

docs.title: Basic Egg
docs.text:
The Basic Egg is the most common type of egg found in the game. It will almost always hatch into a Basic Bee (87% chance), but in rare cases, it can hatch into a Rare Bee (10% chance), an Epic Bee (2.5% chance), a Legendary Bee (0.5% chance), or into a Gifted Bee (0.4% chance), with a 0.348% (1 out of 287.35632184) chance of getting a Gifted Basic Bee from the egg. Mythic bees and Event bees cannot be hatched from this egg. This egg cannot be used on a Basic Bee.

Ways to obtain a Basic Egg:

  • First-time players receive a free Basic Egg in their inventory.
  • Purchasing from the Basic Egg Shop located near the Sunflower Field for a base price of 1,000 Honey and capping at 10,000,000 Honey. Every time the player purchases a Basic Egg, the price of the next Basic Egg scales up.
  • Adding the Round Basic Bee Sticker to the Sticker Stack rewards 1 Basic Egg.

docs.title: Silver Egg
docs.text:
The Silver Egg is a type of egg that will most likely hatch into a Rare bee (64.9% chance), but it has a small chance to hatch into an Epic bee (30% chance), a Legendary bee (5% chance), or a Mythic bee (0.1% chance). A Basic Bee or an Event bee cannot be hatched from this egg.

Ways to obtain a Silver Egg:

  • Purchasing from Ticket Tent for 50 Tickets each.
  • Purchasing from the Robux Shop for 100 Robux.
  • Finishing Black Bear's and Panda Bear's Silver Egg questline.
  • As a reward from Brown Bear's 25th quest.
  • Completing the 25th Sticker-Seeker quest rewards you 1 Silver Egg.
  • An extremely low chance of dropping from a Mantis (in increments of 1 or 5).
  • A low chance of dropping from the King Beetle and Tunnel Bear.
  • A low chance to drop from Rare Sprouts.
  • An extremely rare chance from leaves when collecting pollen in the Clover Field.
  • As a drop from a Festive Planter.
  • A rare chance to drop from stockings.
  • A rare reward from the Winter Memory Match.

docs.title: Gifted Silver Egg
docs.text:
A Gifted Silver Egg shares the same probabilities as a Silver Egg, but the egg will always hatch the bee into its gifted variant.

Ways to obtain a Gifted Silver Egg:

  • Defeating Tunnel Bear for the first time guarantees any type of gifted egg including a Gifted Silver Egg, but with lower chances of obtaining upon subsequent defeats.
  • As a reward for getting Top 25 in the Daily Top Legendary Bee Pollen Collectors by the end of a day.
  • Completing Black Bear's "Getting Stumped" quest.
  • Completing the 100th quest of the Sticker-Seeker Quest Machine rewards you 1 Gifted Silver Egg.
  • An exceptionally rare chance of dropping from werewolves.
  • A rare chance to obtain when defeating the Stump Snail.
  • An exceptionally rare chance of dropping from a Scorpion.
  • Drop from a Sticker Sprout

docs.title: Gold Egg
docs.text:
The Gold Egg is a type of egg most likely to hatch into an Epic bee (79% chance), but it has a chance to hatch into a Legendary bee (20% chance) or a Mythic bee (1% chance). A Basic Bee, Rare bee, or an Event bee cannot hatch from this egg.

5 Gold Eggs are required in order to craft the Honey Mask.

Ways to obtain a Gold Egg:

  • Purchasing from the Ticket Tent for 100 Tickets each.
  • Purchasing from the Robux Shop for 200 Robux each.
  • A rare reward from the Robo Bear Challenge.
  • A rare reward from the Extreme Memory Match.
  • In token form in the Werewolf's Cave, which is guarded by two cave monsters.
  • Completing Black Bear's and Panda Bear's Gold Egg questline.
  • As a reward from Brown Bear's 50th, 340th and 390th quest.
  • Completing the Sticker-Seeker Quest Machine's 50th quest rewards 1 Gold Egg.
  • Capturing Commando Chick 10 times.
  • A low chance of dropping upon defeating the King Beetle.
  • An extremely low chance of dropping upon defeating a Scorpion.
  • A rare chance to drop from Epic sprouts.
  • An extremely rare chance of dropping from leaves when collecting pollen in the Clover Field.
  • A rare drop from a Ticket Planter, Candy Planter, Red Clay Planter, Festive Planter, Pesticide Planter and Petal Planter.
  • A rare drop from the Stockings.
  • A low chance to drop from a Festive Nymph.
  • As a rare reward from the Winter Memory Match.

docs.title: Gifted Gold Egg
docs.text:
A Gifted Gold Egg shares the same probabilities as a Gold Egg, but the egg will always hatch the bee into its gifted variant. This type of egg cannot be applied to craft the Honey Mask.

Ways to obtain a Gifted Gold Egg:

  • Defeating Tunnel Bear for the first time guarantees any type of gifted egg, including a Gifted Gold Egg, but with lower chances of obtaining upon subsequent defeats.
  • As a reward for getting Top 25 in the Daily Top Epic Bee Pollen Collectors by the end of a day.
  • As a Playtime Grandmaster badge reward from donating tickets to the Wind Shrine.
  • Completing 50 Gifted Bucko Bee quests or 50 Gifted Riley Bee quests awards 1 Gifted Gold Egg.
  • Completing 275 Brown Bear quests awards 1 Gifted Gold Egg.
  • Completing the 150th quest of the Sticker-Seeker Quest Machine rewards 1 Gifted Gold Egg.
  • A very rare chance of dropping upon defeating the Stump Snail and the Coconut Crab.
  • An exceptionally rare chance to drop from mantis.

docs.title: Diamond Egg
docs.text:
The Diamond Egg is a type of egg that will most likely hatch into a Legendary bee (95% chance), but it has a rare chance to hatch into a Mythic bee (5% chance). A Basic Bee, Rare bee, Epic bee, or an Event bee cannot hatch from this egg.

5 Diamond Eggs are required in order to craft the Diamond Mask.

Ways to obtain a Diamond Egg:

  • A Diamond Egg token is located past the Bear Gate, under the platform where Onett stands on. The player can use a glider or a parachute and glide towards the token in front of Shadow Bear.
  • Purchasing from the Robux Shop for 400 Robux each.
  • Purchasing from the Ticket Tent for 400 Tickets each.
  • A rare reward from Robo Bear Challenge.
  • A rare reward from the Extreme Memory Match.
  • Completing Black Bear's Diamond Egg questline.
  • Completing Panda Bear's fifth star treat/ant quest, "Colossal Combat".
  • Completing Dapper Bear's tenth quest, "The Long Haul".
  • Completing Brown Bear's 75th and 525th quest.
  • Completing Sticker-Seeker Quest Machine 75th quest.
  • A rare chance of dropping upon defeating the Stump Snail, Diamond Aphids, King Beetle, Tunnel Bear, and Coconut Crab.
  • A very rare chance of dropping upon defeating Spiders, Mantises, and Werewolves.
  • A rare chance to drop from Legendary sprouts.
  • A guaranteed drop from Supreme sprouts.
  • An extremely rare chance of dropping from leaves while collecting pollen from the Clover Field.
  • A very rare reward from catching a meteor.
  • A rare drop from a Festive Planter.
  • A rare reward from Winter Memory Match.

docs.title: Gifted Diamond Egg
docs.text:
A Gifted Diamond Egg shares the same probabilities as a Diamond Egg, but the egg will hatch that bee into its gifted variant. This type of egg cannot be applied to craft the Diamond Mask.

Ways to obtain a Gifted Diamond Egg:

  • Defeating Tunnel Bear for the first time guarantees any type of gifted egg, including a gifted diamond egg, but with lower chances of obtaining upon subsequent defeats as mentioned above.
  • As a reward for being in the top 25 in the Daily Top Honey Gift Recievers.
  • As a Quest Grandmaster badge reward from donating Tickets to the Wind Shrine.
  • Completing 100, 250, 500, 750 and 1,000 Gifted Bucko Bee or Gifted Riley Bee quests awards one gifted diamond egg each.
  • Completing 425 Brown Bear quests awards one Gifted Diamond Egg.
  • Completing the Sticker-Seeker Quest Machine 200th quest awards one Gifted Diamond Egg.
  • An extremely rare chance of dropping upon defeating Tunnel Bear, Stump Snail, or the Coconut Crab.

docs.title: Mythic Egg
docs.text:
The Mythic Egg is a type of egg that will always hatch into a Mythic bee. The player cannot obtain any other type of bee from this egg besides a Mythic bee. (The player can obtain a Gifted Mythic bee from this egg, although it is very rare.)

Ways to obtain a Mythic Egg:

  • As a reward for getting Top 25 in the Daily Top Memory Matchers by the end of a day.
  • Purchasing from the Robux Shop for 1,200 Robux each (limited to 3 eggs per player).
  • Purchasing from the Ticket Tent for 2,500 Tickets each.
  • As a very rare reward from Robo Bear Challenge.
  • An extremely rare chance of getting from Extreme Memory Match.
  • Completing Black Bear's 75th quest, "Myth in The Making".
  • Completing Dapper Bear's 15th quest, "More Than Myth".
  • As a reward from Brown Bear's 100th, 200th, and 400th quests.
  • Completing the Sticker-Seeker Quest Machine 300th quest awards one Mythic Egg.
  • Capturing Commando Chick for the 50th time guarantees a Mythic Egg.
  • An extremely rare chance of dropping upon defeating the Stump Snail, Mondo Chick, and Coconut Crab. Mondo Chick has a higher chance to drop when defeated faster.
  • An extremely rare chance of dropping when catching a meteor.
  • A very rare drop from a Festive Planter.
  • Purchasing it for 500 Snowflakes and 100 Gingerbread Bears in Bee Bear's Catalog.
  • Completing Gummy Bear’s Goo Year’s Beacon quest during Beesmas 2025 rewards you 1 Mythic Egg and other items.

docs.title: Gifted Mythic Egg
docs.text:
A Gifted Mythic Egg shares the same probabilities as the Mythic Egg, but the egg will always hatch that bee into its gifted variant.

Ways to obtain a Gifted Mythic Egg:

  • As a reward for getting Top 25 in the Daily Top Rare Bee Pollen Collectors by the end of a day.
  • Completing 500 Sticker-Seeker Quest Machine quests.
  • A nearly impossible drop from the Robo Bear Challenge.
  • Buying it in the Bee Bear's Catalog for 10,000 Snowflakes and 150 Gingerbread Bears.

docs.title: Choose-A-Mythic Egg
docs.text:
A Choose-A-Mythic Egg allows the player to pick whichever Mythic Bee they want when hatched.

Ways to obtain a Choose-A-Mythic Egg:

  • Purchasing the Merry Mythic Mondo-Haul from the Robux Shop for 4,500 Robux

docs.title: Star Egg
docs.text:
The Star Egg is a type of egg that hatches into any type of gifted bee that is not already in the player's hive, aside from gifted Event bees. If the player already has all the different types of gifted bees in their hive besides gifted event bees, the egg will hatch into a random type of gifted bee instead. The egg will never hatch a gifted mythic bee until all other gifted non-event bees are in the hive.

Ways to obtain a Star Egg:

  • Defeating Tunnel Bear for the first time guarantees any type of gifted egg, including a star egg, but with lower chances of obtaining upon subsequent defeats.
  • Purchasing from the Robux Shop for 800 Robux each (limited to 5 eggs per player).
  • An exceptionally rare chance of dropping from a Mythic Meteor Shower.
  • Completing Mother Bear's first ten quests ("Seven To Seven" quest).
  • Completing Panda Bear's first ten star treat/ant quests ("Royal Rumble" quest).
  • An exceptionally rare chance to drop upon defeating the King Beetle.
  • An exceptionally rare chance of dropping from a Festive Planter.
  • As an exceptionally rare drop from the Party Mechsquito.
  • As an exceptionally rare drop from the Sticker Sprout.

docs.title: Specific Non-Event Bee Eggs
docs.text: Instead of hatching into a random bee of a particular rarity, specific bee eggs will always hatch into the egg's respective bee. All of these eggs share the same appearance of a basic egg.

docs.title: Bumble Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Bumble Bee Egg will always hatch into a Bumble Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Bumble Bee Egg:

  • As a drop from Rhino Beetle (Exceptionally Rare)

docs.title: Rascal Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Rascal Bee Egg will always hatch into a Rascal Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Rascal Bee Egg:

  • As a drop from Ladybug (Exceptionally Rare)

docs.title: Baby Egg
docs.text:
The Baby Bee Egg will always hatch into a Baby Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Baby Bee Egg:

  • As a drop from Tunnel Bear (Extremely Rare)

docs.title: Honey Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Honey Bee Egg will always hatch into a Honey Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Honey Bee Egg:

  • As a drop from Cave Monster (Uncommon)

docs.title: Fuzzy Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Fuzzy Bee Egg will always hatch into a Fuzzy Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Fuzzy Bee Egg:

  • By purchasing the Fuzzy Pack in the Robux Shop for 800 Robux. (Unobtainable)

docs.title: Tadpole Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Tadpole Bee Egg will always hatch into a Tadpole Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Tadpole Bee Egg:

  • Rewarded along with other rewards for giving Bubble Bee Man a Present during the Beesmas 2020 event.

docs.title: Bubble Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Bubble Bee Egg will always hatch into a Bubble Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Bubble Bee Egg:

  • Rewarded when completing BBM's Naughty List quest from Bubble Bee Man. (Unobtainable)

docs.title: Commander Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Commander Bee Egg will always hatch into a Commander Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Commander Bee Egg:

docs.title: Buoyant Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Buoyant Bee Egg will always hatch into a Buoyant Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Buoyant Bee Egg:

docs.title: Precise Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Precise Bee Egg will always hatch into a Precise Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Precise Bee Egg:

  • By purchasing the Precise Pack in the Robux Shop for 1,700 Robux. (Unobtainable)

docs.title: Music Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Music Bee Egg will always hatch into a Music Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Music Bee Egg:

  • By purchasing the Musical Mega-Bundle in Bee Bear's Catalog for 123 Gingerbread Bears.

docs.title: Gifted Bubble Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Gifted Bubble Bee Egg will always hatch into a Gifted Bubble Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Gifted Bubble Bee Egg:

  • By completing Bubble Bee Man's Winter Beesmas 2024 quest.

docs.title: Gifted Carpenter Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Gifted Carpenter Bee Egg will always hatch into a Gifted Carpenter Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Gifted Carpenter Bee Egg:

  • By purchasing the Carpenter's Crafting Pack in the Robux Shop for 400 Robux during Winter Beesmas 2024 (expired March 31, 2025).

docs.title: Gifted Diamond Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Gifted Diamond Bee Egg will always hatch into a Gifted Diamond Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Gifted Diamond Bee Egg:

  • By purchasing the Starry Night Special in the Robux Shop for 1,700 Robux during Winter Beesmas 2024 (expired March 31, 2025).
  • By purchasing the Snow Queen Bundle for 11.111 Snowflakes from Bee Bear's Catalog.

docs.title: Gifted Exhausted Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Gifted Exhausted Bee Egg will always hatch into a Gifted Exhausted Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Gifted Exhausted Bee Egg:

  • By purchasing the Night-Before Bundle for 10 Gingerbread Bears from Bee Bear's Catalog.

docs.title: Gifted Frosty Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Gifted Frosty Bee Egg will always hatch into a Gifted Frosty Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Gifted Frosty Bee Egg:

  • By purchasing the Super Snowman Bundle for 800 Snowflakes from Bee Bear's Catalog.

docs.title: Re://:Swarm Bee Eggs
docs.text: Every bee has its own egg, jelly and Gifted egg. These use the Basic Egg and Royal Jelly icons.

docs.title: Crimbolt Bee Egg
docs.text:
Always hatches into a Crimbolt Bee and also gives 1 Crimbolt Bee Jelly.

  • A rebirth reward at Rebirth 34. See Rebirths.
  • The reward for Sun Bear's last Crimbolt quest, "Crimbolt's Final Test".

The game also has a Gifted Crimbolt Bee Egg, which always hatches into a Gifted Crimbolt Bee, but nothing gives it yet.

docs.title: Painter Bee Egg
docs.text:
Always hatches into a Painter Bee and also gives 1 Painter Bee Jelly.

  • A rebirth reward at Rebirth 35, from Dapper Bear's "Premium Clientele" rebirth quest.
  • Redeeming a Painter Bee Voucher (one per account).

docs.title: 1st Edition Painter Bee Egg
docs.text:
Always hatches into a 1st Edition Painter Bee. It also gives a 1st Edition Painter Bee Jelly, so the bee can never be lost.

docs.title: 1st Edition Mortar Bee Egg
docs.text:
Always hatches into a 1st Edition Mortar Bee. "Only ever sold in the Mortar Bee Pack."

  • The Mortar Bee Pack in the Robux Shop, once per player.

docs.title: Specific Event Bee Eggs
docs.text: Event bee eggs are a special type of egg that will always hatch into a specific type of Event bee. After an Event bee egg is hatched, the player will receive an exclusive type of permanent royal jelly for that specific Event bee. The Event bee royal jelly will turn any bee into that kind of Event bee. It cannot be applied if the player currently has that Event bee in their hive though. And instead of hatching into a random bee of a particular rarity, specific event bee eggs will always hatch into the egg's respective event bee. All of these eggs share the same appearance of the basic egg.

docs.title: Bear Bee Egg
docs.text:
The Bear Bee Egg will always hatch into a Bear Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Bear Bee Egg:

  • A Bear Bee Egg can be obtained in the Robux Shop for 800 Robux This once cost 1,000 Robux, and on the game's release and certain events, it was reduced to 650/600 Robux for a short while (discount expired January 2, 2019). You can also obtain a Bear Bee Voucher from players who have bought the Bear Bee Egg.

docs.title: Cobalt Bee Egg

The Cobalt Bee Egg will always hatch into a Cobalt Bee (100%)

Ways to obtain a Cobalt Bee Egg:

The Crimson Bee Egg will always hatch into a Crimson Bee (100%)

This could once get received from completing all of Bee Bear's quests during his first visit, and it could once have been bought from the Festive Bee Pack for 800 Robux.

The Puppy Bee Egg will always hatch into a Puppy Bee (100%)

docs.title: Vicious Bee Egg

The Vicious Bee Egg will always hatch into a Vicious Bee (100%)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Digital Bee, Vicious Bee, Windy Bee, Bear Bee and Gummy Bee Eggs are the only types of Event bee eggs that could or can be obtained without spending Robux or Tickets. (A Bear Bee Egg can be obtained by redeeming a Bear Bee Voucher.)
  • Star Eggs and Basic Eggs are the only two eggs that can hatch into a Basic Bee(Gifted variant if Star Egg)
  • Plastic Eggs, the Flight of the Bumble Egg (Egg Hunt 2019), and the Swarming Egg of the Hive (Egg Hunt 2020) are the only types of eggs that do not hatch into a bee.
  • Any kind of specific bee egg and event bee egg will have the same icon as a Basic Egg in the inventory.
  • The Bear Bee, Festive Bee, Puppy Bee, Windy Bee, and Digital Bee Eggs are the only type of Event bee eggs that can or could be obtained directly by spending robux. However, as of now, Bear Bee is the only event bee that can be obtained directly by Robux
  • Basic Eggs are the only type of eggs that can be obtained directly with honey.
  • The star that appears on the Star Egg is slightly larger than the stars on the other types of gifted eggs.
  • The Mythic Egg is the only type of egg with the name of the bee rarity that it hatches into.
  • The Mythic Egg is also the only egg that has a 100% of hatching into a certain bee rarity (except for Event bee eggs and specific bee eggs). However, before mythic bees were added, Diamond Eggs used to have a 100% chance of hatching into a Legendary bee.
  • The Diamond and Basic Eggs are the only non-specific or event eggs that can hatch into a bee of their name (the Diamond and Basic Bees, respectively), though you can get other bees from these eggs.
  • The Mythic Egg is also the only egg with a letter on it.
  • The Choose-a-Mythic Egg is the only egg that allows the player to choose which bee hatches.
  • The Fuzzy Bee, Buoyant Bee, and the Precise Bee Eggs are the only (non-event) specific bee eggs that could have been bought from the Robux Shop.
  • The Gifted Silver Egg and the Star Egg are the only Gifted eggs that can be obtained by completing the main questlines from NPCs (Black Bear's "Getting Stumped", Mother Bear's "Seven To Seven", and Panda Bear's "Royal Rumble").
  • The player cannot hatch a specific bee egg on that specific bee. For example, a Bumble Bee Egg cannot be hatched on a Bumble Bee.
  • Even though Basic Eggs don't guarantee a Basic Bee, they still can't be used on Basic Bees.
  • The Basic Egg and Choose-A-Mythic Egg are the only eggs without gifted variants of themselves, excluding specific bee eggs.
  • Similarly, the Star Egg is the only gifted egg without a regular variant.
  • The Bubble Bee Egg is the only non-Event specific bee egg that can be obtained from a quest (B.B.M's Naughty List).
  • The Tadpole Bee Egg is the only egg that can be obtained by giving an NPC present (obtained specifically from Bubble Bee Man).

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

docs.title: Emoticons
docs.text: Emoticons are a mechanic for showing a bee's mood. The mood can affect how much bond a bee gets when it collects pollen[1], bee movespeed[1], and can even enable some bees to find certain stickers when collecting. It does not affect other stats, such as pollen collection rate or honey conversion speed.

docs.title: Bee Moods
docs.text:
A bee will express happiness if it is fed a treat or if it is working (or most recently was working) in a field that it likes. Bees gain extra bond from gathering when working in a field they like and also move slightly faster than usual[1]. Precise Bee will also express happiness when it shoots all the targets during its Target Practice ability.

A bee will express unhappiness if it is working in a field it dislikes or if the last field it worked in was one it dislikes. Bees gain less bond from gathering in fields they dislike, but do not move slower than usual.

docs.text:
"Always gives a bee an Energy Mutation."

The Energized Atomic Treat is a treat that always gives a bee an Energy mutation. It works like an Atomic Treat, but the mutation is always Energy instead of a random one.

docs.title: Energy
docs.text:
Energy represents the number of times a bee will gather pollen from a flower, sip nectar, and attack mobs before returning to the hive to rest. Each action costs one energy. Spawning Ability Tokens does not use up energy. The energy of all bees in a hive can be increased with stacks of Polar Power from Polar Bear's quests, certain mutations, certain Beequips or by leveling up bees.

It takes 30 seconds for a bee to rest and recover all its energy in the hive. However, there are some exceptions. Shocked Bee takes a lesser time to sleep, as well as Exhausted Bee and Photon Bee never sleeping at all. However, if the player dies or resets all bees will return to the hive to sleep regardless of any buffs, and they sleep for 30 seconds except Shocked Bee who sleeps for only 15 seconds.

When a bee runs out of energy, a message will appear, stating, [Type] Bee is out of energy! It's going to sleep.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The bees with the highest finite energy are the Lion Bee and Buoyant Bee.
  • There was a glitch where the energy of a bee would go to an absurd amount if the player used a Royal Jelly on an Exhausted Bee or Photon Bee.
  • There was glitch where dying twice in quick succession caused the player's bees to go to sleep and recover energy, instead of just the 30 second cooldown after death. This included Photon Bee and Exhausted bee, likely due to them not actually having "infinite" energy. This has been patched.
  • Exhausted Bee's base energy is set to 999,999,999,999.
  • Photon Bee's base energy is set to 999,999,999,999,999.

docs.title: Enzymes
docs.text:
Enzymes

"Grants +10% Instant Conversion and x1.25 Convert Rate for 10 minutes."

COOLDOWN

10 minutes

Enzymes are an inventory item that was added in the 2018-11-25 update. When used, it grants +10% Instant Conversion and x1.25 Convert Rate for 10 minutes when activated. Using another Enzymes will not stack them, but will reset the timer. Enzymes can also be used for crafting other accessories or items. Using a Super Smoothie will override the buff.

docs.title: Eviction
docs.text:
Eviction is still in the game's item list, but no shop sells it right now, so it can't be bought.

Eviction Description "Removes a bee from the hive." Cost 50,000 Honey

The Eviction was an inventory item that used to be purchasable in the Mountain Top Shop for 50,000 Honey. When used, it removed a bee from the hive. It was the cheapest item available at the Mountain Top Shop before being removed.

Evictions were mainly used to remove bees and replace them with eggs if the player couldn't afford a Hive Slot, taking note that eggs could not be placed on hive slots with a bee in the game version that had evictions.

Evicting a bee would completely reset the hive slot, meaning that the bee's bond, level, and gifted status, would be reset, so if a new egg were hatched, the new bee would have started at level 1. The previous bee will not affect the bee type or gifted status of the new bee.

All evictions that anyone might have had will no longer be in their inventory.

docs.title: Way(s) To Obtain
docs.text:
There are currently no methods to obtain the Eviction, as it has been removed from the game.

The methods below are no longer possible.

  • Purchasing an Eviction in the Mountain Top Shop for 50,000 Honey.
  • Finishing Bubble Bee Man's Beesmas 2018 quest 'B.B.M. Mission' rewarded 800 Evictions and other items.

docs.title: Removal Reason
docs.text:
As of the 2019-09-28 update, the player can now use eggs on existing bees, removing the need to evict bees, while also allowing a bee to keep its level. Thus, Onett removed the Eviction from both the shop and every player's inventory.

docs.title: Trivia

• Exhausted Bee's energy is set to 999,999,999,999.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: As with practically anything, some questions come up over and over as more people discover the game.

docs.title: How do I cut the vines by the Wealth Clock?
docs.text: You need to have either the Clippers, Scissors, or Scythe equipped and then walk up to the pad in front of the vine and press "E" to cut the vines. You can then enter the area behind the vines with whatever tool you want.

docs.title: How do I get a spirit petal?
docs.text: For every 10 Spirit Bear quests, Spirit Bear will give you a spirit petal. There are 30 quests in all, meaning you can get 3 spirit petals.

docs.title: How do I get a Windy Bee?
docs.text:
There are two ways. One way was to purchase it from the Robux Shop for 800 Robux before Beesmas 2019 began. The other way is to get a spirit petal from Spirit Bear's quests, donating it to the Wind Shrine, and then donating cloud vials to (hopefully) obtain a Windy Bee (Note: all items increase the chance of you getting Windy Bee, and it will most likely take you a long time to get it – see Favor).

You do not need to donate a spirit petal to start increasing your chance of getting Windy Bee, you increase the chance anytime you donate an item to the Wind Shrine. You just have to donate a spirit petal to be able' to have the chance to get Windy Bee.

docs.title: How do I get a translator?
docs.text: Finish Science Bear's new quests.

docs.title: Who should I give my translator to?
docs.text:
It is commonly recommended to give your translator to either Gifted Riley Bee or Gifted Bucko Bee. Stick Bug should be last, because the quest bees have good rewards and other players/Onett can summon Stick Bug. Depending on whether you're a better red pollen collector or blue pollen collector, your first translator should go to the color you specialize in. Give it to Gifted Riley Bee if you are better in red, and Gifted Bucko Bee in blue. This is so you can start doing the easier quests for you and get rewards. If you're balanced in both red and blue pollen, give the translator to Gifted Riley Bee, as its quests may reward stingers, an item that is very useful for acquiring Vicious Bee and the Demon Mask.

Your second translator should go to the other bee that you didn't choose. For example, if you gave your first translator to Gifted Riley Bee, you would be recommended to give it to Gifted Bucko Bee. This is so you can get started on the other quests for more rewards.

As mentioned above, your last translator should go to Stick Bug. Stick Bug should be last, because it isn't as rewarding as the two bees. The Stick Bug Challenge periodically starts because of Onett, and other players can summon it as well if they gave a translator to Stick Bug, so giving the translator to Stick Bug will not make a big difference in terms of gameplay.

docs.title: How do I start the Stick Bug Challenge?
docs.text: First, get a translator, then go talk to the Stick Bug on top of the mushroom. (You'll need a Parachute or Glider, but if you don't have either of those, you're probably not at a high enough level to challenge Stick Bug.)

docs.title: Which Event bee should I get first?
docs.text: The general consensus is to get Tabby Bee first, because the sooner you start collecting Tabby Love, the sooner your Tabby Bee will reach the maximum level. Photon Bee is usually agreed to be the next priority. After that, it becomes a matter of how many bees you have, what colors they are, and which quests are you on, so there is no one-size-fits-all guideline.

docs.title: Should I get the Scythe or the Bubble Wand?
docs.text:
This is a matter of opinion. In terms of absolute numbers based on the pollen collector alone, the Bubble Wand has a slight edge, but that's not the whole story. The right answer for you will depend on multiple factors, such as: Do you have more red bees or more blue bees? Do you prefer collecting pollen in a line or in a circle? Are you on a quest for a large quantity of red pollen? Some people get both tools, using one for red fields and the other for blue fields (and whichever one they happen to have equipped for white/neutral fields).

Note that as you get more bees, your pollen collector starts making less and less difference, because you'll be getting most of your pollen from stacked bombs or critical hits.

Special note about goo: most people find the Scythe works better for collecting goo, because the Bubble Wand's collecting circle is bigger than many goo puddles, so it misses most of the goo.

docs.title: How do I get that royal jelly/ticket that's [insert location here]?
docs.text: Check out the pages on royal jelly and tickets.

docs.title: What is today's code?
docs.text: There's no such thing as "today's code". Codes are issued when Onett deems fit, which is generally not a daily occurrence. ("Monthly" or "yearly" is closer to the truth.) If you've heard that there's a new code, check out the Codes page. If you're not a registered user, make sure to click both of the refresh links in the white box at the top of the page — otherwise, you'll get yesterday's page. Heck, even if you are a registered user, the refresh links can't hurt.

docs.title: There's a new code and I don't see it on the page! How do I add it?
docs.text: We've restricted the Codes in order to prevent misinformation from spreading. If you don't see the code or noticed something wrong, first double check by refreshing the page (in case it hasn't updated yet). If not, please reach out to any active wiki staff and we'll fix it as soon as possible!

docs.title: How long do I have until an Event Bee disappears?
docs.text: There are currently no plans to remove any of the Event bees. "Event Bee" does not mean "temporary"; it just means you can't get this bee through ordinary eggs or royal jellies.

docs.title: How do I access the Test Realm?
docs.text: You must be in Onett's Testing Group to join the Test Realm when it is open. Only Onett approves new members of the group. He tends to only approve new members when he is testing a new update.

docs.title: I used a royal jelly on a bee and the new rarity was worse. Shouldn't it have upgraded?
docs.text: No; the probabilities for royal jelly don't change depending on what bee you're applying it to. Even if you use royal jelly on an Event bee, it will more than likely turn into a Rare bee.

docs.title: If I use a royal jelly on a bee, will it reset the level?
docs.text: Royal jelly only transforms the type of the bee, not its level, so the new bee will still be level 7. It's also very important to remember that Gifted status is part of the type, so it does reset if you use a royal jelly.

docs.title: If I use a royal jelly on Tabby Bee, will my Tabby Love stack reset?
docs.text: No, your Tabby Love will be saved, so it's safe to use royal jelly on Tabby Bee.

docs.title: Whoops, I accidentally deleted my event bee. How do I undo it?
docs.text: Event Bees come with a special royal jelly that will turn any bee into the event bee in question. Note that you can only have one of each type of event bee in your swarm at the same time, so the only use for the special royal jelly is to recover from precisely this situation, i.e. getting your event bee back after converting it.

docs.title: Whoops, I accidentally deleted my gifted bee. Help?
docs.text: Sorry, there's no way to undo this. The same thing applies with mutations.

docs.title: Why is there a "1st" flag on my event bee?
docs.text:
Main article: First Edition Bee

It means that your bee is a 1st edition. Bear Bees bought during the first month of the game's release, Gummy Bees obtained from Gummy Bear's quests, and Tabby Bees bought when it was first put on sale in the Ticket Tent are all first editions.

docs.title: There's a player stuck in my hive! He never moves, and I can't read their name.
docs.text: You're in hive #6, aren't you? That's the Onett statue from on top of the hives. (Onett is the game's creator.) Sometimes, he falls down and lands in odd places, like in the honeycomb of hive #6. You should be able to just play as if he weren't there - your bees will ignore him, and the hive will still be functional.

docs.title: Do the royal jellies or tickets hidden around the map ever respawn?
docs.text: Nope, sorry, they're a one-time-only thing.

docs.title: Where do I report bugs?
docs.text:
First, check that your bug doesn't appear on this page or the Known Glitches page. Next, do the Roblox equivalent of turning it off and back on again: leave the game and come back. (Important: don't reset your character! Actually close the game window and then open the game again.) Is the bug still there?

If it is still majorly affecting your gameplay, it would be sufficient to report the bug through the bug report form.

docs.title: What conventions should I follow when editing?
docs.text: See the Editing Guidelines and Manual of Style page.

docs.title: I'm just getting started. What should I do?
docs.text: Fandom has already a complete and user-friendly answers for editors who are just started to join Fandom. Click here to have a basic knowledge about Fandom.

docs.title: I know about the basics. But how do I add some links and photos?
docs.text: If you already know about the basic knowledge of the Visual Editor, this page will help you about accessing Source Editor efficiently and adding media like photos and videos.

docs.title: How do I get an Admin/Moderator position on this wiki?
docs.text: If you would like to become an admin/mod, you must first display qualities that befit those positions, be helpful and considerate to other users, and have little to no actions taken against your account. Then, staff may notice you and consider giving you those roles.

docs.title: The page is too long. Is there any faster way to do this?
docs.text: Yes, there is. In fact, our staff already had a page that compiles all the wiki coding in one page. It's called FAQ/Wiki Code. This page also has information about our templates. With this, you have the knowledge not only for basic wikitext formatting, but also the templates.

docs.title: I saw a vandal. What should I do?
docs.text: There are two ways to remove the vandal: manually remove the edit by yourself, or report to the staff. To remove an edit yourself, go to the history section of the page (or add '?action=history'), then go to the previous edit, and undo the edit. To report it to the staff, post a message on the wall of any of the admins or moderators (see the list in the sidebar of the main page) with a link to the vandalized page and/or the profile page of the offending user.

docs.title: Festive Bean
docs.text:
Festive Bean

"Plants a Festive Sprout in the field you're standing in."

COOLDOWN

2 hours

A Festive Bean is a special variant of the Magic Bean that always plants a Festive Sprout in a field. When harvested, it grants Tickets, crafting materials, and unique tokens that are commonly found in festive gifts in abundant quantities. There is a 120-minute (2-hour) cooldown between planting Festive Sprouts. Only the player who planted can receive the Festive Blessing and Beesmas Cheer buffs to avoid overuse. When a player plants a Festive Sprout, the following message appears, reading: "🌱 {Username} has planted a Festive Sprout 🌱

Festive Bee is a Red Event bee. It can be purchased in the Ticket Tent for 500 Tickets.

docs.title: Festive Nymph
docs.text:
Not to be confused with Stick Nymphs, the standard version of this mob.

The Festive Nymph is a variant of Stick Nymph that can be summoned by Stick Bug during the Stick Bug Challenge. Festive Nymphs are only available after finishing Stick Bug's Beesmas quest during Beesmas 2020 and beyond: Stick Bug's Nymph Hats. Other players could attack and collect rewards from Festive Nymphs. (The player who started the challenge must complete Stick Bug's quest first, otherwise no Festive Nymphs will appear.)

Festive Nymphs followed the player closest to them and deal damage if they have touched a player, like their regular counterparts. Despite their low stats, Festive Nymphs, along with the Stick Nymphs, would usually be summoned in large groups, often outnumbering players.

docs.title: Drops
docs.text:

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Like Stick Nymphs, Festive Nymphs can follow players out of the field they were in and can either be gone through or be obstructed by some objects. They can also go into certain locations such as the King Beetle's Lair and get into spots where they couldn't reach the player. This allowed the player to exploit them and deal damage from afar.
  • Just like Mondo Chick and the stick nymphs, they lose health every second; Mondo Chick always loses 333 health per second, but Festive Nymph and Stick Nymph's health depletes faster when their level is higher. It is possible for them to be defeated naturally unlike Mondo Chick who would have 300 health left after 15 minutes. They would drop rewards regardless if they have been attacked or not.
  • Onett has also summoned the Stick Bug Challenge with Festive Nymphs.
  • Festive Nymphs are unable to jump, so if the player got higher than the Festive Nymph's hitbox, they would not be able to damage them.
  • Festive Nymphs and Stick Nymphs are the only mobs that can be summoned by another mob.
  • These are two of 18 mobs that cannot spawn naturally, as in the player cannot simply walk in a field and fight it, the other mobs being the five types of Ants, Snowbear, Stick Bug, the five Robo Bear Challenge Mobs, and the four Robo Party mobs.

The Festive Planter is a Beesmas-exclusive single-use planter added in the 2021-12-26 update. Alone, it grows in 4 hours of playtime and stores 250,000 pollen. A player can store up to 100 Festive Planters at a time, and up to 3 planters can be planted at once.

docs.title: Growth, pollen and nectar
docs.text:
• Grows in 4 hours of playtime.
  • Glitter used in its field speeds it up: x1.5 for one, rising in halving steps up to x2 at 6 stacks. The stacks stay on the planter until it is harvested.
  • Holds 250,000 pollen at full growth. A harvest gives capacity × growth × pollen bonus. It has no pollen bonus.
  • Nectar multipliers: x3 Satisfying, x3 Comforting, x3 Invigorating, x3 Motivating, x3 Refreshing. On harvest it gives one Nectar type from its field, lasting grow time × growth × multiplier × 3 seconds.
  • Up to 3 bees can sip from it at once.

docs.title: Puffshrooms
docs.text:
When it reaches 95% growth, it has a 10% chance to smoke and spawn 3 Puffshrooms (one at the planter and two nearby) at levels 1 to 2.

They are always Common.

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Realistic max is the best you can expect to actually see: the most picks of that upgrade that about 1 in 1,000 fully waxed 5 ★ beequips get, each at its top value. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

docs.title: Field Boost
docs.text:
A Field Boost is a stacking buff that provides a bonus to pollen gained, from all sources, from a specific field. Each stack of a field boost increases pollen gained from its field by 100% and has a limit of 400% or x4. Unlike field winds, which last for 30 minutes, field boosts last for 15 minutes, regardless of the source.

Field boosts are obtained through the following methods:

  • Using the Field Booster, Red Field Booster, Blue Field Booster,
  • Using the Coconut Dispenser (only boosts the Coconut Field).
  • Using Glitter.
  • Giving Presents to NPCs during the Beesmas 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2024 and 2025 events.
  • Using Field Dice, Smooth Dice or Loaded Dice.
  • Redeeming certain codes.

Multiple sources of field boosts can be used to reach much higher stacks. With each application, the multipliers add up and the duration resets back to 15 minutes. Thus, it is possible to get a boost from a field booster, use it until there are only a few seconds left, then activate an item that gives a boost for that same field to get another 15 minutes of boosting, such as codes, glitter, and field dice. This time at a higher multiplier and be repeated once again to reach an even higher multiplier. Field boosts stack up to four times.

A field that has been boosted by a field booster or field dice gives off white sparkles. If the player leaves the game and comes back while a boost is still active, the boost in pollen will still be there, but the field will no longer sparkle.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Sometimes, the field glitches after the boost is gone and keeps sparkling. This is a purely visual bug, meaning that the boost is not active.
  • Field boosts used to stack up to x10, but after the 2019-04-05 update, it was nerfed to x5. After that, it was nerfed to x3 in the 2019-09-28 update, but it was buffed to x4 in the 2021-12-26 update to help compensate for the Jelly Beans nerf.
  • If the player redeems certain codes that give a field boost that is x5 or more, it will only give the player a x4 boost.
  • The old icon for field boosts was simply an image of grass placed on a background with a color that corresponded to that of the boosted field.
  • The Ant Field cannot be boosted using glitter, field dice, or field boosters. Trying to boost the Ant Field will result in a message that says, "You can't boost a challenge field."
  • Based on an unused icon representing this field, it's likely that the plan was for it to be possible to boost at an unknown update before the idea was scrapped.
  • Field buffs from codes grant the player field boosts along with increased field capacity.
  • The field boost icon of the Hub Field is the only icon out of any field boost icon to not be outlined in gray.
  • The field boost icon for the Hub Field is also the same image as the Hub Field Stamp Sticker.
  • Smooth Dice and Loaded Dice can produce more than 1 field boost at a time, being the only items which can do so.

docs.title: Field Booster
docs.text: The Field Booster is a booster that provides a field boost to a random field that is either colorless or has no primary color (mixed fields) for 15 minutes. The machine is located beyond the Lion Bee Gate, between the Mountain Top Shop and the Ticket Shop. In order to use it, the player needs to have discovered 20 bee types. The cooldown is 45 minutes.

docs.title: Boosts
docs.text:
• Sunflower Field: +300% pollen
  • Dandelion Field: +300% pollen
  • Spider Field: +200% pollen
  • Clover Field: +200% pollen
  • Pineapple Patch: +200% pollen
  • Pumpkin Patch: +200% pollen
  • Cactus Field: +100% pollen

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This is one of the three field boosters in the game, along with the Blue Field Booster and the Red Field Booster.
  • The Field Booster has the same design as the Red and Blue Field Boosters, the only difference being the colors and that it has a sign.
  • The Coconut Field and the Mountain Top Field cannot be boosted using the Field Booster, despite not being a specifically colored field.
  • Prior to the 2019-09-28 update, the player could access the booster without having 25 bees. They only needed to discover 25 bees to unlock the Red Cannon, which fires them to the Mountain Top Field. Since then, the player will now be teleported back to spawn due to it being an attempt to bypass a gate.
  • Prior to the 2019-09-28 update, the cooldown of the booster used to be 2 hours.
  • The Field Booster gives more pollen for fields that appear at the beginning of the game to compensate for their smaller flower sizes.
  • The Field Booster's model is a modified version of EndorsedModel's Teleport.
  • This is the only Field Booster to give a field boost of 200% today, as in the past, the Red Field Booster granted 200% Strawberry Field boost and the Blue Field Booster granted 200% Bamboo Field boost.

docs.title: Field Capacity
docs.text: Field Capacity is a mechanic that increases the player's Capacity Multiplier depending on what kind of field they are in. There are 2 types of field capacity: colored field capacity (shown as a stat) and field capacity for a specific field (shown as a buff).

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• Donating certain stickers to the sticker stack can grant field capacity.
  • Red Field Capacity can be obtained from Riley Bee's gifted hive bonus, the Demon Mask and Scorching Star.
  • Blue Field Capacity can be obtained from Bucko Bee's gifted hive bonus and Bubble Bloat (Bubble Bloat can only be obtained if the player has Pop Star passive on Supreme Star Amulet).
  • White Field Capacity can be obtained from Exhausted Bee's gifted hive bonus, the Gummy Mask and Gummy Star.
  • Coconut Field Capacity can be obtained from the Coconut Canister (x1.25).
  • Redeeming certain valid codes:
  • ThreeBeeVee (gives Mountain Top Field Code Buff, granting +100% Mountain Top Field Capacity).
  • Using certain Beequips that include a Field Capacity boost stat.
  • The Warm Scarf grants +1% to +3% Red and White Field Capacity.
  • The Pinecone grants +8% to +15% Pine Tree Forest Capacity.
  • The Snow Tiara grants +2% to +5% Blue Field Capacity and +3% to +5% White Field Capacity.
  • The Rose Headband grants 14% to +40% Rose Field Capacity.

docs.title: Colored Field Capacity Formula
docs.text:
The following formula shows how much capacity multiplier a player gets in a field:

Let x equal the colored capacity multiplier. Let y equal the percentage of that pollen type in the field.

Capacity multiplier in the field = \((x-1)\times \frac{y}{100}+1\)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Spider Field is the only field where the player is guaranteed to get 100% of a colored capacity bonus, specifically white field capacity.
  • This is achievable with Exhausted Bee's gifted hive bonus, by using the Gummy Mask, activating Gummy Star, the Warm Scarf's hive bonus, or the Snow Tiara's hive bonus.
  • The only opposite version of this is in the Mountain Top Field; it generates no white flowers and therefore doesn't give white field capacity.
  • It is also possible to get 100% of a colored capacity bonus on any other field if they generate entirely with one color of flowers, but the odds of a field generating like that is mathematically impossible.

docs.title: Field Dice
docs.text:
Field Dice

"Boosts a random field, granting +100% pollen for 15 minutes."

COOLDOWN

1 second

Field Dice is an inventory item added in the 2019-04-05 update. When used, It boosts a random field the player has access to, granting a +100% pollen Field Boost for that field for 15 minutes. If the player uses another field dice, or any other type of dice while a Field Boost from a dice is still active, the new field boost will override the old one, preventing the Field Boost from stacking up.

As of the 2021-12-26 Update, there are currently 3 types of dice in the game, those being Field Dice, Smooth Dice and Loaded Dice.

docs.title: Field Wind
docs.text:
A Field Wind is a stacking buff that grants a bonus to pollen and instant conversion to a specific field. Each stack of a field wind increases pollen gained from its field by a set amount depending on the field, and also gives 3% instant conversion to the field starting with a base of 25%. Field winds last for 30 minutes. Field winds are obtained by donating certain items to the Wind Shrine or using various codes. Field wind tokens from the Wind Shrine have a lifespan of 30 seconds.

With each application, the field winds stacks add up, and the duration resets to 30 minutes. If there's another code that gives a boost for that same field, this can be used to extend or reset the timer for another 30 minutes. The max stack for field winds is x15. Field winds can stack up to x15 if the item donated is rare enough and the player has enough favor.

Field winds can also be replenished with codes, for example, if the Wind Shrine and a code both grant field winds, it restarts the 30 minutes field winds timer.

Unlike its field boost counterpart, fields boosted with winds do not give off sparkles. However, the icons used to identify field winds are the same as field boosts, except they have a white background.

Lower level fields tend to have more field pollen than other fields.

Specific items donated to the Wind Shrine can give specific winds. For example, donating Pineapples makes it more likely to give Pineapple Field Winds. Below is a table containing which items correlate with which fields. Many of these are unknown, and fields with no text in the donation column means it is unknown.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Fields, also referred to as "patches" or "forests" are square/rectangular areas of flowers scattered around the map, where players are able to collect pollen, which can be converted into honey at their hive, or by other methods. There are a total of 23 different fields in the game, including those present in the Ant Challenge and Hive Hub. Each field consists of flowers, which come in three different colors: blue, red, and white. The flowers also vary each time a player joins a server based on how the field is generated. The more flowers in each square, the more pollen it gives and the faster it regrows; however, Fuzzy Bee or any bee equipped with a Poinsettia, Rose Headband or Lei can pollinate it and increase the number of flowers on a square. Guiding Star pollinates flowers when it hovers over a field. Diamond Drain also pollinates blue flowers. Fields can also spawn Honey and Treats in form of tokens.

docs.title: Fire Ant
docs.text:
Fire Ant Location Ant Field while the Ant Challenge is active.

A Fire Ant is one of five ants that are exclusively found in the Ant Challenge, past the Ant Gate.

This is the last Ant Challenge mob that the player will encounter. Fire Ants typically spawn in the later waves, such as after the first Giant Ant.

Fire Ants are colored red and act the same as Regular Ants, but they leave a damaging flame trail behind them as they move. The flames will linger even after the Fire Ant that left it is defeated. However, the fire disappears after a short amount of time.

A Fire Ant's level can increase depending on what wave of the Ant Challenge the player is on. They can range from level 1 up to level 16.

Fire Ants are one of the most threatening of the five ant types, as their flame trails can stack up on the field.

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
• Fire Ants move in predetermined straight lines and are quite slow. This enables to player to easily dodge any coming their way.
  • Standing near the Fire Ant will allow your bees to quickly target the Fire Ant to quickly deal damage and defeat it.
  • Focus on taking out Fire Ants first as they can make the field very hard to navigate without taking damage from their flame trails. This is especially true if there is a large amount of them on the field.
  • Fire Ants will come out in groups and they could overwhelm the player if they are collecting pollen quickly to advance to the next waves. Vicious Bee and Windy Bee provide excellent crowd control with their Impale and Tornado abilities which could greatly help counter the large amounts of Fire Ants landing on the field. Digital Bee can also stun many Fire Ants at once and allow them to take extra damage via Mind Hack.
  • The player can walk through the gap between the Ant Challenge's window and the field to avoid stepping over fire trails.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This is the only ant to have a second method of attack.
  • They have the same health per level as Regular Ants.
  • Noted by Panda Bear, the fire from a Fire Ant is not affected by defense, but this seems to be untrue. Addition, having 100% defense (through Emergency Coconut Shield) will nullify any damage altogether.

docs.title: Fireflies
docs.text:
Fireflies are passive mobs that only appear during nighttime. Individually, they produce sparkles on the flowers that they land on. Fireflies band together to generate various items for the player.

As soon as nighttime begins, a group of eight fireflies will spawn above the Star Hall. These fireflies will then fly to a random fields. Fireflies can fly to the Spider Field, Bamboo Field, Strawberry Field, Pineapple Patch, Cactus Field, or the Rose Field. Once they reach the designated field, they will land randomly in a circle, facing towards the center. Fireflies also spawn sparkles on the current flower they are on.

The player can chase a firefly from its position by walking close to it, forcing it to fly up. They will fly up if a player is within a three-flower radius. If a firefly is nudged away, the flower the firefly sat on will generate sparkles. When all eight fireflies are nudged away and fly up, the following might appear in the middle of the firefly formation:

Possible Drops Rarity Moon Charms Common, increments of 1, 5, 10 Glitter Rare Star Jelly Very Rare Night Bell Extremely Rare Star Treat 1/1,000,000[1] Waxing Crescent Moon Sticker Rare Glowing Smile Sticker Extremely Rare Star Signs Extremely Rare Cyan Star Sticker Exceptionally Rare Shining Star Sticker Exceptionally Rare

The fireflies will continue this cycle in one field three times, and afterward, will target a new field. This cycle repeats until daytime arrives. When daytime arrives, they will fly back above the Star Hall and eventually despawn.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The face of a firefly is the same decal that a Gummy Bee has, however the color of the latter's face is teal, whereas the former's is black.
  • Fireflies, frogs, Chicks, Hostage Chicks, Spotted Chicks, and Bean Bugs are the only passive mobs in the game.
  • Fireflies were the first passive mob introduced to the game.
  • Fireflies are also the only passive mobs to spawn exclusively at night.
  • If a player uses a Night Bell when a group of fireflies are leaving, another group will replace them. In an unknown update, the old group will come back instead of a new one.
  • Despite the fact there are eight fireflies, the Glowing Smile Sticker only shows seven "fireflies".

docs.title: First Edition Bee
docs.text:
A first edition bee is a designation given to certain Event bees bought or earned during their first release. This designation is represented by a white and yellow "1st" flag appearing on top of the bee, and the flag emits a sparkling effect. The flag is purely cosmetic and does not change or affect gameplay at all.

This designation is currently only available for Bear Bee, Tabby Bee, Gummy Bee, Puppy Bee, Festive Bee, Digital Bee, and Windy Bee.

If the player removes a first edition bee, the bee will retain its first edition status when added back to the hive.

docs.title: First Edition Bees
docs.text:
• Bear Bee: Bought during the first month after the game's launch (all First Edition Bear Bees got an additional bonus of being automatically gifted).
  • Tabby Bee and Puppy Bee: Purchased during the their respective release sales (half price).
  • Gummy Bee: Obtained after completing all of Gummy Bear's quests during the Gummy Invasion Event.
  • Festive Bee: Obtained after completing all of Bee Bear's quests during the Beesmas 2018 Event or obtaining it from the Festive Bee Pack for 1,600 Robux in the Robux Shop.
  • Windy Bee: Obtained as a special prize from the Wind Shrine or purchased in the Robux Shop for 800 Robux before October 27, 2019.
  • Digital Bee: Obtained from Robo Bear's Shop behind Robo Bear or by purchasing the Digital Bee Pack for 2,500 Robux in the Robux Shop during Beesmas 2022.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Onett has stated that the reason a First Edition Vicious Bee does not exist is because there is no room for a 1st Flag on its back with the spikes.
  • The earliest 1st Edition Bee was Bear Bee, coming in at the game's release.
  • Even though First Edition Bear Bees are automatically gifted, the gifted status can still be removed if a player adds it to the hive again.

docs.title: Flame
docs.text:
Not to be confused with the flame trail produced by Fire Ants.

Flames are objects that can be produced by certain tools, ability tokens, or passive abilities. Flames have a percentage chance to be spawned by certain bees when gathering, lasting for 4 seconds. Each second, the flames collect 5 red, 3 white, or 2 blue pollen from 9 surrounding flowers (+2% per red bee and +4% per gifted red bee if spawned by the player, +10% per bee level if spawned by a bee), deals 10 + (25% of base Bee Attack) damage per second to any mob (15 if spawned by the player), and grants the player flame heat.

Flames can be generated by the Scythe, Fire Bee, Demon Bee, Spicy Bee's Inferno, bees with the Bead Lizard or Electric Candle beequips, Fire Mask's Ignite passive, and Demon Mask's X-Flame passive.

Flames are used to help grow Scorching Stars.

docs.title: Flame Heat
docs.text: Flame Heat grants extra Red Pollen and Bee Attack starting at x1.2 Red Pollen and +5% Bee Attack Multiplier. The more flames around the player, the faster the Flame Heat grows up to a maximum of 20 seconds at x2 Red Pollen and +25% Bee Attack Multiplier. Flame Heat boosts Spicy Bee's Movespeed and gather speed and can also be consumed by Precise Bee to convert Pollen into Honey.

docs.title: Gathering Flames
docs.text:
The Gathering Flames passive gives a chance for a bee to spawn a flame while gathering pollen from a field. Gathering Flames+ gives a higher chance for a bee to spawn a flame.

There is a 35% chance (50% if gifted) for Fire Bees' Gathering Flames passive to spawn a flame while gathering, and a 65% (85% if gifted) chance for Demon Bees' Gathering Flames+ to spawn a flame while gathering.

The Gathering Flames passive chance can be increased with the Bead Lizard or Electric Candle beequip for individual bees.

  • A Bead Lizard gives from +9% Gathering Flames chance to +14% Gathering Flames chance.
  • An Electric Candle gives from +1% Gathering Flames chance to +5% Gathering Flames chance. Using waxes can increase the amount up to +25% Gathering Flames chance.

docs.title: Dark Flames
docs.text: Flames that are hit with Dark Scythe will be converted into dark flames, a dark violet version of normal flames which collects pollen from 13 surrounding flowers (instead of 9), deals 50% more damage, and grants dark heat and also normal flame heat. Dark flames also grant 33% more growth to Scorching Stars.

docs.title: Flame Stats
docs.text: There are multiple aspects of flames that can be improved by stats and modifiers.

docs.title: Flame Pollen
docs.text:
Flame Pollen is the amount of pollen that flames can collect. The player can check how much flame pollen they have in the system page.

Flame Pollen can be increased in a few ways:

  • The Demon Mask gives a x1.25 Flame Pollen multiplier.
  • Gifted Fire Bee gives a x1.25 Flame Pollen multiplier.
  • Beequips:
  • An Electric Candle gives from +5% Flame Pollen to +10% Flame Pollen for an individual bee. Using waxes can increase the amount up to 50% Flame Pollen.
  • An Electric Candle can give +1% Flame Pollen as a hive bonus. Using waxes can increase the amount up to 11% Flame Pollen.
  • Cog Amulets:
  • The Silver Cog Amulet can give up to +5% Flame Pollen.
  • The Gold Cog Amulet can give up to +8% Flame Pollen.
  • The Diamond Cog Amulet can give from +12% Flame Pollen up to +14% Flame Pollen.
  • The Supreme Cog Amulet can give from +15% Flame Pollen up to +20% Flame Pollen.
  • Stickers:
  • The Small Flame Bee Sticker gives +3% Flame Pollen.
  • The Dark Flame Sticker gives +3% Flame Pollen.
  • The Orange Swirled Marble Sticker gives +3% Flame Pollen.
  • Robo Bear Challenge:
  • Epic Upgrades:
    • Furnace: This upgrade gives x1.5 Flame Pollen.

docs.title: Flame Duration
docs.text: Flame Duration is how long flames will last. Flame Duration can be increased by Spicy Bee's gifted bonus (25% more time) and Gifted Spicy Bee's Flame Fuel ability (50% more time). In addition, Flame Fuel causes the flames to instantly convert 50,000 pollen plus 10% (+5% per Field Boost) of the hive's total convert amount.

docs.title: Instant Flame Conversion
docs.text:
Instant Flame Conversion is how much pollen collected by flames are instantly converted. It can be increased by a few ways.

  • The Fire Mask gives +50% Instant Flame Conversion.
  • The Demon Mask gives +50% Instant Flame Conversion.
  • A Scorching Star gives +50% Instant Flame Conversion.

docs.title: Other Improvements
docs.text:
Certain upgrades from the Robo Bear Challenge can be used to improve flames.

  • Epic Upgrades:
  • Furnace: This upgrade gives x1.5 Flame Duration and x1.5 Flame Damage.
  • Invert: This upgrade makes flames collect x4 pollen from blue flowers.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The maximum Flame Pollen a player can have is 380%. This can be achieved by having the Demon Mask (x1.25), Gifted Fire Bee (x1.25), a Supreme Cog Amulet (+20%), three Electric Candles (+33%), activating the Sticker Stack with certain stickers (+9%), and the Furnace upgrade (x1.5).
  • The exact amount is 379.6875% but it rounds up to 380%.
  • The maximum Instant Flame Conversion a player can have is 100%. This can be achieved by having the Fire Mask (+50%) or the Demon Mask (+50%) while having a Scorching Star (+50%).
  • The texture for flames were changed in the 2021-12-26 update. This was probably to help with the texture for dark flames.
  • Flames generated by another player's bees will appear dark red instead of yellow-orange.
  • Flames are the counterpart of bubbles.

docs.title: Flowers
docs.text:
Are you looking for Pollen or Leaves?

Flowers can be found in all fields. They can be interacted with using different sources to obtain pollen from and later be converted into honey. There are 5 flower sizes: single, double, triple, large, and star. Single, double, triple, large, and star flowers multiply pollen by 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 per harvest, respectively. This number can be increased with better tools, badges, ability tokens, field boosters, etc. They also have base total pollen amounts of 30, 45, 60, 75 and 90 respectively. Total pollen is how much pollen the player can get before the flower's pollen is depleted and the flower has to regrow. In addition, larger flowers grow at a higher rate than smaller ones. Sprinklers, Clouds and Bubbles can regenerate flowers while the pollen haze ability improves flower growth rate.

There are 3 different flower colors: white, red, and blue. Bees also have these colors, and red/blue bees that harvest flowers of the same color get 50% bonus pollen from it. Also, the color of the pollen plays a large role in many quests and bee abilities.

Sometimes, a flower patch might emit green leaves. Collecting pollen from that patch will either grant an item, a sticker, or spawn an aphid.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• There are decals of yellow flowers in Onett's inventory, but they have never made an appearance in the game itself. They were most likely scrapped during the game's development.
  • White flowers are the most common in the game, as practically all fields have white flowers. The only field that doesn't have white flowers is the Mountain Top Field.
  • The only field with exactly one color of flowers is the Spider Field, the color being white.
  • Stump Field is the only blue field to have red flowers.
  • The Ant Field, Stump Field, Mountain Top Field, Coconut Field, and Pepper Patch are the only fields with exactly one type of flower size (single for Ant Field, triple for the rest).
  • Star flowers glow during nighttime.
  • Ant Field flowers hold 50 pollen, plus 10 pollen per tier (up to 90 pollen).
  • Before the 2020-04-06 update, the flower designs were different, and the sizes were only small, double, and large.
  • If the player looks at a field from a nearly flat angle, the flowers will appear to turn to their corresponding colors.
  • Fuzzy Bee's abilities and passive ability, the Diamond Drain passive, the Guiding Star passive, and a bee with the Poinsettia or Lei Beequip are the only ways to pollinate flowers.
  • Blue flowers are stated by Black Bear to taste minty, with red flowers tasting spicy, and white flowers tasting neutral.

docs.text:
"Rerolls a Beequip's potential: 1 pot (38%), 2 pot (30%), 3 pot (20%), 4 pot (9%), or 5 pot (3%). Doesn't use a Wax slot."

Fluxite Wax is a wax added in the Painter Bee event. Using it on a Beequip rerolls that Beequip's potential. Unlike other waxes, it does not use up a wax slot.

docs.title: Flying Ant
docs.text:
Flying Ant Location Ant Field while the Ant Challenge is active.

Flying Ants are one of five mobs that is part of a family called ants that are exclusively found in the Ant Challenge, past the Ant Gate.

This is one of the first Ant Challenge mobs that the player will encounter, capable of appearing on the very first wave. Despite being able to appear on the first wave, Flying Ants usually start appearing at around the second or third waves.

Flying Ants are ants with wings and they will pursue the player. They have the ability to pounce on players from quite a distance are the fastest out of the five ant types. However, they also have low health, much lower than any other ant type.

A Flying Ant's level can increase depending on what wave of the Ant Challenge the player is on. They can range from level 1 up to level 16.

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
• Due to their quick speed, the player will need to react more quickly in order to dodge Flying Ants trying to pounce them.
  • Having bees that can produce Haste tokens can help the player gain more speed needed to maneuver around Flying Ants.
  • Flying Ants occasionally spawn in waves which could overwhelm the player. Vicious Bee and Windy Bee provide excellent crowd control with their abilities which could greatly help counter the large amounts of Flying Ants landing on the field. Digital Bee can also stun many Flying Ants at once and allow them to take extra damage via Mind Hack.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Supreme Ant Amulet resembles a Flying Ant.
  • Despite having "flying" in its name, it doesn't actually fly, but it simply jumps.
  • Flying could mean to move quickly in this context since the Flying Ant moves quite fast.

docs.title: Free Royal Jelly Dispenser
docs.text:
Free Royal Jelly Dispenser Information Usage Grants Royal Jellies based on the number of gifted bees in the player's hive Requirement(s) 1 Gifted Bee Cooldown 22 hours Location Star Hall

Not to be confused with the Royal Jelly Dispenser which requires tickets or the Royal Jelly Shop.

The Free Royal Jelly Dispenser is a dispenser that is located in the Star Hall. It requires at least 1 gifted bee type to redeem Royal Jelly and Haste+. The number of royal jellies the player receives is based on how many gifted bees they currently have in their hive. For example, if the player has 15 gifted bees, but two of them are the same gifted bee, they will still get 15 Royal Jellies.

This dispenser has a cooldown of 22 hours. Currently, players can get a maximum of 50 royal jellies per use with 50 gifted bees.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• While the Royal Jelly Dispenser grants a stack of 10× Haste, the Free Royal Jelly Dispenser grants Haste+ but is free.
  • Using this is one of the two only ways to get the Haste+ Buff, the other being certain codes.
  • Unlike the Royal Jelly Dispenser, which is limited to one Royal Jelly per use, the Free Royal Jelly Dispenser can give up to 50 Royal Jellies.
  • Unlike how the Free Ant Pass Dispenser or the Free Robo Pass Dispenser are directly next to their Ticket counterparts, the Free Royal Jelly Dispenser is not directly next to its ticket counterpart, the Royal Jelly Dispenser.
  • This, the Free Robo Pass Dispenser, and the Glue Dispenser are the only dispensers with a 22-hour cooldown, the longest in the game.
