docs.title: Hive Builder
docs.text:
Plan your hive. Pick a bee from the list, then tap a hive slot or drag across several to fill them. Tap a slot that already has that bee to remove it, or use the Eraser. With no bee picked, drag bees to swap them or out of the hive to remove them, and tap a bee to toggle gifted. Your hive is saved in the page link, so you can share it.

Use Copy code and Import code to move a hive to and from the game's Hive Layouts menu (Honeycomb Blueprint → Layouts). Hive codes only store bees and gifted.

The hive builder needs JavaScript.

docs.title: Hive Hub
docs.text:
Not to be confused with the Hub Field.

The Hive Hub is a unique location added in the 2024-01-12 update. It is inside the Hive Hub Portal, which is beyond the Ant Gate. It has several features, including a total of 36 hives for players to claim, the Public Sticker Board, the Sticker-Seeker, the Hub Field, a Beequip Storage chest, and Sticker Sprouts that spawns every 3 hours. The Hive Hub's purpose is to seek out opportunities to trade with other players and to craft the Sticker-Seeker, a tool that specializes in collecting stickers and unlocks the Sticker-Seeker's quests. The Hive Hub also has a field, aptly named the Hub Field, which instantly converts all pollen collected into honey, as well as flowers regrowing very often, so there is no need for Sprinklers. Bees do not spawn in the Hive Hub to reduce lag. In the Summer Beesmas 2024 event, an obby made out of circular platforms was added. At the end of the obby, you jump up onto a hexagonal platform which has two tokens: a Smooth Dice and a Red Balloon.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Sharing Jelly Beans is possible here. This makes it easy to share Jelly Beans for quests, the sharing buff, or other purposes.
  • Be aware that the Hive Hub isn't very well optimized (Re://:Swarm wasn't made to handle this much data at once), so it's best to have a decent device and set your graphics to 1 in order to avoid crashing and major framedrops.

docs.title: Restricted Items
docs.text:
The following items are not usable in the Hive Hub:

  • Sprinklers
  • Snowflakes
  • Stingers (This means that Star Saw cannot be activated here).
  • Cloud Vials
  • Field Dice, Smooth Dice, and Loaded Dice.
  • Whirligigs
  • Night Bells
  • Every type of balloon.
  • Every type of planter.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• During Beesmas, the hexagonal platform at the end of the obby in the Hive Hub has a Gingerbread Bear token.
  • In Summer Beesmas 2024, the Celestial Gift Box was on the hexagonal platform.
  • In Winter Beesmas 2024, the Speckled Gift Box was on the hexagonal platform.
  • Both Gift Boxes, along with the Gingerbread Bear token, have been removed after their respective Beesmas.
  • Placing a planter used to prompt, “Cannot use (type) Planter in Challenge”. This was fixed in an unknown update.
  • The Sticker-Seeker Quest Machine, Sticker Board, Gift Boxes, & other Hive Hub structures can be seen behind the Bee Swarm Mountain, beyond the TP barrier at the edge of the base plate on the main map.
  • It's possible to enter the Hive Hub without having 20 bees, since the 20 Bee Zone teleport barrier doesn't cover the left side of the area due to the teleport barrier never being increased after the area was expanded. Players can climb the wall to the left of the Ant Gate, then following the wall to the left, they need to jump down. They should find themself behind the Stinger Shop. After that, the player just needs to jump while hugging the wall in front of them, allowing them to gain enough height to be able to climb over the fence, and once they are climbing it, they can either climb over it or fit in the middle hole of the fence.
  • Alternatively, you can just join anybody who is in the Hive Hub directly from their profile without meeting the requirements.
  • Shortly before a natural Sticker Sprout spawns, the following message will be displayed: [🌱 A Sticker Sprout is about to spawn in (Public Server) Hive Hubs… 🌱 ]
  • All of the main machines/features of the Hive Hub are behind the entrance portal.

docs.title: Hive
docs.text:
The Hive is where the player's bees go to rest when they run out of energy, to convert pollen to Honey, or when the player dies. Upon joining a server, the player must first claim a hive by following a red arrow and pressing "E" (on laptop, PC, etc.), "X" (On Xbox), "Square" (on PlayStation) or tapping the "claim hive" button (Tablet, iOS, Android, etc.) to claim it. The player may hatch eggs and use Royal Jellies on hive slots to use them.

There are 6 hives in a server. A basic hive contains 25 slots for bees. The player can expand their hive by buying additional hive slots at the Mountain Top Shop. The maximum number of bees a hive can contain is 50, but the price of that many hive slots is quite high.

On top of the 6th hive, there is a statue of Onett, the game's creator. This statue can very rarely fall off and land in the rightmost hive.

Each bee's hive slot has the face of the bee icon in the bee's color. The background color of the hive slot is based on the bee's rarity; bronze for Common, white for Rare, bright yellow for Epic, aqua blue for Legendary, light purple for Mythic, and green for Event. If a bee is gifted, then a thin yellow glowing line will trace the hive slot border. If a bee is mutated, then the bee's level will turn a different color depending on the mutation.

The player can also customize their hive putting stickers on it, as well as changing the color of the hive using hive Skin Stickers, they may also change the appearance of their Cub Buddy by placing Cub Buddy Skin Stickers in their hive.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Once a player dies, all of their bees return to the hive to rest, but do not recover energy. This is to prevent abusing resetting to get all bees to max energy.
  • There was once a bug that could bypass this by resetting twice in a row, of which all the player's bees returned to the hive and recovered energy, and the energy would go back up to maximum. This could be abused if the player's best bee was out of energy. This bug has been patched; however, and attempting to do this won't recover their energy anymore.
  • The statue of Onett on the top of the 6th hive has 38217 pollen in his Port-O-Hive, which is a reference to a code with the reward of 5 Tickets.
  • The 2018-07-11 update introduced a glitch that when looking on another hive, it shows the wrong rarity. This is mostly patched, but still occasionally happens.
  • Prior to the 2018-11-25 update, there were only 5 hives in the game.
  • In the earlier days of Re://:Swarm, bee faces on hive slots were bigger and they also used to sparkle depending on what rarity the bee was. The rarer the bee, the more sparkles they would've emitted (excluding the Basic Bee hive slot).
  • The blue wall next to the leftmost hive wasn't solid after the 2019-04-05 update. Because of this, it was possible to bypass most of the gates without having the required number of bees. This was fixed in the following update.
  • According to Onett, this was for a test when he was developing the game. However, he forgot to make the wall solid after testing.
  • You can click on your bee's hive slot from any distance, as long as you click the face of the bee.
  • A username will appear in a different font on a hive if that user has the Wavy Festive Hive Skin, Wavy Doodle Hive Skin, or Icy Crowned Hive Skin equipped.

The Honey Bee Gate, also called the 15 Bee Gate, is a gate that requires 15 bees to be able to pass through. It is the third gate that the player should be able to access, ahead of the Brave Bee Gate and the Basic Bee Gate.

There are 4 different fields behind the Honey Bee Gate, being the Cactus Field, the Pumpkin Patch, the Pine Tree Forest, and the Rose Field.

It is given its name from the large Honey Bee located on top of it.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This gate has the highest number of fields behind it, which is four.
  • There were numerous ways to bypass the gate without 15 bees, but as of the 2019-09-28 update, it will always teleport the player back to spawn.
  • It has the second-most quest givers, at 4, with the Starter Zone beating it with 5.
  • This gate holds the ramp that leads to the Lion Bee Gate, also known as the 25 Bee Gate.
  • This gate has the most assets in it, with 19 of them.

Next to the Basic Bee Gate ramp (formerly)

Bee Prerequisites 15 bees

Honey Bee is a Quest Giver and one of the three permanent Quest Bees, the others being Gifted Riley Bee and Gifted Bucko Bee. Honey Bee is located on the rock near the Pine Tree Forest. Added in the 2019-02-01 Update, its original purpose was to give players something to do while the next update was being worked on, but it has now become a Permanent Quest Giver.

It doesn't require a Translator to give quests, making it different from the other quest-giving bees.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Fighting Stick Bug and Stick Nymphs and/or the Mondo Chick are very effective for completing its quests, as they spawn many honey tokens. Defeating normal mobs for their token rewards can also help with Honey Bee's quests.
  • Defeating many Wild Windy Bees is another way of completing this quest faster.
  • Farming sprouts is a viable way, as they spawn many honey tokens.
  • Coin Scatter is also an effective way of collecting honey tokens quickly.
  • Coin Scatter can be easily triggered by having multiple Stubborn Bees, Honey Bees, Carpenter Bees and Vector Bees.
  • Use Coin Scatter on fields where there aren't many decorations blocking them, such as the Mountain Top Field.
  • Catching coconuts and meteors produces many honey tokens.
  • Summoning a honeystorm is also an option.
  • Lower level fields such as the Sunflower Field spawn more honey tokens than higher-level fields such as the Mountain Top Field.
  • Have bees that can spawn honey gift tokens in your hive in order to complete the quests faster.
  • Using the Gummy Star passive would be effective as it spawns many honey tokens.
  • When the quest is finished, claim it ONLY when you're about to boost due to its 2x conversion.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This is the third bee-based NPC in the game. It is also first bee-based NPC that isn't in its gifted form, the second being the Digital Bee NPC.
  • Honey Bee is the only Bee Quest giver that you don't need a translator to talk to.
  • Honey Bee, Science Bear, and Polar Bear are the only quest givers to give a buff as a reward for finishing a quest.
  • Honey Bee, along with Gifted Bucko Bee, Gifted Riley Bee, Onett, Stick Bug, and Bubble Bee Man are the only non-bear quest givers.
  • In the Egg Hunt 2019 update, there was a Plastic Egg token hidden behind it.
  • It has been replaced by a ticket token granting 3 Tickets.
  • Honey Bee was one of the three quest givers that did not give an Egg Hunt quest, the others being Onett and Spirit Bear.
  • Honey Bee is the only NPC whose Beesmas quest affected another NPC's machine (Black Bear's Honey Wreath).
  • Honey Bee along with Spirit Bear are the only quest givers that can summon a Honeystorm.
  • According to Bee Bear, Bubble Bee Man can also summon honeystorms.[1]
  • Honey Bee is one of 3 NPCs who have moved place, the others being Bubble Bee Man and Gummy Bear.
  • Honey Bee's quests are the only repeatable quests which don't contain the NPCs name followed by a colon (:).
  • During Beemas 2021, there was an error with Honey Bee’s ornament that made the Bag of Honey ornament and buffs are not visible to the player. This bug has been fixed and all players who gave Honey Bee a present before 2022-01-06 were refunded.
  • Honey Bee is one of the 2 NPCs (the other being Science Bear) that require you to join the Bee Swarm Simulator Club in order to access the Club Dispensers and complete their quests. Its Beesmas quests require you to use the Honey Dispenser.
  • It used to be located next to the ramp leading to the Basic Bee Gate, but it was moved behind the biggest tree in the Pine Tree Forest in the 2020-06-06 Update.
  • It was possible to start the quest before the 2020-06-06 Update, and not have 15 bees when it moved, making the quest incompletable until you got 15 bees.
  • Honey Bee is the only Bee NPC who doesn't have a specific HQ since Gifted Bucko and Gifted Riley represent the Blue and Red HQ respectively and there is currently no Colorless HQ.

The Honey Dipper is a tool available to be bought in the Pro Shop.

Crafting Ingredients 1,500,000 Honey

It collects 2 pollen from 49 surrounding patches in 0.9 seconds, which comes to a base pollen collection rate of 108.89 pollen per second. This tool does not collect more pollen from a certain color of flower, unlike the Porcelain Dipper.

docs.title: Honey Dispenser
docs.text:
This piece of content contains information obtained through datamining.

Due to the nature of the information, details may be inaccurate or outdated.

Datamined information: The formula for the amount of Honey received based on the number of bees in the player's hive. The table was made using in-game tests. — February 26th, 2026

Honey Dispenser Information Usage Giving Honey in proportion to the number of bees the player has. Requirement(s) None Cooldown 1 hour Location In front of the Lava Obby, near the Ant Gate

The Honey Dispenser is a dispenser that grants Honey and x5 haste every time it's used. It has a 1-hour cooldown and has no requirements. It initially gave 5x haste and 500 Honey, but after the 2018-04-27 update, the amount was changed to 100 Honey per bee in the player's hive and x5 haste. Since then, the amount of Honey was changed again.

It is usually the first dispenser a new player uses.

The Lava Obby can be found behind it and leads to a Royal Jelly token at the back of the Noob Shop and also to the Demon Mask shop.

docs.title: Honey reward amount
docs.text:
The amount of honey given is based on the number of bees the player has in their hive. More specifically, let cnt be the number of bees in the player's hive:

  • The amount of honey the player receives is equal to \(\left\lfloor {cnt}^{1.7}+0.5\right\rfloor \times 100\), or 500 if the result is less than 500.

Below is a table of the amount of honey and treats a player receives, given the number of bees they have.

docs.title: Honey Hammer
docs.text:
Honey Hammer Overview Price Can't be bought Obtained Melittology capstone, "A Beginning to a end." (10 Research Points) Pollen Collection Range 26 Flowers Collecting Pattern Circle (radius 3) collectedyou (facing up)Collects the 26 flowers nearest you in this circle; every 6th scoop slams the same area 5 tiles ahead. Collecting Time 1 second Base Collection 10 Flowers Single Double Triple Large Star White 10 20 30 40 50 Red 10 20 30 40 50 Blue 10 20 30 40 50 Special Multiplier(s): x1.25 White, Red and Blue Pollen. Every 6th scoop slams for 25 pollen per flower.

The Honey Hammer is a tool and the best collector in the game. You can't buy it: it is the reward for finishing the Melittology tree.

"Harnesses the Dark Scythe, Gummyballer, and Tide Popper in one tool. Sweeps flames and bubbles, charges and launches gummyballs, builds tidal power, and unleashes a massive Honey Hammer slam every 6th scoop."

docs.title: Stats
docs.text:
The Honey Hammer collects 10 pollen from 26 flowers in a circle every second, with x1.25 White, Red and Blue Pollen.

Every scoop also uses the abilities of three other tools at once:

  • the Dark Scythe's flames,
  • the Gummyballer's gummyballs,
  • the Tide Popper's waves, which pop bubbles and build tidal power.

These effects trigger even when a scoop hits no flowers.

docs.title: Honey Hammer slam
docs.text:
Every 6th scoop the hammer slams down 20 studs in front of you, just under a second after the swing. The slam collects 25 pollen per flower from the same 26-flower circle, with the same x1.25 multipliers. It counts as Tool pollen.

Flowers Single Double Triple Large Star White 25 50 75 100 125 Red 25 50 75 100 125 Blue 25 50 75 100 125

docs.title: How to obtain
docs.text:
The Honey Hammer is the capstone of the Melittology tree: the node "A Beginning to a end." (tier 61), which costs 10 Research Points. To unlock it you have to master both of your active paths.

Buying the capstone adds the Honey Hammer to your tools straight away. If the capstone is ever refunded, the Honey Hammer is taken away again.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The game calls it "the ultimate collector". It is the only tool that can't be bought from a shop.
  • Unequipping it clears the buffs from the tools it combines: Dark Heat, Gummyball, Gummyball Combo, Tidal Surge, Tide Power and Tide Blessing.
  • The September 18, 2026 update fixed the Honey Hammer taking your head.
  • The September 11, 2026 update added three new Melittology paths after the Honey Hammer: Supreme White, Supreme Red and Supreme Blue.

docs.title: Honey Per Pollen
docs.text:
Honey Per Pollen is a mechanic that increases the amount of honey earned when converting pollen. For example, if a player has 10 pollen in their container, with a 110% Honey Per Pollen multiplier, they would receive 11 honey if converted. 20 to 22, etc. To determine how much honey will be earned when converting pollen, multiply bag space B, by Honey Per Pollen percentage.

Similar to many other boosts, (for example, Instant Conversion) the player can always check their current percentage of Honey Per Pollen on the System Page. It starts off at 100% and increases later on when the player gets more and more Honey Per Pollen boosts.

Honey Per Pollen, along with other boosts like Instant Conversion, goo, and extra capacity, is one of the best ways to get maximum efficiency when producing honey. These boosts, when combined with each other, are extremely helpful overall. It can affect the player's condition when, for example, grinding or converting your hive balloon.

Keep in mind that there is a difference between Instant Conversion and Honey Per Pollen. While both help with honey production, Instant Conversion converts pollen collected in fields into honey instantly. However, Honey Per Pollen affects the amount of honey the player makes for every pollen.

docs.title: Other Honey per Pollen
docs.text:
As there are multiple method to converting pollen into honey, there are other variant of Honey per Pollen that applies from converting in one of those method, such as converting honey at hive and Instant Conversion. Similar to Honey per Pollen they start off at 100%.

Each Honey per Pollen variant stacks multiplicatively with Honey per Pollen, and other Honey per Pollen variant if possible. For example, with 110% Honey per Pollen and 150% Honey at Hive, the player is effectively having 165% Honey per Pollen only when converting pollen to honey at hive.

docs.title: Honey Wreath
docs.text:
The Honey Wreath is one of the Beesmas machines which can be unlocked after completing Black Bear's Honey Wreath quest.

When used, it converts all of the pollen in the player's bag into honey, multiplied by the player's Honey Per Pollen, scattering eight honey tokens around them to collect. The amount of honey obtained is also multiplied by Honey From Tokens. It has a cooldown of 30 minutes, and is located between 35 Bee Zone and the Ticket Tent.

The Honey Wreath can be upgraded by completing Honey Bee's Beesmas quest, "Honey Bee’s Honey Wreath?". This causes the wreath to grant 50% more honey and additionally summon a level 20 Honey Bee that lasts for 30 minutes.

If the player attempts to use the Honey Wreath before it is decorated, it will display text reading: This Wreath looks frankly uninspired...

The Honey Wreath.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text: Before completing Black Bear's quest, it looks like an ordinary wreath. After completing the "Black Bear's Honey Wreath" quest, the wreath is decorated with honey icons and the Flight of the Bumble Egg. After the player completes Honey Bee's "Honey Bee's Honey Wreath?" quest, it changes to have a Gifted Honey Bee face in the center of the wreath.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The wreath model comes from the Christmas Wreath hat on Roblox's catalog.
  • The egg that is hung on the wreath is the Flight of the Bumble Egg. It is a limited item that could be worn on your avatar. It was only obtainable during the Egg Hunt 2019 event.
  • Similar to coconuts, the amount of honey received from the wreath is increased by Honey From Tokens.
  • This is one of the 4 Beesmas machines that grants the player temporary bees (only if the "Honey Bee’s Honey Wreath?" quest is completed), the others being the Honeyday Candles, the Gummy Beacon and Onett's Lid Art.
  • If the player uses the Honey Wreath with less than 801 Pollen in their bag, the tokens will each reward 100 Honey (800 Honey in total), which is modified by Honey Per Pollen and Honey From Tokens.
  • Using the Honey Wreath is required for a few of Bee Bear's quests during his visits, and it is also required for Honey Bee's Beesmas Quest.
  • The Honey Bee given by Honey Wreath can collect pollen for the player is also able to attack the mobs the player's bees are attacking. e.g. if the player's bees attack the King Beetle, the bee summoned from the Honey Wreath will also attack the King Beetle.
  • If the player goes to their hive to convert their pollen, the Honey Bee given by the Honey Wreath does not convert any pollen and stays idle near the player. However, the bees are able to convert when a Honey Mark is active.

docs.title: Honey
docs.text:
The honey icon.

Honey is the main currency in Re://:Swarm.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Honey can be used to purchase many items such as tools, bags, and in-game accessories such as guards and gliding tools, and to play Memory Match. Honey can also be used to purchase products such as Tickets, Basic Eggs, Royal Jellies, Treats, and hive slots. In addition, Honey used along with Tickets, could have been used to purchase Market Boosts from the Boost Market, which is now removed. The price of many consumables increases with each purchase, for example, Basic Eggs.

docs.title: Obtaining Honey
docs.text: Honey is usually obtained by converting Pollen into it. It can be converted at the Hive or (partly) instantly converted using an Instant Converter or with a Micro-Converter, catching a falling Coconut or Science Bear's falling Beesmas Light (only during Beesmas), activating Coin Scatter and/or Diamond Drain. Honey can also be obtained by completing quests, redeeming codes, defeating mobs, and collecting Sparkles and Goo from fields. Vicious Bee's Impale ability spawns a honey token if it hits a mob. Festive Bee's festive gift ability always spawns Honey tokens. Some other bees have the ability to give a Honey Gift or a Token Link. Certain hats, guards, and amulets have the ability to instantly convert a percentage of pollen into honey. Popping bubbles, spawning a flame, having field conversion such as Field Winds, collecting a Bomb token produced by a bee can result in instant conversion as well. The player can also get honey for participating in the Ant Challenge. Honey tokens can appear when the player collects pollen in a field and can be obtained from Honeystorms. The Mythic Meteor Shower awards Honey tokens after catching a meteor. The Honey Dispenser is also an option, however, it is only available to those who are in the Bee Swarm Simulator Club.

docs.title: Convert Rate
docs.text:
Bees convert pollen into Honey at a set rate. For example, Basic Bee makes 80 honey in 4 seconds, translating into a conversion rate of 20 honey per second. Badges, accessories, gamepasses, Enzymes, and Science Enhancement can increase the convert rate. The production rate stacks and adds up. There is currently no convert rate cap in the game.

docs.title: Honeycomb Blueprint
docs.text:
"Manage your hive!"

The Honeycomb Blueprint is a permanent inventory item for managing your hive. Open it from your inventory to see your whole hive and work on your bees from one screen. It has no use cooldown.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Rearrange your hive: tap a bee, then another slot, to swap them. Bees keep their gift, mutations, levels and Beequips when moved. You can zoom in and out to see more of your hive.
  • Buy hive slots and use any item that works on your hive from inside the blueprint.
  • More tools unlock with rebirths:
    • Rebirth 10: level up bees directly. Pick the bees and the level, and it shows the honey cost.
    • Rebirth 15: roll until a chosen mutation. Pick the mutation, the stat or stat range, and the bees.
    • Rebirth 20: roll until a chosen bee with a chosen mutation.

docs.title: Ways to obtain
docs.text: • Every player gets one when they join. Its tools unlock as you rebirth.

This piece of content contains information obtained through datamining.

Due to the nature of the information, details may be inaccurate or outdated.

Datamined information: The probability of getting every item and bee. — December 19th, 2024

The Honeyday Candles are a Beesmas-exclusive machine which is unlocked after completing Gifted Riley Bee's Honeyday Candles quest. They have a cooldown of 10 minutes, and are located next to the Red HQ's interior ladder.

When activated, 3 random level 10 red bees are summoned for 30 minutes, and 3 waxes of a random type are spawned.

The chances for each wax type are as follows:

Wax Chance 3 Soft Waxes ~81.3% 3 Hard Waxes ~16.26% 3 Swirled Waxes ~1.63% 3 Caustic Waxes ~0.81%

The chances for each bee are as follows:

Bee Chance Fire Bee ~70.59% Demon Bee ~23.53% Spicy Bee ~5.88%

When a player stands on top of the pad before completing the quest, a red text box appears on the top of the screen reading: The red bees are having trouble lighting the candles...

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• A Hard Wax token used to be found hidden behind the candles.
  • These are one of the four machines that grants the player temporary bees, the others being Onett's Lid Art, Gummy Beacon, and the Honey Wreath (after completing Honey Bee's Beesmas quest).
  • There is a glitch when the player leaves, the bees generated would stay in place until they despawned.
  • Even when the player joins the same server, the bees will not despawn.
  • They were introduced in the Beesmas 2020 event and returned in all Beesmas updates since.
  • During Beesmas 2020, using these candles were one of the two only ways of getting Swirled Waxes, the other way is by giving Gifted Riley Bee a Present during that same event.
  • For every Beesmas event succeeding Beesmas 2020, the Honeyday Candles would no longer guarantee a Swirled Wax.
  • This is the only machine that can summon bees who produce flames.
  • Loot Luck does not affect Honeyday Candles drops.
  • Summoned bees don't have to rest, even if you die.

docs.title: Honeystorm
docs.text:
A Honeystorm is a server-wide event that can be summoned by using the pad near Brown Bear by anyone who has discovered at least four Legendary Bee types. When summoned, a server-wide announcement will state: [Username] has summoned a Honeystorm! Upon being summoned, a golden-yellow fog will appear along with a multitude of honey tokens and some ticket tokens that will begin to randomly appear across all fields (except the Hub Field). The storm lasts for 20 seconds and has a cooldown of 4 hours. It can also be randomly triggered, in which the announcement says:

A Honeystorm has been summoned! When a honeystorm is summoned, the honey tokens make raindrop-like popping noises when they appear. Like with the Mythic Meteor Shower, there's an audio of a distorted voice clip from IcedTeaLatte, a staff member for the game, saying "Honeystorm" to indicate that a honeystorm has been summoned.[1]

Fields with bigger flowers give higher amounts of honey per token, with their totals being increased by the Honey from Tokens stat. These honey tokens also despawn faster than normal honey tokens.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The honeystorm fog is normally tinted yellow, but during Beesmas in 2018 and 2019, the fog is white.
  • As of Beesmas 2020, this is no longer the case, since Snowstorms use the white fog instead.
  • This and the Special Sprout Summoner are the only machines that require the player to discover Legendary bee types to be activated, with this requiring 4 and the Special Sprout Summoner requiring 8.
  • A honeystorm's yellow tint could generate enough light to make the cave monsters in the Werewolf's cave visible.
  • There is a glitch where if a switch between day and night occurs while a honeystorm is active, the fog will disappear. This is purely visual and the honeystorm will still function as normal. This glitch is shared with Mythic Meteor Showers and Snowstorms.
  • There was a short-lived issue around 2018-05-26 that caused the Honeystorm Summoner to be removed. If a player encountered a server without a Honeystorm Summoner, they could simply leave the game and come back. This was, of course, fixed later.
  • After the 2018-09-10 update, the Honeystorm Summoner was moved and the Wealth Clock now sits in its former spot. Now it is located between the Clover Field and Blue HQ.
  • Upon receiving the quest "Witness Grandeur", Spirit Bear summons a honeystorm.
  • According to Bee Bear, Bubble Bee Man summons the honeystorms.
  • If you summon honeystorms at night, the fog will stay even after the storm until daytime.
  • Honeystorms can stack with other honeystorms. This does not affect the intensity of the honeystorms, but instead increases the duration.

docs.title: Honeysuckle
docs.text:
Honeysuckle

"Automatically makes bees instantly convert some Pollen into Honey when your bag becomes full. (Cooldown 30s)"

COOLDOWN

30 seconds

The Honeysuckle is a consumable inventory item that was introduced in the 2021-12-26 update. Unlike other consumable items with an auto setting, Honeysuckles are automatically used once a player's pollen container is full, and it is also the only item with an auto setting that cannot be put in the hotbar. When a player's pollen container is full, the Honeysuckle causes the player's bees to instantly convert some pollen in their bag into honey. It has a cooldown of 30 seconds before it can activate again, and can be toggled on or off by clicking the item in the inventory.

Unlike most consumables, this cannot be dragged to the hotbar. There is, however, an On/Off switch in the honeysuckle's inventory section. Turning it ON causes it to work automatically when the bag becomes full, and turning it OFF disables using honeysuckles.

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• As a rare drop from Ladybugs.
  • As a drop from planters.
  • Planters in Blue Flower Field, Rose Field and especially Sunflower Field give honeysuckles more often than other fields.
  • The Blue Clay Planters drops honeysuckles as a bonus drop.
  • As a reward from the Robo Bear Challenge.
  • As a reward from the Memory Match, Mega Memory Match, Night Memory Match or Extreme Memory Match.
  • As a Stack Reward for adding certain stickers to the Sticker Stack:
  • The Small Tickseed rewards 10 honeysuckles.
  • The Small White Daisy rewards 10 honeysuckles.
  • The Small Pink Tulip rewards 10 honeysuckles.
  • The Small Dandelion rewards 10 honeysuckles.
  • As a drop from Robo Party mobs.
  • As a reward from the Robo Party.
  • Using the Samovar grants 3-30 Honeysuckles (Starts from 3, increases by 1 each use and caps at 30).

docs.title: Token Locations
docs.text: • A Honeysuckle token is located on the roof of Dapper Bear's Shop which grants 25 Honeysuckles.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text:
Three things are needed for a honeysuckle to activate:

  1. There is an available honeysuckle in inventory, i.e. it is turned on and not on cooldown.
  2. The player's bag is full.
  3. More pollen is collected.

Not to be confused with the Hive Hub.

The Hub Field is a field that was added in the 2024-01-12 update and is located in the trading portal beyond the Ant Gate inside the Hive Hub.

This field contains 697 flowers. They are white, blue, and red, in single, double, and triple sizes.

When planting a sprout using a Magic Bean on the Hub Field, there is a rare chance of it spawning a Sticker Sprout. A Sticker Sprout is also guaranteed to spawn every 3 hours, granted there is no sprout occupying the field.

All pollen collected in this field will instantly convert to honey.

This field can spawn Blueberry, Honey, Pineapple, Strawberry, Sunflower Seed, Treat, and Magic Bean tokens.

Only through the use of glitches, this field grants Comforting Nectar when a planter is planted here.

Note: flower counts within the table may vary due to rounding. Additionally, in game, all flowers are randomly generated and may not precisely align with the percentages.

docs.title: Obtaining Boosts
docs.text: • Using Glitter will add 100% Hub Field pollen onto the current boost for 15 minutes if the boost isn't already maxed out.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This, the Ant Field, and the Stump Field are the only fields that the player can collect pollen from while not directly standing on the flowers.
  • This and the Stump Field are the only non-quadrilateral fields in the game and the only fields that the player can collect pollen from while not directly standing on the flowers.
  • This, the Ant Field, and the Stump Field are the only fields where Wild Windy Bee cannot spawn in nor fly to.
  • This, the Coconut Field, the Pepper Patch, the Ant Field and the Stump Field are the only fields that were added after the game's first release.
  • This, the Mountain Top Field, Ant Field, and the Coconut Field are the only fields that can't be given a field boost by field boosters.
  • This field is one of three fields with no decorations in it, indicating what field it is. The other two fields to do this are the Ant Field and the Mountain Top Field.
  • This field gets its name from the place it is located in, the Hive Hub.
  • The Hub Field is the only field in the entire game without a truly unique field boost icon. Instead, the Hub Field’s icon is reused from its associated field stamp.
  • You cannot use many types of consumable items while on this field.
  • The player cannot use sprinklers, stingers, cloud vials, balloons, snowflakes, planters, whirligigs, night bells or any kind of dice while in this field.
    • As such, this is the only field in the game where Sprinklers are completely disabled.
    • However, you can use Glitter, Jelly Beans, and Box-O-Frogs.
  • This is the only field that instantly converts your collected pollen into honey (the Ant Field does not instantly convert your honey by itself, and it happens instead because of the Ant Challenge Buff).
  • The Hub Field was used to test the max amount of Combo Coconuts that could be caught from a single Combo Coconuts Ability, the idea behind it was that 34 players can cover all spots on the field where Combo Coconut could land, thus, if it could land infinitely, it would last forever, since in normal conditions Combo Coconut accelerates too fast for players to even reach 40th coconut. So, the final result showed that Combo Coconut can land a total of 50 Times, after which it will just finish as if players didn't catch it, but there won't be a message about the player missing it.
  • 5 minutes before a natural Sticker Sprout spawns, the following message will be displayed: [🌱 A Sticker Sprout is about to spawn in Public Server Hive Hubs… 🌱 ]
  • The Hub Field spawns the most colors of Bloom petals out of all fields. The only colors that the Hub Field can't spawn are yellow and merigold.

docs.text:
Hydroponic Planter "Grows in about 12hrs, but faster near Blue flowers. Grants bonus Blue Extracts, Oils, x1.4 Refreshing and Comforting Nectar." Stats Cost750B Honey75 Magic Beans750 Blue Extract500 Soft Wax25 Caustic Wax1 Turpentine ReusableYes Inventory cap- Shop limit1 Grow time12 hours Grows fasterx1.5 in fields with blue flowers Pollen bonusx1.5 in fields with blue flowers, x0.5 in fields with red flowers Nectarx1.4 Refreshingx1.4 Comforting Pollen capacity25,000,000,000 Item tokens35 Puffshroom chance22% Puffshroom level6 to 7 Guaranteed items1 Blue Extract1 Oil3 Ticket

The Hydroponic Planter is a reusable planter added in the 2021-12-26 update. Alone, it grows in about 12 hours and stores around 25 billion pollen. When harvested, it grants bonus Blue Extracts and Oils. It is purchasable in the Blue HQ. It requires the player to complete 150 Gifted Bucko Bee quests for it to be unlocked.

docs.title: Growth, pollen and nectar
docs.text:
• Grows in 12 hours of playtime alone, and grows faster here: x1.5 in fields with blue flowers. A flower-colour bonus is weighted by how much of the field is that colour.
  • Glitter used in its field speeds it up: x1.5 for one, rising in halving steps up to x2 at 6 stacks. The stacks stay on the planter until it is harvested.
  • Holds 25,000,000,000 pollen at full growth. A harvest gives capacity × growth × pollen bonus. Pollen bonus: x1.5 in fields with blue flowers, x0.5 in fields with red flowers.
  • Nectar multipliers: x1.4 Refreshing, x1.4 Comforting. On harvest it gives one Nectar type from its field, lasting grow time × growth × multiplier × 3 seconds.
  • Up to 3 bees can sip from it at once. Blue bees are x1.333 as likely to sip from it; Red bees are x0.5 as likely to sip from it.

Note: It holds 25 billion pollen, not the "around 10 billion" the shop text says.

docs.title: Puffshrooms
docs.text:
When it reaches 95% growth, it has a 22% chance to smoke and spawn 3 Puffshrooms (one at the planter and two nearby) at levels 6 to 7.

  • Rare 22.5%
  • Epic 7.25%
  • Legendary 0.24%
  • Mythic 0.01%

docs.title: Drops
docs.text: A full harvest gives 35 item tokens. Harvesting early gives fewer, in proportion to growth, but always at least 1. Tokens are filled in this order: guaranteed items (full harvests only), then field rules, then random picks from the pool below.

docs.title: Guaranteed
docs.text:
On every full harvest:

  • 1 Blue Extract
  • 1 Oil
  • 3 Ticket

docs.title: Field rules
docs.text:
• In the Blue Flower, Bamboo, Pine Tree or Stump Field: +1 Blue Extract (+3 if full).
  • Sunflower Field: Sitting Mother Bear sticker, 1% when full (0.2% when not).
  • Stump, Blue Flower, Sunflower or Pine Tree: Candy Ring beequip, 1.8% when full (0.4% when not).
  • Full harvests in Blue Flower, Bamboo, Pine Tree, then Stump: 100 Blue Extract, once every 30 days. Otherwise 2.5% chance of 100 Blue Extract per full harvest.
  • Full in the Sunflower Field 3 times in a row: 100 Oil, once every 30 days. Each full harvest also has a 2.5% chance of 100 Oil.
  • Full in the Blue Flower Field: 1 Loaded Dice (once a day). Mushroom Field: 1 Swirled Wax (every 30 days). Coconut Field: 1 Caustic Wax (every 30 days).

"Always gives a bee an Instant Conversion Mutation."

The IC Atomic Treat is a treat that always gives a bee an Instant Conversion mutation. It works like an Atomic Treat, but the mutation is always Instant Conversion instead of a random one.

The value is random and leans towards the low end, but 7% of the time it rolls the maximum. The bee's level doesn't change the range.

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Realistic max is the best you can expect to actually see: the most picks of that upgrade that about 1 in 1,000 fully waxed 5 ★ beequips get, each at its top value. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

docs.title: Instant Conversion
docs.text: Instant Conversion is a mechanic that instantly converts some of the player's collected pollen into honey. The amount of converted pollen depends on how much instant conversion (%) the player has, with support from the respective type of instant conversion (white, red, and blue instant conversion, etc.). This effectively makes the player's bag bigger, in the sense that the player can collect more pollen than the bag would normally hold. The player's Honey Per Pollen stat boosts the amount of honey received from instant conversion. There are also color variants for each flower color (blue, red, white) that only instantly convert pollen of their respective colors.

docs.title: Instant Conversion Variants
docs.text:
Instant Conversion has 8 variants:

  • Flame Conversion
  • Field Conversion (e.g. field winds)
  • Colored Conversion
  • Goo Conversion
  • Bomb Conversion
  • Unique Instant Conversion
  • Instant Tool Conversion
  • Bee Gather Conversion

docs.title: Goo Conversion
docs.text: Goo Conversion converts a flat amount of pollen equal to a percentage of the Goo collected from a flower.

docs.title: Unique Instant Conversion
docs.text:
Unique Instant Conversion is applied independently of all other Instant Conversion types.

For example, if you have two different sources of 50% Unique Instant Conversion, each source is applied separately. This results in an effective 75% Instant Conversion, not 100%.

docs.title: Conversion Order
docs.text:
Instant Conversion is applied in the following order:[1]

  1. Colored Conversion
  2. Field Conversion
  3. Regular Instant Conversion
  4. Goo Conversion

It is unknown where Unique Instant Conversion and Ability-specific Instant Conversion is placed in this order.

For example, if a player has 50% of four different conversion variants and collects 10,000 red pollen, 50% of the pollen is converted, then 50% of the remaining amount, and so on for each variant.

docs.title: Increasing Instant Conversion
docs.text:
• Instant Conversion is increased by:
  • Enzymes (+10%)
  • Tropical Drinks (+10%)
  • Super Smoothies (+20%, overwrites Enzymes and Tropical Drinks)
  • Cactus Badge (+5%)
  • Gifted Photon Bee (+5%)
  • Port-O-Hive (5%)
  • Coconut Canister or Porcelain Port-O-Hive (10%)
  • Star Amulet (up to 12%)
  • Moon Amulet (up to 5%)
  • Festive Blessing Buff (100%)
  • Maximum Instant Conversion is 157% not accounting for codes.
  • Instant White Conversion is increased by amulets, the Pineapple Badge, Gifted Windy Bee or with the Coconut Canister.
  • Instant Red Conversion is increased by the Mushroom Badge (up to 15%), Gifted Crimson Bee (15%), or the Demon Mask (20%).
  • Instant Blue Conversion is increased by the Blue Flower Badge (up to 15%), Gifted Cobalt Bee (15%) or the Diamond Mask(15%).
  • Instant Field Conversion (field winds) are granted by donating to the Wind Shrine or from certain codes.
  • Goo Conversion is increased by the Shell Amulet, Gummy Mask, Gummy Morph, or Gummy Star.
  • Instant Flame Conversion is granted by the Fire Mask, Demon Mask and Scorching Star.
  • Instant Bomb Conversion is granted by Festive Mark and Gifted Demon Bee.
  • Unique Instant Conversion is granted by Coconut Combo, Clouds, Puffshroom Blessing, Beequips, Refreshing Nectar and Blooms
  • Instant Bee Gather Conversion is granted by the Pink Jelly Bean buff.
  • Instant Tool Conversion is granted by the Teal Jelly Bean buff.

docs.title: Effects
docs.text:
• When instant conversion is in effect, and pollen text is turned on, the player will see yellow numbers in addition to the blue/red/white pollen numbers while they're working in the fields. Those yellow numbers are the amount of pollen that instantly became honey; Collected honey amounts also show up in yellow, but those are also listed in the bottom right corner of the player's screen.

  • The formula for the effective increase in capacity given by instant conversion is: (x/(100-x)), where x is the player's total instant conversion.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Festive Blessing buff from Festive Bee's Festive Gift token or Festive Sprouts grants 100% Instant Conversion temporarily. If the player has a full container with 100% Instant Conversion, collecting pollen will not transfer into honey.
  • The Gummy Morph also grants 200% Goo Conversion while covering the whole field in goo.
  • The Ant Challenge Buff grants 100% instant Ant Field Conversion.
  • Pollen collected from the Hub Field is instantly converted.
  • Super-Crits and Golden Bubbles instantly convert all pollen they collect.
  • Tadpole Bee used to give 25% Instant Bubble Conversion before the 2024-05-23 update.

docs.title: Instant Converter
docs.text:
The Instant Converter is a machine used to immediately convert pollen into honey, similar to a hive, but instantly and without the use of bees.

There are three Instant Converters that can be found in the game:

  1. Behind the Basic Egg Shop, next to the Sunflower Field and in front of the Mushroom Field; this one is available to all players.
  2. Just around the corner from the Brave Bee Gate; the player will need 10 bees to access it.
  3. Next to the Mountain Top Field; the player will need 25 bees to access it.

Each machine costs 1 Ticket to use and has a cooldown of 15 minutes.

The player's Honey Per Pollen rate also applies to the Instant Converter, just like it would at the hive.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• The player can use an Instant Converter to squeeze in one more trip to a boosted field. This can be useful when they know that going back to their hive and waiting for their bees to convert their pollen would take longer than the time left on a boost.
  • It is more cost-effective to use an Instant Converter when the player's bag is full.
  • Keep in mind that the cooldown of an Instant Converter is the same as the duration of a field boost, which means the same converter cannot be used twice during a field boost unless the player increases the duration of it.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The player can jump inside the chute of the converter in the Brave Bee Gate, which leads to the White Tunnel where Tunnel Bear spawns. There's a pad in the middle of the tunnel that will teleport the player on top of the converter behind the Basic Egg Shop.
  • Before the 2018-07-11 update, the Instant Converter in the 10 Bee Zone was the only one available in the entire game, and had a cooldown of only 10 minutes.
  • Before the 2018-07-11 update, the conveyor belt in the Instant Converter would push the player out of it.

Behind the converter in the Brave Bee Area, there is a question that asks 'Black Bear's Title?'. This question is a hint to the code, 'Connoisseur', as Black Bear claims to be a Honey Connoisseur in the dialogue of his first quest. * According to Spirit Bear, it was planned for an Instant Converter to be built on the spot where the Wind Shrine sits now.

The Invigorating Vial is a consumable nectar vial item that was added in the 2022-12-26 update. Once used, it grants the player 4 hours of the Invigorating Nectar buff instantly. It can also be used to craft other accessories and tools.

docs.title: Amulets
docs.text:
Amulet Description Cost Source King Beetle Amulet The King Beetle Amulet is an amulet that always drops, at max quality, when the King Beetle is defeated. - King Beetle Moon Amulet The Moon Amulet is an amulet created by spending 100 Moon Charms at the Moon Amulet Generator. This amulet gives a few buffs and allows the player to walk on the moon-shaped platforms (located at the back of Dapper Bear's Shop, in the Diamond Room, and at the 30 Bee Zone Obby) at night. 100 Moon Charms Moon Amulet Generator Ant Amulet The Ant Amulet is an amulet that is always obtained from participating in the Ant Challenge.

The amulet gives the player buffs and will always boost Convert Rate. There are five tiers of Ant Amulets, each awarded at a certain amount of points in the Ant Challenge.

1 Ant Pass By participating in the Ant Challenge Star Amulet The Star Amulet is an amulet that can be purchased in five different tiers (Bronze, Silver, Gold, Diamond, and Supreme) from machines in the Star Hall. They grant buffs to the owner and always increase capacity as they go up a tier. Higher tier amulets grant more and better buffs. Diamond and Supreme Star Amulets also have additional Star Passive abilities. The more gifted bee types the player has discovered, the more likely the stats from the Star Amulets will be at maxed value. 25M-500B Honey Star Hall Shell Amulet The Shell Amulet is an amulet obtainable by defeating the Stump Snail in the Stump Field. Once the player's Stump Snail is defeated, the player is guaranteed to get a Shell Amulet. - Stump Snail Stick Bug Amulet The Stick Bug Amulet is an amulet that can be obtained from the Stick Bug Challenge.

In order to obtain these amulets, the player will need to get Stick Bug to a certain level as well as reach a certain score during the Stick Bug Challenge. Stick Bug Amulets will have at least four buffs, with a fifth and sixth possible buff. These buffs can include -% monster respawn time, red or blue bee attack, general bee attack, and bond from battle.

- Stick Bug Cog Amulet The Cog Amulet is an amulet that can be obtained from the Robo Bear Challenge. In order to obtain these amulets, the player will need to beat certain rounds during the Robo Bear Challenge. The more rounds the player beats, the higher the tier of the Cog Amulet. The average stats of the amulet also scale higher the more cogs you collect in a round. 1 Robo Pass Robo Bear Challenge

docs.title: Jelly Beans
docs.text:
This piece of content contains information obtained through datamining.

Due to the nature of the information, details may be inaccurate or outdated.

Datamined information: The buffs of every jelly bean type. While this information is accessible in-game, Spoiled Jelly Beans have extra information that can't be verified due to its rarity. — December 19th, 2024

Jelly Beans

"Scatters various buff-granting beans on nearby flowers. Works best when shared."

COOLDOWN

30 seconds

CAP

100

Jelly Beans are an inventory item added in the Egg Hunt 2019 update. When used, it spreads jelly beans of varying colors in the direction the player is facing, with each color representing a different buff. They will turn into jelly bean tokens when they land on flowers, making them collectable. Each buff lasts for a minute. Each jelly bean item spawns 11-13 jelly bean tokens.

If multiple players are around, a different player picking up the tokens will give both the owner and the collector the token's buffs, as well as the Jelly Bean Sharing Bonus to the owner. Therefore, it is best to share jelly beans.

The player can only hold a maximum of 100 at a time in their inventory. The player will need to use at least one in order to get any more unless they are obtained from quests, purchased from any Robux pack, or from the Colorful Present (now unobtainable).

Note: Jelly Beans can be activated anywhere, though it is recommended to be in a field because if the beans do not land on a field, no tokens will be spawned.

  • Space Oblivion rewards 10 jelly beans and other items after completion.

docs.title: Tokens
docs.text:
• Going into the Blue Maze next to the Ticket Tent. Taking the path to the right will lead to a jelly bean token.
  • Going into the Coconut Cave on top of the Coconut Dispenser there will be a hole, Going through the hole has jelly beans and others.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Bean Bugs are passive mobs that spawn in random fields. They scatter jelly bean tokens around their current field. They are the second and only other way of getting jelly bean tokens.
  • When picking up a jelly bean item token (the consumable), it said "You found a Jelly Beans!" instead of "You found Jelly Beans!" or "You found a Jelly Bean!". This was an error, fixed at an unknown date.
  • The Merigold Jelly Bean is misspelled throughout the game. The correct spelling should be 'Marigold'.
  • The hearts in the Jelly Bean Sharing Bonus buff are similar to the heart of the Baby Love ability token, but they are not blushing.
  • Rarer jelly beans emit sparkles when being thrown into a field, and the token will also emit a sparkle effect.
  • Prior to the 2019-09-28 update, Jelly Beans did not have a maximum capacity and players could obtain them in an unlimited amount.
  • If the player donates any number of Jelly Beans for the first time to the Wind Shrine, it gives back 7 Jelly Beans.
  • After donating, it says "- ( Number ) Jellybeanss". It should be "Jelly Beans" with one S.
  • When claiming the tokens, it says "+ ( Number ) Jelly Beans ( from >>☻︎ ). This is a clue from the Ready Player Two Event.
  • If the player attempts to throw Jelly Beans in the Ant Field from outside, the beans will be thrown, but no tokens will spawn even if they hit flowers in the Ant Field.
  • Like Field Winds, further Jelly Bean stacks do not add up on each other. Instead, they gain their own stacks of percentage.
  • The Spoiled Jelly Bean is the only jelly bean to grant a debuff.

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Realistic max is the best you can expect to actually see: the most picks of that upgrade that about 1 in 1,000 fully waxed 5 ★ beequips get, each at its top value. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

docs.title: King Beetle Amulet
docs.text:
The King Beetle Amulet is an amulet that is guaranteed to drop every time the King Beetle is defeated.

The amulet grants a random number of buffs. The buffs can be field-specific pollen boosts, Convert Rate bonuses, and/or Bee Attack bonuses.

It always drops at max quality (1). In the quality tables below, only the quality 1 row applies to this game.

If the player has three or more types of amulets, the King Beetle Amulet will be above the player's right shoulder. If the player has two types, it will be above their left shoulder, and if it's the only type, it will be above their head.

docs.title: King Beetle's Lair
docs.text:
King Beetle's Lair is the location where King Beetle spawns. It can be accessed from the light green door between Blue HQ and under the Clover Field and next to the far end of the Blue Flower Field. Inside the lair, the exit can be accessed by climbing a ladder leaning adjacent to the entrance. The interior of the lair is completely empty, except for the ladder for leaving. Both doors are one-way. The player will be pushed through either door if they stand too close, even if they aren't moving. The entrance to the lair cycles in color, so it stands out from the rest of the environment.

The King Beetle spawns on the back wall adjacent to the Noob Shop and Lava Obby.

Near the back right corner of the lair, there is some text on the floor, "Song Name". It refers to the song that plays inside the lair and is a hint to the code, "Crawlers".

docs.title: Music
docs.text: The music here is "Crawlers", which also plays inside the Commando Chick's Hideout and the White Tunnel.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• In early game versions, if players went too close to the side of the lair that is closest to the Noob Shop, they could die due to a lava block clipping into the wall from the lava obby. This was later patched.
  • The bottom of the pole of the Honeystorm Summoner sign pokes into the top of the lair.
  • If there is a sprout in the Clover Field, the bottom of its light column and the remaining pollen number can be seen in the lair.
  • This is similar to when Rogue Vicious Bee’s spikes and clouds spawn in the Clover Field.
  • There is a glitch where the King Beetle can fail to lunge and get stuck when in the 'Song Name' corner.
  • During the Beesmas 2018 Event, the red roof of the lair could be seen on the sides of the flower blocks in the Clover Field.
  • However, the red roof's glow near the Noob Shop wall is still visible even when it was not snowy.
  • Any tool can collect pollen from the Clover Field inside the lair if the player continuously jumps and has enough Jump Power. However, the Spark Staff doesn't require too much Jump Power.
  • If the player has enough Jump Power and jumps high enough, the rhino beetle and ladybug in the Clover Field can be triggered. The player's bees may also think that they are in the Clover Field and start collecting pollen.
  • The entrance to the lair is lighter than the color of the surrounding ground and slightly changes in. During Beesmas, it is much more noticeable as the walls surrounding the entrance are white.
  • The cycling colors of the entrance matches the cycling colors and pattern of any supreme-tier amulet.

docs.title: King Beetle
docs.text:
King Beetle Location King Beetle's Lair Respawns Every 24 hours (20 hours 24 minutes with a Gifted Vicious Bee)

The King Beetle is a level 7 boss mob that resides in his lair. The entrance to his lair is on the wall between the Blue Flower Field and the Clover Field, above the blue flower closest to the Blue HQ via a transparent wall. He has 2,500 health and deals 40 damage to the player per hit if the player has no Defense.

He takes 1 day (24 hours) to respawn after being defeated (20 hours and 24 minutes with a Gifted Vicious Bee). The rewards for defeating him vary, but always include 150 Battle Points, as well as Honey, Royal Jellies, Tickets and Bond.

He always drops a King Beetle Amulet at max quality when defeated. Having more Loot Luck increases the probabilities of other drops. After the 2019-02-01 Update, King Beetle drops honey tokens and rewards in a token circle around the center of the lair unlike all other mobs who drop the circle around the place of their death (except for Stump Snail, Tunnel Bear, and Rogue Vicious Bee) unless the player receives a King Beetle Amulet, in which it goes directly into the player's inventory.

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
Defeating a King Beetle is challenging and he might kill players several times before they succeed (It's recommended that players don't fight King Beetle with a full bag). Here are some recommended strategies for defeating him:

  • Use King Beetle's predictable pattern of behavior to stop and run. He moves toward the player, stops to "aim," and then lunges. If the player stays still long enough for him to aim (about 3 seconds), but then quickly moves away, King Beetle will lunge at where the player used to be, not where the player has moved to. Thus, this method entails running along the edge of the lair, stopping, looking at King Beetle and waiting for him to lock onto the player, and then quickly jumping and running to a different point along the edge of the lair. Rinse and repeat until he is defeated.
  • Circling King Beetle allows the player to defeat King Beetle faster. If the player keeps circling around their King Beetle while keeping a good distance from him, their bees can get very close to King Beetle. Though the player might get hit the first few times, the beetle will most likely be defeated.
  • Run around the lair and occasionally look at his health. It's very helpful if players have Rage Bees, so they can run around and grab the tokens. However, if the player is too far away from him, their bees will come back to them rather than attacking the beetle. Building up maximum Haste can help, although it may run out before King Beetle gets defeated. Using the Parachute or Glider can also help since gliding through the air can be faster than running.
  • If the player is certain that their bees will kill him before they die, they can just wait for their bees to defeat him while the player stands in front of King Beetle, doing nothing during the process.
  • If a Rogue Vicious Bee is active in the Clover Field, players can trick it into damaging King Beetle.
  • Due to a bug, if the player gets the King Beetle stuck on the clue 'Song Name' by standing in the top right corner, King Beetle cannot attack them. This may take several attempts to work.
  • If the player gets too far from King Beetle, their bees will follow them instead of attacking it. But if the player gets too close, it's very easy to accidentally touch its aura which will damage the player.
  • If more than one player is trying to fight King Beetle at the same time, his pattern of behavior can become less predictable. It can also be difficult to tell which King Beetle is targeting them. For best results, wait for the other player's King Beetle to be defeated before entering its lair.
  • If the player's bees' levels are lower than 7, their attempts to attack will most likely miss. This will make defeating it take much longer than if they were level 7 or above.
  • When dodging King Beetle, keep in mind he does not follow directly behind the player but can sidestep to get in their way.
  • If you die, the King Beetle's health will reset, unlike Commando Chick and Stump Snail.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
Some things can help the player defeat King Beetle, regardless of which strategy the player chooses.

  • Having more bees and having bees with high attack power such as Lion Bee, Vicious Bee, Crimson Bee, Cobalt Bee, Riley Bee, Bucko Bee, Rage Bee, Brave Bee, and Precise Bee.
  • Having high-level bees so attacks don't miss (Recommended level 5–7 with at least one Rage Bee and 20 bees).
  • Wearing an Accessory that can boost Bee Attack, Move speed, Jump Power, or Defense, such as guards.
  • Collecting Rage, Focus and Melody tokens can be helpful, especially if the player has fewer bees. Collecting haste and bear morph tokens can also help dodge King Beetle's attack.
  • While it is possible to defeat King Beetle using the arrow keys to move, WASD is the suggested method, because it allows the player to keep looking at King Beetle while they are moving.
  • The Parachute or Glider can be used to quickly get out of King Beetle's attack path.
  • Having at least 20-25 bees with all of them at least level 7 is usually enough to defeat King Beetle using the above strategies.
  • Using a Stinger can be useful with low level bees.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• King Beetle used to guarantee an amulet upon death.
  • In the back right corner of the lair, there is something written on the floor. This is a hint for a code.
  • The clue is "Song Name", which refers to the music that plays in the lair. If the player checks Onett's inventory, the user will see that it's called Crawlers.
  • King Beetle was the first boss to be added to the game.
  • King Beetle has the fifth-largest amount of health in the game for any mob, with Tunnel Bear being the fourth, Coconut Crab the third, Mondo Chick the second, and Stump Snail the first. On certain occasions, Rogue Vicious Bee, Wild Windy Bee, Aphids, and Stick Bug will have more health depending on their level. In this case, King Beetle can be considered the weakest boss in terms of health.
  • King Beetle and Stump Snail are the only mobs that can drop an amulet, the King Beetle Amulet and the Shell Amulet respectively.
  • There was a myth that clicking on King Beetle has an effect. However, this was disproven as Onett has confirmed that King Beetle does not even have a click detector.
  • Before the 2018-07-11 Update, King Beetle took two days to respawn after being defeated, granted more battle points and despawned after about 5 minutes.
  • King Beetle is a hybrid of a Rhino Beetle and a Ladybug, as stated by Onett on Discord.[1]
  • Onett stated that the King Beetle emits toxins that makes the player hallucinate, which is why both he and his lair are strangely colored.[2]
  • An active King Beetle's health bar can be seen through the Clover Field and the Blue Flower Field.
  • King Beetle is the only boss that doesn't have a time limit to kill it.
  • King beetle is also the only boss to drop its loot in a circle.

docs.title: Ladybug
docs.text:
Ladybug Location Mushroom Field, Clover Field, Strawberry Field Respawns Every 5 minutes (4 minutes 15 seconds with Gifted Vicious Bee)

The ladybug is a mob that defends three different fields.

This is one of the first mobs a player will encounter, as they are in 2 out of 5 of the starting fields (the others being Rhino Beetles and the possibility of aphids, Wild Windy Bee, and Rogue Vicious Bee).

It takes 5 minutes for a ladybug to respawn after being defeated (4 minutes 15 seconds with a Gifted Vicious Bee). Defeating one gives 1 Battle Point and about 75 Honey (increased by Honey From Tokens) spread across 4 honey tokens. Various other rewards are also possible with their probability increasing with Loot Luck.

A ladybug's level can range from 1–3, depending on the field it is located in.

docs.title: Leaderboards
docs.text:
This page is for the in-game leaderboards. For this wiki's Achievement Leaderboard, see the Achievement page.

Leaderboards are a feature within the game. Each leaderboard displays the ranks of the top 100 players, showing ten ranks at a time. Leaderboards are usually not in real-time but update very often. Upon standing on the white pad in front of a leaderboard, it will show a message stating the player's score for the corresponding leaderboard.

Out of the 64 total leaderboards, 18 are able to be viewed at various locations around the map, and the rest are available to view in the System Page. There are 6 leaderboards that have been removed.

On daily and monthly leaderboards, players are able to gain rewards by placing high enough in one. The rewards can be tickets, consumable items or stickers.

docs.title: Leaves
docs.text:
Not to be confused with Flowers or Pollen.

Leaves are entities that appear in most fields. They work similarly to sparkles and emit leaf particles. To gather leaves, the player needs to collect pollen on the tile it is on, similar to sparkles. When the leaves are gathered, a rustling sound plays, and multiple leaf particles fly out before the token appears. Rewards vary depending on which field the leaves are in but will always be in quantities of 1. For example, leaves will often spawn blueberries in blue fields. Leaves also have a rare chance of spawning an aphid that varies based on field activity, with the chance increasing if a field has been inactive for a while. They can also summon leaf stickers in most fields.

Leaves in the Mountain Top Field are noticeably much rarer than in any other field and will always spawn an aphid or Lyrate Leaf Sticker, and on rarer occasions, a Bitterberry, Neonberry, Magic Bean, Blowing Leaf Sticker or Super Smoothie token. Leaves in the Stump Field and Ant Field cannot spawn aphids.

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Realistic max is the best you can expect to actually see: the most picks of that upgrade that about 1 in 1,000 fully waxed 5 ★ beequips get, each at its top value. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

The Lion Bee Gate, also known as the Mountain Top Gate or the 25 Bee Gate, is a gate that requires 25 bees to pass through. It is located at the end of the slope beside the Pumpkin Patch.

It gets its name from the large statue of a Lion Bee located on top of it.

This area contains the Mountain Top Field, Mondo Chick, Sticker Printer, Field Booster, Instant Converter, Ticket Shop and the Mountain Top Shop.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• As of the 2019-09-28 update, the player will be teleported back to spawn if they manage to bypass the gate, whether if it was by jumping around it or using the Red Cannon without 25 bees.
  • This and the Ant Gate share a few similarities.
  • They are the only gates that don't have a quest giver behind them.
    • If one were to count the Sticker-Seeker Quest Machine inside the Hive Hub Portal past the Ant Gate, or Gummy Bear, then this would be the only gate that doesn't have a quest giver behind it.
  • They are the only gates that only contain 1 field.
    • If one were to count the Hub Field inside the Hive Hub Portal past the Ant Gate, then this would be the only gate that contains 1 field.
  • This used to be the final gate accessed in the game, until the Bear Gate was added in the 2018-7-11 update.

docs.title: Loaded Dice
docs.text:
Loaded Dice

"Boosts 3 random fields with 300% pollen for 15 minutes. A bit biased towards the field you're in..."

COOLDOWN

3 Seconds

CAP

25

Loaded Dice is an inventory item added in the 2021-12-26 update. It boosts three random fields with 300% pollen for 15 minutes, and the field the player is in has a biased chance, meaning it has a higher chance to boost the field the player is standing in. If the player uses it when there is another dice boost active, it will replace the last dice boosts and duration. It has a cooldown of 3 seconds.

docs.title: Bias Mechanism
docs.text: To activate the bias, the player must be standing on a field. The first loaded dice gives a 25% chance for the first field picked to be the field the player is standing in. As more loaded dice is used, the chance will increase by 25%, maxing out at 100% where it is guaranteed. If the player leaves the field, the chance will reset.

docs.title: Ways to obtain
docs.text:
• Crafting via Blender for:
  • 3 Smooth Dice
  • 3 Hard Waxes
  • 3 Oils
  • 1 Glue
  • As a rare reward from Robo Bear Challenge (Up to 3 Loaded Dice).
  • As a Stack Reward for adding certain stickers to the Sticker Stack:
  • Bomber Bee Bear rewards 1 Loaded Dice.
  • Triple Exclamation rewards 1 Loaded Dice.

docs.title: Drops
docs.text:
• As a very rare drop from the Werewolf.
  • As a very rare drop from Tunnel Bear.
  • As a rare drop from Epic, Legendary, and Mythic Puffshrooms.
  • As a drop from certain planters:
  • Festive Planter
  • Tacky Planter and Petal Planter has a chance to drop 1 Loaded Dice as a bonus drop.
    • Planting the Tacky Planter in the Mountain Top Field may yield 1 Loaded Dice (36-day cooldown).
  • Planting the Heat-Treated Planter in the Mushroom Field may yield 1 Loaded Dice (~1 day cooldown).
  • Planting the Hydroponic Planter in the Blue Flower Field may yield 1 Loaded Dice (~1 day cooldown).

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• Completing Dapper Bear's 10th quest rewards 1 Loaded Dice and other items.
  • Completing Dapper Bear's 15th quest rewards 3 Loaded Dice and other items.

docs.title: Token Location
docs.text: • A token near the Red HQ's roof grants 1 Loaded Dice.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• If you some how roll another dice while a dice is already being rolled, this notification would pop up:

You are already rolling a dice

  • This is the only dice to currently have a cap (25).
  • Field Dice used to have a cap of 25 until the 2021-12-26 update.
  • This and the Smooth Dice are the only items which can produce more than 1 field boost at a time, and produce more than x1 stack of field boost at a time.
  • The fields shown on the dice are the Sunflower Field, the Clover Field, the Coconut Field, the Pumpkin Patch, the Pine Tree Forest and the Blue Flower Field.
  • There also is an X icon on the front dice. It is presumed it's the "biased" slot for the field that the player is standing on.
  • In real life, loaded dice are rigged dice designed to make one side show up more often than the rest, which correlates to the dice's in-game bias of the field your standing in.

• Looker Bee was the "oldest designed character",[1] not necessarily in the form of a bee. It had the signature eyes, was green, and had two little legs.[2]
  • Looker Bee was the first bee to have a royal jelly only turning a bee into it. The jelly was obtainable by using the code, 'ThoseEyes' (expired).
  • The Looker Guard, which can be bought in the Pro Shop, has a special design, name, and stats dedicated to Looker Bee.
  • Looker Bee used to have the same gifted hive bonus as Tabby Bee before the nerf on 2021-12-26 update
  • Looker Bee was one of the first bees that were added to the game in an update, along with Commander Bee, Music Bee, and Photon Bee.
  • Looker Bee and Stubborn Bee are the only Rare bees that were added after the game's launch.
  • Looker Bee's skin is the same as Commander Bee's skin.
  • Looker Bee is the only bee that dislikes Sunflower Field.
  • Looker Bee's field preferences are based on liking good vantage points.[3]
  • The reason Looker Bee likes the Mountain Top Field might be because high places have very good views from above, and possibly for a similar reason as the Clover Field.
  • The reason Looker Bee dislikes the Sunflower Field is because the sunflowers obstruct its view.

docs.title: Loot Luck
docs.text:
Loot Luck is a passive attribute that increases the chances of receiving certain rewards from defeated mobs. The formula to calculate the chance of receiving an item from a mob when the player defeats it is: 1-((1-base chance) ^luck). A rule of thumb is that for every 100% Loot Luck the player has, the player gets an extra roll to get each drop.

It also affects what type of token spawns in fields. Every time a honey token spawns in the field, it rolls a "drop table". Every item has a chance to "pass," with Loot Luck boosting the chance for it to pass. If it does, that item spawns. Otherwise, if it fails, it goes on to the next item. If every item fails, the honey token spawns as it is.

Loot Luck does not affect amulet tiers, stats granted from amulets, drops from chicks, or hatching and transforming bees.

docs.title: Ways to Increase
docs.text: Loot Luck can be increased through belts, buffs, and other ways.

docs.title: Belts
docs.text:
Each belt gives an amount of Loot Luck.

  • The Belt Pocket gives +25% Loot Luck.
  • The Belt Bag gives +50% Loot Luck.
  • The Mondo Belt Bag gives +75% Loot Luck.
  • The Honeycomb Belt gives +100% Loot Luck.
  • The Petal Belt gives +101% Loot Luck.
  • The Coconut Belt gives +102% Loot Luck.

docs.title: Gifted Hive Bonuses
docs.text: • Gifted Baby Bee gives +25% Loot Luck.

docs.title: Buffs
docs.text:
• Baby Love gives +50% Loot Luck.
  • Cool Breeze gives from 1% Loot Luck up to 10% Loot Luck at 100% Cool Breeze.

docs.title: Badges
docs.text:
• The Clover Badge can give up to +50% Loot Luck depending on the badge rank.
  • The Cadet Clover Badge gives +10% Loot Luck.
  • The Hotshot Clover Badge gives +20% Loot Luck.
  • The Ace Clover Badge gives +30% Loot Luck.
  • The Master Clover Badge gives +40% Loot Luck.
  • The Grandmaster Clover Badge gives +50% Loot Luck.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Before the 2019-04-05 update, Loot Luck was simply named Luck.
  • Loot Luck once affected honey tokens. However, this feature was removed due to there already being a Honey From Tokens stat.
  • Before the 2019-09-28 update, the Clover Badge did not give any Loot Luck. This was a mistake, which was fixed after said update.

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Realistic max is the best you can expect to actually see: the most picks of that upgrade that about 1 in 1,000 fully waxed 5 ★ beequips get, each at its top value. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

docs.title: Magic Bean Shop
docs.text:
The Magic Bean Shop is a shop added in the 2018-11-25 update, located next to the Stump Field. It can be used to purchase magic beans with tickets, in increments of 1 and 10, with each bean being 20 tickets.

It is decorated with a small normal sprout on top, along with the magic bean icon on all of its sides.

docs.title: Prices
docs.text: Magic Beans Tickets 1  20  10  200

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• In terms of Robux, the Magic Bean Shop is overpriced. In the Robux Shop, a ticket costs 10 robux, while a magic bean costs 30 robux. The player needs 20 tickets for 1 magic bean. That means the player is getting something for 200 robux when they could get for only 30 robux (This is similar to the Royal Jelly Ticket Dispenser).
  • For comparison, 200 robux can also be used to purchase a bundle of 10 magic beans in the robux shop, effectively meaning the player misses out on 9 magic beans if they buy 20 tickets from the robux shop to spend them on the magic bean shop.

  • As a reward from donating to the Wind Shrine.

  • As a stack reward for adding certain Stickers to the Sticker Stack:
  • Forward Facing Aphid rewards 1 magic bean.

  • Redeeming certain valid codes.
