Magnet Overview Price 5,500 Honey Shop Noob Shop Pollen Collection Range 9 Flowers Collecting Pattern Surround collectedyou (facing up) Collecting Time 0.8 Base Collection 2 Flowers Single Double Triple Large Star White 2 4 6 8 10 Red 2 4 6 8 10 Blue 2 4 6 8 10 Special Multiplier(s): None

The Magnet is a tool that can be purchased at the Noob Shop.

Crafting Ingredients 5,500 Honey

It collects 2 pollen from 9 surrounding patches every 0.8 seconds. It has a base pollen collection rate of 22.5 pollen per second on average, making it the second best tool in the Noob Shop.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• According to Slaries, an administrator on the official Bee Swarm Simulator Discord, the Magnet was the first tool Onett ever made when developing the game.
  • The Magnet is a weaker version of the Electro-Magnet, a tool that can be purchased in the Pro Shop for 300,000 honey.
  • In addition, the Electro-Magnet bears a different appearance to the Magnet; instead of the body color being red, it is yellow. In addition, it has four poles instead of two, and there is electricity in between the poles, unlike the Magnet.
  • The two are the only tools to collect pollen in a square pattern. They also have the same exact collecting pattern.
  • Interestingly, the Magnet's associated sticker portrays a different gray magnet with colored ends.
  • This is the only tool sticker in the entire game that is completely different from the original tool's appearance.
  • The Magnet's design is most likely based upon a real-life horseshoe magnet.

Mantis Location Pineapple Patch, Pine Tree Forest Respawns Every 20 minutes (17 minutes with a Gifted Vicious Bee in hive)

The Mantis is a mob that defends the Pineapple Patch and the Pine Tree Forest.

It takes 20 minutes for a Mantis to respawn after being defeated (17 minutes if the player has a Gifted Vicious Bee).

This Mob's level can range from 4-6 depending on the field it is located at.

The Mantis is green with red eyes. Its arms stick out, similar to a praying mantis.

docs.title: Strategy
docs.text: Due to the Mantis' long attack range, the player's Bees normally won't target it until they get closer/when the mantis itself attacks. Try to get at the very edge of its enormous jump range. Then, when it stops to get ready to attack, walk in a very wide circle around it. If done correctly, the mantis will undershoot and land where you were a few seconds before. This is often close enough for your Bees to start attacking, even once it retreats back. Also, keep in mind the Frozen Field Defenders Glitch can be used to defeat it, just like with most other mobs. When a Mantis is stuck in an object, the player can also defeat it more easily.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• When a Bear gives a quest that involves more than one mantis, its plural form was spelled incorrectly, such as "4 Mantiss" rather than "4 Mantises" or "4 Mantis"; This was fixed at an unknown time.
  • The same incorrect plural form applies to the Werewolf.
  • In Bee Bear's dialogue for his quests, he asks you to defeat x "Mantises", but in the quest list, it still says "Mantiss".
  • In Bee Bear's quest, ‘BEE-liz Honey-dad’, he told the player to defeat 10 Mantises, but if the player talked to him again, he didn't mention this.
  • The mantis in the Pineapple Patch can get stuck in the wall surrounding the field or in the smaller pineapple behind the Treat Dispenser, though this is rare.
  • Before the 2019-09-28 Update, the pine trees in the Pine Tree Forest could be collided with and the mantises could get stuck in them.
  • Mantises have the longest attack jump length of any mob, only rivaled by the Werewolf. Because of this, the mantises can jump outside of the field that they're defending into others.
  • The mantis has the same respawn time as the Scorpion.
  • During Beesmas 2020, you could get the Beesmas Top from the Mantis.
  • As stated by Number1Riker, a former of the Bee Swarm Simulator Discord server, the mantis was originally supposed to be a cricket before being changed into the former. The reason for the change is unknown.

docs.title: Marshmallow Bee
docs.text:
Marshmallow Bee

"+50% White Pollen, +50% Capacity, and +250% Convert Rate for 30 minutes."

COOLDOWN

1 second

CAP

25

The Marshmallow Bee is an inventory item that was added during the Egg Hunt 2019 event. It has a capacity limit of 25, which can only be exceeded by code and quest rewards. Collecting 3 Marshmallow Bees and handing them in to the Egg Hunt Info gave the player the Flight of the Bumble Egg and a badge during the Egg Hunt 2019 Event.

When used, it grants the following buffs for 30 minutes:

  • +50% White Pollen.
  • +50% Capacity.
  • +250% Convert Rate.

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• Redeeming certain valid codes.
  • 15MMembers (Gives 1 Marshmallow Bee + other stuff)
  • ThreeBeeVee (Gives 1 Marshmallow Bee + other stuff)
  • FOURtunate (Gives 1 Marshmallow Bee + other stuff)
  • The Shiny Gift Box rewards 1 Marshmallow Bee and other items.
  • The Confectionary Gift Box rewards 3 Marshmallow Bees and other items.
  • Completing Honey Bee's Beesmas quest rewards 9 Marshmallow Bees and other rewards.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This is the only item to use the word "eat" instead of "use" in the pop-up when double clicked in the inventory.
  • This is one of the four consumables that increase capacity, the others being the Purple Potion, Super Smoothie and Snowflakes.
  • There are sugar crystals on the Marshmallow Bee, something most real life marshmallows don't have. This may have taken influence from/be a reference to the brand Peeps, as they are also animal-shaped marshmallows coated in sugar, and are popular during Easter.
  • Before the April 6th, 2020 update, there was no capacity limit on how many Marshmallow Bees could be stored in the player's inventory. This was likely because the player could only obtain a limited amount of Marshmallow Bees prior to this update.
  • Marshmallow bees are one of the few consumable buffs that won't be overridden by a Super Smoothie buff. The others being Snowflakes, Stingers, Jelly Beans and Glitter.
  • Marshmallow Bee is the only bee that the player can't have in their hive.

docs.title: Mazes
docs.text: Mazes are secret areas in the game that contain items inside of them. To obtain these items, the player needs to navigate through the mazes and find them. There are currently two mazes that exist in the game, each located in their own respective location.

docs.title: Blue Maze
docs.text:
The Blue Maze is located next to the Ticket Tent (or behind the Beige Gift Box in Beesmas 2021) . It was added in the Egg Hunt 2019 Update. This requires no bee requisites to enter since it's located in the Starter Zone.

Inside the maze, the player can obtain 5 tickets by taking a left turn first and then a right turn, and a jelly bean token by taking the path on the right. There used to be a plastic egg where the tickets were in the 2019 Egg Hunt. The player can also find a star jelly token on the right, but it is blocked by a glass wall. It can be obtained by going through a passage behind the Petal Shop.

The music "Vendor" plays in the maze.

Spotted Chicks could spawn in this maze before they were removed.

docs.title: Pro Shop Maze
docs.text:
The Pro Shop Maze is located behind Pro Bear in the Pro Shop. It requires at least 10 bees to pass through the Brave Bee Gate, where the Pro Shop is located.

The player can obtain a royal jelly by going forward to the end and turning right two times, then going to the first opening available. Follow through it to find the royal jelly token.

There is also a sunflower seed token inside the maze that awards 10 sunflower seeds. The player can obtain it by taking same path as the royal jelly, but instead of turning on the last right, go to the end of the hall and follow through the last corridor.

If the player gets close enough, they can grab both tokens through the walls, making collecting them easier.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Before the Egg Hunt 2019 Event ended on 2019-05-13, there was a plastic egg token in place of the ticket token and the Mysterious Figure was in the Blue Maze in place of the star jelly token. These have been removed in the following minor update, as well as other Egg Hunt content with it. The room it was located in is still present, however.

A Mechsquito is one of the five Mobs that spawns during Robo Bear's Challenge.

This is the first Robo Bear Challenge mob that the player will encounter, appearing as early as round one. Mechsquitos often spawn a few seconds into the round.

Mechquitos spawn far away from the player and will fly towards the players' vicinity. Mechquitos hover away from the player when they are near them when not in an attacking state. When starting to attack, they will become immobile and only aim at the player for a few seconds before shooting a small exploding projectile aimed at the player. The projectile explodes upon contact or after a short while. When in the vicinity of its explosion radius, the player will get damaged and receive Mechsquito Toxin, lowering the Pollen and Movespeed of the player and can stack up to 10 times. Note: The toxin projectile cannot damage and/or affect other players, only the player playing the challenge.

A Mechsquito's level can increase depending on what round of Robo Bear's Challenge the player is on.

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
• Mechsquitos aim for where the player is, not where the player will be. Because of this, moving around in circles will often result in Mechsquitos missing their attack.
  • Stand near the Mechsquito, this will allow your bees to lock on to the Mechsquito and quickly deal damage.
  • Vicious Bee and Windy Bee provide excellent crowd control, especially since Mechsquitos often come in pairs or packs. Digital Bee can also stun many Mechsquitos at once and allow them to take extra damage via Mind Hack.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Mechsquito is a portmanteau of "Mechanical" and "Mosquito".
  • Mechsquitos have a party variant called Party Mechsquito.
  • Mechsquitos have a stronger variant called Mega Mechsquito.
  • Mechsquitos are the only mob that can appear in every round of Robo Bear's Challenge.
  • It's also the mob with the most levels in Robo Bear's Challenge.

docs.title: Mega Mechsquito
docs.text:
Not to be confused with Mechsquitos, the smaller counterparts of Mega Mechsquitos or Party Mega Mechsquitos, the Beesmas Edition of these.

Mega Mechsquito Location Any field while the Robo Bear Challenge is active.

A Mega Mechsquito is a mob that appears during Robo Bear's Challenge.

This is the fourth and last unique mob type a player will encounter in Robo Bear's Challenge, first appearing at Round 15.

Mega Mechsquitos behave similarly to Mechsquitos. Flies away from the player when they are not attacking and staying in position while attacking the player from a distance. Unlike the Mechsquitos, they try to get away from the player farther than Mechsquitos and consecutively shoot at the player with 6 small exploding projectiles in a short amount of time, inflicting Mechsquito Toxin debuff upon hitting the player.

A Mega Mechsquito's level can range from 13 to 22 depending on what round of Robo Bear's Challenge the player is on.

In Round 15 of the Robo Bear Challenge, the player has to defeat 10 Mega Mechsquitos and collect 2,000,000,000 pollen of a certain color to complete it.

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
• Mega Mechsquitos aim for where the player is, not where the player will be. Because of this, moving around in circles will often result in Mega Mechsquitos missing their attack.
  • Stand near the Mega Mechsquito, this will allow your bees to lock on to the Mechsquito and quickly deal damage.
  • Vicious Bee and Windy Bee provide excellent crowd control, especially since Mega Mechsquitos often come in pairs or packs. Digital Bee can also stun many Mega Mechsquitos at once and allow them to take extra damage via Mind Hack.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Mega Mechsquitos have a party variant of them called a Party Mega Mechsquito.
  • They also have a smaller counterpart called a Mechsquito.
  • This mob takes the longest to encounter as you need to reach Round 15 first while you can find all the other mob types during Robo Bear's Challenge.

docs.title: Melittology Machine
docs.text:
The Melittology Machine opens the Melittology tree. It's on the yellow ledge on the mountain top, near the Boost Market and Onett's Lid Art, right next to the Melittology Quests pad.

The machine is a big glass light bulb with a smiling cube inside, on a yellow and blue base with red-tipped rods. Its pad reads "Melittology Tree".

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
• The prompt is "Open the Melittology Tree".
  • It needs Rebirth 10.
  • Using it opens the Melittology tree screen, where you spend Research Points. There's no cooldown.
  • You can also open the tree from the Melittology Tree tile in your Boosts bar.

docs.title: Melittology Quests
docs.text:
The Melittology Quests pad gives out the Melittology Research quests, which earn Research Points for the Melittology tree. It's a blue and white pad on the yellow ledge on the mountain top, right beside the Melittology Machine, near the Boost Market and Onett's Lid Art.

There's no NPC: the pad itself is the quest giver. A floating sign next to it reads "was too lazy to put together a build for this".

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
It needs Rebirth 10. The quests come one rank at a time, and the prompt changes with your progress:

When Prompt No quest yet "Begin Melittology Research (Rank N of 25)" Quest in progress "Research Rank N is in progress..." Quest finished "Turn in Research Rank N (+X Research)" All 25 ranks done "All Melittology Research studies are complete."

There's no dialogue. Turning in a rank shows "+X Research". Rank 21 also gives the Eureka! sticker with the message "Eureka! Your research turned up something else."

docs.title: Melittology Research
docs.text: Melittology Research is the questline that earns you Research Points for the Melittology tree. It has 25 ranks, from the Melittology Quests pad on the mountain top.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Every rank needs Rebirth 10 and the rank before it. Each rank can be done once.
  • Each quest is called "Melittology Research: Rank N", with the description "Complete this study to earn X Research."
  • The quests give no items. Turning a rank in shows "+X Research" and gives that many Research Points.
  • Ranks 1 to 20 give 40 Research Points, enough for the whole base tree (38) with 2 left over.
  • Ranks 21 to 25, the Saturation Studies, give 36 more, for the Supreme paths.
  • Rank 21 also gives the Eureka! sticker, once per account: "Eureka! Your research turned up something else."

Goo amounts aren't fixed in the quest list, so they aren't shown here. Numbers use the game's abbreviations, as on the Rebirths page.

docs.title: Melittology
docs.text: Melittology is Re://:Swarm's research tree. It unlocks at Rebirth 10 and lets you spend Research Points on permanent upgrades, ending with the Honey Hammer and upgrades for The Supreme Saturator.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Unlock: you need Rebirth 10. Until then the game shows "Reach Rebirth 10 to unlock Melittology". The research quests need Rebirth 10 too.
  • Opening it: use the Melittology Tree tile in your Boosts bar, or the Melittology Machine on the mountain top.
  • Paths: you pick one Color path (Red, Blue or White) and one Discipline path (Bees, Tools or Abilities). Each path has 10 nodes in a line, and each node needs the one before it.
  • Costs: tiers 1 to 9 cost 1 Research Point each and the tier 10 finale costs 5, so a full path costs 14.
  • Capstone: once both of your paths are finished, the capstone costs 10 Research Points and gives you the Honey Hammer. The whole base tree costs 38.
  • Supreme paths: after the capstone, three Supreme paths upgrade The Supreme Saturator.
  • Respec: free. You can reset your Color path, your Discipline path, both, or only your Supreme paths. Resetting a base path also removes the capstone, everything after it and the Honey Hammer. A Supreme-only reset keeps the capstone.
  • Rebirths don't reset the tree.

docs.title: Research Points
docs.text:
Research Points come only from the Melittology Research quests, given by the Melittology Quests pad on top of the mountain. They're a chain of 25 ranks, and each rank needs the one before it. See Melittology Research for every rank's tasks.

  • Ranks 1 to 20 give 40 Research Points in total: enough for the whole base tree (38) with 2 left over.
  • Ranks 21 to 25, the Saturation Studies, give 36 more. Together with the 2 left over, that's exactly enough for one full Supreme path and two nodes of a second (see below).
  • Rank 21 also gives the Eureka! sticker, once per account.

Each stack also grants +10% Red Pollen, up to an additional x2.5. 5 Searing Flames 1 Flames gather x3 Pollen. 6 Red Ferocity 1 Red bees deal x2 attack. 7 Blazing Barrage 1 Every fifth Red bee attack deals x3 damage and spawns a Flame. 8 Wildfire 1 Entering a mostly Red field spawns one Flame per Red bee over 5 seconds. 9 Incinerator 1 Flames gather x2 Pollen and instantly convert 25% of it. 10 Inferno 5 Grants x5 Flame Pollen, 75% Red instant conversion, x3 Red bee attack, x2.5 Red Pollen, and x1.5 Flame duration.

docs.title: Capstone
docs.text: A Beginning to a end. costs 10 Research Points and needs both of your paths fully researched. "Master both active paths to unlock the Honey Hammer, the ultimate collector." It adds the Honey Hammer to your collectors. If the capstone is reset, the Honey Hammer is taken away again.

docs.title: Supreme paths
docs.text:
These open after the capstone and only work through The Supreme Saturator. Their nodes cost 2, 4, 6, 8 and 12 Research Points, so a full path costs 32.

  • At most two of the three Supreme paths can be active.
  • Once one path goes past 3 nodes, the other is capped at 2. So 5 and 2 or 3 and 3 are allowed, but 4 and 3 is not.

docs.title: Supreme Red
docs.text:
Turns the Saturator's spray into flames.

Tier Node Cost Effect 1 Ignition Spray 2 Each spray has a chance to start 3-10 flames inside its ring. 2 Soot Mist 4 Each spray has a chance to darken a flame inside its ring. 3 Standing Heat 6 Flames inside the ring stop burning down while the sprinkler runs. 4 Backdraft 8 When a dark flame finally burns out it lights 2-3 more around it. 5 Firestorm 12 Every spray starts flames, and dark flames convert part of what they gather on the spot.

docs.title: Supreme Blue
docs.text:
Turns the Saturator's spray into bubbles.

Tier Node Cost Effect 1 Bubble Seeding 2 Each spray has a chance to blow 3-10 Golden Bubbles inside its ring. 2 Skimming 4 Each spray has a chance to cash in bubbles inside its ring without popping them. 3 Slow Swell 6 Bubbles left sitting inside the ring keep growing and hold more. 4 Gold Rinse 8 Each spray has a chance to turn ordinary bubbles inside the ring golden. 5 Tide Lock 12 Every spray cashes in every bubble in the ring, and bubbles stop expiring while it runs.

docs.title: Supreme White
docs.text:
Turns the Saturator's spray into the flowers themselves.

Tier Node Cost Effect 1 Grafting 2 Each spray has a small chance to raise the tier of 3-10 flowers inside its ring. 2 Deep Soak 4 Flowers hit by a spray regrow faster for a while afterwards. 3 Runoff 6 Some of the pollen from sprayed flowers comes back as goo instead. 4 Held Charge 8 Flowers hit by a spray hold a bonus that pays out on the next collection. 5 Full Bloom 12 The whole ring stays at max flower tier while the sprinkler runs.

docs.title: Memory Match
docs.text:
This piece of content contains information obtained through datamining.

Due to the nature of the information, details may be inaccurate or outdated.

Datamined information: The probability of finding every possible reward. — December 19th, 2024

Memory Match is a match-style minigame located in various places throughout the map. The goal is to match as many pairs as possible to win items. There are four (five during Beesmas) of these machines that can be used. Each machine costs a varying amount of honey. (See below.)

docs.title: Gameplay
docs.text:
When activated, a screen will pop up with a board of size 4x4 or 4x5 grids. A player has a limited number of chances to match cards together. Matching a pair also costs a chance. They can gain more chances if they have the required certain ranks of field badges to get it.

Machines with rarer rewards require more honey and a higher badge rank for extra chances. They also have a longer cooldown between each activation.

If at least one match is made, a message will appear in the chat: Winner!, with the items matched and the amount listed below.

If no matches are made, a message will appear in the chat: Better luck next time!

docs.title: Machines
docs.text: Currently, five memory match types can be accessed at any time. There's also a memory match that is started upon receiving certain quests.

docs.title: Micro-Converter
docs.text:
Micro-Converter

"Instantly converts all Pollen in your bag to Honey."

COOLDOWN

4 seconds

CAP

15

The Micro-Converter is an inventory item added in the 2019-04-05 update. When used, it instantly converts all pollen in the player's bag into honey. It acts as an Instant Converter without the need for tickets and the journey to the hive, a significantly shorter cooldown, and is portable.

The amount of honey the player receives from a micro-converter is not affected by their Convert Rate, although it is affected by Honey Per Pollen.

The player can have a maximum of 15 micro-converters in their inventory at a time. Obtaining more than 15 will not add any micro-converters to their inventory unless purchased from the Robux Shop, obtained from Quests, or adding certain stickers to your Sticker Stack.

docs.title: Ways To Obtain
docs.text:
• Rarely dropped when defeating mobs, such as a rhino beetle, mantis, werewolf, Tunnel Bear and aphid, or guaranteed drop from Coconut Crab and Mondo Chick.
  • Completing some of Black Bear's Star Jelly quests and Black Bear's Mythic Egg quests (15 in total).
  • Completing some of Spirit Bear's quests.
  • Completing Dapper Bear's 4th 9th, and 13th quest.
  • Completing 10, 30, 70, 155, 170, 215, and 270 Brown Bear quests will reward an additional 5 micro-converters, and completing 80 will reward an additional 10 micro-converters.
  • A rare gift from Festive Gifts.
  • As a rare drop from Festive Mark.
  • As a reward for donating to the Wind Shrine.
  • Matching a pair of micro-converters in Memory Matches (available in increments of 1, 2, 6, or 5 depending on which Memory Match).
  • Rarely through a Cub Buddy gift in increments of 1 or 5.
  • A token behind Black Bear in between the Red HQ and the Windy Bee Gate.
  • As a drop from a Blue Clay Planter.
  • Planting it in the Spider Field makes it drop at least 10 Micro-Converters.
  • As a reward from Robo Bear Challenge.
  • As a Stack Reward for adding certain stickers to the Sticker Stack:
  • The Alert Icon rewards 3 micro-converters.
  • The Simple Skyscraper rewards 3 micro-converters.
  • The Lightning rewards 3 micro-converters.
  • The Grey Diamond Logo rewards 3 micro-converters.
  • The Magnet rewards 3 micro-converters.
  • The Spark Staff rewards 3 micro-converters.
  • The Cub Buddy Voucher rewards 3 micro-converters.

docs.title: Mobs
docs.text:
There are many different kinds of enemies/creatures/monsters (colloquially called “mobs”) in Re://:Swarm.

The most abundant mob in terms of spawn points is the rhino beetle, as there are five spawn points for them in the game, with Ladybugs being the second, with four spawn points. The mob with the longest spawn time is the Stump Snail, respawning in 96 hours.

The 8 entities that can attack other mobs are bees, flames, frogs, Rogue Vicious Bee, Wild Windy Bee, abilities, passives, coconuts, and the coal summoned from the Naughty List during Beesmas. One method for defeating mobs that reliably works for any mob that defends a field (everything other than the King Beetle, Tunnel Bear, cave monsters, Stick Bug, Rogue Vicious Bee, Wild Windy Bee, and the Commando Chick), with the exception of the Coconut Crab and Mondo Chick, is to jump continuously. It is one of the glitches where when jumping, mobs will freeze and not attack which leads to the player's bees thinking the mob isn't a threat and not attack it. Players would have to make sure their bees "know" to attack a mob before starting to jump - if the mob has not started attacking them - by waiting for their bees to begin attacking the mob before jumping.

Before the 2019-02-01 update, rewards from defeating any mob were sent to the player's inventory right after the mob was defeated. After the update, the mobs were altered to drop a ring of tokens around it instead (battle points do not spawn as tokens). Other players cannot collect tokens dropped by the mob if the mob was not spawned by them. The tokens can be collected by a token link, unless the rewards are from public mobs, meaning other players can collect the drops regardless of whether they attacked it or not.

Mobs have levels that are shown next to their name. If a player's bees are at a lower level than the mob they are attacking, they have a higher chance of missing their attacks depending on how far the level of the bee is from the level of the mob being attacked. This means that the lower the level of the bee, the more likely a mob that has a higher level than the bee attacking will deflect or dodge the bee's attacks.

Some mobs are considered passive. This means that they will not attack the player, nor the player will attack them. These include bean bugs, frogs, fireflies, with the exception of Chicks, Spotted Chicks, and Hostage Chicks.

While some mobs are considered bosses, others do not qualify for this designation. These mobs are called mini bosses, distinct from regular mobs but not qualifying as a boss. Wild Windy Bee, Rogue Vicious Bee, Snowbear, Commando Chick, and Stump Snail are all in this category.

Daylight Saving Time will affect the respawn time of the Stump Snail, King Beetle, and Tunnel Bear.

Loot Luck has the ability to directly affect the quantity and quality of the rewards that mobs drop upon defeat but will not affect honey dropped by mobs (that is instead affected by Honey from Tokens.)

When the Mondo Chick and Commando Chick use their egg block ability, it will block almost all bees' attacks, even if the bee is the same level or a higher level than it.

Stump Snail has the highest health out of all mobs and does not intentionally attack the player. Instead, it moves in a circle around the edge of the Stump Field. However, it will deal damage if the player stands in the front of the snail or in its head. Standing inside the shell will not deal any damage to the player.

From 2022-07-20 to 2022-07-29, there was a Roblox bug that caused mobs to not function properly.

docs.title: Regular Mobs
docs.text:
Regular mobs stay in certain fields and will attack the player if they enter that field. Once defeated, they will respawn after a period of time.

Monster Respawn Time can lower the time it takes for these mobs to respawn. For example, the Stump Snail normally takes 96 hours or 4 days to respawn, however, if the player owns a Gifted Vicious Bee, then that time is reduced by 15% to 81 hours and 36 minutes or 3.4 days.

docs.title: Mondo Chick
docs.text:
Mondo Chick Location Mountain Top Field Respawns Every 45 minutes - 1 hour

The Mondo Chick is a level 8 boss chick located in the Mountain Top Field. It respawns every hour at the full hour (1:00, 2:00, 3:00, etc., not in time zones that are a fractional number of hours away from UTC), and its respawn timer can be found on the side of the Mountain Top Shop. The respawn time is unaffected by the Monster Respawn Time stat. Its rewards can be shared between players.

The Mondo Chick will always spawn at level 8 with 300,000 health. It takes 333 damage automatically each second, causing its health to reach 300 after 15 minutes. If it isn't defeated within 15 minutes of spawning, it will despawn in a similar fashion as the Commando Chick. Similar to the Coconut Crab, player(s) will be rewarded depending on how fast the Mondo Chick is defeated. Due to its large range and damage, it's recommended to keep distance between the player and the Mondo Chick.

If a Rogue Vicious Bee spawns in the Mountain Top Field, it can attack the Mondo Chick, causing its health to drop rapidly.

The Mondo Chick will hide in its egg after several seconds, causing it to stop moving and block some attacks. The egg can be cracked by dealing 7,500 damage to it or by waiting 23 seconds via automatic damage.

When Mondo Chick spawns, a server-wide message displays: Mondo Chick has spawned!

Once it is defeated, players who damaged it get three messages displaying:

Defeated Mondo Chick!

Captured Mondo Chick in [Time] (Fastest Time: [Fastest Time])/[(New Record)]

Reward: Mondo Chick Blessing x[Amount]

Sometimes, the notification box may glitch out, and this would be seen instead:

Captured Mondo Chick in [Time] (Fastest Time:)

When its time runs out, it will jump out of the field towards the Lion Bee Gate entrance. A message notifies players who damaged it when Mondo Chick's time runs out, displaying:

The Mondo Chick got away!

Strangely, for some players, the message that appears when Mondo Chick is captured always says "New Record" next to the time. This includes cases when the time it took for that capture wasn't a fastest time for that player. This is possibly a bug.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• If seeking a higher Mondo Chick Blessing or struggling to kill it, have bees specialized in attack, such as Vicious Bee, Lion Bee, Rage Bee, Spicy Bee, and Precise Bee.
  • Have bees that produce ability tokens such as Focus, Rage, and Melody, that improve Critical Chance, Critical Power, and Bee Attack.
  • Build a Focus stack before the Mondo Chick spawns.
  • If the player owns a Precise Bee, they can try and stack Precision to increase Super-Crit Chance.
  • The Demon Mask or the Fire Mask is recommended, as they have stats and passives that improve the player's attack damage.
  • If the player has the Coconut Canister equipped, they can intentionally activate the Emergency Coconut Shield, giving them 10 seconds of ×1.25 Bee Attack and dropping 5 falling coconuts onto the field.
  • Having Nectars like Invigorating Nectar, which grants ×1.01 - 1.1 Bee Attack.
  • Level up bees to level 8 or higher. Bees with a lower level than the Mondo Chick are likely to miss their attacks, while bees with the same level or higher won't miss.
  • Keep a distance from the Mondo Chick, as it can randomly change direction and deal significant damage to the player.
  • Using various consumables and passives, such as Stingers, Coconuts, Oils, or Star Saw can help defeat Mondo Chick faster.
  • A Rogue Vicious Bee can help kill the Mondo Chick significantly faster, as Rogue Vicious Bee spikes can damage other mobs. However, this requires a Vicious Bee to have spawned during a nighttime sequence, specifically on the Mountain Top Field and shortly before the Mondo Chick spawns (so the Vicious Bee doesn't despawn).
  • It is not advised to use a Night Bell to summon a Vicious Bee for this purpose, as the Vicious Bee may not spawn on Mountain Top Field, and Night Bells are very rare to come across.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Mondo Chick's noises can be heard throughout the entire map.
  • This is also the case with the Cave Monsters.
  • The Mondo Chick is the only mob that has a fixed spawn point in the Mountain Top Field.
  • During the soft launch of the Egg Hunt 2020 update, the Mondo Chick only had 250,000 health. It was later changed to 300,000 the following day.
  • If the player already has the Mondo Chick Blessing buff and defeats another Mondo Chick, the new blessing will override the old buff, resetting its timer and possibly degrading or upgrading the buff depending on the time taken to defeat the Mondo Chick.
  • Mondo Chick, Stick Nymphs, and Festive Nymphs are the only mobs in the game that take damage without anything attacking them.
  • Mondo Chick, Festive Nymphs, and Party Robots are the three mobs in the game that can drop a “blessing” buff.
  • Out of these three, Mondo Chick is the only one to guarantee a blessing buff after defeating it.
  • Mondo Chick does not drop the blessing buff in token form; instead, it goes directly to the player's active buffs.
  • Onett has said on discord that he dislikes Mondo Chick "on a personal level."
  • If the Mondo Chick falls out of the Mountain Top field and into another field, when defeated, the rewards will spawn in that field it was defeated in. However, if it dies outside of a field, its drops will form in a ring.
  • As of the Beesmas 2020 update, the Mondo Chick no longer drops Marshmallow Bees.
  • There is a glitch where the Mondo Chick would fall into other areas outside of the Mountain Top Field, such as into the Bamboo Field, Blue Flower Field or in front of the Pro Shop. Rarely, the fallen Mondo Chick will not be able to move unless it falls into the Pineapple Patch. On an even rarer occurrence, the Mondo Chick will get stuck on the tall rocks adjacent to the Lion Bee Gate.

docs.title: Monthly Top Honeymakers
docs.text: The Monthly Top Honeymakers is one of the 64 leaderboards in the game and is only viewable via the Global Leaderboards menu in the System Page. This leaderboard shows how much honey players have collected over the span of 1 month. It shows 10 leaderboard positions at a time. The player can scroll down the leaderboard to see more players, all the way to the 100th place. Only legitimate players appear on the leaderboards for lengths of time (hackers/exploiters will be removed). The leaderboard resets on the 1st day of every month at 12:00 AM, CST.

docs.title: Moon Amulet Generator
docs.text:
The Moon Amulet Generator is a machine located between Spider Field and Bamboo Field that allows the player to generate and/or replace a Moon Amulet. It costs 100 Moon Charms to use.

It can be reached by traversing the obstacle course between the Spider Field and Bamboo Field, by dropping in from above by cannon and using a gliding tool or by falling off the ramp leading to the Lion Bee Gate and onto the platform.

Every time the player uses the generator, the capacity buff increases, starting at 25k and increasing by 25k each. This buff stops at the maximum of 250k capacity. However, to obtain the Moon Amulet at its highest potential, the player would have to use the generator 25 times, being when the other (potential) stat boosts max out.

When using the generator, it will say: 🌙 The moon seems to grow brighter... 🌙 If the player has reached the maximum capacity buff (+250k), the chat instead states: 🌙 The moon seems happy! 🌙

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Moon Amulet Generator glows at night, although nothing changes mechanically.
  • The Moon Amulet Generator is one of the 6 amulet generators, the other 5 being the star amulet generators in the Star Hall.
  • This is the only amulet generator that requires something other than honey to activate.
  • This is the only Generator that increases the Capacity Buff and stops at maximum.

Datamined information: How many Moon Amulets needed to max out its quality. — December 19th, 2024

The Moon Amulet icon.

The Moon Amulet is an amulet created by spending 100 Moon Charms at the Moon Amulet Generator.

This amulet grants buffs to the owner and allows the player to walk on the moon-shaped platforms (located at the back of Dapper Bear’s Shop, in the Diamond Room, and at the 30 Bee Zone Obby) at night.

The quality of the amulet increases linearly with the number of Moon Amulets the player has generated, up to 40 amulets, where its quality is maxed.

When using the generator, a message will appear in the chat, saying: The moon seems to grow brighter...

If the player has maxed out their capacity buff, the message will instead say:

docs.title: Moon Charm
docs.text:
Moon Charm

"Increases your bond with a bee by 250."

A Moon Charm, when fed to a bee, raises its bond by 250. Moon Charms are also used in generating Moon Amulets and they are used in crafting of glitter and the Helmet. If fed to a radioactive bee, it has a 1/2,500 (0.04%) chance to give that bee a mutation.

Moon charm tokens last for 10 seconds before disappearing.

docs.title: Mortar Bee
docs.text:
Mortar Bee Original Gifted "A lazy artillery bee who would rather shell the field than work." RarityMythic ColorRed Energy50 Speed8 Attack20 Color Scheme Skin#960300#720800#960300

Mortar Bee is a Red Mythic bee. It never gathers pollen or makes honey. Instead it fires mortar shells at the field and at enemies.

Mortar Bee's favorite treat is Strawberries.

The game uses the same picture for normal and Gifted Mortar Bee.

docs.title: Stats
docs.text:
• Does not collect pollen or make honey.
  • 🌟 Gifted Hive Bonus: x1.75 Bomb Pollen.

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text:
Mortar Bee has no active abilities, only passives.

  • Passive: Mortar Shell. This bee never gathers pollen or makes honey. Instead, it hovers high above the field and fires a mortar shell every 9 seconds, usually aimed at one of your other bees in the field, collecting 30 pollen (+10% per level) from 29 flowers. Shells are boosted by Bomb Combo. Each flower hit has a 2% chance (+0.1% per level, +2% if Gifted) to spawn a Flame, and each shell has a 1% chance (+0.05% per level, +0.5% if Gifted) to degrow the flowers where it lands. Each bee caught in the blast instantly converts 5% of your pollen.
  • Passive: Scorching Shells. In battle, this bee fires mortar shells at enemies that explode on impact, dealing 50% damage to other enemies within 15 studs. Each hit has a 10% chance (15% if Gifted) to set the enemy on fire, dealing 50% of this bee's attack every second for 5 seconds. Enemies cannot be set on fire again until 10 seconds after the burn ends.
  • Passive: Steam Engine. This bee's movespeed increases by up to 50% and its fire rate increases by up to 25% with Flame Heat.
  • Passive: Sluggish. Movespeed buffs are 50% less effective on this bee.
  • Passive: Inspiring Shell (Gifted only). When Gifted, this bee has the same chance as other bees to generate Inspire. When it does, it immediately fires an extra bomb-sized shell regardless of cooldown, collecting 15 pollen (+5% per level) from 13 flowers. This shell grants Inspire and pollinates flowers like a Fuzz Bomb, but never spawns Flames.

Mother Bear is a quest giver, and one of the eight permanent quest bears that can be accessed, the others being Black Bear, Brown Bear, Panda Bear, Science Bear, Dapper Bear, Polar Bear, and Spirit Bear. Her quests are focused on leveling up the player's bees and feeding them treats. She is located below the red-and-white-striped awning at the far end of the Sunflower Field, next to the Strawberry Field and Mushroom Field.

Each time she introduces a new treat to feed to the player's bees, she tells them which bees love the treat. Mother Bear gives a Star Egg near the end of the questline and a Star Treat at the end.

docs.title: Dialogue
docs.text:
Mother Bear gives a lot of information in her quest dialogues. Some of the information she gives is not found anywhere else in-game.

Quest Name Dialogue Treat Tutorial

Hello there new beekeeper! I'm Mother Bear, pleased to meet you. My cubs are away at camp, but I still can't help but feel a need to nurture! I've taken to caring for the bees of this mountain as if they were my own children. I'm going to teach you all about Bee Leveling, and the bond you share with your bees. Your bees are more than just honey-making tools you know. They have emotions too! As they grow closer to you, they become better workers. As their bond with you increases, they level up. Higher level bees gather more pollen and produce more honey. They also have more energy, move faster, and can defend you from higher level monsters! You can increase your bond with a bee by gathering pollen from fields they like... From defeating bugs and monsters... And from giving them [Treats]! Here's a [Treat] so you can test it out. Go to your hive and drag thereat] from the Egg menu to the slot of the bee you'd like to feed it to. Their bond with you will immediately increase by 10! Click on a bee's slot in the hive to see information about that bee. You can see how much bond you need to level it up to the next level! When you've done that, come back and I'll have a reward for you!

-During-

To feed a [Treat] to a bee, first go to your hive. Open your Egg menu, and drag the [Treat] to the slot of the bee you'd like to feed it to. When you've done that, come back to me for a reward!

-Completion-

Yes! Exactly like that! Just look how happy that made your little bee. It's begun to warm up to you. It even advanced to level 2! Each level increases the stats of your bees. If you want more treats, you can purchase them with honey from the machine to your left. Keep working to increase your bond with your bees and you could become a Top Honeymaker! Come talk to me again when you're ready for another lesson on caring for bees.

Bonding With Bees Different types of bees have different tastes. They have fields they like, and also fields they dislike. When gathering pollen from a field they like, they are more likely to increase their bond with you! You can see when a bee's bond increases - look for small pink numbers that pop up by your bees. Gathering from fields a bee likes and giving it treats will make it happier. Happier bees move and grow faster! Your next quest is to raise 1 bee to level 3... Raise 2 bees to level 2... And feed 5 [Treats] to your bees!

-During-

When bees become happier or sadder, they'll show it to you. They express their emotions with little smiley face bubbles! You can't please all your bees all the time, so don't worry too much if some are sad. They'll cheer up when you move around. Come back when you've raised 1 bee to level 3... Raised 2 bees to level 2... And fed 3 [Treats] to your bees.

-Completion-

Your bees are really becoming attached to you! They care about you so much they even fight to defend you. Raising the levels of your bees will become more important as you move up the mountain. If your bees are lower level than the bugs and monsters, their attacks may miss! Keeping your bees appropriately leveled will allow them to defend you. Come talk to me again when you're ready for another lesson on caring for bees.

Search For A Sunflower Seed Some treats are more special than others. If you're lucky, you may find rare treats hidden in the fields. You may even receive them from a bug you defeat! For your next lesson, I want you to find a [Sunflower Seed] and feed it to a bee! You can find [Sunflower Seeds] right here in the Sunflower Field. They'll occasionally pop out of the flowers as you collect pollen. They are quite rare, so it could take a while!

-During-

There's no telling exactly how long it can take you to find [Sunflower Seed]. [sic] But when you do, it'll look like a light blue token. Come back when you've raised 3 Bees to level 3 and fed 1 [Sunflower Seed] to a bee.

-Completion-

Oh, wonderful! How long did that take? Each type of bee prefers a different special treat. Basic, Bomber, Looker, Demo, Commander, and Ninja Bee all love [Sunflower Seeds] the most. Feed one to them, and they'll gain twice as much bond! Come talk to me again when you're ready for another lesson on caring for bees.

The Gist of Jellies There are many different types of bees you know! Each bee has it's [sic] own traits, abilities and personality. One way to obtain bees of different types is to transform them with [Royal Jelly]! When you transform a bee, they retain their level and bond, but their other stats change. Why don't you give it a try? You can find [Royal Jellies] around the map. You can also receive them as rewards for Brown Bear's quests. But I'll give you one to get you started! Come back when you've raised 3 bees to level 4, fed 15 [Treats] to yours bees, and used 1 [Royal Jelly].

-During-

Brown Bear lives near the Clover Field. Once a day [sic], he can give you 1 quest that'll reward you with a [Royal Jelly]! Come back when you've raised 2 [sic] bees to level 4... Fed 10 [Treats] to your bees... And used 1 [Royal Jelly].

-Completion-

Exciting, isn't it! You never know what your bee will transform into when you give it a [Royal Jelly]. But keep in mind you might not always like the result! Come talk to me again when you're ready for another lesson on raising bees.

Search for Strawberries Let's talk about my personal favorite treat: [Strawberries]! They're not only delicious and sweet - they're also healthy and raise your bond with a bee by 25. [Strawberries] can be found in the Strawberry Field. Also, if you're lucky, Ladybugs sometimes drop a [Strawberry] when you defeat them. I know many types of bees love [Strawberries] as much as I do... Rascal, Rad, Rage, Riley, Baby, and Shy Bee all love [Strawberries] more than any other treat! When you feed one to them, they gain twice as much bond, and even have a tiny chance to become Gifted! For this lesson, I want you to feed 20 [Treats] and 5 [Strawberries] to your bees. In addition, raise 1 bee to level 5 and 5 bees to level 4.

-During-

You can find [Strawberries] in the Strawberry Field or from defeating Ladybugs. They're the favorite treat of Rascal, Rad, Rage, Riley, Baby, and Shy Bee! Come back when you've fed 20 [Treats] and 5 [Strawberries] to your bees... and raised 1 bee to level 5 and 5 bees to level 4.

-Completion-

The [Strawberries] around here are always ripe and delicious! In fact, this whole mountain is rich and full of life! I attribute that to all the wonderful bees and their caring beekeepers like you. Remember, try to feed your [Strawberries] to a bee who really appreciates them. Rascal, Rad, Rage, Riley, Baby, and Shy Bee all get twice as much bond out of [Strawberries]! Come talk to me again when you're ready for another lesson on raising bees.

Binging on Blueberries [Blueberries] are a little hard to find, but they grow in more places. If you're lucky, you can find them in any field that has mostly blue flowers. Rhino Beetles may also drop [Blueberries]. [Blueberries] are definitely worth the hassle, though. They're the favorite treat of Bumble, Cool, Bubble, Frosty, Bucko, Diamond, and Music Bee! For this lesson, raise 3 bees to level 5 and feed 10 [Blueberries] and 30 [Treats] to your bees.

-During-

[Blueberries] can be found in the Blue Flower Field, Bamboo Field, and Pine Tree Forest. You can also sometimes obtain them from defeating Rhino Beetles. They're the favorite treat of Bumble, Cool, Bubble, Frosty, Bucko, Diamond, and Music Bee! For this lesson, raise 3 bees to level 5 and feed 10 [Blueberries] and 30 [Treats] to your bees.

-Completion-

Very well done! You [sic] bees look so pleased, I bet they loved those juicy [Blueberries]! Remember, try to feed your [Blueberries] to the bees who really love them. Bumble, Cool, Bubble, Frosty, Bucko, Diamond, and Music Bee all get ×2 bond out of [Blueberries]! Come talk to me again when you're ready for another lesson on raising bees.

Royal Jelly Jamboree Have you heard of Gifted Bees? They're very rare and incredibly useful! They look similar to ordinary bees, but they've got beautiful star patterns on them! They also come in unique colors that make them stand out! They collect 50% more pollen and make honey 50% faster than non-Gifted bees. And most importantly, they offer Hive Bonuses that enhance the power of your entire swarm! For example, a Gifted Cool Bee increases all blue pollen you receive by 10%. That's a big deal! You can receive Gifted Bees when hatching or transforming bees. A bee also has a small chance to become gifted if you feed it its favorite treat! There are even special eggs and items that guarantee a Gifted Bee. But we'll talk more about those later... Here's your next lesson: Feed 50 [Treats] to your bees... Raise 1 bee to level 6 and 5 bees to level 5... And use 3 [Royal Jellies]!

-During-

Are you a member of the Bee Swarm Simulator Club? If you are, there's a special Treat Dispenser near the Pro Bear's shop that's very helpful! Once and [sic] hour, it can give you [Treats] free of charge. The more bees you have, the more [Treats] you get! They may be useful for this lesson: Feed 50 [Treats] to your bees... Raise 1 bee to level 6... [sic] And use 3 [Royal Jellies]!

-Completion-

Your bees are absolutely enamored with you! I'm convinced you're one of the most caring beekeepers I've ever met yet... And believe me I've met a lot! If you can complete my next 3 lessons, I'll give you something special! Here's a hint: it has to do with Gifted Bees.

Search for Sunflower Seeds As you progress up the mountain, you'll need higher level bees to defend you! Higher level monsters are able to avoid the attacks of lower level bees. If you see the word "MISS" hover above a monsters [sic] head, that means your bees are underleveled. Keep this in mind before venturing beyond the 15 Bee gate! For this lesson, I want you to raise 3 [sic] bees to level 6. This will allow them to defend you from the level 6 Werewolf [sic] who defends that area. I'd also like you to feed 25 [Sunflower Seeds] to your bees. I've heard Werewolves tend to drop those! (-Missing dialogue)

-During-

You can see how much damage your bees are dealing with enemies as red numbers over the target's head. If you see the word "MISS", that means your bee is lower level than the enemy! The higher the monster's level, the more likely a lower level bee's attack will miss. This means it's very important to keep your bees leveled up as you venture to more dangerous areas! For this lesson, I want you to level 6 [sic] bees to level 6 and feed 25 [Sunflower Seeds] to your bees. [sic]

-Completion-

Your bees radiate pure joy - you can tell they are truly loved! They love you so much that they fight extra hard to defend you! I feel like you've proven yourself to be a truly caring beekeeper. From now on, I'll give you [Royal Jellies] every time you complete one of my lessons! Come talk to me again when you're ready for the next.

Picking out Pineapples [Pineapple] is one of the most popular treats around! Brave, Hasty, Shocked, Exhausted, Honey, Fire, Lion, and Demon Bee all love it the most! That makes sense when you consider it's as sweet has[sic] honey! You can obtain it from the Pineapple Field, but also as a rare drop from a variety of monsters: Scorpions, Mantises, and Spiders have all been known to occasionally drop [Pineapple]. Which is odd because I don't think they eat it... Here's your next lesson: Raise 1 bee to level 7, 8 bees to level 6, and 12 bees to level 5... And feed 250 [Treats] and 25 [Pineapples] to your bees!

-During-

Oh, I forgot to mention! The Treat Dispenser by the Pro Bear's shop also gives 1 Pineapple every time you use it. That may come in handy with completing this lesson: Raise 1 bee to level 7, 8 bees to level 6, and 12 bees to level 5... And feed 250 [Treats] and 25 [Pineapples] to your bees!

-Completion-

Oh good, you've finished! How did your bees like those [Pineapples]? They've got a strong flavor so they're not for everyone! Hopefully you've been feeding the special treats to the right bees. Brave, Hasty, Shocked, Exhausted, Honey, Fire, Lion, and Demon Bee all LOVE [Pineapple]! You get twice as much bond out of a treat if you feed it to a bee who loves it! You can tell they're appreciating the treat if it gives you an alert after feeding like this: "☺️ Brave Bee loves Pineapple ☺️" It really speeds up the leveling process. Come talk to me again when you're ready for another lesson on raising bees.

Seven to Seven Your bees are growing up beautifully! Your love for them really shows! As a reward, I've got something special in store for you... A [Star Egg]! It's a special egg that always hatches into a Gifted Bee. Gifted Bees are special versions of other bees with increased stats. They also come in beautiful colors that really set them apart! The first Gifted Bee of each type increases the performance of your entire hive. If you can finish this quest, I'll gladly give you this [Star Egg]. Feed 25 [Blueberries], 25 [Strawberries], and 500 [Treats] to your bees... And raise 7 bees to level 7!

-During-

Gifted Bees are the hardest working bees out there! They've been touched with inspiration, and that inspires all other bees to work hard as well! We're truly lucky to have them on this mountain! Come back when you've fed 25 [Blueberries], 25 [Strawberries], and 500 [Treats] to your bees... And raised 7 bees to level 7. After that I'll give you a [Star Egg]!

-Completion-

Oooh! I knew you could do it! I'm so thrilled - now I can give you this [Star Egg]. A [Star Egg] always hatches into a Gifted Bee you don't already have. Don't underestimate the power of Gifted Bees! They off much more than just their unique looks. The first gifted bee you obtain of each type grants you a Hive Bonus. This is a special perk that applies to your ENTIRE swarm, and in some cases even to you! For example, a Gifted Basic Bee increases ALL pollen you gain by 20%! That makes it one of the most useful bees in the world! It's definitely worth the hassle to obtain Gifted Bees. I'm so excited to see which one this [Star Egg] hatches into!

Mother Bear's Midterm You and your bees already share an unbreakable bond! But there is always room for more love. If you're willing to go the extra mile and complete these next 4 lessons... I'll reward you with a [Star Treat]! [Star Treats] are the most delicious treat known to beekind. Feed one to a bee, and it immediately becomes a Gifted Bee! This is incredibly useful because it lets you choose a Gifted bee you really want. Here's the first of 4 lessons: Raise 3 bees to level 8, 9 bees to level 7, and 15 bees to level 6... Feed 30 [Sunflower Seeds], [Pineapples], [Strawberries], and [Blueberries] to your bees... And feed 1000 [Treats] to your bees!

-During-

[Star Treats] are one of the most valuable things in the world! In the Ticket Tent, they are a whopping 1000 Tickets!!! But there are 3 [Star Treats] that you can obtain for free, as far as I know: The 1st, of course, is my [Star Treat]! The 2nd belongs to the Panda Bear. He tries to hide it, but I know he's got one hidden away... The 3rd and final [Star Treat] can be received from Onett, the developer of this game! I've heard he's working on something beyond the 30 Bee Gate... If you want my [Star Treat], first I'll need you to do the following: Raise 3 bees to level 8, 9 bees to level 7, and 15 bees to level 6... Feed 30 [Sunflower Seeds], [Pineapples], [Strawberries], and [Blueberries] to your bees... And feed 1000 [Treats] to your bees!

-Completion-

Fantastic job! Oh, by the way, I forgot to mention... Now that you have a Gifted Bee, you should check out the Star Hall! It's a special place dedicated to Gifted Bees located above the Noob Bear's shop. The easiest way to get there is to use a Glider from the top of the mountain. Inside, you'll find a free Royal Jelly dispenser! Once a day, you can claim a Royal Jelly for every Gifted Bee type you have! If you fill your hive with Gifted Bees of many types, you'll get tons of jellies that way! 3 more quests and I'll give you my [Star Treat]...

Eight to Eight There are different ways to obtain special treats. The most obvious way is to search for them in the appropriate flower fields. In addition, bugs and monsters have a small chance of dropping special treats when they're defeated. But one of the most reliable ways to obtain special treats is to participate in challenges. The Ant Challenge grants many special treats - the higher you score, the more you get! This will be useful for completing the remainder of my lessons. Raise 8 bees to level 8, feed 2500 [Treats] and 100 [Sunflower Seeds] to your bees... And transform your bees 8 times with [Royal Jelly]!

-During-

Special treats are one of the most reliable ways to obtain new Gifted Bee types. Although the chances of them converting a bee to Gifted is small... It can still be more reliable than simply transforming many bees with Royal Jellies. Always try to feed your special treats to bees that truly appreciate them! Here's your next lesson: Raise 8 bees to level 8, feed 2500 [Treats] and 100 [Sunflower Seeds] to your bees... And transform your bees 8 times with [Royal Jelly]!

-Completion-

As you've seen, if you love and care for your bees, they'll reward you. As you grow closer to your bees, they'll be motivated to work harder and faster! As you transition into a Top Honeymaker, this becomes more and more important. Just 2 more lessons and I'll give you a [Star Treat]!

Sights on the Stars There's another benefit to Gifted Bees I've yet to mention! And this might be my favorite thing about them... As you collect more types of Gifted Bees, you can generate [Star Amulets]! [Star Amulets] are gorgeous trinkets that grant a variety of perks. But no matter what, they always multiply the space of your backpack! At 5 Gifted Bee Types, you can generate a [Bronze Star Amulet]. At 10 Gifted Bee Types, you can generate a [Silver Star Amulet]. At 20 Gifted Bee Types, you can generate a [Gold Star Amulet]. And at 30 Gifted Bee Types, you can generate a [Diamond Star Amulet]! You can find these amulets in the Star Hall above the Noob Bear's shop. Complete just 2 more of my lessons and I'll give you my [Star Treat]! Up next, raise 3 bees to level 9 and feed 5000 [Treats] and 200 [Strawberries] to your bees.

-During-

Amulets are so interesting! Although they may look alike, most amulets are completely unique! You never know which bonuses a [Star Amulet] will give you. For that reason, it is worth generating many [Star Amulets] to find the perfect one for you. Up next, raise 3 bees to level 9 and feed 5000 [Treats] and 200 [Strawberries] to your bees.

-Completion-

That was my hardest lesson yet, but the bond between you and your bees can overcome anything! Have you checked out the Star Hall above the Noob Bear's shop yet? Isn't it neat? Every time you generate a [Star Amulet] in there, it has randomized perks! The only guarantee is that collecting more Gifted Bee types tends to increase the value of the perks. Just 1 more quest and I'll give you a [Star Treat]! With that you'll be one step closer to obtaining a [Star Amulet] of your own!

The Family Final You truly love your bees, don't you? Well, one thing for sure: they really love you! You and your swarm have been through a lot together! It might seem like your journey here is coming to a close... But don't be fooled, theres a lot more for you and your bees to do! Here's my dream: To see a hive of every Gifted Bee there is! All at level 10 - proof of the ultimate bond between a bee and it's keeper I believe you'll be the first one to make my dream come true! That's why I want to give you my one and only [Star Treat]! Complete this final lesson, and you'll be able to use this treat to turn any bee Gifted: Raise 15 bees to level 8, 5 bees to level 9, and 1 bee to level 10... Feed 10,000 [Treats]... And 250 [Sunflower Seeds], [Pineapples], [Strawberries], and [Blueberries] to your bees!

-During-

You're nearly there! You and your bees have just one more quest to complete before I'll give you a [Star Treat]! Raise 15 bees to level 8, 5 bees to level 9, and 1 bee to level 10... Feed 10,000 [Treats]... And 250 [Sunflower Seeds], [Pineapples], [Strawberries], and [Blueberries] to your bees!

-Completion-

You and your bees make such a beautiful family! Bet you never thought, when you first came here, that you'd fall for a bunch of bugs! But that's what makes this place so special! It's not just our flowers... The honey from this mountain is the best because of the bond the beekeepers share with their hive! Nobody demonstrates this more than you, thats why I want you to take this. My [Star Treat]! Feed it to a bee and it will immediately become gifted. Use this to obtain a new Gifted type to unlock a new Hive Bonus. You'll also receive an additional Royal Jelly every day in the Star Hall! While my lessons are done for now, I'll leave you a final quest (in spirit)... Keep searching for Gifted Bees to earn yourself a [Star Amulet]! In the future, I may have more to give. For now, I'll keep sharing lessons with new beekeepers so they can grow into Top Honeymakers like you!

Exclusive Beesmas Dialogue 2018 There's nothing more magical than Beemas! You are given a choice to give a present to Mother Bear or continue talking like normal. You choose to give her a present. Ooooh! What a wonderful surprise! What could it possibly be? Aww! A lovely framed photo of me and my cubs! How incredibly sweet of you! Well now, I've got something for you as well. You didn't expect me to forget my favorite beekeeper on Beemas, did you? Exclusive Beesmas Dialogue 2020 The Honeydays bring the bees so much joy! You are given a choice to give a present to Mother Bear or continue talking like normal. You choose to give her a present. What's this! Oooh you shouldn't have! Now let's see what you got me. ...(krumple krumple)... Aww! A Tabby Bee plushie! How purrfectly adorable! This'll keep me company while my cubs are away. Now for your gifts! A [Gingerbread Bear], a jar of [Oil]... And the [Stuffed Heart Ornament]! How fitting! With this on the tree, you'll receive the following boosts: +25% Convert Rate +25% Capacity in the Strawberry Field And +10% Pollen from Bees! It's no Tabby Bee plushie, but it's still cute! Exclusive Beesmas Dialogue 2022 The Honeydays bring the bees so much joy! You are given a choice to give a present to Mother Bear or continue talking like normal. You choose to give her a present. Oh! What's this? A present for me? You're the sweetest! ...(krumple krumple)... Oooh! A adorable Puppy Bee Pillow! The Puppy Bee and I share a special connection: we're both about bond with bees. That was very thoughtful of you! No [Reindeer Antlers] on it though. Maybe next year? *wink wink* Hehe. Well, I've also got some gifts for you: A [Gingerbread Bear], a some [sic] [Glitter]... And the [Stuffed Heart Ornament]! With this on the tree, you'll receive the following boosts: +25% Convert Rate +25% Capacity in the Strawberry Field And +10% Pollen from Bees! Can't wait to test my new pillow out tonight. Merry Beesmas! Exclusive Beesmas Dialogue 2024 The Honeydays bring the bees so much joy! You are given a choice to give a present to Mother Bear or continue talking like normal. You choose to give her a present. Oh! Is this for me?How very sweet of you! I'll open it right now! ...(krumple krumple)... Aww! It's a trendy tumbler that can keep my drinks cool! Or warm, considering it's winter... Or is it winter? I'm so confused! My cubs are away at summer camp, yet this place is covered in snow. That's ok though, I'm just greatful [sic] to have you around to share the Honeydays with. Now for your gifts! I got you a few things A [Gingerbread Bear], some [Gumdrops] and [Moon Charms]... And the [Stuffed Heart Ornament]! With this on the tree, you'll receive the following boosts: +25% Convert Rate +25% Capacity in the Strawberry Field And +10% Pollen from Bees! Merry Beesmas! Hope you enjoy these! I'm off to fill my tumbler with a strawberry spritz. Exclusive Beesmas Dialogue 2024 The Honeydays bring the bees so much joy!You are given a choice to give a present to Mother Bear or continue talking like normal. You choose to give her a present. Oh! Is this for me? How very sweet of you! I'll open it right now! ...(krumple krumple)... Aww! It's an evil little Snow Cub plushie! That Snow Cub is always getting up to no good, isn't it. If he were MY cub. Well, he'd probably be just as bad. I'm such a push over. Now go ahead and open up what I got for you! It's the [Stuffed Heart Ornament]! With this on the tree, you'll receive the following boosts: +25 Convert Rate +25% Capacity in the Strawberry Field And +10% Pollen from Bee Gathering! Merry Beesmas! I hope your hive enjoys that! Conclusion The bond you share with your bees reminds me so much of me and my cubs. They're only away at camp for a short while, but I miss them every day! At least I have wonderful creatures like you and your bees to keep me company. I hope your [Star Amulet] quest is going well!

docs.title: Beesmas Quest - Mother Bear’s Gingerbread House

docs.text:
Requirements Rewards
  • Collect 100 Treat Tokens.
  • Collect 100 Strawberry Tokens.
  • Collect 50 Gumdrops Tokens.
  • Feed 50 Blueberries to your bees.
  • Feed 5 Moon Charms to your bees.
  • Use 1 Royal Jelly.

100,000 Honey 5 Tickets 1 Glue 5 Jelly Beans 1 Gingerbread Bear Access to the Gingerbread House

Quest Dialogue Mother Bear's Gingerbread House

Beesmas is about much more than free honey and gifts. The true meaning of Beesmas is spending quality time with the ones you love! My cubs and I simply adore building a Gingerbread House together each year. But with my cubs away at camp, I'm having a having a hard [sic] finishing it... Say, would you and your bees be willing to help me complete it? Together, we'll build the sweetest Gingerbread House this mountain has ever seen! We'll need to collect a bunch of tasty Tokens. And maybe sample some along the way, hehe. Collect 100 [Treat] tokens... Collect 100 [Strawberry] tokens... Collect 50 [Gumdrops] tokens... Feed 50 [Blueberries] and 5 [Moon Charms] to your bees... And use one [Royal Jelly]!

- During -

N/A

- Completion -

This is everything we need to finish the Gingerbread House! Let's just stack it all together and... There! How adorable is that! Now that it's complete, the Gingerbread House will generate [Gingerbread Bears] for you! For every 2 hours you spend ingame, it will generate 1 [Gingerbread Bear]. Or, if you've already redeemed the recently added Offline Voucher... GINGERBREADS OFFLINE! As the cubs would say. The [Gingerbread Bears] generate even if you forget to check the house. Whenever you do check it, it'll give all the stored [Gingerbread Bears] to you! [Gingerbread Bears] are beloved by bees, and even have a chance to turn them Gifted! In addition, you can also use them to purchase special things in Bee Bear's Catalog. They're only here during this time of year, so be sure to stock up!

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• She, Brown Bear, and Onett are the only quest givers to give out tickets in all non-event Quests.
  • She is the first female bear added to the game.
  • She and Spirit Bear are the only female bears in the game.
  • She, Panda Bear, Brown Bear, and Onett are the only quest givers to give a star treat.
  • She is the first permanent bear released in an Update, before Spirit Bear.
  • Mother Bear gives 65 Tickets in total.
  • She also gives a total of 19,438,250 honey throughout her quests.
  • Like Dapper Bear, Mother Bear uses the Stylish Animation Pack.
  • Mother Bear, when giving the player the "Search for Sunflower Seeds" quest, tells the player to get 3 bees to level 6 even though the quest requires 6 level 6 bees.
  • Also, when receiving the "Search for Sunflower Seeds" quest, she mentions that the Werewolf is level 6 when it is actually level 7. This is because the werewolf was level 6 when Mother Bear was introduced to the game but was Leveled up to level 7 later on.
    • Both of these have been fixed.
  • Mother Bear mentions in the "Mother Bear's Midterm" quest that the Royal Jelly Dispenser gives one Royal Jelly per gifted bee type when it actually gives one Royal Jellies per Gifted Bee in the Player's Hive. This is because it gave one royal jelly per gifted bee type when Mother Bear was added but was changed to one royal jelly per gifted bee later on.
  • She is the first bear to give quests about leveling bees, using royal jelly, and feeding treats to bees.
  • Excluding her and Panda Bear's Ornament Quest, she, Gummy Bear, Panda Bear, and Honey Bee (NPC) are the only quest givers so far to not give quests that include collecting pollen.
  • She is self-aware that she is in a Roblox game, along with Panda Bear, Bee Bear, Black Bear, Science Bear, and Spirit Bear, stating in “Mother Bear's Midterm", that the quest-giving Onett is the developer of the game.
  • She, Black Bear, and Brown Bear were "nice" during the 2018 Beesmas Event, as stated by Bee Bear.
  • She is the only quest bear who (outside of event quests) never asks the player to collect pollen OR defeat mobs. Honey Bee and Egg Hunt Info are the only other quest-givers who do not require these.
  • Like Dapper Bear and Gummy Bee, Mother Bear's face decal emits light. This is most noticeable if the player looks at the glass behind Mother Bear at night or if they transform into Mother Bear using a Gifted Bear Bee's Bear Morph or a code and walk into a dark place such as the Werewolf's Cave.
  • She is the only quest bear in the Starter Zone to not have any extensions/changes to their permanent quests.

Motivating Vial

COOLDOWN

1 Second

CAP

10

The Motivating Vial is a consumable nectar vial item that was added in the 2022-12-26 update. Once used, it grants the player 4 hours of the Motivating Nectar buff instantly. It can also be used to craft other accessories.

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• Using the Nectar Condenser to condense 12 hours of Motivating Nectar.
  • Adding the Motivating Nectar Icon to the Sticker Stack rewards 1 Motivating Vial.
  • Completing Dapper Bear's 8th quest rewards 1 Motivating Vial and other items.

docs.text:
Mountain Top Field

FIELD COLOR

Red/Blue

BEE PREREQUISITES

25 bees

NECTAR TYPE

24 × 28 flowers

672

The Mountain Top Field is a field located past the Lion Bee Gate. The Mondo Chick protects this field and respawns roughly every hour.

This field grants Invigorating Nectar when a planter is planted and harvested here.

This field can spawn Red Boost, Blue Boost, Honey, Magic Bean, Ticket, Bitterberry, and Neonberry Tokens while collecting pollen.

Bees that like the Mountain Top Field are Basic Bee, Looker Bee, Frosty Bee, Honey Bee, Precise Bee, Buoyant Bee, Digital Bee, Festive Bee and Gummy Bee. Bees that dislike the Mountain Top Field are Carpenter Bee and Demon Bee.

This is a 24×28 field, containing 672 flowers. The flowers are red and blue, and the natural size is triple.

docs.title: Possible Events
docs.text:
• A level 6-8 Rogue Vicious Bee may spawn here either naturally, when the night starts, or if a player has used a Night Bell.
  • A level 4-6 Wild Windy Bee may spawn here, if manually summoned by a player from the Wind Shrine, it is level 5-6 instead.
  • There are special conditions where a Wild Windy Bee can spawn here.
  • When claiming Spirit Bear's “Tickle the Wind” quest, 3 level 4 Wild Windy Bee's will spawn here.
  • Mondo Chick spawns here at the beginning of the hour.
  • During a Stick Bug Challenge. If Stick Bug is in Pineapple Patch, Pumpkin Patch, and Cactus Field, he may jump to this field.
  • An Aphid may spawn here upon gathering Leaves.

docs.title: Obtaining Boosts
docs.text:
• Using Glitter will add 100% Mountain Top Field pollen onto the current boost for 15 minutes if the boost isn't already maxed out.
  • Using Field Dice, Smooth Dice, or Loaded Dice may add +100% Mountain Top Field pollen for 15 minutes if the current boost isn't maxed out yet.
  • Mountain Top Field Winds can be obtained through the Wind Shrine or codes. They have a base of +20% instant Mountain Top Field conversion and give +5% instant Mountain Top Field conversion and +10% Mountain Top Field pollen for each stack. Mountain Top Field can stack up to a total of 13 times.
  • Redeeming certain valid codes:
  • ThreeBeeVee (Gives Mountain Top Field Boost x3, Mountain Top Field Capacity x3, and Mountain Top Field Code + other stuff).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This is the only field that doesn't produce treats from farming. However, harvesting sprouts in the Mountain Top Field will still drop normal rewards.
  • Leaves in this field are much less frequent, and always either spawn bitterberries, aphids, or a sticker.
  • This was the only field that wasn't targeted by the Gummy Cannon during the Gummy Invasion event. (The Stump Field, Coconut Field, Pepper Patch, and the Ant Field were not in the game at that time.)
  • The Mountain Top Field used to not have a badge dedicated to it.
  • This was changed in the 2024-01-12 Update, when the Mountain Top Field received a badge, thus making the Ant Field the only field without a badge.
  • This is the first field that consists of only triple flowers, the second being the Stump Field, the third and fourth being the Pepper Patch and the Coconut Field.
  • This is also the only field without any white flowers.
  • Before the 2018-11-25 update, the Red Cannon required 22 discovered bee types, but now it requires 25 instead, so the player can't bypass the Lion Bee Gate without 25 bees or 25 bee types discovered.
  • After the 2019-09-28 update, even by bypassing the Lion Bee Gate with 25 bee types discovered but not 25 bees, the player will be teleported back to spawn.
  • The Mountain Top Field requires the most amount of pollen to unlock its Grandmaster badge, at a grand total of 1 quadrillion pollen.
  • The Mountain Top Field is the only field that cannot be boosted without the help of items or codes.

docs.title: Movement Collection
docs.text: Movement Collection is a type of boost that allows the player to collect pollen when walking on flowers. The higher the movement collection, the greater amount of pollen the player collects from walking on flowers. This boost also collects goo if the player walks on any goo patches.

docs.title: Ways to Increase
docs.text:
The player can get this boost from wearing boots or from a Moon Amulet.

  • The Moon Amulet can give from +1 Movement Collection to +3 Movement Collection.
  • Boots:
  • The Basic Boots give +2 Movement Collection.
  • The Hiking Boots give +6 Movement Collection.
  • The Beekeeper's Boots give +10 Movement Collection.
  • The Coconut Clogs give +14 Movement Collection.
  • The Gummy Boots give +16 Movement Collection.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Movement Collection isn't shown in the System Page, unlike most other boosts, such as Loot Luck and Instant Conversion.
  • If the player has movement collection on their Moon Amulet, they can still collect pollen even without boots equipped.
  • The maximum Movement Collection a player can have is 19. This can be achieved by having a Gummy Boots (+16) and a Moon Amulet (+3).

The Mushroom Field is one of the five starting fields any player is able to visit upon starting the game. It is the first red field accessible to players in the game. The field is protected by a level 1 ladybug.

This field can spawn treat, strawberry, bitterberry, ticket, red boost, honey, royal jelly, magic bean, and red extract tokens when collecting pollen.

Item Drops list Strawberries (8.33% Chance)

Treats (5% Chance) Bitterberries (0.04% Chance) Red Extracts (0.0133% Chance) Royal Jellies (0.005% Chance) Magic Beans (0.002% Chance)

Bees that like the Mushroom Field include Rad Bee, Rascal Bee, Fire Bee, Riley Bee, Baby Bee, Demon Bee, and Festive Bee. Bees that dislike the Mushroom Field include Bumble Bee, Frosty Bee, Shocked Bee, and Ninja Bee.

This field gives Motivating Nectar when a planter is planted here.

This is a 32x23 field made up of 736 flowers. The flowers are red and white, in sizes of single and double.

docs.text:
• There is a small parkour course in the Mushroom Field that can be done to obtain a royal jelly.
  • The Bubble Wand model on top of the Blue HQ can occasionally grow a face and blow sparkles onto this field, along with the Blue Flower, Clover, and Dandelion Field.

  • This is one of the two fields in the Starter Zone with a Ladybug in it, the other being the Clover Field.
  • The Yellow Walking Wiggly Person sticker cannot spawn in this field.

docs.title: Mutation
docs.text:
This piece of content contains information obtained through datamining.

Due to the nature of the information, details may be inaccurate or outdated.

Datamined information: The probabilty of getting a certain mutation, and the probability of getting a certain strength of a mutation based on the bee's level. — December 19th, 2024

An example of a mutated bee's hive slot. Note that the number depicting the bee's level is colored.

Mutations are a mechanic that buffs the stats of certain bees in the player's hive. Mutated bees have a different colored level number in their hive slot and on their wings than the standard white, respective to what stat it's mutated with. A mutated bee can become temporarily radioactive, and the radiation can spread to neighboring bees in the hive.

Every time the player feeds a bee a bitterberry, it has a 0.1% chance to get a random mutation. Royal Jellies and Star Jellies has a 0.02% chance of turning a bee into a mutated bee. Atomic treats guarantee a mutation when fed to a bee, regardless of whether it is radioactive or not.

If the bee is radioactive:

  • The chance of a mutation when using a bitterberry is increased to 1%,
  • The chance of a mutation when using a royal jelly or star jelly is increased to 1%,
  • Using many special treats (sunflower seeds, strawberries, blueberries, pineapples, moon charms) have a 0.004% chance to mutate the bee. This is regardless of whether the bee likes the treat or not.

Note that using a royal jelly or an egg on a mutated bee will almost certainly make the bee lose its mutation, just like gifted bees losing their gifted status.

A mutated bee's GUI on discovery shows a pop-up to the left of the bee, which shows the player the mutation the bee has gained, with a text box reading, ☢️ {Bee type} gained a mutation! (+x% [Mutation Buff]) ☢️

  • If a mutation is given as a whole number, it is added to the bee's base stats before multiplicative modifiers are applied.

docs.title: Mutation strength
docs.text:
Some of the information in this section has been modified for better reading. For the raw data, visit Module:Mutation Stats and the data it uses.

The upper bound of a mutation increases with the level of the mutated bee, allowing it to receive better mutations. More specifically, let lvl be the level of the mutated bee:

  • \(lvlPercentage=(lvl-1)/(25-1)\)
  • The upper bound of a mutation is scaled between the minimum and maximum upper bound of the mutation, based on lvlPercentage: \(upperBound=minUpperBound+(maxUpperBound-minUpperBound)\times lvlPercentage\).
  • The lower bound of a mutation also go through this process. However, the minimum and maximum lower bound of any mutation is the same, so there are no changes.

After that, the randomBias function is invoked with the below parameters, and the result is rounded to the nearest interval to give the final result: randomBias(lowerBound, upperBound, lowerBound, 0.5) This gives a random value between lowerBound and upperBound, with a bias to values near lowerBound. This value is then rounded to the nearest interval to get the bee's mutation strength. For more information on how this function works, see the designated module page.

The lower bound, minimum upper bound and maximum upper bound, and the interval of a mutation can be found below.
