docs.title: Temporary Quest Givers
docs.text: Temporary Quest Givers are quest givers that appear exclusively during an event. Once the event they are in is over, they disappear, along with incomplete quests they gave you.

docs.title: Sun Bear
docs.text: Sun Bear is one of the three traveling bears to appear in the game. He has appeared four times, with his first visit starting on April 27, 2018, to May 13, 2018, where he gave 12 quests and 2 belt bags. His second visit started on September 10, 2018, to October 8, 2018, where he gave 14 quests and 3 boots. His third visit was from September 28, 2019, to October 28, 2019. During that period, he handed out quests that were mainly themed around bean bugs with a final reward of 250 tickets. His fourth and last visit started on April 6, 2020, where he participated in the Egg Hunt 2020 event and required the player to help three bears with their Egg Hunt quests. Once finished, he would hand out a small variety of rewards and the Swarming Egg of the Hive.

docs.title: Bee Bear
docs.text:
Bee Bear is one of the three traveling bears who appears every Beesmas. During his 2018 visit, which started from December 19, 2018, and ended on January 31, 2019, his quests focused on creating presents and, at the very end, a Festive Bee (or 500 tickets if the player has purchased the Festive Bee Pack). During his 2019 visit from December 22, 2019, to February 10, 2020, he gave a Cub Buddy after 10 quests and the Bee Cub skin after another 5 quests. During his 2020 visit from December 25, 2020 to March 1, 2021, He rewarded players with a Festive Bee (500 tickets if Festive Bee was already owned by the player) when his first 15 quests were completed, and rewarded a Festive Wreath beequip for the Festive Bee when all his quests were completed. During his 2021 visit on December 26, 2021, He rewarded players with a special type of his own (Festive Planters), and a Cub Buddy (Tickets if Cub Buddy was already owned by the player) when his first 15 quests were completed.

For both of his visits, his quests generally have a huge variety of requirements, including collecting tokens, pollen, and goo, defeating mobs, completing quests from Polar Bear, and more.

During his 2018 Beesmas visit, he stood by the Ant Gate, while in his 2019 Beesmas visit, he stood to the right of the All-Time Top Honeymakers and in front of the Dandelion Field.

docs.title: Radiation
docs.text:
A bee is radioactive when there is an orange and white ☢️ symbol on the right of the bee's slot, along with green particles.

Radiation is a mechanic that gives a temporary “radioactive” status to a bee that lasts for 11 minutes. Bees will stay radioactive regardless of any changes to their hive slots during these 11 minutes.

When a bee is radioactive, it has a higher chance of gaining a mutation when using Bitterberries, Royal Jellies, Moon Charms, or Star Jellies. It also allows the chance of a bee gaining a mutation by feeding it special treats. Certain radioactive bees can find stickers in some fields.

Bees glow green when radioactive. The brightness of the bee is based on how much longer the radioactivity will last: the brighter the bee, the longer until the radioactivity ends. A radioactive bee's hive slot will also emit green particles.

docs.title: Ways of Obtaining
docs.text:
• Feeding a bee a Neonberry will make the bee radioactive.
  • If a bee is mutated, it occasionally becomes radioactive. This has a chance to make surrounding bees radioactive as well.
  • Global radioactivity events are initiated by Onett. At the end of Beesmas 2020, he put up a game-wide message, saying "☢️ Testing global radioactivity... ☢️", and caused many bees to become radioactive.
  • Occasionally, a bee will randomly become radioactive without meeting any of the above criteria.

docs.title: Re://:Swarm
docs.text:
The most used icon for Re://:Swarm.

A Re://:Swarm game thumbnail.

Re://:Swarm is an online multiplayer game made in Roblox by ReplicatedEvents. It is based on Bee Swarm Simulator by Onett, with rebirths added. The purpose of the game is to hatch bees to make a swarm, collect pollen, and make it into honey. Players can also rebirth to trade their honey for permanent multipliers and rewards. The game was released on August 26, 2026.

Please note that this page does not need much expansion or information as this wiki is dedicated to the game. Please check out the other pages for more info.

docs.title: Gameplay
docs.text:
New players start by claiming a free hive. Onett greets them with the Honeyday welcome, and then the game offers the optional Tutorial: a short walkthrough led by Black Bear that teaches hatching the starting Basic Egg, collecting pollen and making honey.

Players collect pollen with their tool in the Fields. Their bag stores the pollen, and their bees turn it into honey while the player is at their hive. Honey buys new tools, bags, Eggs, hive slots and other Items.

The player can also take quests from NPCs, which mainly focus on collecting pollen and defeating Mobs, but can also ask for things like collecting Ability tokens and Goo.

docs.title: Rebirths
docs.text: Once a player has enough honey, they can rebirth. Rebirthing resets their honey to 0 but gives permanent multipliers and item rewards, and it is the game's main way to progress. After the tutorial, Black Bear tells players when they have enough honey for their first rebirth.

docs.title: Rebirths
docs.text: Rebirths are Re://:Swarm's main progression system. Rebirthing spends nothing but your current honey: it sets it back to 0 and in return gives you big permanent multipliers and a set of item rewards. There are 39 rebirths in total.

docs.title: How to rebirth
docs.text:
• Use the Rebirth machine next to the Beequip Storage, near the Royal Jelly Dispenser, the Honey Dispenser and the Dandelion Field. You can also click the Rebirth tile in your Boosts bar to open the Rebirth menu.
  • You need to be holding that rebirth's honey requirement (see the table below).
  • Every fifth rebirth also needs a gate quest finished. The quest is handed to you automatically when you reach the rebirth before it, so you don't have to find the NPC.
  • Rebirths go in order, one at a time.

docs.title: What resets and what you keep
docs.text:
A rebirth only resets your current honey to 0. You keep everything else: pollen, bees and your hive, items, equipment, quests, stickers, badges and your totals.

After rebirthing, the game:

  1. Raises your rebirth count and saves it to the All-Time Rebirths leaderboard.
  2. Gives that rebirth's item rewards. These ignore inventory caps.
  3. Replaces your old rebirth buffs with the new rebirth's buffs. Buffs don't stack between rebirths: you always have the buffs of your current rebirth.
  4. Starts the next gate quest, if there is one.

docs.title: Gate quests
docs.text: Rebirths 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 need a quest finished as well as the honey. You get each quest automatically at the rebirth before it. None of them give rewards of their own: the reward is being able to rebirth.

docs.title: Rebirth 5: Royal Rebirth
docs.text:
From Black Bear.

  • Collect 500,000,000 red pollen.
  • Collect 500,000,000 blue pollen.
  • Collect 125,000,000 goo.
  • Collect 10 leaf tokens.
  • Defeat 1 Spider and 5 Ladybugs.

docs.title: Rebirth 10: It's Snack Time!
docs.text:
From Mother Bear.

  • Collect pollen in each of the 17 fields.
  • Collect goo.
  • Feed 2T treats, plus 1,000 each of Sunflower Seeds, Strawberries, Blueberries and Pineapples to your bees.
  • Collect 2,000 Sprout tokens and 5 leaf tokens in the Sunflower Field.
  • Have 5 bees at level 22.
  • Defeat 2 Werewolves.

docs.title: Red Balloon
docs.text:
Red Balloon

"Floats over the field for 3 minutes. Stores up to 5x your capacity and works best with Red flowers."

COOLDOWN

5 min

CAP

25

The Red Balloon is a consumable item that was added in the 2021-12-26 update. Once used, it creates a red balloon over the field the player is in. The balloon floats over the field, storing pollen collected underneath it. The pollen collected increases by 10%, with red pollen increasing by 20%. It holds up to 5x the player's capacity, and floats over the field for 3 minutes before floating to the hive balloon.

Red balloons have a cap of 25 in the player's inventory, and 1 per player in the field.

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• As an exceptionally rare drop from a scorpion.
  • As a rare reward from the Sticker-Seeker Quest Machine.
  • Completing Dapper Bear's 6th quest gives 1 Red Balloon and other items.
  • A Red Balloon token can be found on top of the Hive Hub after completing the parkour.
  • Redeeming certain valid codes:
  • 15MMembers (gives 1 Red Balloon and other stuff).

docs.title: Red Cannon
docs.text:
The Red Cannon is available for use once the player has discovered 25 bee types. It is located to the right of the hives, next to Black Bear, and near the Ticket Tent and the Blue Teleporter exit. It has a 5-second cooldown period.

If the player has the Parachute or Glider, they can use it in combination with the Red Cannon in order to efficiently navigate around the map due to its large range. It gives access to various places that were once tedious or impossible to access, such as the Star Hall, going outside the map, or to collect most Royal Jelly tokens, like the one on top of the Mountain Top Shop and the one on top of the hives.

If used without any buffs or gliding tools, the player will usually land in the middle of the Mountain Top Field; however, it has been known to undershoot (landing on the ramp up to the Lion Bee Gate, into the Mushroom Field, or very rarely, the fence on the border of the Sunflower Field) or overshoot (shooting the player outside the boundaries of the map). If the player has the Scythe equipped, the Red Cannon may only manage to shoot them into the Spider Field due to unknown reasons. This can also occur without the Scythe equipped. If this happens, simply jumping and pressing E at the same time will allow the cannon to shoot normally. If the player uses the Parachute or Glider and activates the cannon, the cannon will not launch them into the Mountain Top Field. Instead, they will lose momentum as soon as the cannon fires and continue gliding until they make contact with the ground.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Red Cannon is the only differently modeled cannon as for the barrel, containing a hole at the top and having a crosshair at the end.
  • It is one of the four cannons in the game, the other three cannons are the Yellow Cannon, Blue Cannon, and Gummy Cannon.
  • This is one of the three transportational cannons in the game, which the other two cannons are Yellow Cannon and Blue Cannon.
  • This cannon has the biggest range of all the cannons in the game.
  • It is the transportation method that requires the largest amount of discovered bee types to be used.
  • The Red Cannon has a cooldown of 5 seconds. While this is not normally possible to see during regular gameplay as the cannon launches the player too far to return in 5 seconds, the cooldown can be seen by using the Glider/Parachute glitch to stop all momentum as soon as the player exits the cannon.
  • This cooldown is shared by all the transportational cannons.
  • On game release, the cannon could be used by discovering 20 bee types. In the 2018-04-27 update, it was changed to 22 bee types. In the 2018-11-25 update, it was changed to 25 bee types and has remained that way since.
  • It is the only cannon to not launch the player into the Starter Zone, it instead launches the player to the Mountain Top Field, as the cannon is already in the Starter Zone.
  • On the game release, players could launch themselves from the Red Cannon to the Mountain Top Field even if they didn't have 25 bees in their hive. This has been patched.
  • When combined with a Glider, this is commonly used as the best transportation method to go anywhere on the map.
  • This cannon used to shoot the player much higher than before, allowing players to glide outside of the map and stand on top of the Bear Gate. It was later changed and now shoots the player at a much lower angle.

docs.text:
Red Clay Planter "Grows in about 6hrs, but faster near Red flowers. Grants bonus Red Extract, Waxes, and x1.2 Invigorating and Satisfying Nectar." Stats Cost10M Honey5 Magic Beans15 Red Extract20 Soft Wax ReusableYes Inventory cap- Shop limit1 Grow time6 hours Grows fasterx1.25 in fields with red flowers Pollen bonusx0.5 in fields with blue flowers, x1.5 in fields with red flowers Nectarx1.2 Invigoratingx1.2 Satisfying Pollen capacity3,000,000 Item tokens16 Puffshroom chance17% Puffshroom level4 to 5 Guaranteed items1 Red Extract2 Soft Wax1 Ticket

The Red Clay Planter is a reusable planter added in the 2021-12-26 update. Alone, it grows in about 6 hours and stores 3 million pollen. It grants bonus Red Extracts and waxes. It can be purchased in the Red HQ.

docs.title: Growth, pollen and nectar
docs.text:
• Grows in 6 hours of playtime alone, and grows faster here: x1.25 in fields with red flowers. A flower-colour bonus is weighted by how much of the field is that colour.
  • Glitter used in its field speeds it up: x1.5 for one, rising in halving steps up to x2 at 6 stacks. The stacks stay on the planter until it is harvested.
  • Holds 3,000,000 pollen at full growth. A harvest gives capacity × growth × pollen bonus. Pollen bonus: x0.5 in fields with blue flowers, x1.5 in fields with red flowers.
  • Nectar multipliers: x1.2 Invigorating, x1.2 Satisfying. On harvest it gives one Nectar type from its field, lasting grow time × growth × multiplier × 3 seconds.
  • Up to 3 bees can sip from it at once. Blue bees never sip from it; Red bees are x1.25 as likely to sip from it.

docs.title: Puffshrooms
docs.text:
When it reaches 95% growth, it has a 17% chance to smoke and spawn 3 Puffshrooms (one at the planter and two nearby) at levels 4 to 5.

Rarity odds:

  • Common 75%
  • Rare 19%
  • Epic 5.9%
  • Legendary 0.1%

docs.title: Drops
docs.text: A full harvest gives 16 item tokens. Harvesting early gives fewer, in proportion to growth, but always at least 1. Tokens are filled in this order: guaranteed items (full harvests only), then field rules, then random picks from the pool below.

docs.title: Guaranteed
docs.text:
On every full harvest:

  • 1 Red Extract
  • 2 Soft Wax
  • 1 Ticket

docs.title: Field rules
docs.text:
• Full harvests in the Clover, then Spider, then Cactus Field (in that order): 10 Stingers, once every 14 days.
  • Full in the Sunflower Field: 1 Swirled Wax (every 30 days). Pine Tree Forest: 1 Swirled Wax (every 7 days). Clover Field: 1 Caustic Wax (every 30 days).

docs.text:
Red Extract Dispenser Information Usage Grants:

Red Extracts Honey x10 Red Boost Tokens x5 Haste

Requirement(s) None Cooldown 8 hours Location Red HQ, next to the Strawberry Dispenser

The Red Extract Dispenser is a dispenser added in Re://:Swarm. It is located in the Red HQ near Riley Bee, right next to the Strawberry Dispenser. When used, it grants the player Red Extracts, honey, red boost x10 and haste x5.

It has a cooldown of 8 hours and has no requirements, so any player can use it.

docs.title: Honey and Red Extract reward amounts
docs.text:
The amount of honey and Red Extracts given is based on the number of Red bees the player has in their hive. More specifically, let cnt be the number of Red bees in the player's hive:

  • The amount of Red Extracts the player receives is equal to 10 + cnt, so it always gives at least 10.
  • The amount of honey the player receives is equal to (10 + cnt)1.5 rounded to the nearest whole number, times 200, or 500 if the result is less than 500.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This dispenser is unique to Re://:Swarm and does not exist in Bee Swarm Simulator.

docs.title: Red Extract
docs.text:
Red Extract

"Grants x1.25 Red Pollen for 10 minutes."

COOLDOWN

10 minutes

A Red Extract is an inventory item that was added in the 2018-11-25 update. The purpose of it is to use it as a material to craft accessories, or for a 10-minute boost that grants x1.25 Red Pollen. The buff cannot stack and will only reset its timer if you used a Red Extract when there is another one active. Using a Purple Potion or Super Smoothie will override the buff.

A red extract token.

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• Using the Red Extract Dispenser in the Red HQ, which gives 10 plus one for each Red bee in the hive every 8 hours.
  • Crafting it via Blender for:
  • 50 Strawberries
  • 10 Royal Jellies
  • Matching a pair of red extracts in Mega Memory Match (worth 1 red extract) or Extreme Memory Match (worth 3 red extracts).
  • As a reward from the Wind Shrine.
  • As a Stack Reward for adding certain Stickers to the Sticker Stack:
  • Flying Rad Bee Sticker rewards 1 red extract.
  • Round Rascal Bee Sticker rewards 1 red extract.
  • Flying Festive Bee Sticker rewards 1 red extract.
  • Little Scorpion Sticker rewards 1 red extract.
  • Red X Sticker rewards 1 red extract.
  • AFK Sticker rewards 1 red extract.
  • Small Flame Sticker rewards 1 red extract.
  • Shrugging Heart Sticker rewards 1 red extract.
  • Red Doodle Person Sticker rewards 1 red extract.
  • Scythe Sticker rewards 1 red extract.
  • Dark Scythe Sticker rewards 1 red extract.

docs.title: Drops
docs.text:
• As a drop from certain mobs
  • Ladybug (Rare)
  • Scorpion (Rare)
  • King Beetle
  • Rage Aphid
  • Farming in the Mushroom Field, Strawberry Field, Rose Field, or the Pepper Patch can rarely drop red extracts.
  • A rare drop from leaves in the Mushroom Field, Strawberry Field, or the Rose Field.
  • As a rare drop from sprouts (the odds increase depending on the rarity of the sprout and if the sprout is located in red fields).
  • As a drop from a Festive Gift (if Festive Bee is gifted) or Festive Mark.
  • As a rare gift from a cub buddy.
  • As a guaranteed drop from the certain planters:
  • Red Clay Planter
  • Heat-Treated Planter (Drops extra red extracts in red fields.)
    • Planting the Heat-Treated Planter in the Mushroom Field, then the Strawberry Field, then the Rose Field, then the Pepper Patch results in an additional 100 Red Extracts (unknown cooldown).
    • Additionally, it has a small chance to drop 100 Red Extracts upon harvesting in any field.
  • Planters harvested in red fields have a chance to drop red extracts.

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• Completing any of Gifted Riley Bee's quests will always reward one Red Extract.
  • Black Bear gives Red Extracts on the following quests:
  • Get Red-y gives 1 Red Extract and other items.
  • Rocky Red Mountain gives 1 Red Extract and other items.
  • Capsaicin Collector gives 1 Red Extract and other items.
  • Black Bear's repeatable quests occasionally give Red Extracts.
  • Science Bear gives red extracts on the following quests:
  • Meticulously Crafted gives 1 Red Extract and other items.
  • Mushroom Measurement Monotony gives 3 Red Extracts and other items.

docs.title: Red Field Booster
docs.text: The Red Field Booster is a machine that provides a Field Boost to a random red field for 15 minutes. The machine is located in the Red HQ. In order to use it, the player needs to have discovered 5 different red bee types. It has a cooldown of 45 minutes.

docs.title: Boosts
docs.text:
• Mushroom Field: +300% Pollen
  • Strawberry Field: +100% Pollen
  • Rose Field: +100% Pollen
  • Pepper Patch: +100% Pollen (only if player has 35+ Bees)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This is one of the three field boosters in the game, along with the Field Booster and the Blue Field Booster.
  • The Red Field Booster has the same design as the Field Booster and the Blue Field Booster, the only difference being the colors.
  • The Red Field Booster, unlike the Blue Field Booster, is located near the entrance of the Red HQ, while the Blue Field Booster is located on the second floor in the Blue HQ.
  • In an update, the Strawberry Field boost was nerfed from 200% to 100%.
  • Prior to the 2024-05-23 update, this booster was not able to boost the Pepper Patch.

docs.title: Red HQ
docs.text:
Red HQ Location Next to the Rose Field, above the Sunflower Field, and next to the Special Sprout Summoner

The Red HQ is a large, red building with a portal, a shop, and other features. It is located next to the Rose Field and near the Special Sprout Summoner. It has a Riley Bee model above the entrance. To enter, the player must have discovered 4 different red bee types. The Red HQ is the red counterpart to the Blue HQ.

On the roof, there is an enlarged Scythe. Unlike the actual Scythe, the one on the Red HQ doesn't emit flame particles.

docs.title: Interior
docs.text:
On the first floor, there are five things that can be interacted with:

  • A Red Teleporter that can teleport the player to the rock behind Science Bear.
  • The Red Field Booster that gives a 15-minute boost for either the Mushroom Field (3x), Strawberry Field (1x), Rose Field (1x), or the Pepper Patch (1x).
  • The All-Time Top Red Collectors and Daily Top Red Collectors leaderboards, which show the top 100 players who have collected the most red pollen and the top 100 players who have collected the most red pollen in a day respectively.
  • A set of red items for sale. (See the 'Store' section below.)

There is a ticket token hidden near the back of the ceiling visible from the ladder. There are 3 possible ways to reach it:

  • Climb the Red Teleporter and jump/glide onto the token.
  • From outside the HQ, get on top of the All-Time Top Red Collectors leaderboard and then jump to the token.
  • If it's too difficult to land on the leaderboard, the player may need to glide to the token instead.

The player may need boots and/or the parachute/glider for some of these.

The player can climb two ladders to reach the other sections of the HQ. The first ladder leads to a royal jelly token on the roof next to the base, as well as the Strawberry Dispenser and the Red Extract Dispenser, which gives 10 Red Extracts plus one for each red bee every 8 hours. The second ladder leads to the top, where the player will find the Top Riley Bee Helpers Leaderboard and Gifted Riley Bee, who requires a translator to be able to be communicated with. After the player gets a translator from Science Bear and uses it on Gifted Riley Bee, they can complete quests for them. The player will also find the code "ROOF" on the back side of the white facade, near the large Scythe.

docs.title: Store
docs.text: There is a store in the Red HQ that sells nine items. To open the store, press E when not on the Red Teleporter, the Red Field Booster, or the Leaderboards.

• Rogue Vicious Bee can target the player if they are close enough to the wall, next to the Rose Field.

  • After the 2019-04-05 update, a glass roof was added, preventing players from jumping out from the side and into the Rose Field. As of the 2019-09-28 update, the roof is no longer there, due to a new mechanic that teleported players back to spawn if they entered a restricted area.

docs.title: Red Teleporter
docs.text:
The Red Teleporter is a portal located inside the Red HQ. When activated, it will instantly teleport the player on top of the rock located directly behind Science Bear. The transportation is one-way; thus, the destination teleporter cannot be used to travel back into the Red HQ.

To activate the Red Teleporter, the player must walk onto the white teleport pad and press the "E" key on their keyboard if they are on PC or laptop. However, if they are on mobile, then they must walk onto the pad and tap on the button that appears at the top of the screen.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Similar to its blue counterpart, the Red Teleporter used to use an animation where each of the rings would revolve in circles. However, this can get buggy since the rings will start to spin, but then they will slow down until they reach the point of completely stopping.
  • A Ticket token is located near the ceiling of the Red HQ. This can be collected by jumping up on top of the Red Teleporter, then jumping or parachuting to the token. Enhanced Jump Power, such as from bear morph, or boots, is required to jump high enough.
  • The seven circles on the Red Portal near Science Bear are solid, and with enhanced Jump Power, it is possible to jump outside of the barriers of the map by jumping on the center part.
  • The inner parts of the Red Teleporter used to be a sphere, rather than a circle.

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Realistic max is the best you can expect to actually see: the most picks of that upgrade that about 1 in 1,000 fully waxed 5 ★ beequips get, each at its top value. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Reindeer Antlers and the Festive Wreath share many similarities:
  • The two are the only Beequips to have models visible on the bee that they are equipped to.
  • Before the 2024-01-12 update's removal of permanent Beequips, the two were the only permanent Beequips in the game.
    • This is the first permanent Beequip added to the game, followed by the Festive Wreath.
    • These were the only Beequips to have a set potential, with this Beequip always having max potential and the Festive Wreath always having a potential of 3 stars (6 points).
    • They were the only Beequips that cannot be discarded.
    • Caustic Waxes were unable to be used on these two Beequips. However, this is no longer the case.
  • A model of a Puppy Bee with Reindeer Antlers can be found outside the map, next to a model of a Festive Bee with the Festive Wreath.
  • This Beequip is likely a reference to Dr. Seuss’ children's book “How the Grinch Stole Christmas”, where the Grinch dresses his dog as a reindeer.
  • This is the one of three Beequips to give a unique ability.
  • The other two are the Snowglobe and Festive Wreath.

docs.title: Rhino Beetle
docs.text:
Rhino Beetle Location Clover Field, Blue Flower Field, Bamboo Field, and Pineapple Patch Respawns Every 5 minutes (4 minutes 15 seconds with Vicious Bee's hive bonus)

The Rhino Beetle is a mob that defends four different fields. It is the blue variant of the Ladybug.

This is one of the first mobs a player may encounter, as they are in 2 out of 5 of the Starting Fields (the others being Ladybugs and the possibility of Aphids, Wild Windy Bee, and Rogue Vicious Bee).

It takes 5 minutes for a rhino beetle to respawn after being defeated (4 minutes 15 seconds with Gifted Vicious Bee). Defeating it gives 1 Battle Point and about 75 Honey spread across 4 honey tokens. Various other rewards are also possible with their probability increasing with Loot Luck.

A Rhino Beetle's level can range from 1–5, depending on the Field that it spawns in.

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
• Rhino beetles behave similarly to most Mobs: it pauses to aim, then lunges. If the player stops to let them aim, then move, it will attack the spot where the Player used to be, not the Player's current location.
  • Some fields have objects that the player can try hiding behind, such as the stalks of Bamboo in the Bamboo Field.
  • The Frozen Field Defenders Glitch works very well against rhino beetles.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The respawn timer for a rhino beetle currently counts down from 5 minutes. However, as with most mobs, a rhino beetle doesn't always respawn immediately after its timer runs out. (Usually a 5-10 second delay).
  • Rhino beetles are the most common mob, having five distinct spawning points. It also guards the most fields; being four.
  • There is a mob similar to the rhino beetle called the King Beetle. In fact, King Beetle is a hybrid, made up of a Ladybug and a Rhino beetle, as stated by Onett on Discord.
  • It has the lowest health out of all mobs, with merely 10 health at level 1.
  • This is Onett's favorite mob. [1]

docs.title: Robo Bear Challenge
docs.text:
This page is exclusively for the Robo Bear Challenge. For the quest giver and shop owner, see Robo Bear.

The Robo Bear Challenge is a 5-minute challenge that can be started by talking to Robo Bear.

Upon entering the challenge, the player receives 2 quests, which can be rerolled once for free in the whole run. Then, the player picks 3 bees from their hive, which can also be rerolled. After the 3 bees are chosen, all other bees that aren't picked in prior rounds or the current round are locked. The player is then allowed to purchase buffs/upgrades that cost Cogs. After this, the player has 5 minutes to complete the quest that they have chosen. Mechsquitos, Mega Mechsquitos, Cogmowers, Cogturrets, are mainly spawned and Golden Cogmowers spawns at random fields during the challenge. Each 5 rounds completed gets to earn a new tier of Cog Amulet.

docs.title: Before Starting
docs.text:
To start the Robo Bear Challenge, the player must spend a Robo Pass. Once spent, the player receives 10 free Cogs and a Quest Reroll. Then, the player has to select one of two quests. After this, the player will select one of the three selected bees in the player's hive (the player must select 3 bees in the first round and 2 bees in subsequent rounds) and can be rerolled at the expense of cogs. This expense increases as it is used more. The bees in the selection is shown their hive level, their gifted status, their equipped Beequip and their mutation. After choosing the three bees, the player can purchase upgrades for cogs, there are three different upgrades the player can choose from and can also be rerolled for cogs that also has an expense increasing as it is used more.

The cost of rerolling bees and upgrades depends how high the player's current round is, and how many rerolls the player has done within the round. More specifically, let rnd be the player's current round, and cnt be the number of rerolls the player has done within the round:

  • \(baseCost=4+8\times {\frac {rnd-1}{24}}\)
  • The cost of a reroll is equal to \(\left\lfloor baseCost+{\frac {baseCost\times cnt}{2}}+0.5\right\rfloor\).

docs.title: After Starting
docs.text:
After starting the round, the player will receive the quest, the Robo Bear Challenge Debuff, and their selected bees. The unselected bees are shut down in the player's hive. The Robo Bear Challenge Debuff affects Capacity, Tool Pollen, Pollen from Movement Collection, and Pollen from Coconuts.

The player has 5 minutes to finish each quest. During the Challenge, the player is unable to harvest planters and use Beesmas Decorations. All Beesmas-related buffs (Honeyday Event, Galentine's Blessing, Festive Nymph Blessing, Robo Party Blessing and Beesmas Repentance as of the time of writing) will also be disabled during this period.

Upon completion of the quest, the round ends, and the player will receive cogs based on how many cogs the quest said it would give, along with bonus cogs depending on how fast the player finished the quest. The cogs from the Round Speed Bonus is given if the player completes the quest within 3 minutes and 45 seconds and the amount of cogs given is calculated proportionately. If the player has upgrades that grant bonus cogs, they will also be granted bonus cogs based on the total amount of cogs from all Upgrades.

After a round is finished or if the challenge ends, all mobs exclusive in the challenge will be gone along with the upgrades and the Robo Bear Challenge Debuff. This process will repeat again in subsequent rounds, but the player can only select two bees to add on to the bees they already selected.

  • Upon reaching Round 5, there is a guaranteed quest to that requires the Player to defeat 25 Mechsquitos and collect 1,600,000 of a certain color of Pollen. This Round grants the Player a Bronze Cog Amulet upon completion.
  • Upon reaching Round 10, there is a guaranteed quest that requires the Player to defeat 10 Cogmowers that are spread out throughout the mountain and collect 60,000,000 of a certain color of Pollen. This Round grants the Player a Silver Cog Amulet upon completion.
  • Upon reaching Round 15, there is a guaranteed quest that requires the Player to defeat 10 Mega Mechsquitos and collect 2,000,000,000 of a certain color of Pollen. This Round grants the Player a Gold Cog Amulet upon completion.
  • Upon reaching Round 20, there is a guaranteed quest that requires the Player to defeat 20 Cogmowers and collect 60,000,000,000 of a certain color of Pollen. This Round grants the Player a Diamond Cog Amulet upon completion.
  • Upon completing Round 25, the Challenge ends and grants the Player a Supreme Cog Amulet and the Robo Bear Cub Buddy (If not already owned) upon completion.

During and between rounds, cogs may be spent at Robo Bear's Shop.

All cogs in the player's inventory are removed once the challenge ends, which happens when either the player hatches or transforms a bee, the timer of the challenge quest runs out, if the player leaves the game, or if the player presses the “Quit” button which appears on the challenge quest box.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text:
Most upgrades cost a random number of Cogs from their rarity's range, multiplied by 1 + (round − 1) × 0.04 and rounded. That's +4% per round, so costs at round 25 are x1.96.

A few upgrades always cost the same, whatever the round: Overfit: Red (5), Overfit: Blue (5), Defragment (5), Sharpen (5), Homepage (3), SSD: Blue (3) and Bluetooth (3).

docs.text: Mechsquito Cogmower Cogturret Mega Mechsquito Golden Cogmower

docs.title: Pre-Round Preparations
docs.text:
• If you are aiming for a high score, you should use consumables, such as Super Smoothies. You are also able to use field boosts and winds during a round. Even if you're not aiming for a high score, doing so can still be useful.
  • Giving Onett a Present grants the Super Smoothie buff as well as a 3x Mountain Top Field buff. It also gives a free Robo Pass.
  • Attempt to save your quest rerolls or get the Reboot upgrade for an extra quest re-roll. Quest re-rolls are important if you get bad quests (i.e. being a red hive and getting two quests related to blue pollen, or a convert at hive quest).
  • Don't be afraid to save up cogs if the options are bad. They can be spent later on other re-rolls, upgrades, or drives.
  • Use the lock feature when necessary. If there is an upgrade that you need but cannot afford it, this feature will allow that specific upgrade to stay where it is until you select it. There is a lock beside each upgrade.
  • Prioritize attack bees such as Precise Bees, Spicy Bees, Vicious Bee, and Windy Bee. Vicious Bee is especially useful as it can attack entire swarms of mobs with Impale. Windy Bee provides excellent crowd control by damaging multiple mobs at a time with Tornado.
  • Digital Bee can freeze enemies and makes them receive more damage.
  • Avoid picking a "Convert at Hive" quest, unless your hive primarily consists of blue bees or the required amount is low.

docs.title: Tips During Rounds
docs.text:
• Always keep on your toes! Mechsquitoes will apply Mechsquito Toxin on you, which reduces Pollen and Player movespeed. This can quickly accumulate in later rounds and severely hamper your collection. Mega Mechsquitoes can also do considerable damage to a still player.
  • Prioritize Cogturrets if possible. Cogturrets can make large swathes of the field dangerous with their rolling cogs, so try to stay near them so your Bees will attack them and take them down before they pile up and make the field impossible to navigate.
  • In addition, Cogturrets only shoot their rolling cogs forward, to the left, to the right or backwards, so tracking where the rolling cogs will go and avoiding those spaces can be very helpful in dodging their cogs.
  • If the Cogmower/Cogturret spam is becoming too great, use Star Saw (if you have it). Star Saw circles around you for 30 seconds after activation, and while it's difficult to hit Mechsquitoes and Mega Mechsquitoes (owing to their flying hitboxes), Cogmowers and Cogturrets can easily be hit with it, allowing you to quickly take down these threats if the Bees are preoccupied with Mechsquitoes and Mega Mechsquitoes.
  • Finish the round quickly! A fast and decisive completion is key to a good run. As the round drags on, waves of enemies will pile up on each other, making them harder to clear. This in turn leads to a more cluttered field and a higher chance of death, ending in a death spiral that's sure to end in defeat (especially in later rounds).
  • If you're a Blue Hive or a mid-game Bomb Hive, make sure to use both Crimson and Cobalt Bee as the synchronize upgrade can save you. Also, in general there are a ton of upgrades that synergize around bombs and Crimson and Cobalt bee.
  • If you have any boost items active, such as Purple Potion or Super Smoothie when the round seems unbeatable, it is best to leave the challenge to give their buffs more time to be used in later sessions.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text: After the challenge ends, a message box displays the rewards. The number of rewards received tends to increase with a higher score. The rewards also increase in quality and quantity relative to the player's level. A higher level will also give players higher-tier Cog Amulets. The player will also only receive four rewards (other than the amulet) in varying quantities (except for the drive, which is guaranteed to have only one).

docs.title: Rewards List
docs.text:
• Honey
  • Potentially 1-2 items of the following types (has a chance to reward one more type of drive when completing the challenge):
    • Red Drives
    • White Drives
    • Blue Drives
    • Glitched Drives (Past completing round 10, chance increases the higher the round the challenge ended).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Almost all upgrades and their names in the Robo Bear Challenge have to do with actual software and software engineering processes, components, and procedures, like a robot.
  • There is a visual glitch where Cogs spent during a round or gained from Golden Cogmowers do not change the counter of Cogs on the quest menu on the right side of the screen.
  • When you complete a quest, you might briefly see a green 'Finish' button that's in the place of the 'Quit' button. It is unknown what purpose this button would have served, as the round automatically finishes once the quest(s) are completed.
  • There is a glitch where after the timer ends, it disappears and the challenge doesn't end. In this period, you get infinite time to complete the quest. It is unknown why this glitch is caused, but it's most likely caused by lag.
  • If you attempt to use a royal jelly on a bee or hatch an egg in-between Robo Bear Challenge rounds, it will prompt you with the message: "⚠ Hatching or transforming a bee will end your Robo Bear Challenge. Continue?⚠". Choosing "Yes" will end your Robo Bear Challenge, and "No" will cancel it.
  • However, despite being used to transform bees, using a Star Treat on a bee in between Robo Bear Challenge rounds will not cause this message to be prompted, and the bee can be gifted without ending the Robo Bear Challenge.
  • When in the quest picking menu, your bees are frozen in place.
  • If the player ended the session through disconnecting, the player will not obtain the amulet of the session until they claim their hive when they rejoined.
  • You can obtain Cogs outside of Robo Bear's Challenge. To do this, end the challenge right after you kill a Golden Cogmower, however the cogs won't transfer into the next challenge.
  • When you complete a round your balloon blessing will refresh.
  • TurboTobyTwo was the first player to complete the Robo Bear Challenge.
  • While receiving a quest, the players movespeed is set to 0, meaning it's impossible for them to move.
  • If a bee isn't picked in the challenge, its gifted hive bonus, or any bonus on its beequip doesn't apply.
  • Despite being unable to harvest planters during the 5 minutes timer of the challenge, your bees can still sip on it.
  • The final score is calculated with the following formula: Score = (5000 * Rounds_Completed) + (1000 * Last_Round_Progress%) + (Total_Cogs_Earned)
  • If the player manages to triumph the challenge, the score formula is instead: 125,000 + (Total_Cogs_Earned)

The Robo Bear Challenge can sometimes reward items with a quantity higher than its cap, for example, obtaining 16 Micro-Converters even if their cap is 15. The player will still obtain the item normally, not exceeding its cap.

Robo Bear is an NPC released in Beesmas 2022 update. It is located in the 15 Bee Zone, found next to the Red HQ and at the other end of the Rose Field. The main feature of Robo Bear is initiating the Robo Bear Challenge. Before gaining access to Robo Bear, the player will be first given a quest to assemble the missing parts of Robo Bear being Red Drive, White Drive, Blue Drive, and Glitched Drive. The drives can be obtained in the following quests:

  • Science Bear: Repairing the White Drive
  • Dapper Bear: Bartering for the Blue Drive
  • Panda Bear: Ready For the Red Drive?
  • Science Bear: Corrupting the Glitched Drive

When all requirements are met, the player can then access talking to Robo Bear and initiate the Robo Bear Challenge at the cost of 1 Robo Pass, obtainable through the dispensers in the 30 bee zone.

During Beesmas 2022, players were able to complete the quest by purchasing a white drive in Bee Bear's Catalog, completing Science Bear's Beesmas 2022 quest for a red drive, completing Dapper Bear's Beesmas 2022 quest for a blue drive, and completing Bee Bear's “Decorating For Drives” quest for a glitched drive.

docs.title: Robo Party Cake
docs.text:
The Robo Party Cake is a Beesmas-exclusive machine that was added in the second part of Beesmas 2022 and has returned in every Beesmas events since. It is accessible after completing Robo Bear's Party Cake quest and is able to initiate a special challenge every 10 minutes.

The Robo Party Cake frame and its leaderboard.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text:
Before completing Robo Bear's quest, the party cake is only 3 metal trusses, stacked to make a pyramid, with an unlit olive green candle on the top. The candle's number changes every year to show how many years the game's been up.

After the quest is finished, the "number" candle is lit with neon lights and a blue outline. The cake layers are olive green with different colored frames, the bottom layer blue, the middle yellow, and the top purple. Candles and sparklers are placed on the corners, and neon sprinkles are placed around the front of each layer.

docs.title: Robo Party
docs.text:
The Robo Party is a server-wide event where everyone has to defeat all the Party Robots scattered around the fields. The party is started immediately after a player interacts with the cake, and has a time limit of 3 minutes. If all Party Robots are defeated, all participants will be rewarded with Robo Party Blessing, and the player who initiated the Robo Party will be rewarded with items, as well as being able to summon a Robo Party with a higher rank. If not all of the party mobs were killed, the player's rank gets lowered. Robo Parties can also be summoned by Onett.

If all the Party Robots are defeated, the player who used the Party Cake will get an amount of Robo Party Blessing equal to the rank that was finished (Completing Rank 5 would reward the player with 5 stacks of Robo Party Blessing).

docs.title: Mobs
docs.text: The Robo Party summons party variants of Robo Bear Challenge robots. Unlike the Robo Bear Challenge, every enemy will spawn in a field and stay there for the duration of the party. The higher the rank, the higher the level, health and quantity of the robots summoned. There are four types of robots that are spawned during the event: Party Mechsquitoes, Party Cogmowers, Party Cogturrets, and Party Mega Mechsquitoes. Party Cogturrets will spawn on Rank 5, while Party Mega Mechsquitoes will spawn on Rank 15.

docs.title: First-Time Rewards
docs.text:
First-time rewards are the rewards that are given after a player successfully completes a Robo Party rank for the first time. The rewards are always the same for every player. Each rank completed for the first time rewards the player with an amount of Tickets equal to the level of the rank completed, Stingers, and at least one Balloon. Starting at rank 19, at least one Drive is also guaranteed.

docs.title: Strategies for Robo Parties
docs.text:
• Using Stingers will give x1.5 attack to your bees for 30 seconds. This can be very useful when killing high-level mobs like Party Cogturrets or Party Mega Mechsquitoes.
  • If the amount of mobs are too overwhelming, use Star Saw (if you have it). Star Saw circles around you for 30 seconds after activation, and while it's difficult to hit Party Mechsquitoes and Party Mega Mechsquitoes (owing to their flying hitboxes), Party Cogmowers and Party Cogturrets can easily be hit with it, allowing you to quickly take down these threats if the Bees are preoccupied with Party Mechsquitoes and Party Mega Mechsquitoes.
  • Vicious Bee and Windy Bee provide excellent crowd control, especially since most mobs often come in pairs or packs (other than Party Mega Mechsquitos). Digital Bee can also stun many mobs at once and allow them to take extra damage via Mind Hack.
  • Party Cogturrets will always shoot straight at where they are facing so you can avoid their attacks simply by not being in front of them.
  • Party Cogmowers don't aim for the player, allowing players to easily sidestep them.
  • Stand near the Party Mobs, this will allow your bees to lock on to the Party Mobs and quickly deal damage.
  • Party Mechsquitos and Party Mega Mechsquitos aim for where the player is, not where the player will be. Because of this, moving around in circles will often result in them missing their attack.
  • Always keep an eye on your health. While doing Robo Parties, it is easy to be too focused on killing the Party Robots, and not keep track of how much damage you've taken.
  • If you so happen to die, you can look around for fields with Party Robots when you respawn until your bees wake up.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The number on the Party Cake changes based on the game's nearest anniversary relative to its release.
  • The Party Cogturret is the only Party Robot without a party hat.
  • It is not possible to have 2 Robo Parties happening at the same time.
  • The Robo Party Blessing Icon is similar to Gifted Buoyant Bee's Surprise Party ability token.
  • Coincidentally, the Party Hat spawned upon the ability being activated is similar to the one most of the Party Mobs wear.
  • Every Party Mob behaves similar to Golden Cogmowers, spawning in random/specific fields, rather than either swarming the player or spawning in the field they're currently in.

docs.title: Robo Pass Dispenser
docs.text:
Robo Pass Dispenser Information Usage Gives 1 Robo Pass Requirement(s) Access to the 30 Bee Zone, costs 50 Tickets Location Near the entrance of the 30 Bee Zone

Not to be confused with the Free Robo Pass Dispenser, which does not cost anything and has a cooldown timer. The Robo Pass Dispenser is a dispenser located in the 30 Bee Zone. It gives 1 Robo Pass for 50 Tickets, which can be used to participate in the Robo Bear Challenge. Unlike the Free Robo Pass Dispenser, there is no cooldown for this dispenser. Players cannot use this dispenser if they already have 10 or more Robo Passes.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• There used to be a free Robo Pass token behind the Robo Pass Dispenser, this has been replaced with the Broken Drive.
  • This, the Ant Pass Dispenser, the Free Ant Pass Dispenser, and the Free Robo Pass Dispenser are the only dispensers that don't have any visible faucets, and instead have a small compartment, like a vending machine that gives out tickets.
  • This, the Royal Jelly Dispenser, and the Ant Pass Dispenser are the only dispensers that require tickets to use.
  • This, the Free Robo Pass Dispenser, the Free Ant Pass Dispenser, the Ant Pass Dispenser, the Coconut Dispenser, and the Glue Dispenser are the only dispensers that do not grant Haste when used.

docs.title: Robo Pass
docs.text:
Robo Pass

"Used to activate Robo Bear's Challenge."

COOLDOWN

No cooldown

CAP

10

The free Robo Dispenser (22 hour cooldown per Robo Pass)

Robo Pass Dispenser (50 tickets per Robo Pass)

A Robo Pass is an inventory item that was added in the 2022-12-26 update. The player must use one in order to participate in the Robo Bear Challenge. Players can only have a maximum of 10 Robo Passes in their inventory at a time unless purchased from Robux packs or received from quests.

A robo pass can be used by talking to Robo Bear and initiating Round 1 of the Robo Bear Challenge.

docs.title: Methods of Obtaining
docs.text:
• There is a Free Robo Pass Dispenser past the Bear Gate which can be used every 22 hours.
  • There is also a Robo Pass Dispenser to the right of the Free Robo Pass Dispenser which gives a Robo Pass for 50 Tickets with no cooldown.
  • As a rare drop from Rhino Beetles, Ladybugs, Spiders, Scorpions, Coconut Crab, Tunnel Bear, King Beetle, or Armored Aphids.
  • There is a Robo Pass token hidden behind a rock in the Coconut Cave.
  • There is a Robo Pass token on the green cog near the Star Hall.
  • As a possible reward from the Ant Challenge.
  • As a possible drop from Puffshrooms.
  • As a stack reward for adding a certain Sticker to the Sticker Stack
  • Robot Head Sticker rewards 1 Robo Pass.
  • Party Robo Bear Sticker rewards 1 Robo Pass.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Robo Pass took the longest time to get implemented out of all the items in the game, taking over 3 years after it was initially leaked on April 4, 2019.
  • Unlike Ant Passes, a Robo Pass cannot be donated to the Wind Shrine and will not appear when attempting to select an item to donate.

docs.title: Rogue Vicious Bee
docs.text:
Rogue Vicious Bee Location Clover Field, Spider Field, Cactus Field, Rose Field, Mountain Top Field, Pepper Patch Respawns Every 10-30 minutes

This page is for the rogue version of Vicious Bee. For the tamed version, see Vicious Bee.

Rogue Vicious Bee is a Mini-Boss that can spawn in the Clover, Spider, Cactus, Rose, Mountain Top Field, or the Pepper Patch. Rogue Vicious Bee has a high chance to spawn when it turns nighttime, or can be manually spawned with a Night Bell.

Rogue Vicious Bee has a small chance to spawn as a gifted variant (roughly 1 in 30-40 chance, or 2.5-3.3% chance). When gifted, it has more health, higher attack rate, and more damage. In return, it rewards a much larger amount of Stingers and honey. During Beesmas 2020 and beyond, it also has a small chance to drop Icicles. This, however, did not apply during Beesmas 2021.

When it is summoned, a spike sound is played along with a short tune, indicating its presence. The player will need to find it hiding in a field with a small gray spike (golden if gifted) sticking out; it will attack if a player touches or goes near its spike. While in King Beetle's Lair, a player can see a large spike if the Rogue Vicious Bee is in the Clover Field. Once the player walks close/onto this spike (whether silver or golden), the Rogue Vicious Bee will be summoned. This also damages the player if they walked onto the spike. Everyone in the server will receive a notification when a Rogue Vicious Bee attacks a player via a server-wide message: ⚠ [Gifted] Vicious Bee is attacking {Username} in the {Field Name}! ⚠

When it's defeated, a message announces: 🎉 [Gifted] Vicious Bee has been defeated! 🎉

docs.title: Attack Pattern and Rewards
docs.text:
Rogue Vicious Bee attacks players by summoning spikes from the ground. It has two attack patterns - tracking and then attacking randomly. Rogue Vicious Bee sends out 3 spikes to each player in its range and faces the nearest player. After this, it sends out random spikes while spinning in a circle. After each volley of attacks, it moves to a different spot on the field. The higher the level the bee is, the greater the number of spikes summoned. Red circles indicate where a spike is about to appear. The spikes will do approximately 40 damage to players with no Defense, and 50 if gifted.

Gifted Rogue Vicious Bee's spikes form quicker, allowing it to move more often. It also sends out 4 targeting spikes compared to 3.

Unlike other mobs, Rogue Vicious Bee's spikes are able to damage other entities and have no damage cap.

Upon defeat, Rogue Vicious Bee drops stingers and Honey. Bees gain 50 Bond plus an additional 50 for every level of Rogue Vicious Bee above 2. The amount of honey rewarded is based on the total damage dealt to the bee. Stingers are awarded as long as the player deals any amount of damage to the bee, even if the player leaves the field before it is fully defeated and/or if they get killed. The higher the level of the Rogue Vicious Bee, the more stingers are yielded. A daily bonus of 5 Stingers is also given for the first Rogue Vicious Bee defeated that day, with a cooldown of 22 hours after the daily reward.

  • Level 1-3: 1 stinger - Gifted: 6 stingers
  • Level 4-6: 2 stingers - Gifted: 9 stingers
  • Level 7-9: 3 stingers - Gifted: 12 stingers
  • Level 10-12: 4 stingers - Gifted: 15 stingers
  • Chance to give icicle beequip during Beesmas event

Note that the number of stingers given does NOT change based on how many people are fighting them.

Additionally, during Beesmas, Rogue Vicious Bee can drop the Icicles beequip when defeated. The chance of the beequip being obtained increases with the level of the Rogue Vicious Bee.

If Rogue Vicious Bee is in attack mode but there is nobody in its range, it will eventually despawn and a server-wide message will announce: [Gifted] Vicious Bee left...

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• When hunting for hidden Rogue Vicious Bees, angle the camera so that it is aligned with the side of the field to make it easier to see spikes sticking out.
  • When it turns night, check all the fields Rogue Vicious Bee can spawn in, as night signals its possible appearance.
  • When fighting Rogue Vicious Bees, the player can AFK the fight by standing on something higher than the spikes. For example, the player can stand on a cactus if fighting in the Cactus Field. This works on all fields as long as what the player is standing on is more elevated than the field Rogue Vicious Bee spawned in, and close enough to the field that the Rogue Vicious Bee does not despawn. Rogue Vicious Bee may go out of range temporarily but will often move back into range of the player's bees so they can defeat it.
  • Spikes despawn after five minutes of appearance, allowing time for the player to get ready.
  • When a Rogue Vicious Bee starts using tracking spikes, continue moving around the field. This will be indicated if it is looking at a player, and warning circles only appear underneath players.
  • When it starts attacking randomly, stop moving. The player should only move when a warning circle is directly under the character. The attack is indicated if it starts spinning, and a multitude of warning circles appear all at once.
  • The spike hitboxes are smaller than the warning circle radius. This means that not much movement is required to dodge the spikes.
  • The spike hitboxes are only on the base of the spike, meaning that it's possible to jump over it and without taking damage.
  • If a Rogue Vicious Bee is too difficult to defeat, other players that are in the server can help out. It may also be better to leave instead rather than just wasting time if you can't call out other players to help.
  • If a Rogue Vicious Bee spawns nearby, the player might hear a stabbing sound, similar to the Vicious Bee spikes sound effect.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Vicious Bee and Windy Bee are the only mini-bosses and Mobs that are also Bees, Windy Bee's counterpart being Wild Windy Bee.
  • These are the only hostile mobs that have a bee counterpart.
  • Rogue Vicious Bee is the third boss that was added to the game.
  • Rogue Vicious Bee is the first "mob" in the game to not attack by colliding, as it uses a "special ability," being its spikes.
  • It is the second mob to have varying levels, the first being Ants, and the third, fourth and fifth being Stick Bug, Stick Nymphs and Wild Windy Bee, respectively.
  • Rogue Vicious Bee and the Frog are the only mobs that are guaranteed to spawn by using an item, the Night Bells and Box-o-Frogs respectively.
  • If the player exits the field while Rogue Vicious Bee is using its tracking attack, the base of the spike will be hovering in the air.
  • When Rogue Vicious Bee is in tracking mode, it will face where its last spike was. If more than one player is fighting it, it will instead face a random spike.
  • It will continue to attack the player even if they are outside of the field, but only if they are in close proximity to the field.
  • If the player touches the initial spike that sticks out of the ground of the field, they will take damage as if they are one of the bee's attacking spikes. This spike does not activate the Emergency Coconut Shield.
  • When it turns to night, even if Rogue Vicious Bee has recently spawned, there will still be a 1/3 chance of it spawning again.
  • Rogue Vicious Bee is slightly larger than all hive bees, including tamed Vicious Bees.
  • When Rogue Vicious Bee leaves, it makes the same puff of smoke as when other mobs do when they are defeated. The same occurs if its dormant spike is not triggered and despawns.
  • Rogue Vicious Bee shines light directly under itself, unlike its tamed counterpart. The light is only visible at night.
  • The player can angle their camera underneath the field in the location of a spike, where they can get a glimpse of Rogue Vicious Bee hiding beneath the field. It can also be made visible by clearing out the flower the spike is in.
  • There seems to be a glitch where Rogue Vicious Bee's Gifted variant can spawn missing around 5% of its max health.
  • If the player collides with Rogue Vicious Bee by jumping into its body, they will take some damage.
  • Sun Bear mentions in his quest “Vicious Bee Begone” that he has had an encounter with a Rogue Vicious Bee.

The Rose Field is one of the four fields located past the Honey Bee Gate. This field can be found near the Red HQ. It is protected by two scorpions, one level 5, and the other level 6.

This field can spawn honey, strawberry, red boost, red extract, bitterberry, and magic bean tokens when collecting pollen.

Bees that like the Rose Field are Rad Bee, Rascal Bee, Rage Bee, Riley Bee, Precise Bee, Crimson Bee, and Vicious Bee. Bees that dislike the Rose Field are Puppy Bee, Stubborn Bee, Bucko Bee, Demo Bee, Baby Bee, and Diamond Bee.

This field grants Motivating Nectar when a planter is planted here.

A level 5-7 Rogue Vicious Bee has a chance of spawning here.

This is a 20×31 field, containing 620 flowers. The flowers are red and white, in sizes of single, double, and triple.

docs.title: Obtaining Boosts
docs.text:
• Using the Red Field Booster may give a Rose Field Boost. When it does, it will give +100% Rose Field pollen for 15 minutes.
  • Using glitter will add 100% Rose Field pollen onto the current boost for 15 minutes if the boost isn't already maxed out.
  • Using field dice, smooth dice, or loaded dice may add +100% - 300% Rose Field pollen for 15 minutes based on the type used and based on its current stack before getting another one.
  • Rose Field Winds can be obtained through the Wind Shrine or codes. They have a base of +20% instant Rose Field conversion, and give +5% instant Rose Field conversion and +15% Rose Field pollen for each stack. Rose Field Winds can stack up to a total of 13 times.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This is one of six fields that fireflies travel to, with the others being Bamboo Field, Cactus Field, Pineapple Patch, Spider Field, and Strawberry Field.
  • Vicious Bee likes this field most likely because roses commonly have thorns on their stems.
  • It is also the only blue bee to like a field of the opposite color. The only other bee to share this trait is Festive Bee and Pine Tree Forest.
  • This field was one of the fields which has a small section outside of the map.
  • There is a royal jelly token next to this field in a small ledge, which can be accessed by walking a small path along the Badge Bearer's Guild wall.
  • This is the only field past the Honey Bee Gate to not be defended by the Werewolf.
  • After the 2019-09-28 update, treat tokens could naturally spawn in this field.
  • This is the only field to be at a lower elevation than the gate leading to it.
  • If a Rogue Vicious Bee spawns in this field, it can attack players inside the Red HQ with its spikes.
  • Stepping in the row of flowers closest to Robo Bear does not spawn the Scorpions.

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Realistic max is the best you can expect to actually see: the most picks of that upgrade that about 1 in 1,000 fully waxed 5 ★ beequips get, each at its top value. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

docs.title: Royal Jelly Dispenser
docs.text:
Royal Jelly Dispenser Information Usage Gives 1 Royal Jelly and x10 Haste Requirement(s) 6 Tickets Cooldown 3 seconds Location Near the Clover Field and the Noob Shop

Not to be confused with the Free Royal Jelly Dispenser, which does not cost anything, or the Royal Jelly Shop.

The Royal Jelly Dispenser is a dispenser that is located near the Clover Field and the Noob Shop. It requires 6 Tickets to be exchanged for 1 Royal Jelly and 10× Haste.

The dispenser has a cooldown of 3 seconds.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• In terms of honey, the Royal Jelly Dispenser is very overpriced due to 1 royal jelly costing 1 million honey at the royal jelly shop, although if a player were to purchase 6 tickets from the mountain top Ticket Shop, it would cost more than a million honey.
  • The Royal Jelly Ticket Dispenser is one of three dispensers that require tickets to use, the others being the Ant Pass Dispenser and the Robo Pass Dispenser.
  • Coincidentally, all three dispensers have a counterpart that gives their item for free, albeit with a much longer cooldown in between usage.
  • The Royal Jelly Dispenser's free counterpart, however, requires gifted bees in order to become utilized.
  • The Royal Jelly Dispenser, the Honey Dispenser, the Strawberry Dispenser, the Blueberry Dispenser, the Glue Dispenser, and the Samovar are the only dispensers that are required to be used for a quest.

docs.title: Royal Jelly Shop
docs.text:
Not to be confused with the Royal Jelly Dispenser.

The Royal Jelly Shop is a shop located on a rocky hill between the Rose Field and the Pine Tree Forest, to the right of and just below the Blue Cannon. Players can purchase royal jelly in exchange for honey.

The first royal jelly the player buys will cost 250,000 honey. Each subsequent royal jelly will cost an additional 10,000 honey, eventually reaching a maximum of 1,000,000 honey per royal jelly.

The formula for the price of one royal jelly is \(P(n) = \begin{cases}250{,}000+10{,}000n & 0 \leq n < 75\\1{,}000{,}000 & n \geq 75\end{cases}\) \(n\) is the amount of royal jelly already purchased.

Royal jelly can be purchased in increments of 1, 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000, 100,000, 1,000,000, 10,000,000, or 100,000,000.

docs.title: Royal Jelly
docs.text:
Royal Jelly is an inventory item that can be found as a token around the map, received as certain quest rewards, redeemed in valid codes, purchased from various shops or dispensers, or various other different ways. When used on a bee, it turns it into either a Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic, a gifted variant of any of those bees, or a mutated variant of those bees.

The probabilities of Royal Jelly transformations are following:

Variant Chance Common 0% Rare ~70% Epic 27% Legendary 3% Mythic 0.004% (1/25,000) Event 0% Gifted 0.4% (1/250) Mutated (Not radioactive) 0.02% (1/5,000) Mutated (Radioactive) 1% (1/100)

Royal Jelly does NOT necessarily turn a bee into a better rarity. For example, if a player used it on a Legendary bee, they have the same 70% chance of getting a Rare bee as if they had used it on a Basic Bee. This rule also applies to gifted and mutated bees.

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• Completing Brown Bear's quests rewards one or more Royal Jelly and other items. Other quest givers give Royal Jelly less frequently.
  • Completing Black Bear's Diamond Egg, Star Jelly, and Mythic Egg quests rewards one or more royal jellies.
  • Completing Spirit Bear's quests often rewards multiple Royal Jellies. The amount generally increases with each further quest taken.
  • The Royal Jelly Dispenser near the Slingshot, Clover Field, and Dandelion Field dispenses them for 6 tickets each while also giving 10x Haste.
  • Royal Jelly can be purchased individually or in packs of 10 from the Robux Shop. It costs 45R$ for one Royal Jelly, and 300R$ for 10 royal jellies.
  • Royal Jelly can be found in different hidden and hard-to-reach locations. These jellies can be obtained only once for every player (In other words, they don't respawn).
  • Royal Jelly can be claimed using the dispenser in the Star Hall every 22 hours. The number of Royal Jelly the player obtain depends on the number of Gifted bees in their hive.
  • Finishing the Ant Challenge gives at least 2 Royal Jelly with the quantity increasing as the score increases by 50 points.
  • From the sparkles made by the faces that can appear on certain objects or by fireflies.
  • Finishing the Stick Bug Challenge or drops from Stick Nymphs during the challenge.
  • Royal Jelly can also naturally spawn in fields, but the probability is extremely low.
  • Growing a sprout may drop Royal Jelly tokens depending on the type of sprout.
  • The Royal Jelly Shop near the Red HQ, where players can buy a Royal Jelly for 250,000 honey initially, with the price increasing by 10,000 honey with each purchase until capping at 1,000,000 honey.
  • As a drop from specific Planters (Ticket, Plastic, Blue Clay, Tacky, Petal).
  • A sprout in Clover Field drops more Royal Jelly than any other field.
  • As a reward from placing certain Stickers on the Sticker Stack.
  • Defeating mobs may drop Royal Jelly.
  • As a reward from the Memory Match.
  • As a drop from Festive Gifts.
  • As a drop from Festive Mark.
  • As a reward from the Wind Shrine.
  • As a gift from a Cub Buddy.

docs.title: Token Locations
docs.text:
Arranged roughly in order of minimum bees/items required. Not all possible methods are listed here. For example, almost any place that can be reached using the Yellow Cannon plus the parachute can also be reached using the Blue or Red Cannon plus the Glider.

  • No bees are required:
  • On the tallest mushroom in the Mushroom Field. (Parkour starting at the mushroom at the front left corner of the field. Alternatively, parachute down from a high spot.)
  • Above the awning inside the Noob Shop (Obby (parkour) starting behind the Honey Dispenser.)
  • On top of the Ticket Tent.
  • 5 bees are required:
  • On a bamboo shoot in the Bamboo Field (Parkour starting between the Bamboo Field and the Spider Field. Alternatively, parachute/glide down from a suitable high spot).
  • In the blue ramp (Red during Beesmas) near the Bamboo Field (Enter the tunnel either by walking along the ledge toward Blue HQ or dropping down into the area between Blue HQ's roof and Science Bear's platform. Alternatively, jump up from the Bamboo Field with enhanced jump power.
  • Enhanced jump power OR the Parachute/Glider are required:
  • On a hill behind Brown Bear (If the player can, they could jump up from in front of Brown Bear; otherwise, parachute/glide down from a suitable higher place, such as the roof of Blue HQ).
  • 4 blue bee types discovered are required:
  • The second floor of the Blue HQ.
  • 10 bees are required:
  • In a maze behind Pro Bear in the Pro Shop.
  • Parachute/Glider plus 12 bee types and 10 bees are required:
  • On the tallest dandelion in the Dandelion Field (Use the Yellow Cannon and then the parachute/glide. Alternatively, if the player has 15 bees but not 12 types, parachuting from the front of the Lion Bee Gate can also work).
  • On top of the Noob Shop, near the wall next to the Clover Field (Yellow cannon and parachute/glider).
  • 15 bees are required:
  • On a small ledge above the Rose Field (Go around the back of the Badge Bearer's Guild and jump down).
  • Behind a pumpkin in the corner of the Pumpkin Patch.
  • 15 bees plus 4 red bee types OR enhanced jump power are required:
  • On a hill next to the Red HQ (Go inside Red HQ, then go up the ladder. OR, if the player can jump high enough, they could jump from the Sunflower Field to the Red HQ entrance, then jump up to the top of the white picket fence on the left, and from there, it's just a small hop to the jelly).
  • 15 bees plus Parachute/Glider are required:
  • On top of a tree in the Pine Tree Forest (Using the parachute/glider, parkour along the white cliffs starting near the Polar Bear. Alternatively, use the Red Cannon and then deploy the parachute/glider).
  • At the end of a dark tunnel above the Pro Shop - it's the one the player can tantalizingly see, but not reach when they're doing the parkour for the royal jelly above a pine tree. (Parachute down and around from the ramp to the Lion Bee Gate. Make sure to start by jumping up, and making as small a circle as possible onto the roof of the shop. Alternatively, if the player has 25 bees, walking off the edge of the Mountain Top Field onto the Pro Shop works).
  • 25 bee types are required:
  • On top of the Mountain Top Shop (Use the Red Cannon, then land on the top of the shop using a parachute/glider).
  • Behind the Onett statue on top of the sixth beehive (Use the Red Cannon, then deploy the parachute/glider once the player is high enough up to curve back around to the top of the hive. Alternatively, the player may be able to reach this one with the other cannons + Parachute + perseverance or jump from the top of the Puppy Bee on the ticket tent with enough speed and jump power).
  • Need 30 bees plus at night:
  • On top of the 30-bee area in the front of Bubble Bee Man (Parkour starting at the right of the big platform from the entrance where Onett and the lid are on there).

docs.title: Star Jelly
docs.text:
Star Jelly turns a bee into a random gifted bee, with the same rarity chances as normal Royal Jellies.

  • Certain quests are guaranteed to give Star Jellies, while others are randomized.
  • There is a chance to get a Star Jelly for doing Black Bear's repeatable quests.
  • Obtained by finishing all of the quests in Black Bear's Star Jelly questline, by completing Bubble Trouble and Pollen Fetcher 6 on the Mythic Egg questline.
  • Obtained by finishing Science Bear's Beesperanto and Epistemological Endeavor quests in the Translator questline and Corrupting The Glitched Drive in the Drives questline.
  • Obtained by finishing the 90th and 195th quest from Brown Bear.
  • Obtained by finishing the 5th, 15th, and 21st - 30th quests from Spirit Bear.
  • Obtained by starting the 7th Spirit Bear quest.
  • Obtained by finishing the 25th quest from Gifted Bucko Bee or Gifted Riley Bee.
  • Obtained by finishing the 5th quest and 10th quest from Dapper Bear.
  • Obtained by finishing the 2nd quest in the Drive questline.
  • Every 10 quests completed from Honey Bee (NPC) rewards a Star Jelly until the 100th quest.

A Star Jelly token.

  • Can be crafted using the Blender (100 Royal Jelly and 3 Glitter).
  • Obtained from certain Robux packs.
  • A guaranteed drop from Stump Snail, Coconut Crab and when capturing Commando Chick for the 15th time.
  • A chance of being a drop from a Spider, Werewolf, Mondo Chick, Tunnel Bear, Stick Bug, Wild Windy Bee and King Beetle.
  • If a player's score is 10M+ in the Stick Bug Challenge, they are guaranteed at least 1 Star Jelly. The higher their score, the more Star Jelly they can get, and also Star Jelly drops from stick bug when he is defeated.
  • There is an exceptionally rare chance to get a Star Jelly from the Clover Field or from leaves in the Clover Field.
  • There is a chance to get a Star Jelly from a Festive Gift (only if the Festive Bee is gifted).
  • There is a chance to get a Star Jelly from nudging fireflies.
  • Obtained from Rare, Epic, Legendary, Supreme, and Moon Sprouts.
  • A reward from Mega, Night, and Extreme Memory Matches.
  • A slim chance of obtaining through a Cub Buddy gift.
  • Catching a Meteor has a small chance to award a Star Jelly.
  • A rare drop from any planter.
  • A common drop from the Petal Planter and The Planter Of Plenty.
  • As a rare drop from a Puffshroom.
  • A rare drop from Robo Bear Challenge.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Event bee jellies have infinite uses; as long as the hive does not already have that bee, the player can use the jelly.
  • Royal Jelly is based off the real-life counterpart. The eponymous substance is used as nutrition for honey bee larvae and queens.
  • Sun Bear gave a hint about the Royal Jelly on top of the Ticket Tent in his dialogue.
  • When the player is transforming any bee with any type of royal jelly, the number of exclamation marks after the bee's name is the same as that bee's tier.
  • Common/Rare = 1 exclamation mark (!), Epic = 2 exclamation marks (!!), Legendary/Event = 3 exclamation marks (!!!) and Mythic = 4 exclamation marks (!!!!).
  • Using a specific jelly on said bee (e.g. using a Bubble Bee Jelly on a Bubble Bee) does not use the jelly, and no transformation pop-up appears.
  • Event Bee jellies cannot make the bee gifted even if it was gifted before.
  • The plural for royal jelly is incorrectly spelled as 'Royal Jellys', rather than 'Royal Jellies'. This is a mistake that has happened with other items with a plural form that exchanges a 'y' for 'ies'.
  • Using a normal jelly on a gifted/mutated bee is almost CERTAIN to cause the bee to lose its gifted/mutated status. It is a 1/250 chance to get a gifted bee back and 1/5000 chance to get a mutated bee back. However, the bee will most likely have a different mutation.
  • If you attempt to use a royal jelly on a bee in between Robo Bear Challenge rounds, it will prompt you with the message: "⚠ Hatching or transforming a bee will end your Robo Bear Challenge. Continue?⚠". Choosing "Yes" will end your Robo Bear Challenge, and "No" will cancel it.
  • The rarest possible bee obtained from Royal Jelly is a specific mythic bee that is gifted and has the mutation bee ability rate with a chance of 1/104T.
  • The description of Royal Jelly does not actually say that you can get a Mythic bee.
  • Star Jelly token behind Blue Maze used to give 3 Star Jellies, instead of 1.

  • An effective method of obtaining large amounts of Star Jelly is fighting Stick Bug with its Beesmas quests completed, as the player can obtain a few star jellies when the challenge ends and some from Festive Nymphs or Stick Bug himself.

  • Star Jelly’s raw ingredients cost:

docs.title: Samovar
docs.text:
The Samovar is a machine that was added in Beesmas 2021 and has returned in Beesmas 2022, 2024, and 2025. This machine can be unlocked by completing Dapper Bear's Beesmas quest, and when activated, it rewards a random Nectar type and items near the cup. The Samovar has a cooldown of 6 hours.

If a player stands on the activation platform with Samovar without completing Dapper Bear's Beesmas quest, the following message will appear: This strange thing is looking a little rusty...

When a player uses the Samovar, the following messages appear (where "nth" refers to the number of times you've used the Samovar previously):

This is your [nth] time using the Samovar.

Each time you use it, the brew gets stronger...

docs.title: Drops
docs.text:
It is important to note that despite what is said, the Samovar lists how many times it was used previously, not how many uses it is on currently. For example: If the message says you are on the 24th use, then you are actually on the 25th use.

Every time the Samovar is used, the amount of Nectar received will increase by 5 minutes, capping at 4 hours and affected by nectar multipliers. Honeysuckles increases by 1 each use, stopping at 30 Honeysuckles.

The Samovar has a fixed cycle of rewards: Oil -> Enzymes -> Gumdrops -> Glitter -> Ticket Planter.

Every 25th use, a Turpentine is rewarded instead.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This and the Robo Party Cake are currently the only Beesmas decorations not added in the Beesmas 2020 event.
  • It would take 36 uses to get the max amount of nectar from this machine, and therefore 216 hours of cooldown, or 9 days.
  • The nectar collected from the Samovar will contribute to quests requiring a specific type of nectar.

Science Bear is a quest giver, and one of the eight permanent quest bears that can be accessed in the game, the others being Black Bear, Brown Bear, Mother Bear, Panda Bear, Dapper Bear, Polar Bear, and Spirit Bear.

He is the fifth quest bear to be reached in the game. To reach Science Bear, the player must have a minimum of 10 bees to pass the Brave Bee Gate.

Science Bear is located under the Red Teleporter destination, and next to the Yellow Cannon after going up the ramp between the Instant Converter and the Magic Bean Shop.

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
Science Bear's quests require defeating Mobs, discovering bees, and collecting Pollen, Goo, Ability Tokens, and Badges. In return, he will give Honey and a stack of Science Enhancement, which increases the player's bees' honey production rate by 25%. He may also give other items and crafting resources.

There are 16 quests in the initial series and 15 in the Translator series which is a total of 31 different quests. He gives a translator on the 21st, 26th, and 31st quest.

docs.text:
The formula for the Production Rate is as follows:

25(n+1)%, where n is the Level of Science Enhancement.

The formula for the Honey per Second (Basic Bee) is as follows:

5(n+5)%, where n is the Level of Science Enhancement.
