500 Pineapples (Upon receiving quest) 500 Sunflower Seeds (Upon receiving quest) 500 Gumdrops (Upon receiving quest) Play Memory Match (Upon receiving quest)

7,000,000,000 Honey 5 Glitter 5 Star Jellies 50 Magic Beans 250 Moon Charms 250 Gumdrops 15 Micro-Converters 10 Field Dice

Spring Out Of The Mountain (30)
  • Earn 5 Grandmaster Badges.
  • Collect 10,000,000,000 White Pollen.
  • Collect 10,000,000,000 Pollen from the Mountain Top Field.
  • Collect 6,000,000,000 Pollen from the Coconut Field.
  • Collect 4,000,000,000 Pollen from the Stump Field.
  • Collect 3,000,000,000 Pollen from the Dandelion Field.
  • Collect 1,000,000,000 Goo from White Flowers.
  • Share 500 Jelly Bean Tokens.
  • Collect 100 Royal Jelly Tokens.
  • Collect 1000 Tokens from Wild Windy Bee.
  • Donate 50 Cloud Vials to the Wind Shrine.
Summons, in order, delayed by 2 minutes each (Upon claiming quest):
  • 1 level 6 Wild Windy Bee at Mountain Top Field
  • 1 level 7 Wild Windy Bee at Pineapple Patch
  • 1 level 8 Wild Windy Bee at Coconut Field
  • 2 level 8 and 1 level 9 Wild Windy Bees at Mountain Top Field

10,000,000,000 Honey 5 Glitter 5 Star Jellies 1 Spirit Petal

docs.title: Dialogue
docs.text:
Spirit Bear gives plenty of information in her dialogues. Some of the information she gives is not found anywhere else in the game.

Quest Dialogue Spirit's Starter

Doesn't the mountain look nice from up here? Oh yes, this is the best spot to watch from. Watch all you beekeepers and your bees. So so busy! Not like me! I'm retired. I take it easy! Hmm... oh you - you're not who I thought. Have we met, honey bun? Oh, what's it matter. I'm Spirit Bear, and you're another beekeeper. It's happened before, and it's happening again. You need my guidance to reach the next level of beekeeping. I've got some time to give it to you! Since you've got that many bees you must know the drill. Hmm... ...Did you know? I planted the sunflowers in the Sunflower Field, you see. Well, my sister, she was the one who wanted sunflowers. For the bees, and also for the seeds, she loved to snack on the seeds. I used to like them too, hmm, but over time I grew sick of them. Quite a nasty habit - the shells get everywhere. (Cough) I planted the sunflowers, many more than you see today. The dandelion field [sic] used to be covered in them as well. I did most of the work, my sister, she wasn't much of a gardener. Hmm... Oh, yes. What is it you needed? That's right! That's right, alright. A quest. As if you weren't busy enough! Well, I've got plenty. And plenty other things store [sic] for you once you've finished. Things they don't make anymore, mind you. Quite special things, magical things. You believe in magic, don't you? Heheh! What's it matter, now. My sister, she wasn't as spiritual as I am. She didn't believe in magic, not in the same way as I do. Well, I used to tell her, that's why her plants would shrivel up. She wasn't in tune with the magic of nature, thus she never knew what they needed. Not quite like me. I can feel it, hear it - what the plants need. Even before they need it! Oh yes, I'm quite special in that way. Years ago, so many years ago, there was a terrible drought. I was the only one who felt it coming! I planned ahead, stockpiled. I became quite wealthy that year, for a while, anyhow. Hmm... oh right. Quests can seem so tedious, so meaningless, don't you agree? Why? why why why? Why in this field, why that color of flower? What's it all for? Well, child, if I told you now, you wouldn't be satisfied. I wasn't satisfied! As a cub I hated nothing more than questing. But the quests work on you as you work on the quests. They're more than a means of making honey. Do you believe what I'm saying? Hehe! What's it matter. Quests will come to you and you'll take them how you will. ...Whats [sic] that? Oh, my quest? You want a quest from me? Hmm, give me a second dear. ... There you go, right in there. Right in your Quest Menu. Go on now, go on. Spirit Bear need a little quiet time... ...(She appears to have fallen asleep)...

-During-

(Somehow she's standing in her sleep) ...sticky ...stubborn... (Why not let her rest while you complete her quest?)

-Completion-

(Yawn) Not in the honey pot! Take it outside! Oh! There you are, dear. ...Oh yes, your quest. It's complete - give me just a second. ... ...(Her eyes close, she begins to smile)... ... ...(She may have fallen asleep)... OK! Ok, ok. (Yawn) Oh, it's so hard to stay awake on sunny days like today. Yes... the sun, in my old age I've begun to appreciate it more. Warms you up down to your bones! But it's not good for your skin, no no no. You: stay out of the sun when you can. Protect yourself from wrinkles. Too late for me! Hah... What's that? Oh, you're too kind. Now, for your reward: Do you know about [Glitter]? You ought to know about it by now. In any case, it's exceedingly rare. Very important for a beekeeper. [Glitter] boosts pollen in a field you're standing in by 100%! Maybe, more importantly, it can be used to extend Field Boosts, Like those you get from [Field Dice]. Well, as I'm sure you've noticed, it's rather hard to come by. But those who know, they know... I know! Heh hee. Yes I know. [Glitter] to me is like Honey to you! I'd say I'm a [Glitter] Grandmaster. Glit-ah glit-ah! Falls down to us from the moon! Or rises up from the depths below! Too heavy or too light, to stick around for long. Unless... They used to sell this stuff for 5m Honey a pouch. That was a lot back then, I'll have you know. Not for me, of course. For others, yes. ... You look so familiar... Your bees.. no, no they don't look that familiar. Anyways, here you are. Let's keep busy, hmm. If you complete just 9 more quests, I'll give you a [Spirit Petal]. You've heard of them, surely. You've got 35 bees. Don't you read the wiki? Well you'll need these [Spirit Petals] to craft the items I'm wearing: The [Petal Wand] and the [Petal Belt]! The magic of nature itself can be channeled through them... To fire Petal Shurikens all around you! Like some sort of gardening ninja! When those fly through your bees, the bees instantly convert some pollen to honey. Exceedingly useful. Practically a necessity, even. I am the only one with [Spirit Petals] as far as I know. I've got plenty. Inherited them years ago. I take good care of them. It's my duty to preserve them and distribute them to beekeepers like you. LIKE you. Not you. Not yet, dear. 9 more quests for the 1st one.

The First Offering

The Wind Shrine: a beautiful - mystical - icon of the mountain. Older than most things here - older than me! Can you believe it? Not as old as some things. But older than most things. And through it, we maintain a living bond with a certain past. All of us - the bears, the bees, the Robloxians or whatever you are... Blow through time like petals in an evening's breeze. The Shrine stands sturdily, solemnly... As a constant reminder of that fleeting dance. It also acts as a convenient time gate, and item sink, for the sake of this game. Donate something to the Wind Shrine, and many things could happen. Usually it will stir up the winds spawning Clouds and providing perks to certain fields. But it also acts as the means of obtaining a [Windy Bee Egg]. Windy Bee - oh, you could say it's a favorite of mine. An unpredictable creature difficult to grasp. So delicate yet so powerful! And certainly the most beautiful, yes yes. Are you listening to us now, Windy Bee? ... Don't be coy! Not with me! ...(She tosses a handful of dried petals into the air)... ...(She watches them intently as they swirl and fall)... ... Heheheh! Alright then. Swirl away like the rest of them! ...(The petals blow away into the fields)... Look, one's stuck to Black Bear's head. Don't tell him! Right - why don't you give the Wind Shrine a try? Test your luck with a [Cloud Vial]. Maybe Windy won't be so coy with you. But that's not all, of course. Oh no no... The Pumpkin Patch... The Clover Field... The Blueberries... They're ready for you now!

-During-

(Somehow she's standing in her sleep) ...too...loud... ...people...staring... (Why not let her rest while you complete her quest?)

-Completion-

(Yawn) Shush up Stick Bug! Shush!! Oh, it's you dear. The Wind Shrine... Ah, you offered it a Cloud Vial... Windy Bee didn't respond - of course not. You haven't offered a [Spirit Petal]. You'll need to do that before Windy Bee will even think about calling back to you. Still, your favor with Windy Bee has gone up. In time, it'll come. My apologies, dear. I'm so forgetful. Anyways, well done! Yes yes. Easy stuff for you! Easy stuff for many. Still easy for you! That's right - don't worry about the others. The Leaderboards - pretend they don't exist. Your first [Spirit Petal] will arrive after you complete 8 more quests.

Rules Of The Road

I'm not blind! I'll say it - Honey rules the world! The rules of all roads are written in honey, roads paved in honey. This mountain is nothing but a hulking honeymaking [sic] highway to nowhere! Honey for this, honey for that. Why? We can't eat all this honey. You bees, yes you. Buzzing arounds [sic] like you don't understand me. You did this! This is your fault! They are YOUR rules. ...(She closes here [sic] eyes, smiles)... Oh, but they are sweet. Yes, yes very sweet. Honey is very sweet. [Strawberries] and [Pineapple], they're sweet, not as sweet. Us bears, we just can't get enough honey. Isn't that right, Honey Bear? Not you dear. The Honey Bear. He can eat all this honey! He did eat all this honey and he'll do it again! Bees, who am I talking about? Your partner in crime in this great honeymaking conspiracy! Who is your TRUE KEEPER? (Her eyes dart towards the eyes of each of your bees) Nothing to say? Heheheh. (She tosses petals into the air) Wee, there are other worlds with other rules! ... Oh, what am I on about? Keep me straight, dear. We've got questing to do, you know that.

-During-

(Somehow she's standing in her sleep) ...not...quite... ...red...blue... (Why not let her rest while you complete her quest?)

-Completion-

(Yawn) That's not even a real color! Oh! There you are, dear. You startled me. All done, good good. Complete 7 more quests, and I'll give you your first [Spirit Petal]. ... Do you read what I say? You know, at your age, I wouldn't have. Oh no. No no no. I sped through it all. My sister - she was even worse than me. Worse in both ways, she didn't read and she talked for miles! We'd both somehow talk and talk, and nothing would be said. We take after our mother. Now she was a true rambler! But everything she said, it had a purpose. I thought so. I couldn't tell you what it was, though.

QR Quest

... ...(She's sleeping)... ... ...(You try to wake her, but she doesn't react)... ...(You notice a note rolled loosely in her hand)... (It reads:) No soliciting. Do not wake. If you are a beekeeper looking for a quest [sic] Please scan this code with your Quest Menu [sic] (You scan the code with your Quest Menu) (It brings you to Spirit Bear's website) (It appears incredibly old) (Top and center, there's a highly compressed image of young Spirit Bear) (Below that, a crude animated gif of Windy Bee flying across the screen) (Below that, a list of the quest tasks loads very slowly) (You write them all down) (Toward the bottom of the website there's an icon says [sic] "Sign My Guestbook") (You click on it, but it fails to load) (Below that, a page visit counter that reads 23488) (You reload the page, but the counter doesn't go up)

-During-

(Somehow she's standing in her sleep) ...daily...specials... (Why not let her rest while you complete her quest?)

-Completion-

(Yawn) You call yourself a "Gifted" Bee and you can't even read? Oh! There you are, dear. Sorry, just catching up on sleep. Let me tell you, I just had the strangest dream. Stick Bug and I were having a picnic in the Bamboo Field, as we do. Well, we used to, it's been ages, anyhow: I opened our picnic basket, and out flew a Frosty Bee. I figured Stick Bug put it there to keep our food cool. But when I reached inside, there was no food! I said, "Stick Bug, didn't you pack something for us to eat?" He said to me "Panda Bear is bringing the food." I thought, well OK, but then why did we bring this basket? Before long, Panda Bear arrived. But it was strange. He brought us menus and asked to take our order. The Frosty Bee buzzed into my ear: "Can you tell me if they've got [Blueberries]?" And I woke up! Hmm... when I say it out loud, it doesn't sound so strange. Anyhow dear, let me give you your rewards. ... Let me just look up again what they are. Give me a moment. (She loads her website on her Quest Menu) You know, this website, it wasn't my idea - I didn't set it up. I still hardly understand it, it works though... ... Let me just sign in now. I have to sign in to see the quest rewards. What was my password... give me a second, dear. I always forget... I don't - wait. I think I have it written down. I know it has to do with "bees". It is something like, "BeesBuzz123". ... Yes, yes that's it. Here we are, take these. Complete 6 more quests and I'll give you the first [Spirit Petal]!

Pleasant Pastimes

... This beautiful world of ours... Is it our only world? Maybe... Maybe not... How could we know? We can't know, can we? Hehe. What's it matter, hmm. We know and don't know what we can. Probably? Certainly? Oooh, isn't it all the same? Would it be any different if this were only a game? I wouldn't change my ways, oh no. I do what I like! ...(She dozes off for a minute)... As long as I'm able, there's things that I'll do. You know, ever since I was young, you know one thing... One thing I've always loved. Two things actually. Two things I've done since I was just a cub. Well, theres [sic] a few other things, but these two things... Oh, I hope they never go away. They shouldn't. That's playing the Memory Match, and tossing [Jelly Beans]. Yes, yes. Even back then, they had Memory Match. Pay a bit of honey and test your memory (and your luck)! Helps keep you sharp, and fills your inventory with rare goodies. Like [Jelly Beans] - Toss them around, share them with friends. Generosity - feels good and makes you quite popular! As a cub, I didn't have many friends. Isn't that sad? Hah. My sister, yes, she was my friend. But she had to be! I didn't have many friends, until [Jelly Beans] came along. That's right - winning [Jelly Beans] in Memory Match is how you earn friends. ... Everything changes, over time. So it seems. But now Memory Match. Oh no, that's a constant. Who could resist? As I've gotten older. I'd say I've only grown to love it more. Although I'm not quite as good as I used to be... heh. ... Is there something you need? Oh! Oh, right. Yes. Your next quest. Your 5th quest! A milestone. A real milestone. You'll need to be prepared to go any further. Are you keeping up with your badges? You should, really. To be sure, I won't let you move beyond this quest until you've collected 15 Ace Badges. Ace is the 3rd rank in each set of badges. Keep up! Complete this one, and I've got a special [Star Jelly] for you... Go out and partake in pasttimes [sic]! Let's make them traditions. You'll need more than a few of these. If you need even more [Jelly Beans], you'll have to take them back from the ants. In the Ant Challenge. That's probably the fastest way to get them, [Jelly Beans].

-During-

(Somehow she's standing in her sleep) ...new...mask... (Why not let her rest while you complete her quest?)

-Completion-

(Yawn) 100 [Glitters], are you out of your mind? Oh! There you are, dear. Tell me, did you make any friends out there? Hehe, what's it matter. Who needs friends when you've got bees. Hmm, moving along rather swiftly. Yes... but don't get ahead of yourself. Don't you know how these work by now? They start easy and ramp up. That's right - like many things in life, they just get more and more difficult! But you get stronger and stronger as well, don't you? Your bees, they get stronger. Look at them. (She smiles at you bees) Yes, you. Precious. You all grow stronger together with every quest. Every day, stronger and more determined! But you can only go so far on strength and determination alone. You'll need your wits, maybe a little divine intervention... If you want to go all the way. A gift to set you apart. Gifted Bees to set you apart. A gift from me - a [Star Jelly] from me, dear. Complete 5 more quests and I'll give you the first [Spirit Petal]. But first, give Spirit Bear some alone time. She's off to the Memory Match.

Nature's Lessons

The majesty of nature exceeds anything we could ever create ourselves. Profoundly clever - the things nature can do. Yes, my entire life, I've spent it in awe of nature. I've tried to understand it, truly understand it. I've had to listen to it, really listen. Yes, it's so easy for us to speak over nature... To see in it what we've already seen. What we want to see. Opening your eyes is not enough, not to truly see. ...(She closes her eyes)... Hmm. Feel that gentle breeze. It wants to tell you something... Smell the rich aroma of the flowers, and of the earth. It wants to show you something... In so many ways, nature wants to inform us. But unfortunately for us, it's ways are not always our own! ... This is practical stuff, dear. Pay attention now. "Crazy old Spirit Bear rambles on for hours about listening to trees" Yes I know what it sounds like! I know! But look at what I'm holding, hmm. See any other bears with one of these? No you don't. That's because they don't know how to make them. Even if they did, they wouldn't know how to use them. You could read a thousand books of collector mechanics... And learn less than you would in a single day of gardening. Not usually, no. This doesn't work for everybody. But those who know, know... I know... heheh... Nature... ... ...5 more quests... ... [Spirit Petal]... ...(She's fallen asleep)...

-During-

(Somehow she's standing in her sleep) ...honey...stuck... ...bear... (Why not let her rest while you complete her quest?)

-Completion-

(Yawn) You're turning it the wrong way, you red-headed half wit! Oh! There you are, dear. Let me, let me tell you a few things about plants. Sprouts specifically. Different fields yeild [sic] different rewards through Sprouts. The fields up here, up in the 35 bee zone... Offer more treats in general. If you are looking to pad your pockets with a variety of treats. I suggest planting [Magic Beans] in the Pepper Patch. Now - if you're looking for a specific treats [sic], you have options. Sprout in the Sunflower Field yield 7 times more [Sunflower Seeds] than in typical fields. Similarly, the Pineapple Patch yields 7 times more [Pineapples]. Fields with mostly red flowers yield 4 times more [Strawberries] While primarily blue fields yield 6 times more [Blueberry]. The Strawberry Field yeilds [sic] twice as many [Strawberries] as other red fields. And Coconut Field is the only field in which Sprout grants [Coconuts] and [Tropical Drinks]. The Coconut Field also grants about twice as many of each treat. It's good overall. Each of the fields is a little different, you see. And these numbers - well, they're subject to change, and aren't necessarily 100% accurate.. [sic] Try planting more sprouts to figure out more. It's important to harvest Sprouts in the correct fields to obtain the ingredients you need. Hmm... What other things, about Sprouts... Give me a second, dear. ...(She takes out a book from her [Petal Belt])... Hmm... ...(She takes out her reading glasses from her [Petal Belt] and puts them on)... Sprouts. Sprouty sprouty sprouts... Mmmhmmm... Oh yes! Yes. Sprouts planted at night have an over 65% chance of becoming Moon Sprouts. Moon Sprouts always grant Moon Charms, that's right. And Moon Sprouts in the 35 Zone yield on average about 20% more Moon Charms. Interesting stuff, isn't it? The variety of nature is endlessly facinating [sic]. I could go on for hours about it - and I do, regularly. Science Bear and I have had countless discussions on the subject. Such an intelligent bear, with a true thirst for knowledge! His means of acquiring it, perhaps not as effective as he thinks. But it's reassuring to see the younger generation have a true interest in nature! Mmhmm... Alright then. Complete 4 more quests and I'll give you the first [Spirit Petal].

The Gifts Of Life

What does it mean to be "gifted, hmm? Are some bees just better than the others? A silly phrase! Just silly. We're all gifted - sounds sappy but it's true! Perspective is everything. If theres [sic] anything I know, it's that. What would life be without the challenges each one of us faces in our own way? Now - I'm not saying all challenges are good... But I'm also not saying that all challenges are bad. No no. These are the only gifts I care about: The gift of life! The gift of nature. The marvelous things we experience through those gifts alone, Are [sic] enough to validate us all! Even the most Basic of Basic Bees. Now, with that said... You're in the honeymaking [sic] business. Making ever more honey is your challenge [sic entire sentence]. For now, at least. And for this practical purpose, "Gifted" Bees truly are a gift. They collect 50% more pollen, convert 50% more pollen to honey at a time... Deal 50% more damage when defending you from enemies... Offer stat bonuses to your entire hive! And even spawn "Inspire" tokens which dramatically boost your pollen for 5 seconds. We appreciate all bees - their variety of traits, talents and hinderences... [sic] Reveal to us the benefits and strengths of all others. Each one shines a singular light, and together, they reveal the full picture. Your humble beginnings provide the context in which your accomplishments have meaning at all. Do you get what I'm trying to say, dear? Yes?... Well, don't dwell on it. Just know that a gift's not a gift alone... A gift giver can't give gifts to someone who doesn't appreciate it!

-During-

(Somehow she's standing in her sleep) ...too...rare... ...too...be... (Why not let her rest while you complete her quest?)

-Completion-

(Yawn) Mythical shmithical! These aren't for you! Oh! There you are, dear. Hmm... Have I told you about my years living over seas? And more! Far far away, in distant lands all over... As a young bear I was quite adventureous [sic]. Almost too adventurous! Not everywhere is as relaxing and safe as where we are now. I was never a trouble maker, no no... Never got into anything I shouldn't have, I wouldn't say. But like most bears, I had a wild side. Have a wild side! Heheh. No no... Wild is too much work. I take it easy now. (Cough) All around. Forest, mountains, seasides... [sic] Not deserts, no. Far too hot - no flowers or plants. But all over, wherever there was adventure, I went. my sister, she was the opposite. She was adventurous, but not in the same way. Not as brave. Bless her heart. She'd never step foot on a boat. I've been on boats, and in planes. And I've been to places you can't reach in either of those! Would you believe me if I said I've been to space? How about the clouds? Me, a bear attuned to the winds and weather. Not so unbelievable, is it? Yes, living up in the sky, watching the world below. That's where I met Windy Bee! ... Listen to me! I must sound ridiculous. You've got to understand something about me, dear: If you're hoping for a purpose to my rambling, you're hopeless! Oh, what's it matter. Just 3 more quests and I'll give you the first [Spirit Petal].

Out-Questing Question

Who are we? You and I, and the bears of the mountain. Oooh, a frightening question, when you really get to thinking about it. Frightening? Yes... There's nothing to fear but fear itself. Itself - is that us? Heh. No, but really... Who are you? Are you what you do? Is what you do it is because you do it? Those two together - That wouldn't make any sense, now would it? Why do I give quests to beekeepers like you? Why do you talk to bears like me? AH! There's no end to the questions - just a bottomless pit of answer. Don't look down, you could get dizzy! ... Who am I? I'm Spirit Bear! I could be many bears, I probably am. I could be Onett (whose typing right now), but mainly I'm Spirit Bear. You're a beekeeper completing quests to earn my Spirit Petals. That's not all you are, but you're mainly that, at least to me. Can't we leave it at that! ...(She smiles at your bees)... They know who they are. They know. ... Hmm... You're very close to that [Spirit Petal] now! Let me give you some information about it so you have time to make a decision. With the [Spirit Petal], you can craft either of the Petal items I'm wearing... But you can also use it to activate a chance to obtain Windy Bee. Donate it to the Wind Shrine, and from that point on... Any [Cloud Vial] you donate to the Wind Shrine will have a chance of giving: A [Windy Bee Egg]! Now, this is not a guaranteed thing. Oh no. Far from it. Windy can be an unreliable - downright fickle bee. That's right, do you hear me Windy? ... (She throws some petals into the air) FICKLE bee! Do you hear me now? (Cough) Every donation you make to the Wind Shrine impresses Windy Bee more. Rare items are preferred, but every offering is appreciated. Increases your favor with Windy, and thus increases your odds of obtaining the egg. In addition, increased favor results in greater rewards from the Shrine in general. Listen to the Wind Shrine's responses - they give you insight into where your favor stands. Over time, slowly but surely, you'll win the bee over. It took me ages! Ages, yes. Windy Bee wasn't always as sociable as it is now, you can thank me for that. ... Who am I... hah... I'm the bear who planted half the plants you see on this mountain! Like you don't know who I am, pfft. Well, not half. Not quite that quite that many, but still. ...(She opens her quest menu)... Give me a second, dear. ...(She's loading up some quest information)... Pineapples, sparkles... Aren't those a bit weird. Gross. Sparkles... The plants spit out bubbles and you collect it. Quite nasty when you think about it. What have we learned today: don't think too much about anything! Hmm... Alright. There we are. They're ramping up now! Get ready! But first, how about some Memory Match? I've got it on my Quest Menu computer thing. You play with that while I take a little nap...

-During-

(Somehow she's standing in her sleep) ...blue... ...berries... (Why not let her rest while you complete her quest?)

-Completion-

(Yawn) You're coo-coo! Coo-coo for [Coconuts]! Oh! There you are dear. You know, that Blue Flower Field? Well, it used to be a [Blueberry] Field. There are still some [Blueberries] growing in it, yes. ...Hmm Those [Blueberries] are lurking around in many of the fields now, actually. Still, they're not as common as they used to be. What happened to them? Good question, dear. I don't know what happened to them. ...(She stares into the distance)... Mmm... [Blueberries] are healthy for you, though. I ate a lot of them as a cub. And I'm still healthy! My age - now that's a real testament to their health benefits. Oh, and let me just say, that bowl of [Blueberries] drizzled in honey... Now that's a treat that's hard to beat. Heheh. ... Are you - are you here for some [Blueberries]? Oh! Oh your quest. Ok, well I can help with that. But you should take at least one of these [Blueberries], really. Please dear I have too many of them, do take one.

Forcefully Friendly

What do you think of us bears? You can be honest with me, dear. I won't tell the others what you say. You know, some people, they say we're a bit simple around here. That we don't - don't get out much. They're not wrong. Well, about me, yes they're wrong. But most bears on this mountain... Oh, they don't know much about the world outside it. Well, I really shouldn't generalize like that, no no. Polar Bear isn't even from this mountain. But still... he hasn't been around. Science Bear, he knows about the world from books. But has he left? I don't recall. The younger bears, they really ought to get out there... while they're young. It's important to see the world - to put everything into perspective. Put it in perspective while your mind is still forming. There's more to life than collecting pollen and making honey. You wouldn't believe that if you spent every day here! Hmm... Many of the fruits here, well, they're a result of my traveling. The [Strawberries]? I bought them here myself, picked them wild from Sweden. The Pineapple Patch, well, I didn't bring those, but they're foreign nonetheless. Can you imagine? A Re://:Swarm without [Pineapples]? Without [Enzymes]? I can. It wasn't very different, honestly. But many of the bees do truly love those [Pineapples]. ...(Yawn)... Oooh, that's one thing I hope you beekeepers take away from these quests. No - not the [Pineapples], dear. I hope you take away a fond impression of us bears. That we leave a little mark on you - that you let us do so! Even if we are a bit simple around here. Every seemingly simple person, well they're still worth understanding. Yes... we're all simple in our own ways, aren't we? Hmmm, why am I on about this? Oh yes! The reason I was asking. You see, I've been told - I won't say by who. But by some. I've been told us bears on this mountain come off as TOO friendly. Yes, yes. Too friendly. Can you believe it? So friendly - almost artificially friendly. Like we want something! You know, after some of the places I've been, and things I've seen. I say what's the harm in that? In being as friendly as possible? Is it always genuine? What's it matter? ...(She smiles at your bees)... Bees, always selfless, and always friendly. Or so it seems... Thank you, dear, thank you! This is going on the top of my tree next year, the very top is where little [alien wizard] belongs. ... ...(she's staring off into the distance)... Mmhmm, the very top. ... OK, goodbye now. ... Oh! YOUR gift! Yes yes I have one for you! A few things, actually. Including my [Memory Match Ornament]! With that on the tree, well, I don't quite recall what it does. You can check the tree yourself. (Yawn) First, why not go check out that strange [Snowflake] in the Dandelion Field. Merry Beesmas, dear! Exclusive Beesmas 2024 Dialogue Mmmm...mhmm...(she's murmuring to herself with her eyes close [sic])... You are given a choice to give a present to Spirit Bear or continue talking like normal. You choose to give her a present. ... Huh? I'm up, I'm up. Hello. Good to you see you. [sic] Hmm... what? Wait. What's in your hands? Oh! What? Wait a second... (She looks around) Why have you got that? Why does everything look like this? What's going on? What day IS it, dear??? ... That doesn't add up. But I've honestly no sense of time any more. [sic] You could tell me it was October and I'd believe you. Although, I had a suspicion I had forgotten something this year... Hmm. Oh! Wait. (She reaches into her [Petal Bag]) Heheh, I hadn't forgotten at all! I've had a [Present] waiting for you in all along... How long has it been in there? So long I don't even remember what it is! But it has your name on it, so surely it's meant for you. The one you brought me looks nicer, though. So I suppose I should go ahead and open it. Unless... ... Would it not be wrong? To open this now... willy nilly... whenever... I thought the point of Beesmas gifts was that they were an annual tradition? The rhythms of the seasons, accentuated by the Honeydays, or other customs... Produces a familiar sway that acts as a point of reference, no? For our progress... For our growth... Mmmh. They give the structure to our lives upon which change can grow! Our daily, our monthly, our yearly routines establish themselves like vines on that lattice. So would we dare shake it up!? (Cough) Dare to exchange these NOW? And risk losing that rhythm? Might knock our petals off! Before you know it, you'll be just like me. Lost in a timeless, sleepy fog. No clue what month it is. ... Hmm, but you do have a point, dear. The rhythm's already lost! Perhaps we've already moved on to this, mmm, post-annular era. Perhaps the years themselves are getting longer... Or maybe tradition was alawys a silly concept. A cage more than a stage. I mean, I've always been an innovator. A trailblaizer. [sic] Always tried to switch things up - to never settle into a groove. So why shouldn't Beesmas be now? We could open these [Presents] up, and begin to make it so. So. Let's see what you brought Spirit Bear! ...(krumple krumple)... Oh! A Flying Windy Bee Sticker! I don't remember seeing this sticker in the, what do you call it That menu that lists all the Stickers, you know, dear. The compendium? No. That's not right. ... The Index! Yes, of course. The Sticker Index. Well, last I checked this Sticker wasn't in it. That makes it extra special! Thank you so much, dear! I'll stick this somewhere nice. (She sticks it on her [Petal Wand]) Ok. Now, you open yours! Go on! ...(krumple krumple)... That's the [Memory Match Ornament]! My Memory Match Ornament. The one I won myself way back in... well, it was a long time ago. Oh, it says right there: way back in 1983! Probably before you were born, you do look so young. With that on the tree, you'll receive these boosts: +25% Convert Rate +25% Capacity in the Stump Field And +5% from Bee Abilities! Don't think they give these out anymore. The Memory Match Committee isn't what it used to be. People don't need to practice to keep their memory sharp when they've got smartphones. Every answer in their [sic] As if Memory Match actually helps with memory at all. I mean, look at me. Memory Match Champ and I can't even keep track of the month. But you enjoy that, it'll look nice on the tree! Happy Honeydays, I suppose! Conclusion (Yawn) Oh! Hello dear. Did you - did you need something? That's it for now. All I've got for you... Why not... maybe check with me later... Mmhmm... much, much later... ...(She falls back asleep)...

This was removed from the game.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• She is one of the two female bears in the game, the other being Mother Bear.
  • You can get to her without 35 bees by using the Red Cannon, then using the Parachute or Glider to glide over, then make sure you have high ping so you are able to talk to her before you get kicked out of the 35 bee zone/disconnected.
  • Her idle animation comes from the Elder Animation Package.
  • She quite often refers to her sister, another bear who was very close to her.
  • She, Stick Bug, the Cub Buddies, Bee Bear and Shadow Bear are the only NPCs that dance.
  • She is the second NPC to hold a tool, the first being Onett, which makes her the only bear holding a tool.
  • She is the third NPC to wear a belt, the other two being Sun Bear and Onett.
  • Spirit Bear, Sun Bear, and Dapper Bear are the only Bears to wear accessories, Spirit Bear and Sun Bear being the only bears to wear in-game accessories.
  • Spirit Bear is based off of Kermode Bears, which are sometimes referred to as spirit bears.
  • Kermode bears are a rare subspecies of the black bear.
  • She mentions the Re://:Swarm Wiki in the quest "Spirit's Starter".
  • Both she and Science Bear have items that are only obtainable from their quests, which are Spirit Petals and Translators respectively.
  • The Code "BeesBuzz123" is her account's password on her own website, proven from her dialogue in "QR Quest".
  • She, Panda Bear, Black Bear, Gummy Bear and Science Bear are the only bears that mention/have a code.
  • It is possible to glitch into Spirit Bear and get a quest from her. The player has to jump on the Windy Bee statue on top of the 35 Bee Gate and glide or jump to her, or, if the player has enough ping, climb up the big rock left of the gate and nearest to the Coconut Field and talk to her.
  • She has the most words per quest in her dialogue, at around 2,000 per quest, even surpassing Science Bear with the most words per quest dialogue.
  • She has around 21 thousand words in her whole dialogue.
  • Spirit Bear, Robo Bear, and Dapper Bear are the only permanent quest bears to not have a Bear Morph.
  • All of Spirit Bear's quests require collecting an increasing amount of white pollen. (With the exception of her Beesmas quests.)
  • Spirit Bear is the second bear to require the completion of another bear's quest, the first being Bee Bear and Sun Bear being third.
  • Spirit Bear can summon a multitude of server-wide events.
  • She is the only quest giver that can summon a Wild Windy Bee, and a Snowstorm.
  • She, along with Honey Bee, are the only quest givers that can summon a Honeystorm.
  • She, along with Bee Bear, are the only quest givers that can summon Nighttime alongside .
  • According to Bee Bear, Bubble Bee Man can also summon honeystorms.
  • She is self-aware that she is in a game, as she mentions "game balance'' in ''Sway Away."
  • This could be because of multiple reasons, such as her saying "Ol' Stumpy", her mentioning the wiki you are viewing this on, or her age.
  • She is the only permanent quest giver that requires the player to play Memory Matches.
  • She is the only permanent quest giver that requires the player to use the Wealth Clock for her quests.
  • Spirit Bear refers to the Stump Snail as ''Ol' Stumpy''. This may be a reference to the youtuber ThnxCya as he references it as ''Ol' Stumpy'' too.
  • Sources confirm that she's a 1983's Memory Match tournament champion, and that explains why she gives quests that require players to play Memory Match.
  • Some of her quests give items upon receiving the quest. These items include: Jelly Beans, Star Jelly, Glitter, Magic Beans, Coconuts, Pineapples, Sunflower Seeds and Gumdrops.
  • Her favorite holiday is Galentine's Day.
  • Her sleep talking during the quest "Do You Bee-lieve In Magic?" is probably a reference to the image of Basic Bee winking that can be found at the end of the White Tunnel, hinting to the code "Wink".
  • In the 2021 Beesmas Quest, when she tells the player where to get Satisfying Nectar, she mentions the wrong fields; The Dandelion Field, the Bamboo Field, and the Pine Tree Forest is where the player can get Comforting Nectar, not Satisfying Nectar.
  • In her first quest, Spirit Bear reveals that she planted the Sunflowers in the Sunflower Field.
  • The Sunflowers were requested by her sister, who loves to snack on Sunflower Seeds.
  • The dialogue of her quest "Witness Grandeur" reveals she has known Brown Bear since he was a cub.
  • In the quest “Beauty Duty“, she mentions that her fur was originally a shade of white, specifically one close to a cream color.
  • Spirit Bear mentions in her quest “The Ways Of The Winds / The Wind And Its Ways” that her mother was always in a state of stress, and that she would pull on her fur as a nervous tick.
  • Spirit Bear mentions in her quest “Rhubarb That Could Have Been” that she initially wanted to plant Rhubarb to bake pies. She let Stick Bug decide and the rhubarb field was replaced by the Pineapple Patch.
  • Through the donation quests in her storyline, your favor in the Wind Shrine will increase by 486,753 (might need a recalculation).

Spirit Petal

"A delicate flower petal used in rituals."

COOLDOWN

N/A

Not to be confused with petals, spawned by blooms.

The Spirit Petal is a special crafting material that can be used as one of the ingredients to craft the Petal Wand and the Petal Belt. It can also be donated to the Wind Shrine to allow the player a chance of obtaining a Windy Bee (or a Star Treat, if player already had Windy Bee) when donating Cloud Vials. Note that players are only able to donate one Spirit Petal with Cloud Vials to the Wind Shrine to get a chance to obtain a Windy Bee, as the other two are strictly to be used for crafting the Petal Belt and Petal Wand.

There are 3 Spirit Petals that are given every 10th Spirit Bear quest, first one being Sway Away, second being Tickle The Wind, and third being Spring Out Of The Mountain.

docs.title: Sprinklers
docs.text:
Sprinklers

"Use while standing in flowers to place a Sprinkler."

COOLDOWN

1 second

Sprinklers are items that can be placed in fields by players to help with flower regeneration. They can be bought in the Badge Bearer's Guild, accessible by obtaining 15 badges of any kind. There are five sprinklers in the game: the Basic Sprinkler, the Silver Soakers, the Golden Gushers, the Diamond Drenchers and The Supreme Saturator. They all look similar; a simple sprinkler that stands up from the ground beneath the flower the player is standing on. The material the sprinkler is made of is based on the tier color. (The only exception to this is The Supreme Saturator, which has a giant golden sprinkler sticking through a neon blue bear head.) The higher level the sprinkler is, the more players can place (with the exception of The Supreme Saturator) and the more effective it can be. Sprinklers can't be placed in the Hub Field.

The Basic Sprinkler is unlocked as soon as a player is able to enter the Badge Bearer's Guild. However, the Silver Soakers require 10 Hotshot badges, the Golden Gushers require 10 Ace badges, the Diamond Drenchers require 10 Master badges and The Supreme Saturator requires 10 Grandmaster badges.

Players cannot place their own sprinklers within 8 flowers of each other. However, they can place their sprinklers right next to a different player's sprinkler. When they place their sprinkler too close to another one of theirs, the player gets a message that says: Cannot place sprinklers this close to eachother [sic]

However, the the Sprinkler Glitch can occur if the player places a sprinkler mid-air, overriding the restriction and planting sprinklers closer than normal.

Note that what players are able to buy is actually a sprinkler builder, which is a permanent tool that players can access via the eggs/items tab whenever they like. Players can activate it by placing the item on the bottom middle of their screen and clicking it (or their corresponding hotkeys, if the player is on a PC). If a player places more sprinklers than they can place, the oldest one will be removed. A sprinkler that is placed in a field will stay there until the player who placed it removes it by placing it elsewhere, or until the player dies or leaves the game.

docs.title: Sprout
docs.text:
Were you looking for Magic Bean?

A sprout is a plant that spawns in the center of a field. Sprouts emit a bright yellow beacon that reaches the sky, and have a counter at the base of it representing a pollen amount. When players collect pollen, or when a cloud is on the field (requires at least one player being in the field for the cloud give growth), the number counts down and it gradually grows taller. Once the pollen counter reaches 0, it sends out shockwave and scatters various tokens throughout the field. If no interaction with a sprout happens for more than 5 minutes, it will despawn.

docs.title: Spawning
docs.text:
Sprouts can spawn randomly around the map and can also be planted using Magic Beans. They can also be summoned by using the Special Sprout Summoner near the Red HQ, by anyone who has discovered all eight Legendary Bee types, once every sixteen hours.

When a sprout spawns, it will broadcast a server-wide message: 🌱A (Rarity) Sprout has appeared...🌱

If a player has planted a sprout, the message would read:

🌱 {Username} has planted a (Rarity) Sprout...🌱

If Sticker Sprouts are about to spawn in the Hive Hub, the message will read:

🌱Sticker Sprouts are about to spawn in the Hive Hub...🌱

  • If the player were to be in a Private Server, the message will instead read:

🌱A Sticker Sprout is about to spawn in Public Server Hive Hubs...🌱

When the Sticker Sprout has spawned in the Hive Hub, the message will read:

🌱 A Sticker Sprout has spawned in the Hive Hub...🌱

Sprouts cannot spawn or be planted in the Ant Field.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
There are ten different variants of sprouts:

  • Sprout (Green) (Common)
  • Rare Sprout (Silver) (Rare)
  • Epic Sprout (Gold) (Very Rare)
  • Legendary Sprout (Teal) (Extremely Rare)
  • Supreme Sprout (Luminescent green) (Unfathomably Rare)
  • Moon Sprout (Luminescent blue during both night and day, only available during nighttime (common))
  • Gummy Sprout (Translucent pink) (Very Rare)
  • Sticker Sprout (Rainbow, colors shifting) (Spawns only every 3 hours in the Hub Field, or an extremely rare chance when planting a magic bean in the Hub Field)
  • Festive Sprout (White and Red stripes) (Planted by Festive Beans or Onett)
  • Debug Sprout (Black) (Can only be planted by Onett)

The amount of pollen needed for the sprout for it to be harvested depends on the rarity of the sprout and the field it's in.

docs.title: Location Specific Drops
docs.text:
Depending on where the sprout is planted, the drops spawned can vary in amounts or may drop certain items.

  • A sprout in a red field yields 4 times more Strawberries than in any other field. No Blueberries will spawn.
  • A sprout in the Strawberry Field will yield twice as many Strawberries than sprouts in other red fields.
  • A sprout in a Blue field yields 6 times more Blueberries than in any other field. No Strawberries will spawn.
  • A sprout in the Sunflower Field yields 7 times more Sunflower Seeds than in any other field.
  • A sprout in the Pineapple Patch yields 7 times more Pineapples than in any other field.
  • A sprout in the 35 Bee Zone yields 20% more rewards than sprouts in other areas. It also requires significantly more pollen to pop.
  • A sprout in the Coconut Field yields Coconuts and Tropical Drinks in addition to other treats.
  • Other fields may produce more regular Treats than any other treats depending on the field.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Various items, abilities, and equipment can boost player movespeed, helping to collect tokens more efficiently before they despawn.
  • Using Oils grants 1.2x player movespeed.
  • Equipping the Hasty Guard grants 1.1x player movespeed.
  • Having haste can increase the player's movespeed up to 2x.
    • Haste producing bees are the primary source of this buff.
    • The Honey, Treat, Strawberry, and Blueberry Dispensers give 5 stacks of Haste.
    • The Royal Jelly Dispenser gives 10 stacks of Haste.
  • If the player and has either the Coconut Clogs or the Gummy Boots equipped, they can have a coconut fall on them and grant the player a short burst of Coconut Haste Surge.
  • Bear Bee's Bear Morph ability can significantly increase player movespeed as well.
  • The Free Royal Jelly Dispenser gives a stack of Haste+.
  • Tadpole Bee and the Boxes-O-Frogs can summon frogs that collect sprout tokens.
  • The Star Saw can collect massive amounts of sprout tokens.
  • Windy Bee's Tornado can also collect massive amounts of sprout tokens.
  • Cub Buddies can also collect sprout tokens.
  • For Sticker Sprouts in particular, try to stick to one spot, and collect whatever loot spawns close to you. Loot that spawns too far from you will almost certainly be picked up by another player before you reach it, so stick to whatever's in reach.

docs.text:
• If a Festive Bean is planted by a player, the Festive Blessing and Beesmas Cheer buffs are only obtainable by the player that planted it.

  • Many of the treat drop statistics are mentioned in Spirit Bear's dialogue.
  • Sprouts were originally called "Seedlings" when they were released and then the name got changed in the 2019-12-23 update. Its original message was "🌱A Seedling has sprouted...🌱"

  • Since the 2019-23-12 update, Onett has been able to plant sprouts server-wide throughout the game. They can be planted under unique names.

docs.title: Star Amulet
docs.text:
This piece of content contains information obtained through datamining.

Due to the nature of the information, details may be inaccurate or outdated.

Datamined information: Star Amulet's possible stats and relevant information. — December 19th, 2024

The Star Amulet is an amulet that can be purchased in five different tiers from machines in the Star Hall.

The amulets grant buffs to the owner and always increase capacity as they go up a tier. Higher tier amulets grant more and better buffs. Diamond and Supreme Star Amulets also have additional Star Passive abilities.

Each Star Amulet requires the user to have a certain number of gifted bee types discovered. After the user generates a Star Amulet, the user must wait 1 second to generate another one.

The quality of the amulet increases linearly with the number of discovered gifted bee types up to a certain number, where its quality is maxed:

  • For non-Supreme Star Amulets, the player needs 45 types.
  • For Supreme Star Amulet, the player needs 50 types.
  • Note that this is currently not attainable, as there are only a total of 46 bee types in the game.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Supreme Star Amulet Generator takes the place of the original spot taken by Diamond Star Amulet Generator, only a bit more moved back.
  • The Diamond Star Amulet and Supreme Star Amulet are the only two Amulets in the game that can have or always have passive abilities on them.

  • The Diamond Star Amulet can only give 2 types of passive abilities, being Guiding Star and Star Shower.

  • The Supreme Star Amulet is the only Star Amulet added after the original release of Star Amulets. It was introduced in the 2020-06-06 update, while the others were released in the 2018-07-11 update.

  • The Star Amulets used to require the gifted bee types in the player's hive. However, this was changed to only requiring discovering gifted bee types when the Supreme Star Amulet was added in the game.

  • The Supreme Star Amulet is the only Star Amulet that can have double passive abilities.

  • The Diamond Star Amulet is the only Star Amulet that has received a buff after its release.

  • In the 2020-06-06 update, Diamond Star Amulets got a 1/100 chance of getting a passive when generated.

  • The summoned Gummy Star/Pop Star/Scorching Star rotates counterclockwise around the player.

  • The background audio of Supreme Star Amulet passive abilities plays 3 times for Gummy and Scorching star, 1.5 times for Pop star and 7 times for Star Saw.

  • An Ant Pass token is located behind the Supreme Star Amulet Generator.

  • It used to be behind the Diamond Star Amulet Generator before the Supreme Star Amulet Generator took its place.

  • The Star Shower passive functions similarly to Science Bear's Beesmas Lights.

  • The audio for obtaining a Star Amulet was the same audio for completing the Ready Player Two ROBLOX event (if the player has ALL the event badges).
  • When the Star Shower Passive is activated, the big star that indicates the area that the stars will fall has a slightly stretched top.
  • If a player dies while Scorching Star, Pop Star, or Gummy Star is active, the star will continue to hover wherever the player dies. It will be without the star's model and will not follow the player, but it will still play its tune. It will also continue giving the buffs that the passive grants.
  • In some cases, if the player has activated Pop Star and reaches the time limit, sometimes it will activate another Pop Star buff. However, it won't count the number of popped bubbles.
  • If the player has between 490 billion and 500 billion honey, it is still possible to buy the offer of granting a guaranteed double passive on a Supreme Star Amulet, costing only 490 billion.
  • The Diamond Star Amulet has a 1/1,000,000 chance of giving a Star Cub Skin.

docs.title: Star Hall
docs.text:
The Star Hall is located on the roof of the Noob Shop. Players can reach it using the Parachute or the Glider after using a cannon. They can also glide down from the Lion Bee Gate. If the player has enough Jump Power, they can glide from the rock that is above Brown Bear to the edge of the Star Hall or jump off the top of the Royal Jelly Dispenser that is next to the Clover Field, the player can also use the stockings decoration during beesmas and glide to the edge of the star hall.

Outside of the Star Hall, there is a Royal Jelly token to the right of the gate and a Green Cog with a Robo Pass token to the left of the gate. Inside, it has five types of Star Amulet Generators, an Ant Pass token (located behind the Supreme Star Amulet Generator), and the Royal Jelly Dispenser.

  • Royal Jelly Dispenser: Allows players to claim 1 Royal Jelly per Gifted Bee in their hive and activates the Haste+ boost. This boost lasts for exactly 60 seconds after using the machine. Naturally, players need at least one Gifted Bee in order to use the machine. It does not cost anything to use the machine, but there is a 22-hour cooldown.
  • Bronze Star Amulet Generator: Players must discover 5 Gifted Bee types (not gifted bees in hive) to use this machine. It costs 25 million honey to generate a Bronze Star Amulet and has a 1 in 100,000 chance to give the player a Black Star Sticker upon use.
  • Silver Star Amulet Generator: Players must discover 10 Gifted Bee types (not gifted bees in hive) to use this machine. It costs 50 million honey to generate a Silver Star Amulet.
  • Gold Star Amulet Generator: Players must discover 20 Gifted Bee types (not gifted bees in hive) to use this machine. It costs 250 million honey to generate a Gold Star Amulet and has a 1 in 100,000 chance to give the player a Shining Star Sticker upon use.
  • Diamond Star Amulet Generator: Players must discover 30 Gifted Bee types (not gifted bees in hive) to use this machine. It costs 1 billion honey to generate a Diamond Star Amulet and has a 1 in 10,000 chance to give the player a Cyan Star Sticker upon use. It is also has a 1 in 1 million chance (1,000,000) to grant a Star Cub upon summoning.
  • Supreme Star Amulet Generator: Players must discover 40 Gifted Bee types (not gifted bees in hive) to use this machine. It costs 10 billion honey to generate a Supreme Star Amulet and an option to spend 500 billion honey (if the player has 500 billion concurrent honey) to guaranteed two Supreme Star Amulet Passive Abilities.
The interior of the Star Hall.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The room gets its name from the music playing inside it: "starhall".
  • The cog outside the Star Hall is a hint to the in-game code, "Cog".
  • This room contains 5 of the 6 Amulet Generators in the game, the last one being the Moon Amulet Generator.
  • Before the 2019-09-28 update, the Royal Jelly Dispenser inside the Star Hall gave out 1 Royal Jelly per Gifted Bee type, rather than the number of gifted bees you have.
  • Before the 2020-04-06 update, the Ant Pass token used to be behind the Diamond Star Amulet Generator. This is because of how the Diamond Star Amulet Generator sat in the location of the Supreme Star Amulet generator before the 2020-06-06 update.
  • The Supreme Star Amulet Generator is currently the only Amulet Generator in the Star Hall that has not been released with the Star Hall itself, as the generator was released in the 2020-06-06 update.
  • In order to use the Supreme Star Amulet Generator, the player must discover at least 1 Gifted Mythic bee types (if not counting Bear Bee), because there are only 39 non-mythic bee types (zero Mythic bee type if including Bear Bee).
  • The sound pitch when creating a Star Amulet decreases when going up in tiers.
  • An ant pass can be found at the back of the Star Hall before the 2020-06-06 update
  • If the player jumps on top of the Supreme Star Amulet Generator, the player can partly glitch outside the roof.

docs.title: Star Treat
docs.text:
Star Treat

"Turns a bee into a Gifted bee!"

A Star Treat is a special type of treat that, when fed to a bee, raises its bond by 1,000 and transforms the bee into its gifted form. It is the only treat in the game which is guaranteed to turn a bee gifted. It is also one of the only ways to get gifted Event bees, including Gingerbread Bears and Aged Gingerbread Bears.

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• Buying it for 1,000 Tickets inside the Ticket Tent.
  • Playing Night Memory Match/Extreme Memory Match/Winter Memory Match (exceptionally rare).
  • Given by the Wind Shrine if you already have a Windy Bee after buying the Windy Bee Pack.

docs.title: Drops
docs.text:
• An exceptionally rare drop from the Mondo Chick, Coconut Crab, and fireflies.
  • Capturing Commando Chick for the 100th time guarantees a star treat.
  • An exceptionally low chance of dropping from Mythic Meteors.
  • An extremely rare drop from Festive Planters.

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• Completing all of Onett's quests, Mother Bear's quests, and Panda Bear's quests.
  • Completing 750 Brown Bear quests rewards a star treat. Every 500 quests after the 750th Brown Bear quest also rewards a star treat. Additionally, his 1000th quest grants the player 5 Star Treats.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This and the Atomic Treat give the most bond (1,000 bond) out of any treat, followed by a single Neonberry and Aged Gingerbread Bears (500 bond), then Gingerbread Bears and Moon Charms (250 bond).
  • The star treat, along with Aged Gingerbread Bears are the only treats that cannot be obtained from sprouts.
  • The star treat formerly gave 100 bond instead of 1,000.
  • Feeding a Star Treat to a gifted Bear Bee has a 1/3 chance to spawn a Bear Bee Offer sticker.

docs.title: Stats
docs.text:
This page is for stats that apply to bees. For stats that apply to the player, collecting pollen, and the hive, see System Page.

Stats (short for statistics) refer to the aspects of each bee that are the basis for how that bee performs. Certain stats increase with higher levels.

docs.title: Rarity
docs.text: Rarity refers to how often bees of each category can be expected to be generated from eggs or royal jelly. Bees of greater rarity tend to be of higher stats and possessing their own unique ability, but rarity itself does not have any bearing on performance. An Event tier of bees are acquired through their unique obtainment method.

docs.title: Color
docs.text: Color affects a bee's ability to gather pollen from flowers, improving their Gather Amount by 50% when collecting from flowers of a matching color. Blue and Red are the only colors of bees that have this bonus. Colorless bees do not experience any boost to Gather Amount, even from white flowers.

docs.title: Bond
docs.text:
Main article: Bond

Bond is a stat to determine if a bee has enough "experience" to level up. The following methods can affect experience:

  • Treats
  • Collecting Pollen
  • Bond from battle
  • Puppy Love
  • Digging in to the Beesmas Feast during Beesmas.

docs.title: Energy
docs.text:
Main article: Energy

Energy represents the number of times a bee will gather pollen from a flower and attack mobs before returning to the hive to rest (30 seconds to fully recharge upon entering the hive)

  • Spawning Ability Tokens does not cost a bee any energy
  • The energy of all bees in a swarm can be increased with stacks of Polar Power from Polar Bear's quests, or from an energy mutation
  • Energy is increased by 5% for each level above 1
  • Resetting yourself will cause bees to go back to the hive, but they will not recharge their energy
  • An energy reset can be achieved by reseting again when bees are inside of the hive after a prior reset

The formula for energy is: Base Energy * (1 + .05 * (Level - 1)) * Polar Power + Energy Mutation

docs.title: Speed
docs.text:
Speed, short for Bee Movespeed, is how fast a bee moves and performs actions (contrary to its name). Speed indrectly affects all basic processes of a bee such as:

  • Gathering
  • Attacking
  • Sipping nectar in a planter
  • Converting at hive.

Bees move at approximately 1.5 times their move speed when not close to their owner and 0.5 of their move speed when returning to the hive to rest. The speed of all bees in a swarm can be increased by Gifted Ninja Bee's hive bonus, Beesmas Cheer, Playtime Badge, oil, super smoothies, and activating Coconut Haste.

The formula for Bee Movespeed is: Base Bee Movespeed * (1 + .03 * (Level - 1)) * (1 + Ninja Bee Hive Bonus + Playtime Badge Bonus)

docs.title: Attack
docs.text:
Attack is how much damage the bee will do when fighting mobs. Attack remains constant at all levels, but can be boosted through various accessories, items, amulets, certain gifted hive bonuses and ability tokens. Gifted bees have 50% more attack.

The formula for a bee's Attack is: (Base Attack Damage + Attack Buffs) * Attack multiplier (* 1.5 If the bee is gifted)

docs.title: Gather Amount
docs.text:
Gather Amount describes how much pollen a bee will collect from a flower and how quickly it does so. The amount collected increases by 10% for each level above 1. Gather amount may be increased with; amulets, certain Gifted Bee bonuses, Gamepasses, or items.

The formula for Gather Amount is: Base Gather Amount * (1 + .10 * (Level - 1)) * Gifted Multiplier

docs.title: Production Amount
docs.text:
Production Amount describes how much pollen a bee will convert into honey at the hive and how quickly it does so. The amount converted increases by 10% for each level above 1.

The formula for Production Amount is: (Base Production Amount + Production Amount) * (1 + .10 * (Level - 1)) * Conversion Rate * Gifted Multiplier

docs.title: Mutations
docs.text:
Main article: Mutation

Mutations are a bonus granted through feeding bitterberries to a bee when they are under the radioactive effect. Mutations can grant bonus:

  • Attack
  • Convert Amount
  • Gather Amount
  • Energy
  • Bee Ability Rate
  • Bee Movespeed
  • Critical Chance
  • Instant Conversion

docs.title: Gifted
docs.text:
Main article: Gifted Bees

Gifted is a bonus granted through feeding a bee's favourite treat, Star Treat, Gingerbread Bears, or Aged Gingerbread Bears. This stat grants:

  • Multiplier to gather amount, convert amount, and bee attack all together by 1.5x
  • Ability to spawn - [Inspire] tokens
  • A gifted hive bonus (only once for each bee)
  • A gifted ability (if the bee has one)
  • A new appearance

docs.title: Stick Bug Amulet
docs.text:
The Stick Bug Amulet is an amulet that can be obtained from the Stick Bug Challenge. In order to obtain these amulets, the player will need to get Stick Bug to a certain level as well as reach a certain score during the Stick Bug Challenge.

The amulets grant buffs to the owner and always increase capacity, convert rate and Tool Pollen as they go up a tier. Higher tier amulets grant more and better buffs.

The amulet's quality is worked out per tier. It rises linearly from that tier's minimum score to the next tier's score, so it starts again from 0 at each tier. The "next" scores are 8M for Bronze, 20M for Silver, 50M for Gold, 150M for Diamond and 3B for Supreme. For example, a Silver amulet at 14M score has quality (14M − 8M) / (20M − 8M) = 0.5.

docs.title: Requirement(s)
docs.text:
The requirements are based on your score and Stick Bug's level on a challenge.

Requirement(s) Amulet At least 1M score, must be at least a level 5 Stick Bug Bronze Stick Bug Amulet At least 8M score, must be at least a level 8 Stick Bug Silver Stick Bug Amulet At least 20M score, must be at least a level 11 Stick Bug Gold Stick Bug Amulet At least 50M score, must be at least a level 13 Stick Bug Diamond Stick Bug Amulet At least 1B score, must reach and defeat a level 18 Stick Bug Supreme Stick Bug Amulet

Stats in a "Select N" group are drawn evenly without repeats, so each one has an N in M chance. "Separate chance roll" means the stat only appears if an extra chance roll succeeds. "Low values more likely" means high values of that stat are rarer.

docs.title: Stick Bug Challenge
docs.text:
The Stick Bug Challenge is a boss fight feature that lasts 10 minutes. It is primarily activated when a player talks to Stick Bug and starts the challenge but can also initiate when a player begins Spirit Bear's "Dancing With Stick Bug" quest, when Onett chooses to activate it globally, and during Beesmas when completing Stick Bug's Beesmas quest or giving him a present. Starting the challenge by yourself requires having given a translator to Stick Bug, and either costs 50 tickets or can be started for free once every 36 hours/1.5 days. The option to pay 50 tickets will be unavailable if the challenge can be started for free. The challenge takes place across the entire server and can be participated in by anyone. Giving a present to Stick Bug or starting the Egg Hunt quest will also start the challenge (if a translator has been given to Stick Bug).

When the challenge starts, a message in the chat appears, saying: ⚠️ {Username} has started the Stick Bug Challenge! ⚠️ Then, Stick Bug spawns in the Sunflower Field. If Onett summons Stick Bug, it would say:

⚠️ Onett has started the Stick Bug Challenge! ⚠️ During the challenge, Stick Bug moves around to different fields and fights players using various attacks. After players deal enough damage to Stick Bug, it will go to a different field, leaving a circle of rewards behind. When Stick Bug moves to different fields, it gains more health, becomes faster, gets better attacks (e.g. more Stick Nymphs will spawn) and gains a level. During the challenge, a brown window on the side of the screen shows how long the Stick Bug Challenge will be active, what level and which field Stick Bug is in, and how many points the player has obtained so far.

Stick Bug will only appear in the Sunflower Field, Clover Field, Strawberry Field, Bamboo Field, Pineapple Patch, Cactus Field, Pumpkin Patch or Mountain Top Field. Stick Bug always starts in the Sunflower Field. When Stick Bug moves to a different field, a message in the chat will appear, saying:

⚠️ Stick Bug's headed to the {Field Name}! ⚠️

docs.title: Attacks
docs.text: Stick Bug will attack in many different ways.

docs.title: Normal Behavior and Sequence
docs.text:
Stick Bug will run towards one of the players in the field regularly and before initiating an attack. Getting hit by him will deal damage to the player. Stick Bug's movement speed, his stick nymphs, and his speed in using his attacks increase with his level. He uses a fixed sequence of attacks, with the arrangement of:

  • Splinter Trap
  • Spinners
  • Flailing Sticks
  • Summon Stick Nymphs
  • Stick Totem
  • Flailing Sticks
  • Hide
  • Stick Flail

Stick Bug uses certain attacks when he reaches certain levels. But he will use the attack in the same pattern.

docs.title: Flailing Sticks
docs.text:
Stick Bug moves with the dance emote, and a large red warning circle appears around him with a radius of about 6 flowers, after a few seconds, he will flail sticks and deal damage (Damage scales from his level). Flails only deal damage by one time and the player cannot be damaged by the same flail again. After a moment, he will summon a few Stick Nymphs around himself. The number of Stick Nymphs deployed depends on the emote he used. He will either use:

  • The dance emote
  • The dance2 emote
  • The point emote

docs.title: Stick Nymphs
docs.text:
Main article: Stick Nymph

Stick Bug moves with the dance3 emote and a large red warning circle appears with a radius of about 6 flowers. After a few seconds, he will wave, and a horde of stick nymphs are summoned inside the red circle. The movement speed, amount of stick nymphs spawned, and the stick nymphs' level are based on Stick Bug's level, increasing as he has higher levels.

If the player had completed Stick Bug's beesmas quest past 2020, there is a chance that he will instead summon a special variant called Festive Nymphs. They have the same attributes as normal stick nymphs but drop better loot.

docs.title: Spinners
docs.text: 3 or 4 (depending on Stick Bug's level) red warning circles appear on the field, they will always be located near the corners of the field, and the spinners have a radius of about 3 flowers. After a while, he will deploy rotating one-bladed flails on the red circles, the speed of the rotations gradually increases as Stick Bug levels up. As Stick Bug reaches higher levels, he will initiate this attack more than once, stacking more than a single blade in a single spot at once. The deployed flails disappear after a while.

docs.title: Hiding
docs.text: After his attack sequence is finished, he will stand still and hide in the field. He becomes 2 dimensional and can be seen by shadows in the flowers. Stick Bug cannot be targetable in this phase; to get him out of the 2d form, players must collect pollen in the affected flowers on his 2d forms. The requirement increases by his level. After putting it down to 0, he will become 3d again and stand still before restarting his attack sequence. Splinter trap will activate after this ability is executed.

docs.title: Splinter Trap
docs.text:
Upon hiding, Stick Bug leveling up, or during a level 12+ Stick Bug. Stick Bug stands still for a short time and uses the point emote, after that. Players who contributed to attacking Stick Bug during the current level will become targeted by this attack and get put on by a splinter trap on top of their head/s. The Splinter trap decreases the players' movespeed and jump power by 25% and damages the player by 3 per second.

When a player is trapped in twigs, they will receive a message in the chat, saying:

You've been trapped in twigs! Collect pollen to remove them. Note that the splinter trap icon is the same as the Haste+ icon.

docs.title: Defense Totem
docs.text:
When Stick Bug reaches level 6 and above, Stick Bug will build a defense totem based on a nearby field. When the totem is active, Stick Bug receives 25% defense, decreasing the damage he receives by the same amount. Stick Bug can stack them up to 3 times (75% defense) and will not use this attack when there are 3 consecutive totems active. To destroy the totem, the player/s must collect pollen in the field of the defense totem. Upon destroying a totem, the totem will drop rewards.

Drop table of Defense Totems Honey

Treats Royal Jellies Gumdrops Pineapples Sunflower Seeds Oils Enzymes

Stick Bug builds a totem in the following fields. Note that the fields he summons the totems are based on the field he is currently standing in:

  • Mushroom Field
  • Dandelion Field
  • Blue Flower Field
  • Spider Field
  • Stump Field
  • Pine Tree Forest
  • Rose Field

A server-wide message is sent when he uses this attack, saying: ⚠️ Stick Bug has built a Defense Totem in the {Field Name}! ⚠️

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
In this section, there will be some tips to progress further in the Stick Bug Challenge.

  • Make sure there are no mobs to distract the players' bees, like the Mondo Chick, before starting the challenge.
  • Level up your bees. Bees with a lower level than Stick Bug would most likely miss its attacks.
  • Try to get as many strong players on the server as possible. A way of communicating with other players, like voice chat, can be used. The more players that are doing the challenge, the faster Stick Bug will level up.
  • Stickbug has a pattern after landing on a field, which is Flailing sticks then attacking the player.
  • Level 12+ Stickbug has a different pattern than Level 1-11, doing 2 Spinner attacks first then attacking the player.
  • Try to use most optimal paths to save time traveling between fields.
  • The Bamboo Glitch can help stun the stickbug. To do this, go to the stairs in Bamboo.
  • Certain equipment can be very useful in the challenge.
  • Many gears boost bee attack in some way.
  • The Fire and Demon Masks boost multiple helpful stats, like bee attack and defense, as well as spawning many flames with their passives.
  • The Gummy Mask's Gummy Morph passive greatly boosts Gummy Bee's stats, including attack.
  • The Dark Scythe can create Dark Flames, which boost Super-Crit Power. The flames themselves also deal more damage.
  • The Coconut Canister has two useful passives, being Inspire Coconuts and Emergency Coconut Shield.
    • When activating the Emergency Coconut Shield, it grants 100% defense and x1.25 bee attack for a few seconds. Try to make the most of these boosts, like using the invincibility to escape or using the increased attack to do lots of damage.
    • It should be activated later on in the challenge. Activating it early would be a waste. Before the Stick Bug Challenge, the shield should be intentionally activated so that there is no risk of it activating early.
  • The Glider and boots can help with navigating the map or escaping tough situations.
    • The Coconut Clogs/Gummy Boots' Coconut Haste Surge can prove useful in a pinch.
  • There are many bees that are recommended for the Stick Bug Challenge.
  • Some bees, like Lion Bee, Precise Bee, Spicy Bee, Vicious Bee and Windy Bee have high attack stats, passive or abilities that do lots of damage.
    • Vicious Bee, Windy Bee and Spicy Bee abilities are helpful for dealing with both Stick Bug and Stick Nymphs as they deal damage to every mob within their range.
    • Impale ability can be used the moment Stick Nymphs are summoned to increase it's efficiency.
    • Tornado pathing can't be controlled, but you still can lure Sticks Nymphs into it.
  • Bees with helpful gifted hive bonuses like Brave Bee, Looker Bee, Commander Bee, Rage Bee or Precise Bee will increase damage output.
  • Certain abilities from bees can grant useful buffs.
    • Precise Bee's Target Practice can boost Super-Crit Chance.
    • Multiple bees have Focus, which boosts Critical Chance.
    • Music Bee's Melody boosts Critical Power.
    • Rage Bee and Spicy Bee have Rage, which boosts attack.
    • Haste-producing bees are also helpful in traversing the map and dodging attacks.
    • Flame Heat gives additional +5% to +25% Bee Attack
    • Digital Bee's Mind Hack can stun the Nymphs and Stick Bug.
  • All gifted bees have x1.5 attack over their non-gifted counterparts.
  • Certain mutations can grant attack or ability rate bonuses.
  • Certain beequips can grant useful bonuses or abilities.
  • Many items can be used to further enhance helpful stats.
  • Using Stingers will boost bee attack by 1.5x for 30 seconds.
    • Using stingers activates Star Saw, which can deal lots of damage to both Stick Bug and the Stick Nymphs. (Note that you will need the Supreme Star Amulet with the Star Saw passive in order to use it)
  • The player can use Oils to increase movespeed, and Tropical Drinks to increase the chance for critical hits, each for 10 minutes.
    • Super Smoothies can also be used for both improved buffs and an additional +1% Super-Crit Chance.
  • Coconuts will deal lots of damage when landing on Stick Bug or any Stick Nymphs.
    • Besides using the coconut item, the two Coconut Canister passives can also summon coconuts.
  • Try to save Invigorating Nectar for an additional x1.01 to x1.10 bee attack. The bee attack depends on how much time the nectar has left.
  • When Stick Bug builds a defense totem on a nearby field, send the teammate(s) who can deal with it the fastest. For example, if a totem is built in the Blue Flower Field, the player with the best blue pollen collection should be sent to take the totem down.
  • If the defense totem is in the Stump Field, send somebody who has taken down the Stump Snail recently instead of somebody with a Stump Snail still in the field.
  • Stick bug totems can be safely dealt with when Stick Bug hides into flowers, as in this state it's not able to build more and Stick Nymphs are very likely to despawn by player's return to field.
  • One teammate can try to lure the Stick Nymphs away from the other players so that their bees will not be distracted by them.
  • Place sprinklers in the field in which Stick Bug is currently in. Since flowers (especially in low-level fields) tend to "drain" quickly, this puts players at risk of dying from the Splinter Trap or losing time when Stick Bug is hiding in flower patches.
  • Clouds can also help with flower regeneration.
  • Lag may be an issue for players, so making optimizations, like reducing the graphic settings, could help in the challenge.
  • Stand at higher areas like the ramp at the Pumpkin Patch. Stick Nymphs will not be able to reach these places, and most of Stick Bug's attacks will not hit.
  • Sticker Stack may be useful for the challenge, if it has Bee Movespeed, Critical Power, Super Crit Power or Bee Attack buffs.
  • Vector Bee and Precise Bee can help a lot with pollen collection when Stick Bug is hiding in the field.

docs.title: Stick Bug
docs.text:
Stick Bug Location On top of the tallest mushroom in the Mushroom Field. Respawns Every Every 36 hours or anytime with 50 tickets

This page is for the Stick Bug NPC. For attack behaviour and the actual challenge, please see Stick Bug Challenge

Stick Bug is a NPC found on the tallest mushroom in the Mushroom Field, next to the Top Stick Bug Fighters Leaderboard. It is accessible by using the Red Cannon/Yellow Cannon/Blue Cannon with the Parachute/Glider, or using the Beekeeper's Boots and jumping from the second mushroom to the one with the Royal Jelly. Players will need a Translator to talk to Stick Bug, where they can then ask it to start the Stick Bug Challenge. Stick Bug then appears as a boss mob and always spawns in the Sunflower Field first. Upon defeat, it flees to a random Field from this list:

  • Sunflower Field
  • Clover Field
  • Strawberry Field
  • Bamboo Field
  • Pineapple Patch
  • Cactus Field
  • Pumpkin Patch
  • Mountain Top Field

The player can start the Stick Bug Challenge for free every 1 and a half days (1d, 12hr), by initiating it anytime for 50 Tickets, or by giving Stick Bug a Present during Beesmas.

When the challenge ends, the player will be awarded an amulet depending on their score (More information in the Stick Bug Amulet page).
