docs.title: System Page
docs.text:
This page is for stats that apply to the player, collecting pollen, and the hive. For stats that apply to bees, see Stats.

The System Page is shown by clicking the cog in the menu bar. It is in between the Badges page and the Robux Shop page. Here, the player can redeem codes, send Trade Requests, view the Global Leaderboard, use the Cub Console, view the players' stats, turn on and off in-game music, toggle Pollen Text, Abbreviate Pollen, allow Trade Requests, display and hide other players' bees, toggle Reducing Strobing VFX, and toggle Auto-Jelly. Turning off all in-game music only silences the music, not the sound effects (such as the sounds of Ability Tokens and obtaining Legendary, Mythic, Gifted, and Event). You can mute all sound by turning off the in-game sound on the Roblox menu.

docs.title: Character Stats
docs.text: The tab also lists many of the player's active stat values, though not all of them. The following values are listed and explained:

docs.title: Convert Amount
docs.text: Boosts the base conversion of your bees before multipliers by a certain amount. Example: A Basic Bee with 20 Convert Amount will convert 100 Honey in 4 seconds instead of 80 Honey in 4 seconds. It can be boosted with amulets, the Honey Mask and certain belts. This stat was formerly named 'Conversion Amount' until it was changed in the Beesmas 2019 update.

docs.title: Convert Rate
docs.text: Boosts your bees conversion by the following percentage. Example: A Basic Bee with 200% Convert Rate will convert 160 Honey in 4 seconds instead of 80 Honey in 4 seconds. It can be boosted with amulets, Enzymes, Marshmallow Bees, Super Smoothies, Science Enhancement, the Conversion Buff, the Honeyday Event buff, the Honey Badge, Gifted Diamond Bee, the Yellow Jellybean, Jellybean Sharing Bonus, certain Stickers in the Sticker Stack, some beequips and most Bags. This stat was formerly named 'Conversion Rate' until it was changed in the Beesmas 2019 update.

docs.title: Convert Rate At Hive
docs.text: Boosts your bees’ conversion by the following percentage at the hive. This stat can stack with Convert Rate. Example: A level 1 Basic Bee with 200% Convert Rate and 200% Hive Convert Rate will convert 320 Honey in 4 seconds while converting at the hive, but it will only convert 160 Honey outside of the hive. It can be increased with the Pumpkin Badge, Bubble Bloat and certain items. This buff was used to be "Hive Convert Rate" until the 2021-12-26 update.

docs.title: Bonus Convert Amount
docs.text: Increases the base conversion of the player's bees. It can be increased by certain amulets and items.

docs.title: Loot Luck
docs.text: Loot Luck is a passive attribute that increases the chances of receiving rewards from defeated mobs. It can be increased with Baby Love, the Clover Badge, Baby Bee's Gifted Hive Bonus and certain items. This stat was formerly named 'Luck' until it was changed in the 2019-04-05 update.

docs.title: Critical Chance
docs.text: The chance of your bees hitting stronger or collecting more pollen. More accurately - by how big your Critical Power is. Example: A Basic Bee with 50% Critical Chance will hit with increased damage half of the time. It can be boosted with amulets, Tropical Drinks, Focus, the Green Jellybean, Gifted Commander Bee and certain items. Currently, the highest critical chance a player can have at a time is 88%.

docs.title: Critical Power
docs.text: This stat multiplies how strong a Critical Hit will be. It applies to fighting and pollen collecting. Example: Basic Bee with 300% Critical Power (on critical hit) will hit with the power of 3 Basic Bees (3 damage). It can be boosted with the Ant Amulet, Melody, the Battle Badge, Gifted Tabby Bee, Gifted Looker Bee and with certain items. The calculated max Critical Power is 695%.

docs.title: Super-Crit Chance
docs.text: The possibility for a critical hit to Super-Crit. Super-Crits deals 33% more damage and collect twice as much pollen as a regular critical hit, and are instantly converted. When a hit is a Super-Crit, there will be a purple color indicating the damage and the ! sign next to it. It can be boosted by having a Gifted Precise Bee, Tabby Blessing, Precision, a precise mark, the Bruteforce upgrade in the Robo Bear Challenge or using a Super Smoothie. The max possible Super-Crit Chance you can have at a time is 53% (assuming you are in the Robo Bear Challenge).

docs.title: Super-Crit Power
docs.text: The amount pollen is multiplied by when performing Super-Crits (after applying Critical Power). Super-crit attacks are only increased by 33% as much as Pollen Super-crits. It can only be boosted by the Whistle and Kazoo Beequips, a Cog Amulet or temporarily boosted by the Dark Scythe.

docs.title: Bee Ability Rate
docs.text: Increases the speed at which the player's bees create Ability Tokens. Example: If it takes a bee about 20 seconds to produce a token, with 20% Bee Ability Rate, the bee is likely to take ~16 seconds to produce the token. Bee ability rate can be boosted by Star Amulets, Motivating Nectar, certain masks, items, bee mutations, and Beequips.

docs.title: Pollen
docs.text: Increases pollen from all sources (both from bees and tools). Example: With 100% pollen, the player can collect 1,000 pollen, and with 110% pollen, it will able to collect 1,100 pollen from the same amount of time and flowers. It can be increased with amulets, Bear Morph, Inspire, Baby Love, Pollen Marks, the Honeyday Event buff, from Clouds, Gifted Basic Bee, Gifted Bear Bee, the Periwinkle Jellybean or with certain items.

docs.title: White Pollen
docs.text: Boosts your white pollen collection. It can be increased with amulets, Tropical Drinks, Marshmallow Bees, White Boost, the Spider Badge, the Coconut Badge, Gifted Shocked Bee, the White Jellybean, Wind Boosts, or with certain items.

docs.title: Red Pollen
docs.text: Boosts your red pollen collection. It can be increased with amulets, Red Extracts, Red Boost, Flame Heat, the Strawberry Badge, Gifted Rad Bee or with certain items.

docs.title: Blue Pollen
docs.text: Boosts your blue pollen collection. It can be increased with Amulets, Blue Extracts, Blue Boost, with the Bamboo Badge, Gifted Cool Bee or with certain items.

docs.title: Bomb Pollen
docs.text: Boosts your pollen collection from all bombs. Example: If the player collects 5,000 pollen with a Buzz Bomb token, with 200% Bomb Pollen they will collect 10,000 pollen from the same flowers. It can be increased with Amulets, Bomb Combos, Gifted Bomber Bee, Festive Mark, Black Jelly Bean or with certain items.

docs.title: Buzz Bomb Pollen
docs.text: Boosts your pollen collection from Buzz Bombs and Fuzz Bombs. It can be increased with amulets, Gifted Demo Bee, or with certain items.

docs.title: Red Bomb Pollen
docs.text: Boosts your pollen collection from Red Bombs. It can be increased with Amulets, Gifted Rascal Bee, Festive Mark or with certain items.

docs.title: Blue Bomb Pollen
docs.text: Boosts your pollen collection from Blue Bombs. It can be increased with Amulets, Gifted Frosty Bee, or with certain items.

docs.title: Bubble Pollen
docs.text: Boosts your pollen collection from bubbles. Example: If the player collects 5,000 pollen with a bubble, with 200% Pollen from Bubbles they will collect 10,000 pollen from the same flowers. It can be increased with Gifted Bubble Bee, Cog Amulet, Bubble Mask or the Diamond Mask.

docs.title: Flame Pollen
docs.text: Boosts your pollen collection from flames created by bees, ability tokens, and passive abilities. Example: If the flames collect 1,000 over time, with 200% Pollen from Flames they will collect 2,000 pollen from the same flowers. It can be increased with Gifted Fire Bee, Cog Amulet, or the Demon Mask.

docs.title: Bee Gather Pollen
docs.text: Boosts pollen collection for all bees. Example: With 200% Bee Gather Pollen, Basic Bee will collect 20 pollen in 4 seconds. It can be increased with amulets, Glues, Gifted Music Bee, the x2 Pollen from Bees Gamepass or with certain items.

docs.title: Bee Ability Pollen
docs.text: Boosts pollen collection from all bees' abilities and passives. It can be increased with Gifted Shy Bee Hive Bonus, certain Beequips, or Sticker Stack.

docs.title: Tool Pollen
docs.text: Boosts your pollen collection from your tool. Example: With 100% (base) Tool Pollen, the player will collect 1,000 pollen with their tool at once. With 125% Tool Pollen player will collect 1,250 pollen with their tool at once at the same place. It can be increased with amulets, Glues, Gifted Carpenter Bee, with the Stump Badge or with certain items.

docs.title: Instant Conversion
docs.text: Instantly converts your pollen when you are collecting pollen on a field. Example: a Basic Bee with 50% Instant Conversion that collects 10 pollen will make half of it instantly convert into Honey. You will have 5 Honey and 5 pollen, so you can collect more pollen. It can be boosted with amulets, Enzymes, the Dandelion Badge, the Cactus Badge, Gifted Photon Bee, Festive Blessing buff, or with certain items.

docs.title: Instant White Conversion
docs.text: Instantly converts white pollen you collect, in addition to Instant Conversion. It can be boosted with amulets, the Pineapple Badge, Gifted Windy Bee, or with the Coconut Canister.

docs.title: Instant Red Conversion
docs.text: Instantly converts red pollen you collect, in addition to Instant Conversion. It can be boosted with amulets, the Mushroom Badge, Gifted Crimson Bee, or with certain items.

docs.title: Instant Blue Conversion
docs.text: Instantly converts blue pollen you collect, in addition to Instant Conversion. It can be boosted with amulets, the Blue Flower Badge, Gifted Cobalt Bee, Diamond Mask, or with certain items.

docs.title: Instant Bomb Conversion
docs.text: Instantly converts pollen collected by the player's bomb. It can be temporarily boosted by standing in a festive mark, or can be permanently increased by owning a Gifted Demon Bee.

docs.title: Instant Flame Conversion
docs.text: Instantly converts pollen collected by the player's summoned flames. It can be boosted by having the Demon Mask equipped, or you can temporarily get 50% Instant Flame Conversion by triggering the Scorching Star Passive.

docs.title: Instant Bubble Conversion
docs.text: Instantly converts pollen collected by the player's popped bubbles. There are currently no ways to obtain it.

docs.title: Honey Per Pollen
docs.text: Allows you to make more Honey from the same amount of pollen, which works on conversion, Instant Converters, Micro-Converters, and Instant Conversion. Example: With 200% Honey Per Pollen, a player will make 2,000 Honey from 1,000 Pollen. It can be increased with the Moon Amulet, the Wealth Clock, the Goo Badge, Gifted Gummy Bee or Nectar.

docs.title: Honey At Hive
docs.text: Increases the Honey you convert when converting at hive. You can boost this stat with Satisfying Nectar and Balloon Blessing. Diamond Bee's Shimmering Honey directly multiplies this stat.

docs.title: Movespeed
docs.text: Movespeed of your character in studs. It can be increased with amulets, Oil, Super Smoothie, Haste or Haste+, Bear Morph, Coconut Haste, Gifted Hasty Bee, or with boots.

docs.title: Movement Collection
docs.text: Allows the player to collect pollen when walking on flowers. The player can get this boost from wearing boots or from a Moon Amulet. The higher the movement collection, the greater amount of pollen the player collects from walking on flowers. This boost also collects goo if the player walks on any goo patches.

docs.title: Jump Power
docs.text: Jump power of your character in studs. It can be increased with Bear Morph, all boots (except for the Basic Boots), or the Propeller Hat. The minimum jump power is 55 and the maximum jump power is 97.

docs.title: Defense
docs.text: Reduces the damage that you take. Example: If a mob deals 50 damage, with 50% Defense it will deal 25 damage instead. It can be increased with the Shell Amulet, hats, or with guards. Having 100% defense means that you take no damage and can be achieved by activating the emergency coconut shield passive. The maximum defense without the emergency coconut shield is 60%. This is achieved by having the Demon Mask or Diamond Mask (+35%), both the Crimson and Cobalt Guards (+10% each), and +5% on a Shell Amulet. Defense was originally Damage Reduction.

docs.title: Bond From Treats
docs.text: Gives additional bond for your bees when you give them treats. Example: If you feed 100 normal treats (1,000 total bond) to your bee, with 125% Bond From Treats it will grant 1,250 bond instead. It can be increased with the Moon Amulet, Gifted Puppy Bee or as a Hive Bonus from the Reindeer Antlers beequip.

docs.title: Bond From Battle
docs.text: Gives additional bond for your bees when you are defeating a mob. Example: Normally, scorpions give 15 bond for each of your bees when you defeat it. With 150% Bond From Battle, your bees will receive 22.5 Bond instead. It can be increased with amulets.

docs.title: Honey From Tokens
docs.text: Boosts Honey that you receive from all Honey giving tokens (Honey Gift, Honey Gift+, Impale, mob loot, Coin Scatter, Honeystorm, and others). Example: A level 2 Diamond Bee will give 2,000 Honey with its Honey Gift+ token. With 200% Honey From Tokens, it will give 4,000 Honey instead. It can be increased with amulets, Gifted Honey Bee, or with certain items.

docs.title: Bee Attack
docs.text: Makes all your bees, regardless of their colors, deal more damage per hit. It will add one bee attack (Damage) per bee attack stat that you have. Example: With +4 Bee Attack, Basic Bee will attack with the power of 5 Basic Bees (Base Attack + Bee Attack multiplier). It can be increased with amulets, with Rage, or Gifted Brave Bee, or with certain items buffs and beequips.

docs.title: Red Attack
docs.text: Same as Bee Attack, but applies only for Red bees. It can be boosted with amulets or certain items.

docs.title: Blue Attack
docs.text: Same as Bee Attack, but applies only for Blue bees. It can be boosted with amulets or certain items.

docs.title: Colorless Attack
docs.text: Same as Bee Attack, but applies only for Colorless bees. It can be boosted with amulets, or certain items.

docs.title: Attack Multiplier
docs.text: Multiplies attack of all bees, but with a percentage. It can be increased with Amulets, Stingers, Flame Heat, Emergency Coconut Shield , Gifted Rage Bee or the Demon Mask.

docs.title: Goo
docs.text: Multiplies all collected goo. It can be increased with the Shell Amulet, Gummy Morph, Gummy Mask, Gummy Boots, Gummy Star, or Gummyballer.

docs.title: Goo Conversion
docs.text: Instantly converts pollen equal to the goo gathered, which can convert all the pollen gathered (effectively serving as 100% Instant Conversion) with a high enough Goo Conversion % and Goo multiplyer. It can be increased by amulets, Gummy Mask, Gummy Morph, or Gummy Star.

docs.title: Capacity Multiplier
docs.text: Gives additional pollen storage by the amount of the percentages. Example: If your backpack can hold up to 200,000 pollen, with 200% Capacity Multiplier, your backpack can hold up to 400,000 instead. It can be increased with amulets, Sunflower Badge, Quest Badge, Bumble Bee's Gifted Hive Bonus, Buoyant Bee's Gifted Hive Bonus and with certain items. If your capacity multiplier is a decimal percentage, it doesn't show the decimal and rounds the number, but the rounding doesn't affect your capacity.

docs.title: White Field Capacity
docs.text:
Gives additional pollen storage by the number of percentages based on the percentage of white flowers in a field.

Example: If you have 15,000,000 Capacity (With Capacity Multiplier) and your White Field Capacity is 180%, your total capacity if in the Spider Field is 27,000,000. It can be increased with things like the Gummy Mask, Exhausted Bee's Gifted Hive Bonus, Polar Bear's Ornament and other inventory items. If your capacity multiplier is a decimal percentage, it doesn't show the decimal and rounds the number, but the rounding doesn't affect your capacity.

docs.title: Red Field Capacity
docs.text:
Gives additional pollen storage by the number of percentages based on the percentage of red flowers in a field.

Example: If you have 15,000,000 Capacity (With Capacity Multiplier) and your Red Field Capacity is 150%, your total capacity if on a field with all flowers being red is 22,500,000. It can be increased with things like Demon Mask, Riley Bee's Gifted Hive Bonus, Gifted Riley Bee (NPC) Ornament, the Rose Badge and other inventory items. If your capacity multiplier is a decimal percentage, it doesn't show the decimal and rounds the number, but the rounding doesn't affect your capacity.

docs.title: Blue Field Capacity
docs.text:
Gives additional pollen storage by the amount of percentage based on the percentage of blue flowers in a field.

Example: If you have 15,000,000 Capacity (With Capacity Multiplier) and your Blue Field Capacity is 200%, your total capacity if on a field with only blue flowers is 30,000,000. It can be increased with buffs like Bucko Bee's Gifted Hive Bonus, Gifted Bucko Bee (NPC) Ornament, the Pine Tree Badge, and other inventory items. If your capacity multiplier is a decimal percentage, it doesn't show the decimal and rounds the number, but the rounding doesn't affect your capacity.

docs.title: Convert Total
docs.text: The total convert amounts of all of your bees combined (after conversion modifiers).

docs.title: Gather Total
docs.text: The total gather amounts of all of your bees combined (before pollen modifiers).

docs.title: Ticket Chance
docs.text: A stat boost which increases chances of obtaining Tickets, can be obtained through the Moon Amulet, Festive Wreath, stacking the Ticket Vouchers and the now unobtainable Ticket Chance gamepass.

docs.title: Attack Total
docs.text: The total attack of all of your bees combined (after attack modifiers).

docs.title: Auto-Jelly Settings
docs.text:
The Auto-Jelly Settings can be found at the bottom of the System Page. There are options for Royal Jellies or Star Jellies to auto roll until the requirements are fulfilled. It can be used to help players obtain a bee they desire quickly. There are options for the requirement the jelly will roll into:

  • Until Legendary: Jellies will auto roll until you get a Legendary or Mythic Bee.
  • Until Mythic: Jellies will auto roll until you get a Mythic Bee.
  • Require Gifted: Jellies will auto roll until you get a Gifted or Mythic Bee.
  • Require Mutation: Jellies will auto roll until you get a Mutated or Mythic Bee.

Multiple options can be turned on at a time, whilst also making the auto jelly stop on the combined requirement. Example: When the Legendary and Gifted options are turned on, the jellies will auto roll until you get a Gifted Legendary Bee. When the Legendary, Gifted, and Mutation options are turned on, the jellies will auto roll until you get a Gifted Legendary Bee with a Mutation.

If the Until Legendary option or both the Until Legendary and Until Mythic options are turned on, it will auto roll until you get a Legendary Bee or Mythic Bee. If only the Require Gifted option is turned on, it will auto roll until you get a Gifted Bee or a Mythic Bee. If only the Require Mutation option is turned on, it will auto roll until you get a Gifted Bee or a Mutated Bee. If both the Require Gifted and Require Mutation options are turned on, it will auto roll until you get a Gifted Mutated Bee or Mythic Bee.

If the Mutation option is turned on, but the bee you selected isn't radioactive, a pop-up after using a Royal Jelly will say that you can't auto-roll Royal Jellies for mutation. Unless the bee is radioactive, you will have to use the Royal Jellies one at a time.

When using a Royal Jelly on a bee with an auto-jelly option enabled, a reminder appears after the message that the auto-jelly option is on.

If you turn on the following options, an extra pop-up will warn the player that the options they selected are very rare:

  • Mythic and Gifted.
  • Mythic and Mutation.
  • Mythic, Gifted, and Mutation.
  • Legendary, Gifted, and Mutation.

When using a Star Jelly on a bee, another pop-up will appear, reminding the player that an auto-jelly setting is on and will use as many star jellies as it needs in order to fulfill its requirement. This pop-up will appear even if only the Until Gifted option is turned on. If you are using the Require Gifted option with Star Jellies, you will still receive the warning, but nothing will happen.

docs.title: Tabby Bee
docs.text:
Tabby Bee Original Gifted "This affectionate bee was raised by cats. It becomes a better worker as it warms up to you." RarityEvent ColorColorless Energy28 Speed16.1 Attack4 Color Scheme Skin#f99d28#634927#f99d28

Tabby Bee is a Colorless Event bee that hatches out of a Tabby Bee Egg, which is currently available in the Ticket Tent for 500 Tickets.

Like all other Event bees, this bee does not have a favorite treat, and the only way to make it gifted is by feeding it a Star Treat, Gingerbread Bears or Aged Gingerbread Bears.

Tabby Bee likes the Spider Field and Clover Field. It dislikes the Cactus Field.

docs.title: Stats
docs.text:
• Collects 10 Pollen in 4 seconds.
  • Makes 160 Honey in 3 seconds.
  • +40% Energy, +15% Movespeed, +25% Convert Speed, +3 Attack, up to +1680 Convert Amount, up to +100 Gather Amount.
  • 🌟 Gifted Hive Bonus: +50% Critical Power.

Unlike other bees, this bee has a unique perk: its stats increase permanently with the collection of Tabby Love tokens. At the cap of 1,000 Tabby Love, this bee's maximum stats are:

  • Collects 110 Pollen in 4 seconds.
  • Makes 1,760 Honey in 3 seconds.
  • Collects 88 Pollen from 3 lines of 4 flowers with Scratch (1,056 pollen).

• Scratch Collects 7 (+1 per lvl) Pollen from 3 lines of 4 Flowers. If Gifted, Scratch always does Critical hits.
  • Tabby Love Permanently grants Tabby Bee +1% Gather Amount, Convert Amount, and pollen from Scratch. Stacks up to 1,000 times.
  • If at max stacks, Tabby Love grants Tabby Blessing, giving +1% Critical Chance and +25% Critical Power for 20 seconds (+2s per level). If Gifted, it grants Tabby Blessing+, which adds +1% Super-Crit Chance as well.

docs.title: Stickers
docs.text:
Tabby Bee has no working sticker drop of its own.

Game bug: The Tabby Scratch sticker says it comes from collecting Tabby Love at max stacks while a Stinger is active, but nothing in the game gives it, so it can't be obtained.

Game bug: The Tabby From Behind sticker says it comes from feeding a Moon Charm at max Tabby Love, but the game never rolls stickers when you feed a bee, so this way doesn't work.

Like any bee, it can also find the stickers listed under Bee sticker drops.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• When Tabby Bee was added, the maximum Tabby Love stack was mistakenly set to 500. This mistake was fixed in a later update.
  • Tabby Bee cost 250 Tickets when it was originally released.
  • There used to be an Easter Egg behind the hives, which was a block with a distorted photo of Tabby Bee on it. It was removed around 2 June 2018. This was possibly a hint for one of the codes, more specifically, "Meow", which gave five tickets before it expired.
  • Tabby Bee is one of three bees to have an official plush on the Official Bee Swarm Simulator Website, the others being Basic Bee and Vicious Bee.
  • Because of a timer glitch that stopped players from buying it early, Tabby Bee returned on sale between June 2 and June 6, 2018.
  • Tabby Bee was the third Event bee to be added to the game, after Photon Bee and Bear Bee respectively.
  • This bee, Bear Bee, Gummy Bee, Puppy Bee, Festive Bee, Windy Bee, and Digital Bee are the only Event bees which can be a first edition bee when hatching them during its first release in-game.
  • Tabby Bee, Bear Bee, Gummy Bee, Festive Bee, Photon Bee, Tadpole Bee, and Vicious Bee are the only bees to have a gifted bonus that affects their signature ability.
  • The player's tabby love stack will not be removed if the player transforms Tabby Bee in any way.
  • Before the May 23, 2024 update, if the player already had max Tabby Love (x1000) and collected another one, it would neither increase the existing buff nor have any effect.
  • Tabby Bee is a reference to Onett's real-life cat named Sam. This is hinted in one of Onett's dialogues in his star journey quests, and later confirmed on Discord.
  • Tabby Bee, along with Basic Bee and Rascal Bee, are Onett's favorite bees.
  • Tabby Bee is mentioned in Panda Bear's dialogue during his Ultimate Ant Annihilation 1 quest. As Tabby Bee's description says, he states that Tabby Bee was raised by cats.
  • Tabby Bee is one of the few bees based off from animals other than just bees, the others being Lion Bee, Tadpole Bee, Puppy Bee, and Bear Bee.
  • Tabby Bee, despite having a 50% energy increase compared to Basic bee listed in its stats, has a base energy of 28, which is only comparable to a 40% energy increase.
  • Tabby Bee can have the highest conversion rate in the game at maximum Tabby Love.
  • This was one of the few bees that could have been summoned from Onett's Lid Art.
  • If a Tabby Bee from Onett's Lid Art produced a tabby love token, the buff would not be removed after the Tabby Bee despawns.

Tacky Planter "Grows in about 8hrs, but faster near the hives. Grants bonus Field Dice, Sunflower Seeds, and x1.25 Satisfying and Comforting Nectar." The Tacky Planter is a reusable planter added in 2021-12-26 update. Alone, it grows in about 8 hours and stores around 15 million pollen. When harvested, it grants bonus Field Dice and Sunflower Seeds. It can be purchased in Dapper Bear's Shop.

docs.title: Growth, pollen and nectar
docs.text:
• Grows in 8 hours of playtime alone, and grows faster here: x1.25 in Sunflower Field, x1.25 in Mushroom Field, x1.25 in Dandelion Field, x1.25 in Blue Flower Field, x1.25 in Clover Field. A flower-colour bonus is weighted by how much of the field is that colour.
  • Glitter used in its field speeds it up: x1.5 for one, rising in halving steps up to x2 at 6 stacks. The stacks stay on the planter until it is harvested.
  • Holds 15,000,000 pollen at full growth. A harvest gives capacity × growth × pollen bonus. Pollen bonus: x2 in Sunflower Field, x2 in Mushroom Field, x2 in Dandelion Field, x2 in Blue Flower Field, x2 in Clover Field.
  • Nectar multipliers: x1.25 Satisfying, x1.25 Comforting. On harvest it gives one Nectar type from its field, lasting grow time × growth × multiplier × 3 seconds.
  • Up to 3 bees can sip from it at once.

docs.title: Puffshrooms
docs.text:
When it reaches 95% growth, it has a 20% chance to smoke and spawn 3 Puffshrooms (one at the planter and two nearby) at level 5.

Rarity odds:

  • Common 70%
  • Rare 23.5%
  • Epic 6.3%
  • Legendary 0.2%

docs.title: Drops
docs.text: A full harvest gives 22 item tokens. Harvesting early gives fewer, in proportion to growth, but always at least 1. Tokens are filled in this order: guaranteed items (full harvests only), then field rules, then random picks from the pool below.

docs.title: Guaranteed
docs.text:
On every full harvest:

  • 1 Field Dice
  • 1 Ticket

docs.title: Field rules
docs.text:
• Full in the Pumpkin Patch: 1 Swirled Wax. Bamboo Field: 1 Caustic Wax. Mountain Top Field: 1 Loaded Dice. Each once every 30 days.
  • Full harvests in the Mushroom Field then the Blue Flower Field: 1 Purple Potion.
  • Full harvests in Clover, Coconut, Stump, Pepper, then Mountain Top, in order: the Dapper From Above sticker, once per account.

Tadpole Bee likes the Pine Tree Forest and Stump Field. It dislikes the Cactus Field.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Tadpole Bee, Lion Bee, Tabby Bee, Bear Bee, and Puppy Bee are the only bees to represent realistic animals.
  • The Tadpole Bee is the only Mythic bee that represents a realistic animal.
  • Tadpole Bee and Baby Bee are the only bees with the Baby Love ability.
  • Tadpole Bee and Baby Bee are also the only bees that appear smaller than the normal bee size.
  • Tadpole Bee and Windy Bee are the only bees with 2 gifted bonuses, excluding other Event Bees who enhance their ability.
  • Tadpole Bee, Vector Bee, Fuzzy Bee, Spicy Bee, Buoyant Bee and Digital Bee are the only bees with gifted exclusive abilities.
  • This bee and Spicy Bee are the only bees who can summon other entities.
  • This is the only bee that can summon a Mob.
  • Tadpole Bee and Bubble Bee are the only bees with the Gathering Bubbles passive ability.
  • Tadpole Bee, Fuzzy Bee, Spicy Bee, Buoyant Bee, and Digital Bee all have four different Abilities, the most for any bee.
  • Tadpole Bee used to be the only bee in the game that had a decimal base attack (0.5).
  • Tadpole Bee is the only Mythic bee that has its Gifted-exclusive ability token shared with another bee.
  • Along with Vector Bee and Spicy Bee, Tadpole Bee was one of the first Mythic Bees to be introduced to the game.
  • A Tadpole Bee Egg could be obtained by giving Bubble Bee Man a Present during the Beesmas 2020 event.
  • Tadpole Bee is the second mythic bee to have an egg of its own, the first being Fuzzy Bee.
  • Tadpole Bee is one of the 8 other bees with a unique trail.
  • Tadpole Bee is the blue counterpart of Spicy Bee.
  • Tadpole Bee and Fuzzy Bee are the only Mythics, when gifted, to not have any glowing parts.

docs.title: The Planter Of Plenty
docs.text:
The Planter Of Plenty "Grows in about 16 hours, but faster in late-game fields. Grants many bonus items and x1.5 of all Nectar." Stats Cost100T Honey500 Magic Beans100 Super Smoothies100 Swirled Wax100 Caustic Wax25 Turpentine ReusableYes Inventory cap- Shop limit1 Grow time16 hours Grows fasterx1.5 in Stump Field, x1.5 in Pepper Patch, x1.5 in Coconut Field, x1.5 in Mountain Top Field Pollen bonusNone (not working in game) Nectarx1.5 all Nectar Pollen capacity1,000,000,000,000 Item tokens60 Puffshroom chance33% Puffshroom level9 to 10 Guaranteed items5 Neonberry10 Ticket

The Planter Of Plenty is a reusable planter added in the 2021-12-26 update. Alone, it grows in about 16 hours and stores 1 trillion pollen. When harvested, it grants many bonus items, including Neonberries, Waxes and Turpentine. It can be purchased at the Dapper Bear's Shop.

docs.title: Growth, pollen and nectar
docs.text:
• Grows in 16 hours of playtime alone, and grows faster here: x1.5 in Stump Field, x1.5 in Pepper Patch, x1.5 in Coconut Field, x1.5 in Mountain Top Field. A flower-colour bonus is weighted by how much of the field is that colour.
  • Glitter used in its field speeds it up: x1.5 for one, rising in halving steps up to x2 at 6 stacks. The stacks stay on the planter until it is harvested.
  • Holds 1,000,000,000,000 pollen at full growth. A harvest gives capacity × growth × pollen bonus. It has no working pollen bonus (see the note below).
  • Nectar multipliers: x1.5 Satisfying, x1.5 Comforting, x1.5 Invigorating, x1.5 Motivating, x1.5 Refreshing. On harvest it gives one Nectar type from its field, lasting grow time × growth × multiplier × 3 seconds.
  • Up to 3 bees can sip from it at once. Gifted bees are x1.5 as likely to sip from it.

Note: The game data has a x1.333 pollen bonus for the Mountain Top Field, but it is stored under the wrong key, so the planter gives no pollen bonus. The shop text's "+50% pollen in late-game fields" does not apply; only the growth bonus works.

docs.title: Puffshrooms
docs.text:
When it reaches 95% growth, it has a 33% chance to smoke and spawn 3 Puffshrooms (one at the planter and two nearby) at levels 9 to 10.

Rarity odds:

  • Rare 67%
  • Epic 29%
  • Legendary 3.9%
  • Mythic 0.1%

docs.title: Drops
docs.text: A full harvest gives 60 item tokens. Harvesting early gives fewer, in proportion to growth, but always at least 1. Tokens are filled in this order: guaranteed items (full harvests only), then field rules, then random picks from the pool below.

docs.title: Guaranteed
docs.text:
On every full harvest:

  • 5 Neonberry
  • 10 Ticket

docs.title: Field rules
docs.text:
• Full in the Bamboo Field: 10 Super Smoothies, once every 30 days.
  • Each full harvest: 12% chance of 5 Swirled Wax (at most once every 30 days), and a 4% chance of 100 Neonberries.
  • Full in the Clover Field: 2% chance of the Hourglass sticker.

docs.title: The Supreme Saturator
docs.text:
The Supreme Saturator Requirement 10 Grandmaster Badges Cost 55,555,555,555 Honey Description The ultimate sprinkler. Nobody knows how it works or where it came from.

The Supreme Saturator is the highest tier sprinkler available for purchase in the Badge Bearer's Guild. To unlock it, the player must obtain 10 different Grandmaster badges. Once the player unlocks it, they can purchase it for ~55.5 billion Honey. Its description reads, “The ultimate sprinkler. Nobody knows how it works or where it came from."

The Supreme Saturator is a single sprinkler. Its radius extends to 16 flower tiles, its rate is 1 second, and its power is 10. This adds up to 8042 pollen per second, outperforming four Diamond Drenchers (1809 pollen per second) by over 340% (4.44x as effective).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The shape of The Supreme Saturator resembles the head of a bear.
  • The Supreme Saturator is currently the most expensive sprinkler in the game.

  • Before the 2021-12-26 update, The Supreme Saturator was the second most expensive item in terms of honey in the game (excluding hive slots), only behind the Gummy Boots.

  • SDMittens was the first player to buy The Supreme Saturator. She purchased it on September 19, 2018, and an in-game message appeared in every server in order to congratulate her on the achievement. The message said: "Wow! SDMittens has unleashed THE SUPREME SATURATOR on the mountain!"

  • This is the only sprinkler capable of completely covering a single field; those being:
  • The Stump Field.
  • Theoretically, it could also cover the Hub Field as well.

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Realistic max is the best you can expect to actually see: the most picks of that upgrade that about 1 in 1,000 fully waxed 5 ★ beequips get, each at its top value. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

docs.title: Ticket Planter
docs.text:
Ticket Planter "Grows in about 2 hours of playtime. Grants Tickets and spawns a Puffshroom!" Stats CostNot sold in shops ReusableNo Inventory cap100 Shop limit- Grow time2 hours Grows fasterNone Pollen bonusNone Nectarx2 all Nectar Pollen capacity50,000 Item tokens25 Puffshroom chance100% Puffshroom level1 to 2 Guaranteed items10 Ticket

A Ticket Planter is a single use planter added in the 2021-12-26 update. Alone, it grows in about 2 hours and stores 50,000 pollen. When harvested, it grants bonus Tickets. A player can store up to 100 Ticket Planters at a time, and up to 3 planters can be planted at once.

docs.title: Growth, pollen and nectar
docs.text:
• Grows in 2 hours of playtime.
  • Glitter used in its field speeds it up: x1.5 for one, rising in halving steps up to x2 at 6 stacks. The stacks stay on the planter until it is harvested.
  • Holds 50,000 pollen at full growth. A harvest gives capacity × growth × pollen bonus. It has no pollen bonus.
  • Nectar multipliers: x2 Satisfying, x2 Comforting, x2 Invigorating, x2 Motivating, x2 Refreshing. On harvest it gives one Nectar type from its field, lasting grow time × growth × multiplier × 3 seconds.
  • Up to 3 bees can sip from it at once.

docs.title: Puffshrooms
docs.text:
When it reaches 95% growth, it always smoke and spawn 3 Puffshrooms (one at the planter and two nearby) at levels 1 to 2.

They are always Common.

docs.title: Drops
docs.text: A full harvest gives 25 item tokens. Harvesting early gives fewer, in proportion to growth, but always at least 1. Tokens are filled in this order: guaranteed items (full harvests only), then field rules, then random picks from the pool below.

docs.title: Guaranteed
docs.text:
On every full harvest:

  • 10 Ticket

docs.text:
"Chance per token" is the chance that one random token is that item, before any field extras.

docs.title: Ways to obtain
docs.text:
• Dapper Bear gives 3 Ticket Planters if the player speaks to him for the first time.
  • As a reward from certain quests:
  • If the player completes Dapper Bear's quests and they already got Beequip slots from Bee Bear in previous years, they get a Ticket Planter for each Beequip slot.
  • Bee Bear's "Searching For Snowflakes" quest rewards 1 Ticket Planter and other items.
  • As a rare drop from Sticker Sprouts.
  • As a Stack Reward for adding certain stickers to the Sticker Stack:
  • Dapper From Above Sticker rewards 1 Ticket Planter.
  • Ticket Voucher rewards 1 Ticket Planter
  • Buying the Tempting Ticket Pack from Bee Bear's Catalog for 55,555 Snowflakes gives 5 Ticket Planters and other items.
  • As a drop from Dapper Bear's Samovar after every 5th use (except for the 25th, which drops a turpentine instead).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This is one of the two planters that is guaranteed to spawn a Puffshroom. The other is the Sticker Planter.
  • This, the Sticker Planter and the Paper Planter share the same base model.
  • They also share the same outline for their decals.
  • It is one of two planters that mentions an in-game item in its name, the other planter is the Sticker Planter.
  • It gives the second-best nectar multiplier in the game, 2x, behind the Festive Planter with 3x.
  • It is one of 4 single-use planters, the others being the Paper Planter, the Festive Planter and the Sticker Planter.
  • This, the Sticker Planter and the Paper Planter are the only one-use planters in the game that can be obtained infinitely.

docs.title: Ticket Shop
docs.text:
This piece of content contains information obtained through datamining.

Due to the nature of the information, details may be inaccurate or outdated.

Datamined information: The formula for calculating the cost of buying a ticket. — March 18th, 2026

Ticket Shop Location Outside the Mountain Top Shop

This page is for the shop that sells tickets. For the shop that sells items for tickets, see the Ticket Tent page.

The Ticket Shop is a shop located outside the Mountain Top Shop to the right of the Field Booster. It sells Tickets for Honey in increments of 1, 10, 100, and 500 tickets. It has a similar appearance to other shops like the Basic Egg Shop, Royal Jelly Shop, Stinger Shop and the Treat Shop, but has a ticket on top, along with its icon on the front and sides. The shop also contains a black semicircle with a grey separator as the vending mechanism, which seems to make it a rotary dispenser.

The price to buy a ticket goes up with the number of tickets the player has bought. The player can buy at most 100,000 tickets from the shop.

To calculate the price of the next ticket, the below formula can be used, where:

  • \(P(n)=\) the price of the nth ticket the player has bought from the shop;
  • \(n=\) the number of tickets the player has already bought \(P(n)={\begin{cases}100{,}000+1000n^{1.2},&{\text{for }}0\leq n<500\\100{,}000+1000n^{1.7},&{\text{for }}500\leq n\leq 50{,}000\\100{,}000{,}000{,}000+10{,}000{,}000(n-50{,}000)^{1.85},&{\text{for }}n>50{,}000\end{cases}}\)

Alternatively, if less than 50,000 tickets have been bought, this linked spreadsheet can be used to calculate the cost of a number of increments of tickets.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Before the 2018-11-25 update, the cost formula was \(S=n[5000(n-1)+X]\), where \(n\) is the amount being bought and \(X\) is the current ticket price.
  • The maximum number of tickets a player can buy from the shop was increased from 50,000 to the current 100,000 in an unknown update.

docs.title: Ticket Tent
docs.text:
Ticket Tent Location Behind the Red Cannon

This page is for the shop that sells items for tickets. For the shop that sells tickets, see the Ticket Shop page.

The Ticket Tent is a shop located behind the Red Cannon and near the Hives. It sells six types of Event Bees, Silver Eggs, Gold Eggs, Diamond Eggs, Mythic Eggs, and Star Treats. They can only be purchased with Tickets, hence its name. There is also a Royal Jelly token on top of the Ticket Tent.

docs.title: Eggs
docs.text: Item  Tickets Description  Silver Egg 50  Usually hatches into a Rare Bee (64.9% chance). May be Epic (30%), Legendary (5%), or Mythic (0.1%).  Gold Egg 100 (Originally 50)  Usually hatches into an Epic Bee (79% chance). May be Legendary (20%) or Mythic (1%).  Diamond Egg 400  Usually hatches into a Legendary Bee (95% chance). Has a 5% chance to be Mythic.  Mythic Egg 2500  Always hatches into a Mythic Bee!

docs.title: Bees
docs.text: Item  Tickets Description  Puppy Bee Egg 500 (Originally 250)  This bee loves to play! Throw it's [sic] tennis ball around to collect pollen! Keep the ball going to win Treats!  Photon Bee Egg 500  An entity made of pure light! Fires beams from the sky to collect massive amounts of pollen at once.  Tabby Bee Egg 500 (Originally 250)  An affectionate bee who becomes a harder worker as it warms up to you.  Festive Bee Egg 500  A generous bee who hands out random gifts to every player on your server!  Crimson Bee Egg 250  Defender of all things Red! Excels in hives with many Red Bees. Has enhanced abilities when working with Cobalt Bee.  Cobalt Bee Egg 250  Defender of all things Blue! Excels in hives with many Blue Bees. Has enhanced abilities when working with Crimson Bee.

docs.text: Item  Tickets Description  Star Treat 1000  Turns a bee into a Gifted Bee! Gifted Bees have many perks, including increased stats and bonuses for your entire swarm.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The only bee in this shop that could be obtained without tickets (for a limited time) was Festive Bee.
  • This used to also apply to Gummy Bee, which is now permanently available for 2500 gumdrops.
  • The Royal Jelly token on top of the Ticket Tent was mentioned by Sun Bear in his dialogue.
  • Buying a star treat from here is one of the only ways to obtain star treats without Robux.
  • Before the 2019-04-05 update, if the player had the Goo Hotshot Badge, they could go up to the Gummy Bee on top of the tent and use gumdrops to enter Gummy Bear's Lair. However, this mechanic was moved to the Gummy Bee Claimer when it was added.
  • The wings on the gifted Photon Bee's model are not transparent, while the giant Festive Bee and Puppy Bees' wings are.
  • Additionally, the wings of the Festive Bee model aren't solid, while the wings of the Puppy Bee and Gifted Photon Bee models are.
  • The Photon Bee is also the only model that is in gifted form.
  • When the Ticket Tent was implemented, the most expensive item was the star treat, costing 1,000 tickets. However, after the Beesmas 2019 event ended, the most expensive item was the Cub Buddy, costing 2,000 tickets. After the 2024-05-23 update, Mythic Eggs now cost the most, at 2,500 tickets.
  • Like the Noob Shop or Pro Shop, Spotted chicks could spawn here during the Egg Hunt 2020 event.
  • Cub Buddies used to be sold in this shop for 2,000 Tickets, but after the 2024-05-23 update, this is no longer the case.
  • It is possible to see the back of the Ticket Tent by going out of bounds behind the Coconut Field.

docs.title: Ticket
docs.text:
Ticket

"Used to activate and purchase special things!"

Tickets are a form of currency added in the 2018-04-27 update. They can be used to purchase certain items.

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
The Ticket Shop.

  • The player can obtain Tickets as a reward for acquiring badges. Collecting badges gives:
  • 5 Tickets for earning Cadet badges.
  • 10 Tickets for earning Hotshot badges.
  • 15 Tickets for earning Ace badges.
  • 25 Tickets for earning Master badges.
  • 40 Tickets for earning Grandmaster badges.
  • In total, 2,375 Tickets can be obtained from Badges. (2,335 Tickets if not counting the currently impossible Sticker Stack Grandmaster Badge.)
  • The player can buy Tickets from the Ticket Shop with Honey, located outside the Mountain Top Shop. The price increases with every Ticket bought.
  • Some bears give Tickets as rewards for completing certain quests.
  • Redeeming certain valid codes:
  • 38217 (Gives 5 Tickets).
  • Bopmaster (Gives 5 Tickets).
  • Crawlers (Gives 5 Tickets).
  • Roof (Gives 5 Tickets).
  • Connoisseur (Gives 5 Tickets).
  • Wax (Gives 5 Tickets + other items).
  • Buying them from the Robux Shop for Robux:
  • 1 Ticket for 10 Robux ( 10 Robux per Ticket).
  • 100 Tickets for 400 Robux ( 4 Robux per Ticket).
  • 510 Tickets for 1,700 Robux ( 3.33 Robux per Ticket).
  • 1,800 Tickets for 4,500 Robux ( 2.5 Robux per Ticket).
  • The Wealth Clock gives Tickets every hour after interacting with it, and increases incrementally every hour, stopping at the fifth (1 ticket first time, 2 second time, 3 third time, 4 fourth time, and 5 fifth time and onwards).
  • They can spawn as a potential match from Normal, Mega, Night and Extreme Memory Matches.
  • Clicking on any Hidden Sticker grants 1 Ticket each (excluding seeker-stickers).
  • Adding certain Stickers to the Sticker Stack grants Tickets.
  • As a Reward for being in the top 100 of any daily leaderboard, ranging from 25, 50 to 100 Tickets depending on the leaderboard.
  • Redeeming a Ticket Voucher grants 100 Tickets.
  • 1,000 Tickets will be given if you already have a Digital Bee after purchasing the Robo Bear's Shop's Digital Bee deal.

docs.title: Drops
docs.text:
• As a drop from planters:
  • The number of Tickets it can potentially drop depends on the type of planter.
  • Ticket Planters always drop 10+ Tickets when harvested at full growth.
  • As a common drop from Mythic Meteors.
  • As a drop from Stockings.
  • There is a chance of getting a Ticket as a reward for defeating mobs. The probability depends on the type of mob as well as the player's Loot Luck.
  • Tunnel Bear, Stump Snail, and King Beetle are guaranteed to grant Tickets upon defeat.
  • Wild Windy Bee will yield a limited amount of Tickets per day.
  • The Commando Chick will always drop 1 Ticket upon being captured.

  • Capturing it for the 25th time rewards 100 Tickets.

  • Defeating Snowbear will drop an amount of Tickets equal its level upon defeat.

  • Completing a Robo Party will reward an amount of Tickets equal to the party's rank.
  • Through a Cub Buddy gift.
  • Puffshrooms drop Tickets (the rarer the Puffshroom, the more it gives).
  • Honeystorms are guaranteed to spawn Ticket tokens.
  • As a rare drop from Festive Gifts.
  • As a Sprout reward, besides Moon and Debug variants (the rarer the sprout, the more Tickets it will yield; rare sprouts and above guarantee Tickets).
  • Sparkles may yield Tickets.
  • Very rarely, flowers may generate a Ticket token. The base probability is around 1/1000 (0.1%), however it does increase with Loot Luck and Ticket Chance.

docs.title: Token Locations
docs.text:
• On top of the biggest pineapple in the Pineapple Patch. Grants 3 Tickets.
  • At the back of the cave that the spider comes from. Grants 1 Ticket.
  • In the back of Red HQ, near the ceiling (the best way to get it seems to be to get x5 Haste, climb on top of the teleporter, jump up and walk on the edge of the leaderboard, and then glide to the Ticket. The enhanced jump ability granted by certain hats, boots, and/or the bear morph will also help).
  • Next to the Glider inside the Mountain Top Shop.
  • On a platform in the Cloud Obby, fairly high above the Pine Tree Forest and Pumpkin Patch. Grants 5 Tickets. (Jump off the tip of the red shoulder guard of the 30 Bee Gate, then glide or parachute down to it).
  • On a small ledge between the Lion Bee Gate and the Brave Bee Gate. Grants 5 Tickets. The player must use the slingshot and move to the left. Parachute at the right moment to land on the rock. Alternative: Jump down from in front of the Lion Bee Gate. A Parachute/Glider can be helpful, but not absolutely necessary.
  • Behind the red shoulder guard of the Bear Gate (i.e. inside the 30 Bee Area). Grants 10 Tickets.
  • On the awning over Mother Bear's area. (Easily reached from the ramp that leads to the Honey Bee Gate). Grants 1 Ticket.
  • On top of the Ant Gate. Grants 5 Tickets. (Reachable by jumping on top of the Stinger Shop, then crossing to the ledge.
  • Behind the Honey Dispenser in the Lava Obby. Upon entering, immediately turn right, and jump up onto the ledge. Grants 3 Tickets. This replaced one of the Plastic Egg locations.
  • Underneath the Basic Bee Gate ramp, where Honey Bee used to be. Grants 3 Tickets. This replaced one of the Plastic Egg locations, when they were removed.
  • In the Blue Maze, turn left and then take the first right. Grants 5 Tickets. This replaced one of the Plastic Egg locations.
  • Inside the tunnel behind the Coconut Dispenser in the Coconut Cave. Grants 5 Tickets.

docs.title: Uses
docs.text:
The Ticket Tent.

  • Buying a Royal Jelly From the Royal Jelly Dispenser for 6 Tickets with a cooldown of 3 seconds.
  • Buying Gumdrops from the Gumdrop Shop at the cost of 1 Ticket per 3 Gumdrops.
  • Buying Stingers from the Stinger Shop at the cost of 10 Tickets per Stinger.
  • Buying Magic Beans from the Magic Bean Shop at the cost of 20 Tickets per Magic Bean.
  • 1 Ticket is required to use an Instant Converter.
  • 10 Tickets are required to use the Ant Pass Dispenser.
  • The Ticket Tent has the following items available:
  • Silver Egg (50 Tickets).
  • Gold Egg (100 Tickets).
  • Diamond Egg (400 Tickets).
  • Mythic Egg (2,500 Tickets).
  • Cobalt Bee Egg and Crimson Bee Egg (250 Tickets each, one time purchase).
  • Miscellaneous Event Bees (500 Tickets each, one time purchase).
  • Star Treat (1,000 Tickets).
  • 50 Tickets are required to start another Stick Bug Challenge when the player's free challenge is already used.
  • Tickets can be used to speed up materials that are currently being made in the Blender.
  • 5 Tickets are required to store nectar in the Nectar Pot.
  • 50 Tickets are required to use the Robo Pass Dispenser.
  • Varying amounts of Tickets can be used to increase the maximum amount of Beequips one can hold in their Beequip Storage, requiring 123,500 Tickets in total to max it out.
  • Varying amounts of Tickets (Starting at 20 and capping at 1,000 per upgrade) can be used to increase the maximum amount of Stickers one can hold in their Sticker Storage, requiring 42,420 Tickets in total to max it out.
  • Tickets, along with Honey, are used to purchase Beequips in Dapper Bear's Shop.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• It bears the face of a Basic Bee.
  • Currently, the most expensive purchase that can be made using Tickets is the final slot upgrade for the Beequip Storage, costing 20,000 Tickets to increase storage from a maximum of 95 stored Beequips to 100 stored Beequips.
  • Tickets, along with Honey, were used to purchase Market Boosts from the Boost Market.
  • You need a total of 179,420 Tickets in total to Max out Sticker and Beequip storages, buy all event bees from the Ticket Tent and gift all of the event bees with Star Treat.

docs.title: Tide Popper
docs.text:
This piece of content contains information obtained through datamining.

Due to the nature of the information, details may be inaccurate or outdated.

Datamined information: How much pollen Tide Popper collects on its own. — December 19th, 2024

Tide Popper Overview Price (Needs to have 250 Gifted Bucko Bee quests completed) 1,500 Blue Extracts, 150 Stingers, 150 Tropical Drinks, 75 Swirled Waxes, 50 Super Smoothies, 3 Comforting Vials, 2.5T Honey Shop Blue HQ Pollen Collection Range 22 Flowers Collecting Pattern Spike collectedyou (facing up) Collecting Time 1 second Base Collection 5 Flowers Single Double Triple Large Star White 6 12 18 24 30 Red 5 10 15 20 25 Blue 12.5 25 37.5 50 62.5 Special Multiplier(s): x1.25 Blue Pollen

The Tide Popper is a tool that can be crafted in the Blue HQ. The player needs to have completed at least 250 Gifted Bucko Bee quests to unlock it.

Crafting Ingredients 2.5T Honey

1,500 Blue Extracts 150 Stingers 150 Tropical Drinks 75 Swirled Waxes 50 Super Smoothies 3 Comforting Vials

Every 3rd swing releases a wave of water that collects pollen, pops bubbles, and converts pollen when a bee is hit by the wave.

When a bubble from the player is popped by any means, it grants a stack of "Tide Power" (2 stacks if it was a golden bubble), which grants faster tool swinging speed and stronger waves. Higher stacks grants a stronger buff.

When Tide Power reaches 495 stacks or greater, each swing of the tool will release a large wave. When Tide Power reaches 500 stacks, it is replaced with "Tidal Surge". It lasts for 10 seconds and grants x2.5 to x1.5 tool swinging speed (starting at x2.5 and gradually decreasing until it reaches x1.5), and every swing releases a large tidal wave. Popping a bubble during a Tidal Surge extends the duration of it.

Activating a Tidal Surge grants 1 minute of "Tide Blessing". Whenever a tidal wave hits a Balloon of the player's, it causes the balloon to convert up to 8% of your Convert Total into Honey Tokens worth x2.5 that (these tokens can not be collected by token link) and if the balloon is golden, grants 10 seconds of Tide Blessing. Tide Blessing stacks up to 4 hours, and grants up to x1.2 Blue Pollen, Honey From Tokens, Convert Rate at Hive, Pollen from Bees, and Tool Pollen.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Tide Popper was originally called the "Aqua Popper".
  • Its red counterpart is the Dark Scythe, which is sold in the Red HQ, and its white counterpart is the Gummyballer, which is sold in Gummy Bear's Lair.
  • If a wave is as high as a balloon, it can make the balloon convert pollen without Tidal Surge.
  • There is currently a glitch that makes the player holding the Tide Popper have black trails.
  • This is tied with the Dark Scythe for being the fifth most expensive item in the game, both having a cost of 2.5T Honey. In front of the Tide Popper and Dark Scythe is the Petal Planter, costing 5T Honey, Coconut Belt costing 7.5T Honey, the Gummyballer, costing 10T Honey, and The Planter Of Plenty, costing 100T Honey.
  • The Tide Popper's raw ingredients cost:
  • 2.5T Honey
  • 603,750 Blueberries
  • 528,750 Strawberries
  • 112,500 Sunflower Seeds
  • 641,250 Pineapples
  • 7,425 Bitterberries
  • 1,950 Neonberries
  • 6,750 Honeysuckles
  • 4,500 Coconuts
  • 417,900 Royal Jellies or 418B Honey
  • 450 Magic Beans or 9,000 Tickets
  • 150 Stingers or 1,500 Tickets
  • 3 Comforting Vials or 36 hours of Comforting Nectar
  • On December 28, 2021, the Tide Popper was obtainable through an exploit that was able to give you the Tide Popper, the same going for the Gummyballer and Dark Scythe. This was later patched by Onett and everybody who used the exploit would get a full reset on their account.
  • On 2022-01-01, there was a glitch where if the Tide Popper was viewed in the shop, it would cause the game to freeze and not let the player exit.
  • There was a glitch allowing players to buy the Tide Popper without completing 250 Gifted Bucko Bee quests. If the Tide Popper was bought without doing 250 Gifted Bucko Bee quests, the item could be equipped after doing 250 Gifted Bucko Bee quests. This was also the case with the Dark Scythe.
  • After the 2024-05-23 update, the Tide Popper needs 3 Comforting Vials and 150 Stingers, more than the previous 0 and less than the previous 200 (respectively) before.
  • The Tide Popper, alongside the Dark Scythe and Gummyballer are the only items without an in-game description which details stats.
  • The Tide Popper, as well as any other item that costed more than 1 billion Honey, used to display the honey cost as the full number, rather than shortening it.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Tools are items that can gather pollen. Some tools have special abilities that help assist in gathering pollen, while some collect better from certain colored flowers, which include white, red, and blue. All tools can be boosted through the Tool Pollen stat. The newest tool in the game is the Honey Hammer. There are currently twenty-one tools in the game.

Every player starts out with the Scooper. Better tools can be bought from different shops. The Noob Shop sells the cheapest tools, ranging from 0 - 14 thousand honey. The Pro Shop follows with tools ranging from 40 thousand - 1.5 million honey, while the Red HQ and Blue HQ both have 2 tools each that can range from 3.5 million honey - 2.5 trillion honey. The Mountain Top Shop has the fourth most expensive tools, with prices that range from 20 million - 150 million honey. The Petal Shop has the third most expensive tool at 1.5 billion honey. Currently, the most expensive tool in the game is the Gummyballer, which can be bought for 10 trillion honey and other various crafting materials in the Gummy Bear's Lair. Unlike any other tool, the Gummyballer can directly take goo off a field. The best tool, the Honey Hammer, can't be bought at all: it is the reward for finishing the Melittology tree.

The player can auto-click their pollen collector by holding down the mouse button on a computer. On a mobile device, holding on an open part of the screen does the same. Using Glue gives a 10-minute boost that grants x1.25 Tool Pollen and bees. Using a Purple Potion can also give x1.25 Capacity, x1.25 Convert Rate At Hive, x1.5 Red Pollen, x1.5 Blue Pollen, x1.3 Bee Gather Pollen, and x1.3 Tool Pollen for 15 minutes. There is also a glitch for computer in which holding down click then Ctrl + Esc or Alt + tab automatically uses your tool, but clicking the screen removes it. This can also be achieved by moving the mouse outside of the boundaries in windowed mode, but it can only be done on the launcher version of the app.

Twenty-one tools are currently available in the game: Scooper Rake Clippers Magnet Vacuum Super-Scooper Pulsar Electro-Magnet Scissors Honey Dipper Bubble Wand Scythe Sticker-Seeker Golden Rake Spark Staff Porcelain Dipper Petal Wand Tide Popper Dark Scythe Gummyballer Honey Hammer

Top Bear is a bear who runs the Mountain Top Shop. Like other Shop Bears, Top Bear's presence is not required to make any purchases in the shop.

Top Bear's appearance is yellow skin, white shirt, green pants, and a smiley face. Top Bear is similar to Noob Bear and Pro Bear, as the only difference between them is the colors of their clothing.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Top Bear is the only NPC in the 25 Bee Zone.
  • This bear is one of the six bears without any function quest-wise, the other five being Noob Bear, Pro Bear, Shadow Bear, Tunnel Bear and the Snowbear.
  • This bear, Noob Bear, Pro Bear, and Shadow Bear are the only bears without a function whatsoever.
  • Unlike the other Shop Bears, Top Bear was introduced in 2018-07-11 update, whereas the other two Shop Bears were already present when the game was released. This means that the Mountain Top Shop was once not run by any bears.
  • Before the 2019-09-28 update, players were able to cause a Rogue Vicious Bee to damage or even kill Top Bear if they stood near him. This was later patched in said update, where the bear was given infinite health.

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Realistic max is the best you can expect to actually see: the most picks of that upgrade that about 1 in 1,000 fully waxed 5 ★ beequips get, each at its top value. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

docs.title: Trading
docs.text:
Trading is a mechanic added in the 2024-01-12 update, which allows players to trade Beequips, Cub Buddy Skins and stickers.

Players may request a trade from another player using the trade request menu, accessible in the settings menu, or by accepting the prompt shown when walking over the requested player's hive. If the requested player accepts the trade, a new menu will pop up, where both players can add or remove an item by interacting with the button in the top left corner of the item. When ready, both players select the accept button before waiting for a length of time dependant on the total value of the trade. Once the time is over, the trade menu closes, and both players receive their items and get taken to the items' stats. If one of the players instead decides to cancel the trade, both players keep their items, and the trade menu closes before a popup appears telling both players that the trade has been cancelled.

Trading can be done an unlimited number of times to an unlimited number of players, but the player may not trade with multiple players at a time. The requested player has to accept or decline a trade request before it is possible to request a trade from them again. It is possible to disable trade requests by going into the settings menu and disabling "Allow trade requests".

A player can be ineligible to receive trade requests for either not having unlocked trading yet or having their trade requests disabled. The requirements for unlocking trading are:

  • 20 Bees
  • Playtime Cadet Badge (8 hours of playtime)
  • Ability Cadet Badge (2500 Ability Tokens)
  • Battle Hotshot Badge (1000 Battle Points)

If a player is unable to receive trading requests, the requester will receive one of two messages depending on which reason it is:

  • If they don't have trading unlocked:

{Player} has not unlocked trading (Requires Playtime Cadet, Ability Cadet, and Battle Hotshot Badges)

  • If they have trading requests disabled:

{Player} has disabled trading

There are also many other notifications that can pop up, which can be viewed below.

Onett may decide to disable trading for any number of reasons for a period of time. During this period, no player can request a trade or use the Public Sticker Board. This has been observed a number of times:

  • Trading was disabled for short periods to fix bugs when it was first introduced, on January 13 and January 16, 2024.
  • The first long period started on September 26, 2025, and was fully re-enabled on December 28, 2025, lasting 93 days.
  • Trading was already re-enabled on December 17, 2025, but only in the Hive Hub and players could not trade Cub Buddy Skins at the time. The restriction on Cub Buddy Skins was lifted on December 19, 2025 but was reverted almost immediately.
  • The second long period started on July 20, 2026, and ended on August 13, 2026, lasting 24 days.

Onett may also decide to restrict trading items that were created or traded during a period of time. This has been observed once, restricting items created or traded between July 15, 2026 and July 31, 2026.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Beware of scams involving trust trades or cross trades. Make sure that the items traded are of similar value before accepting the trade.
  • Make fair and cancel unfair trades. If you make an unfair trade, or if the other player makes an unfair trade, it is likely that the trade will be cancelled, and you should cancel an unfair trade.
  • Use the item inspector. You should use the item inspector to your advantage to make sure the item's balanced (if you are also a collector) also take the item's rarity into consideration. The item inspector is a must in ensuring that Beequips have the stats that you are looking for.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The item inspector in the trading menu is the only official way to see the methods of obtainment for the Play Button and Gamer Chat Icon stickers, as they do not appear in the Sticker Index.

docs.title: Translator
docs.text:
Translator

"A device used to decipher languages you don't understand."

COOLDOWN

N/A

Translators are inventory items that allow the user to speak with Gifted Riley Bee, Gifted Bucko Bee, and Stick Bug.

To use a translator, the player needs to talk to the NPC they want to use the translator on. The NPC will talk to the player in its language. It will then prompt the player the option to give the translator to the NPC or leave. Clicking on the option to give the NPC the translator will allow the player to talk and receive quests from the NPC.

Translators are single-use - once the player gives an NPC a translator, the translator will be taken away from their inventory, but the player will be able to speak with them forever. If the player accidentally uses a translator on an NPC, they can leave the game as the translator only gets taken away after the player finishes speaking to that NPC.

All three translators can only be obtained from Science Bear. He rewards the player with a translator after completing the following quests: "Limits of Language", "Beesperanto", and "Epistemological Endeavor" (which are the 21st, 26th and 31st quests).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The player can acquire a total of three translators throughout the game so that they can speak to all three of the NPCs that require them.
  • Without translators, it is impossible to take quests, receive rewards, talk or give presents to Gifted Bucko Bee, Stick Bug, and Gifted Riley Bee.
  • Translators were originally implemented in the 2018-11-25 update when Science Bear received an additional 10 quests. Only two were available at that time, as the third could only be obtained in Epistemological Endeavor, which is Science Bear's last quest. His last 5 quests weren't added until 2018-12-19, thus making the total amount of translators available 2 at the time.
  • There is a 5 quest difference between each translator, Limits of Language being the 21st quest, Beesperanto being the 26th, and Epistemological Endeavor being the 31st.
  • This is one of the two unique items that can only be obtained while completing a bear’s questline, the other being Spirit Petals from Spirit Bear.
  • This is one of the only items that can be given to an NPC, the other item being Presents.
  • Trying to give Gifted Riley, Gifted Bucko, or Stick Bug a present without giving it a translator will result in the regular dialogue being displayed.

This piece of content contains information obtained through datamining.

Due to the nature of the information, details may be inaccurate or outdated.

Datamined information: The formula for the amount of Honey and Treats received based on the number of bees in the player's hive. The table was made using in-game tests. — February 26th, 2026

Treat Dispenser Information Usage Gives Honey, Treats, Pineapples and Haste Requirement(s) None Cooldown 1 hour Location Next to the Pro Shop

The Treat Dispenser is a dispenser located between the Pineapple Patch and the entrance of the Pro Shop. Any player can use it to collect Honey, Treats, 1 Pineapple, and x5 Haste every hour. The number of Treats varies, depending on the number of bees the player has.

docs.title: Honey and Treats reward amounts
docs.text:
The amount of honey and treats given is based on the number of bees the player has in their hive. More specifically, let cnt be the number of bees in the player's hive:

  • The amount of honey the player receives is equal to \(\left\lfloor {cnt}^{1.5}+0.5\right\rfloor \times 50\), or 500 if the result is less than 500.
  • The amount of treats the player receives is equal to \(\left\lfloor {\frac {{cnt}^{2.5}}{100}}+0.5\right\rfloor\), or 10 if the result is less than 10.

docs.title: Treat
docs.text:
Treat

"Increases your bond with a bee by 10."

A Treat is a type of treat that can be fed to a bee to raise its bond by 10. They are the easiest treat to obtain but are not the favorite treat of any bee. They can also be used to craft the Honey Mask where 9,999 treats are needed.

A treat token.

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• Using the Treat Dispenser near the Pro Shop/Pineapple Patch (Like the Honey Dispenser, this requires being a member of the BSS Club).
  • Buying from the Treat Shop next to under Mother Bear's awning for 100 Honey per treat and capping out at 10,000 Honey per treat.
  • As a reward from memory matches.
  • As a stack reward for adding certain stickers to the Sticker Stack:
  • The Fork And Knife rewards 500 treats.

docs.title: Drops
docs.text:
• Farming in the Dandelion, Mushroom, Clover, Spider, Cactus, Pumpkin, Coconut, or Stump Fields.
  • Drops from leaves in these fields may also yield treats.
  • A relatively high chance of dropping from rhino beetles, ladybugs, spiders, mantises, scorpions, werewolves, aphids, Stick Bug, Stick Nymphs, Tunnel Bear, King Beetle, and stump snail.
  • A guaranteed drop from Mondo Chicks.
  • 2nd and 3rd capture of Commando Chick rewards 2 and 5 treats respectively.
  • "Playing" Fetch with Puppy Bee.
  • As a drop from a Festive Gift or Festive Mark.
  • As a gift from a cub buddy.
  • As a reward for completely growing any kind of sprout except for Gummy and Debug sprouts.
  • Harvesting sparkles.
  • As a drop from Puffshrooms.
  • As a drop from Planters, which include:
  • Plastic Planters
  • Candy Planters
  • Red Clay Planters
  • Tacky Planters
  • Activating certain targets grants a small amount of treats.
  • Using Polar Bear's Beesmas Feast during Beesmas will give treats and other items.

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• Black Bear gives treats on the following quests:
  • Get Red-y gives 100 treats.
  • One Stop On The Tip Top gives 200 treats.
  • Blue Mushrooms 2 gives 300 treats.
  • Pretty Pumpkins gives 400 treats.
  • Black Bear, Why? gives 500 treats.
  • Bee A Star gives 1,000 treats.
  • The Mythic Egg questline gives treats on all quests, at a sum of 195,500 treats.
  • Black Bear's repeatable quests also reward treats.
  • Science Bear gives treats on the following quests:
  • Mark Mechanics gives 3,000 treats.
  • Epistemological Endeavor gives 10,000 treats.
  • All of Mother Bear's quests give treats, 4,020 treats in total.
  • All of Polar Bear's quests give 10 treats.
  • All of Onett's quests give treats, 25,000 treats in total.
  • Every 5th completion of Honey Bee's quest may give treats.

docs.title: Treats
docs.text:
Treats are items which grant bond to bees. There are currently twelve different types of treats.

To feed treats to their bees, players must go to their hive and open their item menu. The player must then drag the treat from the menu and to the cell of the bee to be fed, and then either type in the number of treats to feed that bee, use all of the selected treats or if possible, feed the number of treats needed to level up the bee. If the player is feeding a bee their favorite treat, gingerbread bears, or aged gingerbread bears, there is an "Until Gifted" option that automatically rolls until the bee becomes gifted, similar to using auto-jelly. The player cannot feed other player's bees.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• A singular star treat or atomic treat gives the most bond (1,000 bond), followed by a single neonberry and aged gingerbread bear (500 bond), then gingerbread bears and moon charms (250 bond).
  • Before the 2019-04-05 update, when asked to feed strawberries or blueberries to a bee, the plural was incorrectly spelled as "Strawberrys" and "Blueberry" instead of "Strawberries" and "Blueberries."
  • However, when using fruit to craft gumdrops, for example, it is still spelled as "Blueberrys" and "Strawberrys."
  • Despite being mentioned by Spirit Bear as once being a Blueberry Field, the Blue Flower Field doesn't seem to yield more blueberries than other blue fields.
  • Treats, pineapples, strawberries, and blueberries are the only treats that can be obtained from dispensers.
  • There is a glitch in which dragging an item that is not a treat (ex: magic bean, gumdrops) to the bee causes the hive slot to turn red.
  • Onett has said that bees don't actually eat the treats, instead, they take them as gifts and hide them in fields for others to find, though Mother Bear says to feed a treat to a bee in her first quest.
  • Before the 2018-11-25 update, moon charm tokens from fireflies didn't glow.
  • Before Beesmas 2019 ended, star treats were the most expensive item in the Ticket Tent, at the price of 1,000 tickets. Since then, the cub buddy went on sale for 2,000 tickets. docs.title: Tropical Drink
docs.text:
Tropical Drink

"Grants x1.25 White Pollen, +10% Instant Conversion and +5% Critical Chance for 10 minutes."

COOLDOWN

10 minutes

Tropical Drink is a craftable inventory item added in the 2019-09-28 update. When used, it grants following buffs for 10 minutes:

  • x1.25 White Pollen
  • +5% Critical Chance
  • +10% Instant Conversion

It can also be used as a material to craft certain items. Using a Super Smoothie will override the buff.

docs.text:
• Crafting it via Blender for:
  • 10 Coconuts
  • 2 Enzymes
  • 2 Oils

  • Black Bear's "Boss Battles" quest rewards 3 Tropical Drinks.
    • Black Bear has a chance to reward Tropical Drinks after the completion of the "Black Bear: Triple Treck" quest in his repeatable questline.
  • As a drop from sprouts in the Coconut Field (the odds increase depending on the rarity of the sprout).
  • Matching a pair of Tropical Drink in Extreme Memory Match or Mega Memory Match or Winter Memory Match.

docs.title: Tunnel Bear
docs.text:
Tunnel Bear Location White Tunnel Respawns Every 48 hours (2 days), 40 hours 48 minutes (1.7 days) if Gifted Vicious Bee is in the player's hive.

Not to be confused with Shadow Bear, a similar-looking bear inside the 30 bee gate.

Tunnel Bear is a hostile level 9 boss mob.

Tunnel Bear spawns in the White Tunnel. The entrance to the White Tunnel sits underneath the Instant Converter near Science Bear.

Tunnel Bear respawns every 48 hours (2 days), but it can instead respawn every 40 hours and 48 minutes (1.7 days) if Gifted Vicious Bee is in the player's hive.

docs.title: The White Tunnel
docs.text:
Main article: White Tunnel

To enter the White Tunnel, go to the Instant Converter near the Pineapple Patch. Players can either jump through the chimney on the top or go in the right end of the Instant Converter and then drop down into the chute. Alternatively, players can climb up the hill to the Yellow Cannon/Science Bear and jump down from there.

Upon entering the White Tunnel, players will land in a small entryway with two green walls and two white walls. One of the white walls looks semi-transparent. Go through the semi-transparent white wall to find the tunnel. You have to move a little bit after going through the white wall as Tunnel Bear will quickly drop down through the roof near the entrance. The walls will also gradually get narrower, making it harder to turn back as players head deeper into the White Tunnel.

If Tunnel Bear does not appear and instead a countdown timer floats in mid-air, then that means the player will need to wait for the countdown on the respawn timer to finish before battling Tunnel Bear again.

To exit the White Tunnel, stand on top of the Teleport Pad and use it. The Teleport Pad will teleport the player on top of the Instant Converter near the Sunflower Field. The Teleport Pad looks like a flat gray circle that sits in the middle of the White Tunnel.

docs.title: Basic Strategies
docs.text:
Tunnel Bear possesses 10,000 health and can instantly kill players if they touch/get too close to Tunnel Bear ("Too close" is not the same as "touching," as the hitbox is bigger than its body). However, Tunnel Bear moves very slowly at a constant speed without ever speeding up, and on a very predictable path as it heads straight towards the player's location. Because of this, players could follow the recommended strategy of walking in front of Tunnel Bear and staying just close enough for their bees to keep attacking while leading it down the tunnel.

When entering the tunnel, keep Tunnel Bear near the beginning of the White Tunnel and keep close to one of the walls on the sides (this will only slow the bear a little bit because now he has no collisions), and occasionally jump around Tunnel Bear. This alternative will only work at the beginning (before the exit) because the White Tunnel narrows down the further players go down it, trapping them if they travel too far in. However, this should be the chosen strategy for the first defeat as to ensure getting the gifted egg. If the player's bees are mostly level 9, they will not have to jump around it, as their bees will most likely kill it first.

When Tunnel Bear spawns, players will only get 2 minutes and 30 seconds to defeat it. The timer is directly above its head, showing how much time remains for players to defeat it until it despawns. Note that it takes Tunnel Bear less than two and a half minutes to traverse the entire length of the White Tunnel.

If the player defeats Tunnel Bear too late, some items may appear outside of the tunnel past the winking eye face. This isn't an issue however, as Tunnel Bear's tokens automatically collect before they despawn.

If needed, the player can pre-activate Rage, Focus and precision using the Pineapple Patch enemies or Stump Snail in the Stump Field to get certain bees to spawn the tokens.

docs.text: Note that unlike the other mobs, Tunnel Bear drops its tokens in a straight line when it is defeated.
