docs.title: Strategy
docs.text:
• Own bees with a high attack stat. Bees such as Cobalt Bee, Brave Bee, Crimson Bee, Demon Bee, Vicious Bee, Lion Bee, Riley Bee, Bucko Bee, Precise Bee, Spicy Bee, and Rage Bee deal higher amounts of damage than other bees, making them more useful when fighting Tunnel Bear (or any other mob).
  • Own bees that boost fighting stats. Some specific bees will raise the effectiveness of the entire hive, either by boosting Attack (Gifted Rage Bee or Gifted Brave Bee), by boosting Critical Chance (Looker Bee, Music Bee or Gifted Commander Bee), by boosting Critical Power (Gifted Looker Bee, Gifted Tabby Bee, or Music Bee) or by boosting Super-Crit Chance and Power (Gifted Precise Bee).
  • Own bees that create Token Link tokens. Music Bee, Rage Bee, Exhausted Bee, and Shocked Bee possess the Token Link ability. Equipping the Paper Angel beequip on a valid bee teaches it Token Link as well. If a token appears too close to Tunnel Bear, use the Token Link instead of going back to get said token. That way, the player will not risk dying to Tunnel Bear.
  • Have high energy bees. Bees such as Photon Bee and Exhausted Bee have endless energy, and bees like Bumble Bee, Shy Bee, Lion Bee, Buoyant Bee, Fuzzy Bee, Precise Bee, Vector Bee, Gummy Bee, and Vicious Bee have at least double the energy of a typical bee. If the player's bees have low energy, then their bees will most likely go to sleep after just a few attacks. One method to refill essential bees' energy levels is to fight mobs until they go to sleep and recharge, as this will increase the player's odds of defeating Tunnel Bear faster. Completing Polar Bear’s quests can also help increase bee energy.
  • Level up bees to Level 9 or higher. Bees with a lower level than the mob will most likely miss when they attack. Bees with levels much lower than the level of the mob will have a higher chance of missing their attacks on the mob. Bees with an equal Level or higher Level than the mob will never miss it. During Beesmas 2020 and 2021, bees summoned when gandering at Onett's Lid Art, using Honeyday Candles, or using the Gummy Siege might be able to help defeat Tunnel Bear.
  • Stay logical. If players know that they cannot beat Tunnel Bear with the length of the tunnel, or if they keep dying, they should not keep trying to continue battling it. Instead, they should focus on getting better bees and equipment that can help them defeat it. The player should also wait until they can defeat it fast enough before it reaches the end of the tunnel since the tokens can despawn outside of the tunnel.
  • Move a distance from the start of the White Tunnel. Tunnel Bear can drop down at unexpected moments, instantly crushing players upon impact. If they make sure to keep a safe distance, Tunnel Bear will instantly start walking toward the player once he gets down.
  • When Tunnel Bear gets to low health, do not do risky actions. Whenever Tunnel Bear gets to low health, DO NOT attempt to go for tokens, such as rage tokens that sit near Tunnel Bear. Just keep going until it is defeated.
  • Keep a safe distance away from the Tunnel Bear. Players often die because they do not keep their distance. The farther players stay away from Tunnel Bear, the more space they get to collect tokens, but they should not stay out of the range that bees attack within, or the bees will stop fighting and just follow the player.
  • Know a method. If players decide to do the turn around method, they should remember to avoid going past the Teleport Pad or back into the drop location since the Teleport Pad will prevent players from successfully turning around, while the entryway will cause Tunnel Bear to despawn.
  • Own a Cub Buddy. Cub Buddies can help by collecting tokens, so owning a Cub Buddy can let the tokens that sit behind Tunnel Bear get collected in order to make the battle easier. Players can also use the alternative strategy, though it's riskier.
  • Use stingers. This is not recommended, as players should save them for Vicious Bee, but stingers can help to get the last bit of damage needed before Tunnel Bear despawns.
  • Have a Vicious Bee. Having a Vicious Bee is helpful, as its Impale can deal massive amounts of damage to Tunnel Bear.
  • Equipping the Fire Mask or Demon Mask. Both masks boosts the player's bees' attack.
  • Get attack mutations. Players can either feed atomic treats to guarantee a mutation, or feed neonberries first to make it radioactive, and then use bitterberries to have a higher chance of mutating a bee.
  • Empty your bag. If the player is going to try and defeat it, there's a chance they might die and lose their pollen. The player should empty their bag before attempting to defeat Tunnel Bear as a precaution.
  • Let your bees tell you how far to stay from Tunnel Bear. When the player's bees are far enough away to head back to the player, they should move a bit closer. The bees can help determine how far away the player is from collecting tokens.
  • Abuse a glitch method. When Tunnel Bear drops down into the tunnel, purposely walk to the left side of the tunnel. When Tunnel Bear attempts to follow you, his arm will clip into the wall, and as a result he will become stuck. This makes it extremely easy to defeat Tunnel Bear.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Tunnel Bear uses the Cartoony Animation Pack.
  • When Tunnel Bear despawns, it will do the wave emote and disappear. This occurs when the player dies, when the timer runs out, when the player goes back to the entrance or leave.
  • Tunnel Bear will also do the wave emote when stunned by Digital Bee's Mind Hack.
  • Tunnel Bear possesses a hitbox a bit wider than its body, so players may not touch Tunnel Bear and still die (this acts similarly to King Beetle's yellow "aura").
  • Since the 2019-04-05 update, the despawn timer was added. This makes it much more difficult to defeat since players now cannot defeat the boss by circulating the tunnel numerous times with a low attack rate.
  • Tunnel Bear despawns at the end of the White Tunnel.
  • Sometimes, a glitch can happen where Tunnel Bear can spawn on top of the tunnel.
  • Tunnel Bear is occasionally able to be seen leaping into the tunnel from outside of the map.
  • Tunnel Bear is 1 of the 5 bosses in the game, the others being King Beetle, Stick Bug, Coconut Crab, and the Mondo Chick.
  • Tunnel Bear got added as the first of three bears in the game that acts hostile to players, with Gummy Bear as the second and Snowbear as the third. Shadow Bear does not count because it does not kill players, the floor does.
  • Tunnel Bear serves as the second boss added to the game.
  • Tunnel Bear (1,000 damage) and cave monsters (10,000 damage) are the most powerful mobs in the game in terms of damage, as they can instantly kill players upon contact, the only exception being if the Emergency Coconut Shield is active.
  • Tunnel Bear takes the second most amount of time to respawn with Stump Snail being the first.
  • Tunnel Bear, Onett, and Gummy Bear acted "Naughty this year”, as stated by Bee Bear during Beesmas 2018.
  • Tunnel Bear looks exactly the same as Shadow Bear. However, Shadow Bear does not act hostile to other players and it is much larger than Tunnel Bear in terms of width and length.
  • Tunnel Bear, Shadow Bear, and Snowbear are the only faceless bears.
  • Tunnel Bear's location is revealed by Panda Bear in his quest "Ultimate Ant Annihilation 5".
  • Tunnel Bear and King Beetle are the only mobs that have a place that are only revealed by Panda Bear.

  • There is a chance that one of Tunnel Bear's arms can clip outside the tunnel walls, which significantly reduces its walk speed and/or renders it completely immobile, making it easier to kill.

  • In previous versions, Tunnel Bear would fall face down, slamming its face into the ground after spawning at the top. Then it will stand up and chase the player.

  • This is one of the two things in the game that drop loot in a straight line, the other being Mythic Meteors.
  • Additionally, this is the only mob that drops loot in a straight line.

docs.title: Turpentine
docs.text:
Turpentine

"A strong solvent that can remove all Waxes from a bee's Beequip."

CAP

25

Turpentine is a craftable inventory item added in the 2021-12-26 update. It is used to remove all waxes from a Beequip.

Turpentine have a maximum cap of 25. Obtaining while having more than 25 turpentines will not add them to the player's inventory unless received through quests, redeeming codes, or purchasing them in the Robux Shop through limited-time offers.

docs.title: Tutorial
docs.text: The Tutorial in Re://:Swarm is a guided walkthrough led by Black Bear. Instead of flipping through picture pages, new players get one objective at a time in Black Bear's dialogue panel, and each step moves on as soon as they actually do it. Movement is never frozen.

docs.title: Who gets it
docs.text:
The walkthrough is offered to players who have made less than 1,000 honey in total and have no bees in their hive yet.

  1. Claim a hive.
  2. Onett welcomes you with the Honeyday welcome.
  3. Shortly after Onett's welcome closes, the game asks "You look new here! Want to do the tutorial?"

Answer Yes to start the walkthrough or No to skip it. There is no skip button once it has started, and it cannot be replayed later.

While any NPC conversation is open, the walkthrough's panel hides itself so it does not cover the conversation.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
Every line comes from Black Bear. A step you have already done is skipped automatically.

# Black Bear says Objective 1 "Welcome! Let me get you started. This won't take long." Click to continue 2 "First, a hive of your own. Follow the arrow and stand on any free hive to claim it." Claim a hive (usually already done, so this step is skipped) 3 "That hive is yours. Now open your Eggs bag." Open the Eggs tab (the button pulses) 4 "There it is -- a Basic Egg. Every bee starts as one of these." Click to continue (the Basic Egg is highlighted) 5 "Drag it onto one of the glowing slots in your hive." Place the egg in your hive (the bottom middle slots glow) 6 "Your first bee! Head to a flower field and walk over flowers to gather pollen." Collect some pollen 7 "Bag full? Walk back onto your hive to turn all that pollen into honey." Convert your bag at the hive 8 "Nice work. Here's 5 Royal Jelly for that -- use them on a bee to reroll it into a random type." Click to continue 9 "Honey buys everything: tools, bags, hive slots. Here! Complete my first quest -- collect 100 pollen from the Sunflower Field." Click to accept the Sunflower Start quest 10 "Collect it, then come back to me in the Sunflower Field to turn it in. There's a Magic Bean in it for you." Turn in Sunflower Start 11 "That's the loop: pollen, honey, spend, repeat. Later, Rebirth resets your honey but makes you permanently stronger. I'll tell you when you're ready." Click to finish

Steps 9 and 10 are skipped if you have already completed Sunflower Start.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
Reward How 5 Royal Jelly The first time you ever convert pollen into honey at your hive. You get this once per account, even if you skipped the walkthrough. 200 Honey Turning in Black Bear's Sunflower Start quest (collect 100 pollen from the Sunflower Field).

Black Bear mentions a Magic Bean in step 10, but the quest only gives honey.

docs.title: Rebirth reminder
docs.text:
After the walkthrough ends, Black Bear lets you know when you have enough honey for your first Rebirth:

"You've got enough honey to Rebirth! It resets your honey but makes you permanently stronger. Follow the arrow, or press the Rebirth symbol in your Boosts."

An arrow leads to the Rebirth shop, the shop glows purple, and the Rebirth tile in your Boosts bar pulses. The reminder hides if your honey drops below the requirement and goes away for good after your first Rebirth. Players who skipped the walkthrough do not get it.

docs.text:
Released: September 18, 2026

A new Mythic bee, new bag models, the Honeycomb Blueprint and many fixes.

docs.title: What's new
docs.text:
• New Mythic bee: Mortar Bee, "A lazy artillery bee who would rather shell the field than work." More info is in the in-game Index.
  • New pack: Mortar Bee Pack, with two Mortar Bee Eggs, a Flying Mortar Bee sticker, a Happy Mortar Bee sticker and an Explosion sticker.
  • New sticker: Flying Mortar Bee, a rare drop from Mortar Bee's shells.
  • New item: Honeycomb Blueprint, a free permanent item unlocked at Rebirth 10. Open it from your inventory to rearrange your hive: tap a bee, then another slot, to swap them. Bees keep their gift, mutations, levels and Beequips when moved. Zoom in and out to see more of your hive.
  • New models for every bag (see them in the shops).
  • Bucko Bee and Riley Bee quests now give a permanent stacking buff: +0.01x blue pollen (Bucko Stack) or +0.01x red pollen (Riley Stack) per quest completed.
  • Added a skip option to the Tutorial.
  • Buying a Basic Egg auto-hatches it if you have an empty hive slot.
  • New settings: Festive Gifts toggle (sound and popup) and Loot Popups toggle (all loot popups).

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• Bucko and Riley quests scale much harder and go further into the endgame.
  • Refreshed styles for all tool stickers, and made them about 10x easier to get.
  • Shop restock every 7 days > every 2 days.
  • Changes to endgame Melittology requirements.
  • Rebirth quests are given automatically.
  • Removed the Ant Challenge from Rebirth 5.
  • All Memory Match cooldowns halved.
  • Mortar Bee now deals area damage at 50% of its attack, and is more likely to shoot at other bees.
  • Mortar Bee converts 5% of current pollen per bee, instead of 10k + bee conversion x (6% + 6% per boost stack).

docs.text:

  • Fixed some hive issues.

  • Fixed not being able to peel vouchers off your hive.
  • Fixed Memory Match.

docs.title: What's new

docs.text:
• Vector Bee's stats follow a Geometric Progression pattern, where each number is double the amount of the previous number.
  • Vector Bee is the only Mythic bee to not share any of its abilities with other bees. It is also the only Mythic Bee to not have a Passive Ability.
  • Vector Bee is the only bee to have a different skin pattern on each of its sides.
  • Vector Bee's design is heavily inspired by mathematics.
  • Its relation to trigonometry is implied in its description and the triangular motifs on its head.
  • Vectors reference Euclidean vectors, objects with magnitude and direction. A triangle can be composed of three vectors.
  • Triangulation is a method to determine the location of a point through forming triangles from known points.
  • Vector Bee, Spicy Bee, Precise Bee and Buoyant Bee emit light when they are gifted.
  • Vector Bee shares similar color schemes with Brave Bee.
  • Triangulate is Onett's favorite ability, due to the fact that he thinks it's satisfying.
  • Mark Surge token is considered by the game as "mark" token despite what the ability does doesn't create mark like what all other mark tokens do. This means the collection of Mark Surge token counts toward some quests, Coin Scatter passive ability, and anything that requires the collection of "mark" tokens.
  • Triangulate, however, is not considered as "mark" ability token.
  • In a similar fashion, Fuzz Bombs (Fuzzy Bee's ability token), Bomb Sync (Cobalt Bee and Crimson Bee's ability token) are not considered "bomb" ability tokens, and Honey Mark isn't considered as "honey" token.

docs.title: Vicious Bee Claimer
docs.text: The Vicious Bee Claimer (called the Vicious Bee Egg Claim in Bee Swarm Simulator) is a platform found between the Spider Field and Strawberry Field that lets the player exchange 250 stingers for a Vicious Bee egg. The platform is decorated with a large Vicious Bee and a "⚠️ WANTED ⚠️" sign. The pad's color is black, and the number "250" is printed on it, indicating that the player needs 250 stingers to claim a Vicious Bee egg. This exchange can only be done once per player. When the player walks on the platform and they do not have 250 or more stingers, a message on the top of the screen shows “Turn in 250 Stingers to Claim a Vicious Bee (Number of stingers/250)".

docs.title: Claiming the Egg
docs.text: If a player doesn't have 250 stingers and attempts to claim a vicious bee, the platform prompts the player with "Turn in 250 Stingers to Claim a Vicious Bee". If they have claimed the Vicious Bee egg but have more than 250 stingers and attempt to claim a vicious bee, the game will prompt them with "You've Already Claimed a Vicious Bee". Whenever a player purchases the Vicious Bee egg, the Rogue Vicious Bee victory jingle is played and a server-wide announcement is made: 🎉 {Username} has tamed a Vicious Bee 🎉

> This page is for the tamed version of Vicious Bee. For the hostile version, see Rogue Vicious Bee.

Vicious Bee is a Blue Event bee. It can be claimed for 250 Stingers at the Vicious Bee Claimer.

Like all other Event bees, this bee does not have a favorite treat, and the only way to make it gifted is by feeding it a Star Treat, Gingerbread Bears or Aged Gingerbread Bears.

Vicious Bee likes the Cactus Field and the Rose Field. It dislikes the Dandelion Field.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Vicious Bee's base attack was previously 7 before it was increased to 8 in the 2021-12-26 update.
  • Gifted Vicious Bee's impale ability gets golden-colored spikes, instead of the normal colored (gray) ones. The Impale ability does more base damage when gifted due to the +50% gifted attack bonus. The attack bonus is applied to the bee itself, but it indirectly increases the amount of damage Impale does—though this is not a significant buff due to the majority of Impale's attack scaling off of mob health.
  • Vicious Bee is the only Bee who can summon an Ability Token that directly attacks enemies.
  • This bee and Precise Bee are the only bees who have abilities that directly attack the enemies, namely Impale and Sniper respectively. (Digital Bee's Mind Hack ability doesn't count since it doesn't directly attack enemies).
  • Vicious Bee is one of three bees to have an official plushie on the Official Bee Swarm Simulator Website, the others being Basic Bee and Tabby Bee.
  • Vicious Bee is the only blue bee that likes the Rose Field. It may like the Rose Field along with the Cactus Field due to the fact that roses and cacti have thorns on them. The Rogue Version can also spawn in both of these fields.
  • Vicious Bee and Windy Bee are the only bees with a hostile variant.
  • It would cost the player 2,500 Tickets if they were to buy all 250 stingers from the Stinger Shop to get a Vicious Bee, which makes it the most expensive event bee to get by spending tickets.
  • Vicious Bee, Ninja Bee, and Cobalt Bee are the only blue bees that don't like Blueberries.
  • Vicious Bee, Bear Bee, Gummy Bee, Windy Bee, and Digital Bee are the only Event bees that cannot be purchased in the Ticket Tent. These four bees, along with Festive Bee and Puppy Bee, are also the only Event bees that could have been obtained without spending tickets. Gummy Bee was in the Ticket Tent at one point, however.
  • Vicious Bee, Cobalt Bee, Crimson Bee, and Photon Bee are the only event bees that can't have a 1st Edition Flag.
  • Onett has stated that the reason a First Edition Vicious Bee does not exist is because there is no room for a 1st Flag on its back with the spikes.[1]
  • Vicious Bee, the Stick Bug Amulet, and the Spider Field Market Boost are the only sources of the -% Mob Respawn Time stats.
  • According to Black Bear's dialogue during his quest "Black Bear, Why?", Black Bear dislikes this bee.

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Realistic max is the best you can expect to actually see: the most picks of that upgrade that about 1 in 1,000 fully waxed 5 ★ beequips get, each at its top value. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

docs.title: Waxes
docs.text: Waxes are Inventory Items that were added in the 2021-12-26 Update. They are used by players to modify the stats and abilities of Beequips. There are currently 4 different Waxes, and each Wax can affect a Beequip differently. The player can only use up to 5 Waxes on a Beequip, so if the Player would like to use more Waxes on a Beequip, they must use a Turpentine on the Beequip to remove the waxes. Doing this will change the stats back to the original ones the Beequip had. Waxes can also be used to craft Planters, Tools, and better waxes in the Blender.

docs.text:

docs.title: Wealth Clock
docs.text:
The Wealth Clock is a machine that boosts Honey Per Pollen and grants tickets to the player. The Wealth Clock is located next to Brown Bear, the entrance to Commando Chick's Hideout and the Honeystorm Summoner.

To use the clock, the player will need to have discovered 5 types of bees. The clock can only be used every hour of playtime. Each use grants x1.01 Honey Per Pollen, which stacks up to 5 times, with a maximum of x1.05 Honey Per Pollen. The Wealth Clock is also able to award Tickets, starting at 1 for the first use, increasing the amount of tickets awarded by 1 for every subsequent use until capping at 5 Tickets, on which the Wealth Clock will only produce 5 Tickets per use. Every subsequent use will award the player 5 Tickets. Every time it does, it will say the following:

(First four times)

[🕒 The Wealth clock has powered up... 🕒]

[It increases Honey made from pollen by #%.]

[It printed a Ticket/# Tickets!]

[Come back in 1 hour and it'll print #!]

[Remember, it resets if you leave the game.]

[+# Ticket (from Wealth Clock)]

(Fifth Time Onward)

[🕒 The Wealth clock is fully powered! 🕒]

[It prints 5 Tickets per hour!]

[Remember, it resets if you leave the game.]

[+5 Tickets (from Wealth Clock)]

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• There is a 15-minute grace period (can be offline for 15 minutes) until the Wealth Clock buff resets. This means the player can exit and rejoin, while still maintaining the boost, as long as they join within the 15-minute grace period.
  • However, if the player joins in that period of time, the Wealth Clock cooldown will reset back to an hour.
    • This can be evaded by abusing a bug. If you enter the hive hub and leave the game, the wealth clock will not reset.
  • The player can obtain wealth clock boost by redeeming certain codes:
  • FrogFix (Activates Wealth Clock x5 + other stuff)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Wealth Clock is located where the Honeystorm Summoner used to be.
  • As of the November 25, 2018 update, it increases the number of tickets it prints each interval. It will also start printing tickets the moment the player starts using it, but the player has to be in the server for 1 hour to use it instead of the previous 30 minute cooldown.
  • The amount of tickets granted by the Wealth Clock is based on the player's current stack of the Wealth Clock buff rather than how many times the player has used it (e.g. if the player has 1 stack of the Wealth Clock buff and then uses the Wealth Clock for the first time, it will grant 2 tickets instead of 1).
  • The Playtime Badge is represented by the Wealth Clock.
  • The Wealth Clock has a 1/250 (0.4%) chance to spawn an Hourglass Sticker in the Clover Field.
  • A mathematical formula can be used to represent the total number of tickets a player earns over x hours, expressed as the following function: \(f(x)={\begin{cases}0&{\text{if }}0\leq x<1\\1&{\text{if }}1\leq x<2\\3&{\text{if }}2\leq x<3\\6&{\text{if }}3\leq x<4\\10&{\text{if }}4\leq x<5\\5x-10&{\text{if }}x\geq 5\end{cases}}\)

docs.title: Werewolf's Cave
docs.text:
You might have been looking for Cave Monster.

The Werewolf's Cave, located beyond the Honey Bee Gate, sits between the Cactus Field and the Pumpkin Patch. It is home to the werewolf and two spider-like creatures called Cave Monsters inside of it that will try to kill you. There is a Gold Egg token at the end of the cave.

To get the gold egg easily, prepare items or gear that give haste, such as boots, guards, Oil, Bear Morph, and stacks of Haste and/or Haste+. Afterwards, make a run for it, jumping the whole way to avoid getting killed. Extra boosts, however, are not required nor needed. If you are lucky, you may be able to get the golden egg through jumping. Sometimes, there is a glitch where the cave monsters don't spawn or they are lagging, and in that case, it is easy to get the gold egg without preparation. Getting Haste+ by using the Royal Jelly Dispenser in the Star Hall or by using codes can help, and another option is to defeat the cave monsters in the cave, and then get the gold egg, though that solution can be hard. If you have pollen in your bag and wish to keep it, you can exit the cave using a Whirligig to exit the Werewolf's Cave safely.

If there is a sprout in the Mountain Top Field, its light beam is visible inside of the Werewolf's Cave. If there's a cloud on the Mountain Top Field, the rain might be visible. Honeystorms, snow storms, and mythic meteor showers are also visible while inside the cave.

docs.title: Werewolf
docs.text:
Werewolf Location Cactus Field, Pumpkin Patch Respawns Every 60 minutes (1 hour) (51 minutes with Gifted Vicious Bee)

The Werewolf is a level 7 mob found only behind the Honey Bee Gate. Unlike other mobs, it defends three fields instead of one: the Cactus Field, Pine Tree Forest, and the Pumpkin Patch. It spawns at the entrance of the Werewolf's Cave, in between the Cactus Field and the Pumpkin Patch.

It takes 1 hour for the werewolf to respawn after being defeated (51 minutes with Gifted Vicious Bee).

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
The main strategy players use is to have something in the way between them and the werewolf. The main things players use are the bigger cactus or the smaller pumpkin. The werewolf will bounce off the object when he tries to attack, making killing him easy.

The run-and-jump method also works: like most Mobs, the werewolf gets confused while the player is in the air and will lunge at the point the player was when they jumped, not where they're at after they jumped.

The Frozen Field Defenders Glitch works well against the werewolf.

Players can also just go through the Honey Bee Gate, then quickly run behind the Pine Tree nearest to the Badge Bearer's Guild. Then, if he goes back to the cave, just walk beside him and then run back behind the tree. The player should keep doing this until they defeat him.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This mob and the Spider are the only regularly-respawning mobs that can attack players beyond the field they spawn in.
  • This is the only normal mob to defend three fields (Cactus Field, Pumpkin Patch, and Pine Tree forest).
  • The werewolf uses the "White Fang Package" on the Roblox Catalog.
  • This was the first non-bug/arachnid mob added into the game.
  • The player can earn more than one egg after defeating the werewolf; for example, he can drop 5 Silver Eggs at once.
  • This is the second strongest normal mob in the game, only beaten by the estimated health of the cave monsters.
  • This is the first mob in which the respawn timer is 1 hour or more, the other 7 being Stump Snail, Snowbear and all other bosses.
  • If you run inside the Werewolf's Cave, you would be faced with a tunnel, which, if you cross, rewards you with a Gold Egg. However, the cave is guarded by Cave Monsters that you will have to rush past to reach the egg.

docs.title: Whirligig
docs.text:
Whirligig

"Teleports you and your bees back to your hive and briefly increases Convert Rate."

COOLDOWN

5 seconds

CAP

100

Whirligigs are inventory items added in the Beesmas 2021 update. Using one simply teleports the player and their bees back to their hive, as well as temporarily increasing Convert Rate.

Whirligigs have a limit of 100. Obtaining any while having more than 100 whirligigs will not add them to the player's inventory, unless they are obtained through quests or codes.

Attempting to use a Whirligig without claiming a hive will prompt the message: You must claim a hive to use a Whirligig

docs.title: Ways to Obtain
docs.text:
• A common drop from the Robo Bear Challenge.
  • As a rare drop from mobs such as Rhino Beetles and Mantises.
  • As a reward from finishing your own Robo Party.
  • As a drop from Robo Party mobs.
  • Buying the Frozen Forest Pack from Bee Bear's Catalog.
  • Buying the Winter Winds Pack from Bee Bear's Catalog.
  • As a drop from certain planters.
  • Planters harvested in Pine Tree Forest have a higher chance to drop whirligigs than other fields. Petal Planter gives the most whirligigs, although Blue Clay Planter has the highest chance of dropping them.
  • As a Stack Reward for adding certain stickers to the Sticker Stack:
  • The Launching Rocket rewards 10 whirligigs.
  • The Simple Mountain rewards 10 whirligigs.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Using a whirligig during an Ant Challenge will teleport the player to the center of the Ant Field.
  • Using a whirligig used to teleport the player away from the challenge, thus ending it.
  • This is also one of the ways to exit the White Tunnel other than defeating or being killed by Tunnel Bear, leaving and rejoining the game, and using the gray plate at the middle of the tunnel.
  • They are based on maple tree seeds (nicknamed whirligigs), which, when falling, spin, thus traveling further from the tree. This may have inspired the whirligig's mechanic of teleporting or rather "carrying" you back to your hive.
  • Before the 2022-12-26 update, Whirligigs had a cooldown of 5 minutes.
  • If the player has the Frozen debuff (from Snowbear), the whirligig will only teleport the player's bees.
  • This may also occur if the player is lagging.

docs.title: Max possible stats
docs.text:
A beequip takes 5 waxes, and a failed wax still uses a slot. Soft and Hard Wax give at most 10 upgrade rolls. Caustic Wax and Debug Wax give 4 rolls each, so 5 of them give 20 rolls and can also pick Caustic-only upgrades; Debug Wax always succeeds, while Caustic only succeeds 25% of the time and destroys the beequip when it fails. Every roll picks one upgrade at random, and an upgrade stops being picked once it reaches its max picks.

Best base value is the top roll before any wax, with how often a roll lands on it at 1 ★ and 5 ★. Realistic max is the best you can expect to actually see: the most picks of that upgrade that about 1 in 1,000 fully waxed 5 ★ beequips get, each at its top value. Absolute ceiling is the most the game allows, with every roll landing on that upgrade up to its max picks. Where it is higher than the realistic max, players are very unlikely to ever see it.

docs.title: White Balloon
docs.text:
White Balloon

"Floats over the field for 5m. Stores up to 10x your capacity and works best with White flowers."

COOLDOWN

10 min

CAP

25

The White Balloon is a consumable item added in the 2021-12-26 update. Once used, it creates a white balloon over the field the player is in, storing pollen collected underneath it. The pollen collected below it increases by 10%, with white pollen increasing by 20%. It holds up to 10x the player's capacity and floats over the field for 5 minutes before floating to the hive balloon.

White balloons have a cap of 25 in the player's inventory, and 1 per player in the field.

  • The Long Haul rewards 1 white balloon and other items.
  • Solitarily Steadfast rewards 3 white balloons and other items.

docs.title: White Tunnel
docs.text:
The White Tunnel is a hidden location behind the Brave Bee Gate that can be entered via the Instant Converter near the Pineapple Patch and Stump Field and exited by standing on a platform in the middle of the tunnel. It is home to Tunnel Bear. It does not contain any items, but it does have a picture of a winking Basic Bee face at the end of the tunnel, hinting towards the code "Wink" (valid). The farther down the tunnel you go, the narrower the tunnel becomes. This makes exploiting Tunnel Bear harder as you can only "turn around" at the beginning of the tunnel, elongating the fight.

The interior of the White Tunnel.

docs.title: Entrances
docs.text:
There are two ways to enter: by jumping into the top of the instant converter, or by hopping up into the right side of the converter. To use the first method, either hop up on one of the shorter parts of the converter, then jump into the chute at the top, or if you don't have enough jumping power to do that, go up to the Yellow Cannon and jump down from there, or jump on the converter from the ledge beside it.

Another way to enter is to glide to the walls of the map (in the direction of Stump Field), and then hop over to the gap in the ground, which is an alternate way of entering the White Tunnel.

There is an exit platform about a third of the way down the tunnel that will teleport you on to the top of the Instant Converter next to the Sunflower Field.

docs.title: Music
docs.text: The music here is "Crawlers", which also plays inside the King Beetle's Lair and the Commando Chick's Hideout.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The winking bee at the end of the tunnel is the same winking bee picture in a previous Re://:Swarm thumbnail.
  • Before the 2018-09-10 update, the tunnel could also be entered by going outside the map and finding the spot on the top of the tunnel where Tunnel Bear enters it. The update buried the tunnel under green grass (white snow during Beesmas) to make it more tunnel-like, so this entrance is now much harder to find. However, the cover is non-collidable so you can pass through it.
  • Before the 2018-11-25 update, the width of the tunnel was the same throughout the entire tunnel, instead of getting narrower.
  • To enter through the alternate entrance, you would have to jump over the wall behind science bear. Best way to do this is to use the Wind Shrine to get on the wall, then make your way over.

docs.title: Wild Windy Bee
docs.text:
Wild Windy Bee Location All Fields except the Stump Field, Ant Field. and the Hive Hub.

This page is for the Wild version of Windy Bee. For the tamed version, see Windy Bee.

The Wild Windy Bee is a Mini-Boss that spawns in the Dandelion Field, Pineapple Patch, Pumpkin Patch, Mountain Top Field, and Coconut Field.

During the Beesmas event, Wild Windy Bee could also spawn in the Clover Field, Spider Field, Bamboo Field and Pepper Patch in addition to the fields that it normally appears in.

A Wild Windy Bee may spawn naturally every two in-game Day/Night Cycles or from an offering to the Wind Shrine. If the first line of dialogue from offering to the Wind Shrine is “A sudden breeze sweeps the {item} into the sky" a Wild Windy Bee will spawn in a random field. If the player does not touch the cloud Wild Windy Bee is in for 3 minutes, it will de-spawn.

It can also be spawned by receiving Spirit Bear's "Tickle The Wind" [20] Quest that summons 3 Wild Windy Bees at Mountain Top Field, by completing Spirit Bear's "Space Oblivion" [24] quest that summons a single Wild Windy Bee, And by receiving Spirit Bear's "Spring Out Of The Mountain" [30] Quest that summons a single Wild Windy Bee.

When a Wild Windy Bee spawns, the player needs to find a floating Cloud over a field with Windy Bee inside. It will be camouflaged inside the cloud and have a distinct white trail. Touching the cloud in time will initiate the fight. The starting level of Wild Windy Bee upon discovery is random but can only go up to level 6 (unless spawned by Onett).

When Windy Bee starts its attack, all players on the server receive the message: "☁️ (Player Username) found Windy Bee in the {field} Field! ☁️". When the Windy Bee's HP reaches 0, the bee will drop rewards and immediately move to a random field, excluding the Hub Field, Ant Field, and Stump Field. It leaves successively better rewards behind each time it's forced to move. When it leaves the map after its 5-minute timer elapses, the server states: ☁️ Windy Bee is fleeing... ☁️

If the chimes on the Wind Shrine moves continuously from left to right, it indicates that Wild Windy Bee is on the map, either camouflaged in a cloud or fighting in the open.

You can see its level on its wings, much like the bees in your hive.

docs.title: Attack Pattern and Rewarding
docs.text:
Wild Windy Bee uses 2 different attacks. Its first attack is summoning 3 tornadoes that wipes Pollen off the field and deals damage every 0.5 seconds. The damage dealt depends on the proximity between the tornado and the player, plus the number of times Wild Windy Bee is defeated. The duration and speed of the tornadoes also depend on the number of times Wild Windy Bee is defeated. This attack can damage other mobs. The damage will vary from 1-20. This attack will happen first, then cycled after 3 Wind blows.

Wild Windy Bee's second attack is forming a gust of wind that blows players away with great force in a rectangular area. It will deal no damage, but the player(s) will be flung away if caught in the rectangular area, unable to deal damage for some time. A red attack indicator is shown for about one second to show where Wild Windy Bee is about to attack. The direction of attack depends on Wild Windy Bee's current position and the position of a randomly targeted player on the field. The size of the attack is based on how far the edge of the field is from where Wild Windy Bee is looking. If Wild Windy Bee cannot detect any players on the field, it will attack in a random direction. This attack is cycled in after Wild Windy Bee finishes the tornado attack.

Upon defeat, Wild Windy Bee leaves behind a cloud in the middle of the field that regrows flowers and gives +25% pollen for 10 seconds (+50% pollen if you have a Gifted Windy bee) for 10 seconds if you stand under the cloud(s) and gets refreshed while under the clouds. Its also grants +10% Unique Instant Conversion. A ring of tokens then appears underneath Windy Bee like Stick Bug, and each player gets their own loot ring proportional to the amount of damage dealt. Afterward, Windy Bee flies off to a different field. Wild Windy Bee will continue doing this for 5 minutes before fleeing.

Every time Wild Windy Bee is defeated, it levels up with more health, similar to Stick Bug. It also has a higher chance of dropping Cloud Vials and rarer items.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• When summoning one, 5 - 10 Field Dice/3-5 Oils/5-10 Glue is the best way if the player wants a cheap but reliable way.
  • Other options include: 1 Star Jelly, 3-5 Glitters.
  • Before summoning one, the player should make sure to defeat any tough mobs and bosses beforehand that would make fighting the windy bee much harder, particularly the Coconut Crab and Mondo Chick.
  • Nectars such as Invigorating Nectar grants x1.01 - x1.10 Bee attack and Motivating for 1% - 5% Bee Ability Rate.
  • Equip accessories that improve bee attack, such as the Fire Mask, Demon Mask, Coconut Clogs or Gummy Boots.
  • You can use Stingers for an extra 1.5x bee attack, though if you don't have a Vicious Bee it is not recommended.
  • Use Oils and/or Tropical Drinks for 1.2x player and Bee Movespeed and +5% Critical Chance.
  • Use Super Smoothies for both improved Movespeed, Bee Movespeed, Critical Chance and Super-Crit Chance. Though it's not recommended due to its expensive crafting recipe and its rarity.
  • Try and build up a Focus stack before starting the battle as critical chance improves the chances of a critical hit, increasing attack damage.
  • Try and build up a precision stack before starting the battle as precision grants Super-Crit chance that are 33% stronger than a critical hit and also reduces the cooldown for your Precise Bees to attack again by 75%.
  • You can also collect Melody to gain 100% critical power for 30 seconds.
  • The player can use the sound effects created by the windy bee to tell what attack it is going to execute next.
  • It will also start using a wind gust attack after summoning three tornadoes.
  • During the wind gust attack, the player should go into an open space to avoid the attack easily.
  • If possible, stand on decorations and ramps around the field to gain some height. This makes the Windy Bee think there is no one in the field and it won't target the player.
  • Going out of the field but near the Wild Windy Bee prevents its tornadoes from causing damage to the player although its wind gust attack still works.
  • Since the tokens from Wild Windy Bee have a relatively long lifespan, the player should follow the Windy Bee to its next field first, and then collect the rewards using a Token Link or get hit by a bullet or hitting all targets from Precise Bee's target practice.
  • Use the Transportation Devices to get to certain fields quicker.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The player can tell if a Wild Windy Bee is in a field when the wind chimes of the Wind Shrine are continuously moving (and if there wasn't a recent donation).
  • If the timer ends before it generates reward tokens, it will leave without making any rewards. However, if it has already started producing them, it will finish spawning them as Windy Bee flees.
  • Like Mythic Meteor Showers and Puffshrooms, the quality of its rewards are affected by the law of diminishing marginal utility. The more times the player receives loot from Wild Windy Bees in one day, the worse the rewards gradually get.
  • Windy Bee and Vicious Bee are the only bosses/mobs that are bees, Vicious Bee's counterpart being Rogue Vicious Bee.
  • Unlike Rogue Vicious Bee, the Wild Windy Bee does not have a gifted variant.
  • Similar to Rogue Vicious Bee's Impale attack, the tornado can deal damage to other mobs.
  • Onett would sometimes spawn Wild Windy Bee in fields, including fields where it wouldn't naturally appear, usually to help grow sprouts that he also spawns.
  • If Onett spawns them in the Stump Field, the Windy Bees freeze in the air upon defeat until the timer is up, as they are not programmed to fly to any other field from Stump Field.
  • At the end of Beesmas 2020, Onett spawned a couple of Wild Windy Bees called "The Windy Gang".
  • The Windy Gang made a return in Beesmas 2021, spawning a Festive Sprout and appearing in the Mountain Top Field.
  • On 2025-06-06, he summoned six level one Wild Windy Bees in Sunflower Field.
  • Black Bear mentioned this bee in one of his dialogues before it was added to the game, where he said "A powerful bee destroyed fields with gusts of wind."
  • This is the only mob/enemy that can knock players back.
  • This is the fifth mob to have non-fixed levels, the first four being Ants, Stick Bug, Stick Nymphs and Festive Nymphs. and the sixth being Snow Bear.
  • It is possible to damage a Wild Windy Bee while it is summoning rewards, by using flames.
  • This, along with the Commando Chick and Snowbear are the only Mini-bosses that drop loot in a circle.
  • This, King beetle and Commando Chick are the only mobs that drop loot only in the center of the location they are in, even when they are not close to the center.
  • When Wild Windy Bee flees, it will face all players in the server before flying off.
  • If the player collides with Wild Windy Bee's body by jumping into it, they will take some damage, as Wild Windy Bee has contact damage.
  • Windy Bee will not leave a cloud behind if the field has reached its cloud limit.

docs.title: Wind Shrine
docs.text:
The Wind Shrine is located beyond the Windy Bee Gate, next to the Pepper Patch. It allows players to donate items to it in exchange for rewards such as Field Winds and honey. The Wind Shrine has a cooldown of 1 hour between each donation. Donating cloud vials after donating a Spirit Petal is currently the only way to obtain a Windy Bee.

The Wind Shrine also indicates if a Wild Windy Bee is active in one of the fields. If the chimes are continuously moving around and nobody has donated recently, a Wild Windy Bee will be somewhere around the map.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Upon interacting with the shrine, it says "Would you like to make an offering to the Wind Shrine?" If the player clicks on the dialogue, a window pop-up will appear, in which it allows the player to donate any amount of almost any item in their inventory to the shrine. Upon doing so, a message follows, with the chimes moving around swiftly. If the player cancels the donation, it instead says "You canceled the donation."

If the player interacts with the Shrine during cooldown, it says "You may only donate to the Shrine once per hour. Come back in x: y." (x = minutes, y = seconds)

If the player wants to donate multiple items at once, they can hold down the "+" button. The rate at which the amount of that certain item increases the longer the "+" button is held down.

docs.title: Favor
docs.text:
Favor is a mechanic that affects the player's rewards from the Wind Shrine. Favor is increased by donating items.

A Spirit Petal is NOT required to be donated to start increasing favor.

All donations grant favor (5,000 + the favor value of all of the items donated). Below is a list of all items that can be donated to the shrine and their favor values.

This information might be inaccurate.

The information provided can often change and may become inaccurate.

docs.title: Honey
docs.text:
Each donation grants honey depending on the type and amount of the item donated. All donations, excluding spirit petals, grant honey, regardless of the other rewards. docs.title: Obtaining a Windy Bee
docs.text:
To get the Windy Bee from the Shrine, players must first donate a spirit petal to it. After donating a Spirit petal, any Cloud Vial donated gives the player a chance to obtain a Windy Bee Egg. The player's chance to obtain the Windy Bee Egg depends on how much favor the player has with the shrine.

If the player receives a Windy Bee Egg, the Wind Shrine will display the following message: "And it calls back to you!". The Windy Bee victory jingle will play, and server-wide message will appear in the chat, reading "🎉 [Player] has tamed a Windy Bee! 🎉", but if it fails, the message will instead read, "But it doesn't respond..."

If the player had purchased a Windy Bee Egg from the Robux Shop, they would get a star treat in place of a Windy Bee Egg.

docs.title: Badge Shivers
docs.text:
Badge shivers are rewards that are linked to the player's Badges. The player can shiver a badge when they have the required badges by donating certain items. Shivering a badge does not do anything to the badge itself, only granting certain rewards if you have certain badges. Donating more items at a time gives a higher chance of shivering the related badge. Some badge shivers may require multiple badges or certain tiers of badges. Other badges cannot be shivered, or they are currently unknown. Below is a list of all known badge shivers.

docs.title: Field Winds
docs.text:
When you donate certain items to the shrine, you have a chance to summon Field Winds. The winds are random and not guaranteed. The more of the item you donate and the higher your favor, the better chance you have at getting a high stack of winds.

  • Generally, the color of item you donate correlates with the color of field you get.
  • Purple potion has bias to get a large stack in red or blue fields. Generally, it is recommended to donate a purple potion for boosting.
  • Eggs often give a large stack in most of the fields. The rarer the egg, the better and more winds.
  • Swirled wax tends to give 7-8x white field winds.
  • Gifted Gold Egg often gives 7-9x winds.
  • Gifted Diamond Egg often gives 10-11x winds.

docs.title: Donations
docs.text:
The shrine will grant different rewards depending on the item donated. All donations will grant Honey and favor (both of which increase based on the amount donated), but other effects may vary. A list of possible outcomes is written below.

  • Summoning clouds on fields and granting field winds.
  • Summoning a Wild Windy Bee.
  • Summoning Bean Bugs and granting a Jelly Bean.
  • Granting badge rewards.
  • Enabling the player to receive a Windy Bee and granting other rewards.
  • This refers to when you donate the Spirit Petal, which can only be done once, which grants 500 Treats, 1 Star Jelly, 5 Enzymes, 5 Oils, 5 Red Extracts, 5 Blue Extracts, 5 Tropical Drinks and 5 Magic Beans.
  • Failing to obtain a Windy Bee and granting Treats.
  • Succeeding to obtain a Windy Bee.
  • Granting Galentine's Blessing, and other rewards during Beesmas.
  • Granting 7 Jelly Beans (Ready Player Two Event, although still possible as of 2025-11-28).

Certain items are more likely to have certain effects. For example, donating eggs other than Basic Eggs and Honey Bee Eggs will always grant field winds and donating Star Jellies, Magic Beans or Field Dice is likely to summon a Wild Windy Bee. Some items also have biases when granting field winds, such as Purple Potions being more likely to grant field winds for colored fields. Donating a diamond egg (or blue extracts) has a higher chance of granting winds for blue fields.

Keep in mind that the rewards are somewhat random, as offering the same donation twice in the same amount may have a different result. However, more items in the donation can grant better rewards.

docs.title: Galentine Shrine
docs.text:
The Galentine Shrine can be obtained after the player completes Spirit Bear's Beesmas 2020, 2021, 2022, 2024 and 2025 quests. It is the Wind Shrine decorated specifically for Galentine’s Day. There are five hearts, a large red bow on the top, and a smaller white bow between two hearts. The Wind Shrine's two 'pillars' are also coated in pink paint.

If the player donates Strawberries, there is a chance for the player to receive several rewards and the Galentine's Blessing buff which lasts for 2 days. The odds for a successful donation starts at 1% at 1 Strawberry, and scales linearly with the number of Strawberries donated in that single donation, up to 50,000 where it is guaranteed.[1] The player can only receive the rewards once.

The following equation determines the probability of receiving the Galentine's Blessing, where x is the number of Strawberries donated and P(x) is the probability: \(P(x)=({\frac {0.99}{49999}}(x-1)+0.01)\bullet 100\%\)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Wind Shrine is based on a percussion instrument, the wind chimes.
  • According to Spirit Bear, the Wind Shrine is one of the oldest standing monuments in the game. She also mentions that it is even older than she is.

  • She also says that the Wind Shrine gives you different responses depending on your favor.

  • Using the Wind Shrine is the only way to obtain a Windy Bee, other than buying it in Robux Shop when it was first released.

  • If the player donates something, but disconnects before the rewards fade out, the next donation will give the rewards of the last donation and set a cooldown of 1 hour. This will not happen if at least one reward is collected from the Wind Shrine.

  • If a player happens to reach the Wind Shrine without having 35 bees and tries to donate an item, a message will come up saying "Error: Player does not have 35 bees. Please show Onett. (Version {Server version})".

  • Super Smoothies, Translators, Sprinkler Builders, certain Specific Bee Eggs (all except for Honey Bee Egg), Specific Bee Jellies, Spirit Petals (if the player has already donated one), Gingerbread Bears, Snowflakes, Balloons, Planters, Robo Passes, the Beequip Case and 7-Pronged Cogs are items in the player's inventory that cannot be donated.

When donating 0 of something (e.g. 0 tickets), a message will appear saying "Error: Player does not have selected quantity of items. (Version {Server version})", or "Error: Cannot donate 0 items."

  • The chimes on the Wind Shrine are collidable and aren't anchored. This means if you try running into them, they will move.
  • The Galentine Shrine is a possible reference to the Parks & Recreation episode “Galentines Day”.
  • According to Spirit Bear, an Instant Converter was supposed to take the spot of the Wind Shrine.
  • Donating any amount of Jelly Beans for the first time will always give 7 in return.
  • The chimes (especially the right one) can sometimes get stuck on the top of the Wind Shrine. This is uncommon.
  • Donating while the chimes are still moving will result in them swinging further than usual.

The Windy Bee Gate, or the 35 Bee Gate, is a gate that requires 35 bees to unlock. It is located on the right of the Ticket Tent and Red Cannon. It gets its name from the large Windy Bee figure on top of it.

Inside this Gate is the Coconut Field, the Pepper Patch, Spirit Bear, the Wind Shrine, the Extreme Memory Match, and two Shops: the Petal Shop and Coconut Cave. The Petal Shop sells the Petal Wand, Petal Belt and the Petal Planter. while the Coconut Cave sells the Coconut Canister, Coconut Clogs and Coconut Belt.

docs.title: Music
docs.text: The soundtrack "overflowin4" plays past this gate.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This gate is the first and currently the only gate in the game that has an Event bee representing it.
  • This gate, along with the Bear Gate, are currently the only gates that require purchasing hive slots to pass.
  • The gate also plays the same music as the Bear Gate.
  • This gate gives access to the blocked off area in the Blue Maze through the Petal Shop.
  • This gate is the only place where sprouts can't appear naturally or be planted with the Special Sprout Summoner.
  • The sprouts planted by a player require more pollen to grow than in other locations for better loot and guaranteed more drops.

This page is for the tamed version of Windy Bee. For the hostile version, see Wild Windy Bee.

Windy Bee is a Colorless Event bee that hatches from a Windy Bee Egg, which can be obtained from donating Cloud Vials after having previously donated a Spirit Petal to the Wind Shrine.

Like all other Event bees, this bee does not have a favorite Treat, and the only ways to make it gifted are by feeding it a Star Treat, Gingerbread Bears or Aged Gingerbread Bears.

Windy Bee likes the Dandelion Field and the Coconut Field. It dislikes the Bamboo Field and the Strawberry Field.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Windy Bee's tornado path doesn't actually travel across the field randomly. It instead loosely follows a grid. This is slightly more noticeable when more haste tokens are spent and the tornado is faster.
  • It was formerly available to purchase for 800 Robux until the deadline, October 27 of 2019.
  • This was the 3rd bee available to be bought for Robux; the second being Festive Bee and the first being Bear Bee.
  • There is a gate dedicated to it, known as the Windy Bee Gate or the 35 bee gate.
  • This, and Vicious Bee are the only bees to have a hostile variant.
  • This bee, Music Bee, Vector Bee, Tadpole Bee, Spicy Bee, Fuzzy Bee, Buoyant Bee, Festive Bee and Digital Bee are the only bees with three different ability tokens, the most of any bee.
  • This bee, Ninja Bee, Shy Bee, and Fuzzy Bee are the only bees that have only one skin color.
  • This bee is the only bee to have the same skin color when it turns gifted.
  • This bee and Puppy Bee are the only event bees that don't have an 'enhanced' ability when gifted.
  • This bee is the only bee to have 2 gifted bonuses, excluding other Event bees who enhance their ability.
  • Currently, this bee, Bear Bee, Gummy Bee, Digital Bee and Vicious Bee are the only event bees that can't be bought in the Ticket Tent.
  • This is the only Event Bee to dislike 2 fields.
  • This, along with Buoyant Bee, are the only bees to be able to produce a White Boost token. However Buoyant Bee only produces it through Surprise Parties.
  • The Tornado ability, frogs, Puppy Bee's Fetch ability, the Cub Buddy and Star Saw are the only entities that can pick up items outside of personal tokens for the player.
  • This bee and Festive Bee are the only non-gifted bees that have tinted wings.
  • This bee was hinted at during the Black Bear quest "Black Bear, Why?" when he says this: "Vicious Bee isn't the only bee that causes trouble! One time, I saw a strange bee destroy a whole field with powerful gusts of wind! I wonder if there are any other mysterious bees roaming free out there?"
  • At one point, a model of a Windy Bee could be found outside the map, alongside with a model of a Vicious Bee.
  • Supposedly, Windy Bee likes the Dandelion Field because dandelion seeds 'go wherever the wind takes them'.

docs.title: Yellow Cannon
docs.text:
The Yellow Cannon is available for use once the player has discovered 12 bee types. It is located on a hill accessible from the Brave Bee Gate next to Science Bear and the Red Teleporter exit. It has a 5-second cooldown period. It targets the spawn platform.

If the player has the Parachute or Glider, they can use it in combination with the Yellow Cannon to perform a few shortcuts around the map as well as collect Royal Jelly tokens formerly inaccessible, such as the one in the Dandelion Field, on top of the hives, on top of the Noob Shop near the entrance of the Star Hall and the one near Brown Bear.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• This is one of the four cannons in the game, which the other three cannons are Blue Cannon, Red Cannon, and Gummy Cannon.
  • This is one of the three transportational cannons in the game, which the other two cannons are Blue Cannon and Red Cannon.
  • The Yellow Cannon has a cooldown of 5 seconds. While this is not normally possible to see during regular gameplay as the cannon launches the player too far to return in 5 seconds, the cooldown can be seen by using the Glider/Parachute glitch to stop all momentum as soon as the player exits the cannon.
  • This cooldown is shared by all the transportational cannons.
